title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試録序
皇上登寶位之二年適
龍飛第一科鄉試巡按雲南監察
御史陳天祥謹循舊典諗于
有司禮聘儒紳以專校文而
貴州應試之士例亦附焉時
兩藩奉
===
命内外臣工鎮守太監崔安張誠
右少監孫清總兵官黔國公
沐崑巡撫右副都御史吳文
度右僉都御史王質巡按監
察御史董鉦朱衮清刑郎中
朱塗皆慎重其事傅等如期
畢至以八月丁丑入院傅與
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試録序

皇上登寶位之二年，適龍飛第一科鄉試。巡按雲南監察御史陳天祥謹循舊典，諗于有司，禮聘儒紳以專校文，而貴州應試之士例亦附焉。時兩藩奉命内外臣工：鎮守太監崔安、張誠，右少監孫清，總兵官黔國公沐崑，巡撫右副都御史吳文度、右僉都御史王質，巡按監察御史董鉦、朱衮，清刑郎中朱塗，皆慎重其事。傅等如期畢至，以八月丁丑入院。傅與
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination

The second year after His Majesty ascended the precious throne coincided with the first Provincial Examination of his reign. Chen Tianxiang, the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor for Yunnan, respectfully followed established precedent and notified the responsible authorities. Confucian scholars of the gentry were ceremoniously invited to take sole charge of assessing the examination essays. According to precedent, candidates from Guizhou also joined this examination.

At that time, the central and provincial officials serving under imperial commission in the two provinces were Cui An and Zhang Cheng, Grand Directors serving as Regional Commanders; Sun Qing, Junior Director of the Right; Mu Kun, Duke of Qian, serving as Regional Commander; Wu Wendu, Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right, and Wang Zhi, Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Right, serving as Grand Coordinators; Dong Zheng and Zhu Gun, Investigating Censors serving as Regional Inspectors; and Zhu Tu, a Bureau Director charged with reviewing penal cases. All treated this undertaking with great care. Fu and the others all arrived as scheduled and entered the examination compound on the dingchou day of the eighth month. Fu and…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
教諭朱麒為考試官劉譓劉
漢杜誥廖軫程一嘉為同考
試官提調則左布政使熊祿
左參議陳一經監試則副使
李裕中僉事王經而左布政
使任弘按察使劉杲左右參
政沈林馬金孫春副使丁珝
===
陳振朱璣左右參議黎民表
胡拱林鐄僉事朱儀張弘宜
范玶彭程則協恭於外也合
雲貴就試生儒一千二百有
奇皆提學副使彭綱毛科所
擇三試之得士五十人以文
之優者萃而為錄傳僭序之
punctuated:
教諭朱麒為考試官，劉譓、劉漢、杜誥、廖軫、程一嘉為同考試官。提調則左布政使熊祿、左參議陳一經；監試則副使李裕中、僉事王經。而左布政使任弘、按察使劉杲、左右參政沈林、馬金、孫春、副使丁珝、陳振、朱璣、左右參議黎民表、胡拱、林鐄、僉事朱儀、張弘宜、范玶、彭程，則協恭於外也。
合雲貴就試生儒一千二百有奇，皆提學副使彭綱、毛科所擇。三試之，得士五十人，以文之優者萃而為錄，傳僭序之。
translation_en:
… and Zhu Qi, an Instructor, served as Examiners. Liu Hui, Liu Han, Du Gao, Liao Zhen, and Cheng Yijia served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Xiong Lu, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Chen Yijing, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner. Those overseeing the examination were Li Yuzhong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Wang Jing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. The officials who cooperated respectfully outside the examination compound were Ren Hong, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Liu Gao, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Shen Lin, Ma Jin, and Sun Chun, Left and Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Ding Xu, Chen Zhen, and Zhu Ji, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Li Minbiao, Hu Gong, and Lin Huang, Left and Right Assistant Administration Commissioners; and Zhu Yi, Zhang Hongyi, Fan Ping, and Peng Cheng, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners.
Altogether, more than twelve hundred students from Yunnan and Guizhou presented themselves for the examination. All had been selected by Peng Gang and Mao Ke, Surveillance Vice Commissioners serving as Education Intendants. After three examination sessions, fifty men were selected. The finest of their compositions were gathered into this record, for which I, Chuan [probably Fu; transcription doubtful], have ventured to write a preface.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
竊惟世運一新文運隨之故
曰八音與政通而文章與時
高下况
國家景運重開制度文為翕張
變化天下萬國耳震霆之洪
音目太陽之赫曜莫不動心
駭目手舞足蹈以鼓舞維新
===
之政而文章之在世表裏元
化感動轉旋之機尤莫先焉
與試之士固皆
列聖培養之素而
皇上又作新之譬諸稼焉耕耘盡
人之力雨露得天之功而收
穫之際風日清美飽滿成就
punctuated: 竊惟世運一新，文運隨之。故曰：「八音與政通，而文章與時高下。」况國家景運重開，制度文為翕張變化，天下萬國耳震霆之洪音，目太陽之赫曜，莫不動心駭目，手舞足蹈，以鼓舞維新之政。而文章之在世，表裏元化，感動轉旋之機，尤莫先焉。與試之士，固皆列聖培養之素，而皇上又作新之。譬諸稼焉，耕耘盡人之力，雨露得天之功，而收穫之際，風日清美，飽滿成就
translation_en: I humbly reflect that when the course of the age is renewed, the fortunes of letters follow. Thus it is said: “The eight sounds of music communicate with government, while writing rises and falls with the times.” How much more is this so now, when the auspicious fortunes of the dynasty have opened anew, and institutions and cultural undertakings expand, contract, and transform. Throughout all the lands under Heaven, people hear the mighty sound of thunder and behold the blazing radiance of the sun. None are unmoved in heart or undazzled in sight; all wave their hands and stamp their feet in joyful celebration of the renewed government. As for writing in the world, it works in concert with the great transforming process of Heaven and Earth; as a means of stirring hearts and turning the course of events, nothing takes precedence over it. The scholars sitting this examination have all long been nurtured by the successive sage emperors, and His Majesty has now renewed them once more. They may be compared to crops: ploughing and weeding exhaust human effort, while rain and dew supply Heaven’s contribution. At harvest time, with clear and lovely weather, they grow full and reach maturity…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無淫霖爛之疾風氣之宜乎
得美稼矣傳忝司文柄凡諸
士之文悉得過目佳者類亦
不一或淵奧蒼古或宏博富
麗或平淡爾雅或舂容紆徐
或簡勁奇偉光彩絢爛精神
流動其盛矣哉夫以雲貴僻
===
地而學者之造詣如此非世
運一新之會人自磨濯何以
致之雖然諸士負文藝而至
主司懸文鑑以臨之固一以
文事相與也科舉之設止文
而已乎盖將因文求人而措
之用者也自德行興賢高不
punctuated:
無淫霖爛之疾，風氣之宜乎，得美稼矣。傳忝司文柄，凡諸士之文悉得過目。佳者類亦不一：或淵奧蒼古，或宏博富麗，或平淡爾雅，或舂容紆徐，或簡勁奇偉。光彩絢爛，精神流動，其盛矣哉！夫以雲貴僻地，而學者之造詣如此，非世運一新之會，人自磨濯，何以致之？
雖然，諸士負文藝而至，主司懸文鑑以臨之，固一以文事相與也。科舉之設，止文而已乎？盖將因文求人而措之用者也。自德行興賢，高不
translation_en:
…free from the affliction of rotting under excessive rains. How favorable the weather! Fine crops have indeed been obtained. I, Chuan, unworthily entrusted with authority over literary assessment, have been able to read every candidate’s work. The excellent pieces are of varied kinds: some profound and antique in style; some expansive, learned, rich, and splendid; some plain, restrained, and elegant; some ample and unhurried; and some concise, forceful, striking, and magnificent. Their brilliance dazzles, and their vital spirit flows. What flourishing achievement!
Although Yunnan and Guizhou are remote lands, their scholars have attained such mastery. Had they not encountered an age of renewal and worked to polish and purify themselves, how could they have achieved this?
Nevertheless, the candidates arrive bearing their literary accomplishments, and the presiding examiners confront them with the mirror of literary judgment: their dealings are indeed entirely through writing. Yet were the civil-service examinations established for writing alone? Their purpose is surely to seek men through their writing and put them to service. Since the promotion of worthy men on the basis of virtuous conduct belongs to an antiquity so remote that it cannot…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
可考射御選士卑不足行於
是後世不能不設科求之其
為制莫盛於唐宋若韓柳之
文章韓范之功業周程張朱
之道學率由是而進者科目
得人盖不誣也我
國家右文崇儒遠過前代自洪
===
武永樂以来所得魁傑命世
之英視前賢無讓者不可悉
數科目之盛可謂極矣諸士
與登鄉書其陟於有位可待
尚期近追
當代之英遠繼往古之哲為科
目之光以無負
punctuated: 可考，射御選士，卑不足行。於是後世不能不設科求之，其為制莫盛於唐宋。若韓柳之文章、韓范之功業、周程張朱之道學，率由是而進者，科目得人，盖不誣也。我國家右文崇儒，遠過前代。自洪武永樂以来，所得魁傑命世之英，視前賢無讓者，不可悉數。科目之盛，可謂極矣。諸士與登鄉書，其陟於有位可待。尚期近追當代之英，遠繼往古之哲，為科目之光，以無負
translation_en:
…be verified; selecting men through archery and charioteering was too lowly to be practicable. Thus later ages could not but establish examinations to seek worthy men. This institution flourished most under the Tang and Song. Men such as Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan, distinguished in literary composition; Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan, in public achievement; and Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, in the Learning of the Way, generally advanced through this route. The claim that the examinations secured worthy men is surely no falsehood.

Our dynasty honors letters and esteems Confucian learning far beyond previous dynasties. Since the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, the outstanding men it has secured—talents born to serve their age, yielding nothing to the worthies of the past—have been too numerous to count. The flourishing of the examinations may be said to have reached its utmost height. You gentlemen have joined those inscribed on the provincial roll, and your advancement to official positions may now be expected. We further hope that you will emulate the outstanding men of the present age and carry forward the legacy of the sages of antiquity, bringing glory to the examinations, so as not to fail…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
龍飛第一鄉試之選斯為得之
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正
王傳謹序
punctuated:
龍飛第一鄉試之選，斯為得之。
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正王傳謹序。
translation_en:
…their selection in the first Provincial Examination following His Majesty’s accession; thus the selection would have fulfilled its purpose.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Wang Chuan, Instructor of the Confucian School of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili).

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
正德二年雲貴鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史陳天祥〔元吉武功左衛籍直隸吳江縣人丙辰進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使熊禄〔曰貴江西進賢縣人戊戌進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參議陳一經〔宗文四川成都後衛人甲辰進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司副使李裕中〔容正四川資陽縣人丁未進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事王經〔文濟□□山陰縣人庚戌進士〕
===
考試官
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正王傅〔希說廣東番禺縣人壬子貢士〕
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭朱麒〔汝祥福建懷安縣人丙午貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭劉謙〔益之山東濱州人己酉貢士〕
四川重慶府榮昌縣儒學教諭劉漢〔天章湖廣麻城縣人戊午貢士〕
順天府薊州豐潤縣儒學教諭杜誥〔汝欽山東即墨縣人辛酉貢士〕
浙江處州府雲和縣儒學教諭廖軫〔鍾宿江西崇仁縣人戊午貢士〕
直隸寧國府宣城縣儒學教諭程一嘉〔懋中福建莆田縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
正德二年雲貴鄉試

監臨官：
巡按雲南監察御史陳天祥〔元吉，武功左衛籍，直隸吳江縣人，丙辰進士〕。

提調官：
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使熊禄〔曰貴，江西進賢縣人，戊戌進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參議陳一經〔宗文，四川成都後衛人，甲辰進士〕。

監試官：
雲南等處提刑按察司副使李裕中〔容正，四川資陽縣人，丁未進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事王經〔文濟，□□山陰縣人，庚戌進士〕。

考試官：
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正王傅〔希說，廣東番禺縣人，壬子貢士〕。
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭朱麒〔汝祥，福建懷安縣人，丙午貢士〕。

同考試官：
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭劉謙〔益之，山東濱州人，己酉貢士〕。
四川重慶府榮昌縣儒學教諭劉漢〔天章，湖廣麻城縣人，戊午貢士〕。
順天府薊州豐潤縣儒學教諭杜誥〔汝欽，山東即墨縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
浙江處州府雲和縣儒學教諭廖軫〔鍾宿，江西崇仁縣人，戊午貢士〕。
直隸寧國府宣城縣儒學教諭程一嘉〔懋中，福建莆田縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination, second year of Zhengde (1507)

Supervising Official

Chen Tianxiang, Regional Inspector of Yunnan serving as an Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Yuanji. He was registered in Wugong Left Guard, was a native of Wujiang County in Zhili, and became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the bingchen year.

Proctors

Xiong Lu, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Yuegui. He was a native of Jinxian County, Jiangxi, and became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.

Chen Yijing, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Zongwen. He was from Chengdu Rear Guard, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.

Examination Monitoring Officials

Li Yuzhong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Rongzheng. He was a native of Ziyang County, Sichuan, and became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.

Wang Jing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan, had the courtesy name Wenji. He was a native of Shanyin County in □□ [illegible] and became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.

Examiners

Wang Fu, School Director of the Confucian School of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Xishuo. He was a native of Panyu County, Guangdong, and became a tribute scholar (gongshi) in the renzi year.

Zhu Qi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, had the courtesy name Ruxiang. He was a native of Huai'an County, Fujian, and became a tribute scholar in the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners

Liu Qian, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yizhi. He was a native of Binzhou, Shandong, and became a tribute scholar in the jiyou year.

Liu Han, Instructor of the Confucian School of Rongchang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, had the courtesy name Tianzhang. He was a native of Macheng County, Huguang, and became a tribute scholar in the wuwu year.

Du Gao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Fengrun County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruqin. He was a native of Jimo County, Shandong, and became a tribute scholar in the xinyou year.

Liao Zhen, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yunhe County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Zhongsu. He was a native of Chongren County, Jiangxi, and became a tribute scholar in the wuwu year.

Cheng Yijia, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Maozhong. He was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and became a tribute scholar in the xinyou year.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事陳鎰〔用之湖廣臨武縣人吏員〕
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事袁銳〔廷用四川成都中衛人監生〕
收掌試卷官
雲南府知府葉元〔本貞江西貴溪縣人甲午貢士〕
尋甸軍民府知府李逵〔士行直隸固安縣人丙辰進士〕
受卷官
大理府同知張壇〔主器福建龍溪縣人丁酉貢士〕
楚雄府同知曾顯〔克達江西泰和縣人丁酉貢士〕
===
彌封官
鶴慶軍民府同知楊金〔時重四川左護衛人丙午貢士〕
臨安府通判趙繼宗〔叔敬浙江慈谿縣人庚戌進士〕
澂江府通判晁必登〔汝吉四川宜賓縣人庚戌進士〕
謄錄官
景東府通判劉瑞〔世吉河南衛輝守禦所人壬子貢士〕
順寧府通判韓奎〔文東江西永豐縣人丙午貢士〕
曲靖軍民府馬龍州知州陳亮〔志明直隸廣德州人戊戌進士〕
對讀官
punctuated:
印卷官
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事陳鎰〔用之，湖廣臨武縣人，吏員〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事袁銳〔廷用，四川成都中衛人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官
雲南府知府葉元〔本貞，江西貴溪縣人，甲午貢士〕。
尋甸軍民府知府李逵〔士行，直隸固安縣人，丙辰進士〕。

受卷官
大理府同知張壇〔主器，福建龍溪縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
楚雄府同知曾顯〔克達，江西泰和縣人，丁酉貢士〕。

彌封官
鶴慶軍民府同知楊金〔時重，四川左護衛人，丙午貢士〕。
臨安府通判趙繼宗〔叔敬，浙江慈谿縣人，庚戌進士〕。
澂江府通判晁必登〔汝吉，四川宜賓縣人，庚戌進士〕。

謄錄官
景東府通判劉瑞〔世吉，河南衛輝守禦所人，壬子貢士〕。
順寧府通判韓奎〔文東，江西永豐縣人，丙午貢士〕。
曲靖軍民府馬龍州知州陳亮〔志明，直隸廣德州人，戊戌進士〕。

對讀官
translation_en:

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
今吾於人也聽其言而觀其行
德者本也財者末也
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
易
大君之宜吉
揚于王庭孚號有厲告自邑不利即戎
盛德大業至矣哉
===
天地設位聖人成能
書
皐陶曰都愼厥身修思永惇叙九族庶明
勵翼邇可遠在茲禹拜昌言曰俞皐陶
曰都在知人在安民禹曰吁咸若時惟
帝其難之
俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一哉王心
曰聖時風若
太保率西方諸侯入應門左畢公率東方
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

今吾於人也，聽其言而觀其行。

德者，本也；財者，末也。

集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。

易

大君之宜吉。

揚于王庭，孚號有厲，告自邑，不利即戎。

盛德大業，至矣哉！天地設位，聖人成能。

書

皐陶曰：「都！愼厥身修，思永，惇叙九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠，在茲。」禹拜昌言，曰：「俞！」皐陶曰：「都！在知人，在安民。」禹曰：「吁！咸若時，惟帝其難之。」

俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」

曰聖，時風若。

太保率西方諸侯入應門左，畢公率東方
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Now, in judging people, I listen to their words and observe their conduct.”

“Virtue is the root; wealth is the branch.”

“To bring together the complete achievement is to begin with the sound of bronze bells and conclude with the resonance of jade chimes.”

Book of Changes

“The great ruler’s fitting course brings good fortune.”

“Proclaim it in the royal court; cry out in sincerity that there is danger. Make the announcement from one’s own city. It is not advantageous to resort to arms.”

“How consummate are flourishing virtue and great achievement! Heaven and earth establish their positions, and the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment.”

Book of Documents

“Gao Yao said: ‘Ah! Be mindful of cultivating yourself, and let your thoughts reach far ahead. Generously maintain the proper order among the nine degrees of kinship; the many enlightened men will exert themselves to assist you. From what is near, you can reach what is distant: it lies in this.’ Yu bowed in acknowledgment of these excellent words and said: ‘Yes!’ Gao Yao said: ‘Ah! It lies in knowing people and bringing peace to the people.’ Yu said: ‘Oh! To accomplish all this—even the emperor would find it difficult.’”

“Cause all the people to say: ‘Great indeed are the king’s words!’ And also: ‘Undivided indeed is the king’s heart!’”

“It is called sagacity; timely winds respond in accordance with it.”

“The Grand Guardian led the regional lords of the west into the left side of the Ying Gate; the Duke of Bi led those of the east …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
諸侯入應門右皆布乗黄朱賔稱奉圭
兼幣曰一二臣衞敢執壤奠皆再拜稽
首
詩
其儀一兮心如結兮
樂只君子天子葵之
其胤維何天被爾禄君子萬年景命有僕
其僕維何釐爾女士釐爾女士從以孫
子
===
令妻壽母宜大夫庶士邦國是有
春秋
元年〔隱公〕
無駭帥師入極〔隱公二年〕季孫行父如齊
〔宣公元年〕晉侯使士匄來聘〔襄公八年〕
叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋
向戌衞齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭
罕虎許人曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕仲孫何
忌會晉韓不信齊高張宋仲幾衞世叔
punctuated:
諸侯入應門右，皆布乗黄朱。賔稱奉圭兼幣，曰：「一二臣衞，敢執壤奠。」皆再拜稽首。

詩
其儀一兮，心如結兮。
樂只君子，天子葵之。
其胤維何？天被爾禄。君子萬年，景命有僕。其僕維何？釐爾女士。釐爾女士，從以孫子。
令妻壽母，宜大夫庶士，邦國是有。

春秋
元年〔隱公〕。
無駭帥師入極〔隱公二年〕。季孫行父如齊〔宣公元年〕。晉侯使士匄來聘〔襄公八年〕。
叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衞齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕。仲孫何忌會晉韓不信、齊高張、宋仲幾、衞世叔
translation_en:
…the regional lords entered on the right of the Ying Gate. All set out teams of yellow horses with red manes [?]. The guests presented jade tablets together with silk offerings, declaring: “We, your servants who guard the realm, venture to present the offerings of our lands.” All bowed twice and touched their foreheads to the ground.

Book of Odes
His bearing is constant; his heart is as firmly bound as a knot.
Joyful is the noble lord; the Son of Heaven esteems him [?].
What shall his succession be? Heaven bestows its blessings upon you. May the noble lord live ten thousand years; the great mandate rests upon him. How shall it rest upon him? By granting you a noble lady. By granting you a noble lady, and following her with grandsons and sons.
Bring honor to your wife and long life to your mother; be well suited to the grandees and the many servicemen, and possess the state.

Spring and Autumn Annals
First year. 〔Duke Yin.〕
Wu Hai led an army into Ji. 〔Second year of Duke Yin.〕 Jisun Xingfu went to Qi. 〔First year of Duke Xuan.〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a diplomatic visit to Lu. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao. 〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕 Zhongsun Heji met with Han Buxin of Jin, Gao Zhang of Qi, Zhong Ji of Song, and Shishu of Wei…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
申鄭國參曹人莒人薛人杞人小邾人
城成周〔昭公三十二年〕
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭〔同〕
盟于戲〔襄公九年〕

禮記
臨財毋苟得臨難毋苟免
以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟以和夫婦
===
發號出令而民說謂之和
其寬裕有如此者儒有內稱不辟親外舉
不辟怨
第貳場
論
仁義人主之術
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元元年〕
punctuated:
申、鄭國參、曹人、莒人、薛人、杞人、小邾人城成周。〔昭公三十二年〕
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭，〔同〕盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕
用田賦。〔哀公十二年〕

禮記
臨財毋苟得，臨難毋苟免。
以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以和夫婦。
發號出令而民說，謂之和。
其寬裕有如此者。儒有內稱不辟親，外舉不辟怨。

第貳場
論
仁義，人主之術。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔。〔建元元年〕
translation_en:
…Shen, Guo Can of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Xue, Qi, and Little Zhu fortified Chengzhou. 〔Thirty-second year of Duke Zhao〕
The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng; 〔“together” [?]〕 they covenanted at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕
A levy on fields was instituted. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Ai〕

Record of Rites
When faced with wealth, do not seek improper gain; when faced with danger, do not seek improper escape.
To set right relations between ruler and minister, deepen affection between father and son, promote amity between brothers, and foster harmony between husband and wife.
When commands are issued and orders promulgated, and the people are pleased, this is called harmony.
Such is his breadth of mind and generosity. The scholar, when recommending someone from within his own circle, does not exclude relatives; when putting forward someone from outside it, he does not exclude enemies.

Second Session
Discourse
Benevolence and righteousness: the arts of the ruler.
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials.
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor calling for the recommendation of worthy and good men, upright and principled, who will speak frankly and remonstrate forcefully. 〔First year of Jianyuan〕

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬纂修
孝宗敬皇帝實錄成
進呈表
判語五條
講讀律令
賦役不均
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
===
干名犯義
第叄場
策五道
問帝王之興宜有一代之文以為教於天
下後世是之謂君師之道然天之於人
不能使之盡得其全而無少不足者大
哉帝堯君哉帝舜二典之載特史臣所
紀之詞堯舜未嘗發於精神心術以為
文也若六經之文孔子以是為萬代事
punctuated:
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬纂修孝宗敬皇帝實錄成進呈表。
判語五條：講讀律令；賦役不均；服舍違式；優恤軍屬；干名犯義。
第叄場
策五道
問：帝王之興，宜有一代之文，以為教於天下後世，是之謂君師之道。然天之於人，不能使之盡得其全而無少不足者。大哉帝堯！君哉帝舜！二典之載，特史臣所紀之詞，堯舜未嘗發於精神心術以為文也。若六經之文，孔子以是為萬代事
translation_en:
Draft a Tang patent appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor. 〔Third year of Zhenguan〕
Draft a memorial presenting the completed Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong Jing.
Five legal judgments, on: expounding and reading the statutes and ordinances; unequal assessment of taxes and labor services; clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed regulations; preferential relief for military dependents; and offending against familial status and violating moral obligations.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: When emperors and kings arise, there ought to be writings distinctive to their age to instruct the world and later generations. This is what is called the Way of the ruler and teacher. Yet Heaven, in its dealings with human beings, cannot enable them all to possess its gifts in their entirety, without the slightest deficiency. Great indeed was Emperor Yao! A true ruler indeed was Emperor Shun! What is recorded in the two Canons consists merely of words set down by the court historians; Yao and Shun themselves never gave expression to their spiritual energies and the workings of their minds in writings. As for the writings of the Six Classics, Confucius made these his undertaking for ten thousand generations…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
業堯舜所不得與者而君師之位孔子
未之有焉造化之不足於人者固如是
乎我
太祖高皇帝有大誥三編
太宗文皇帝有為善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝有五倫書
列聖皆以天地之德帝王之位奎璧之文齊堯
舜而兼孔子矣天之所以全其賦畀者
亦有可知者歟生斯世為斯民居治教
===
之中於
聖製之文固宜服膺也試舉宏綱大要一二與
諸生論之
夫誥之布至於再三屢出而不厭者其故何
居丁寧而不已者其指安在其間為條
凡幾何者為始何者為終可得言歟
為善陰隲有治獄而能活人者何人有用兵
而能活人者何人昆虫之活細事也何
以亦獲天之報瓜菓之設小善也何以
punctuated:
業，堯舜所不得與者，而君師之位，孔子未之有焉。造化之不足於人者，固如是乎？我太祖高皇帝有《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝有《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝有《五倫書》。列聖皆以天地之德、帝王之位、奎璧之文，齊堯舜而兼孔子矣。天之所以全其賦畀者，亦有可知者歟？生斯世，為斯民，居治教之中，於聖製之文，固宜服膺也。試舉宏綱大要一二，與諸生論之。
夫誥之布，至於再三，屢出而不厭者，其故何居？丁寧而不已者，其指安在？其間為條凡幾？何者為始？何者為終？可得言歟？
《為善陰隲》有治獄而能活人者，何人？有用兵而能活人者，何人？昆虫之活，細事也，何以亦獲天之報？瓜菓之設，小善也，何以
translation_en:
…an undertaking for ten thousand generations, in which Yao and Shun could not participate; yet Confucius never possessed the position of sovereign and teacher. Is this indeed how the creative workings of Heaven leave human beings incomplete? Our Emperor Taizu Gao produced the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao); Emperor Taizong Wen produced the two books Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Wei shan yin zhi) and Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi); and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang produced the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu). These sage emperors, possessing the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the station of emperors, and writings resplendent as the Kui and Bi constellations, have equaled Yao and Shun while also combining their achievements with those of Confucius. Can we discern how Heaven has bestowed its gifts upon them in full? Born in this age, belonging to its people, and living under its governance and instruction, we should surely take these imperial writings to heart. Let us select one or two of their broad principles and essential points for discussion with you candidates.
As for the promulgation of the Pronouncements, what explains their being issued a second and third time, repeatedly and without wearying? What is the purport of their unceasing admonitions? How many articles do they contain altogether? Which comes first, and which last? Can you explain this?
In Doing Good and Hidden Recompense, who was able to save lives while adjudicating criminal cases? Who was able to save lives while conducting military operations? Saving insects is a trifling matter: why did it nevertheless earn Heaven’s recompense? Setting out melons and fruit is a small kindness: why …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
亦獲福之隆
孝順事實孰為帝王之孝孰為公卿之孝孝
一也而何以有孝忠孝義之異又何以
有孝友孝節之殊
五倫書所載君臣之倫何其詳父子兄弟夫
婦之倫何其略堯舜禹湯君之聖也謙
德之所載無堯節儉之所載無舜豈舜
不能儉而堯不能謙乎叙君道臣道之
善行為類各四十有八其間亦各有序
===
乎否也
三誥三書有司者懼吾人莫不飲食鮮能知
味也故於秋闈發之諸生試鋪張而條
答焉則與凡民異矣
問封建之制古有之矣肇於何時盛於何
代何為而國増益多何為而國減復少
秦罷侯置守廢封建而為郡縣後世論
封建者惟秦之罪然自漢以来封建之
行何代無之豈秦之所廢者果非此乎
punctuated:
亦獲福之隆？
《孝順事實》，孰為帝王之孝？孰為公卿之孝？孝一也，而何以有孝忠、孝義之異？又何以有孝友、孝節之殊？
《五倫書》所載，君臣之倫何其詳，父子、兄弟、夫婦之倫何其略？堯、舜、禹、湯，君之聖也；謙德之所載無堯，節儉之所載無舜，豈舜不能儉而堯不能謙乎？叙君道、臣道之善行，為類各四十有八，其間亦各有序乎？否也？
三誥三書，有司者懼吾人莫不飲食，鮮能知味也，故於秋闈發之。諸生試鋪張而條答焉，則與凡民異矣。
問：封建之制，古有之矣。肇於何時？盛於何代？何為而國増益多？何為而國減復少？秦罷侯置守，廢封建而為郡縣。後世論封建者，惟秦之罪。然自漢以来，封建之行，何代無之？豈秦之所廢者果非此乎？
translation_en:
…also receive such abundant blessings?

In Records of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), which examples illustrate the filial piety of emperors and kings, and which that of dukes and high ministers? Filial piety is one virtue: why, then, are there distinctions between filial piety joined with loyalty and filial piety joined with righteousness? Why, too, are there distinctions between filial piety joined with fraternal affection and filial piety joined with steadfast integrity?

In the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), why is the relationship between ruler and minister treated in such detail, while those between father and son, elder and younger brothers, and husband and wife are treated so briefly? Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were sage rulers. Yet the accounts of humble virtue do not include Yao, and those of frugality do not include Shun. Could it be that Shun was incapable of frugality and Yao incapable of humility? The good deeds illustrating the way of rulers and the way of ministers are arranged into forty-eight categories each. Does each set also have an internal order, or not?

Concerning the Three Proclamations and the three books, the responsible officials fear that, although all of us eat and drink, few can discern the flavor. Therefore they have raised these matters in the autumn Provincial Examination. Let you students expound upon them and answer point by point; you will then distinguish yourselves from the common people.

Question: The system of enfeoffment existed in antiquity. When did it originate? In which age did it flourish? Why did the number of states increase, and why did it subsequently decrease? Qin abolished the lords and appointed governors, replacing enfeoffment with commanderies and counties. Those in later ages who discuss enfeoffment lay the blame solely upon Qin. Yet, from the Han onward, in what dynasty was enfeoffment not practiced? Could it be that what Qin abolished was in fact something other than this?

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
我
太祖高皇帝立國廟謨酌古準今萬代無弊郡
縣之制固在而封建之制亦未嘗無嘗
竊論之有封建之名而非前代封建之
實者天下之
宗室是也有封建之實而非前代封建之名
者四裔之酋長是也其間立法之善有
可得而言歟三代以上之封建不可復
矣而經生學士尚有是古之論盖以前
===
人甲可乙否迄無定說姑舉一二大儒
言之有曰公天下之端自秦始有曰封
建者公天下之大端大本也有曰封建
者爭之端亂之始也有曰必如是然後
能公天下以為心而達君臣之義於天
下數家之說孰得孰失古之封建其果
可行乎不可行乎請折衷以已見用袪
萬世之疑
問古之為民者四士農工商是也兵為國
punctuated:
我太祖高皇帝立國廟謨，酌古準今，萬代無弊。郡縣之制固在，而封建之制亦未嘗無。嘗竊論之：有封建之名，而非前代封建之實者，天下之宗室是也；有封建之實，而非前代封建之名者，四裔之酋長是也。其間立法之善，有可得而言歟？三代以上之封建不可復矣，而經生學士尚有是古之論，盖以前人甲可乙否，迄無定說。姑舉一二大儒言之：有曰：「公天下之端自秦始。」有曰：「封建者，公天下之大端大本也。」有曰：「封建者，爭之端，亂之始也。」有曰：「必如是，然後能公天下以為心，而達君臣之義於天下。」數家之說，孰得孰失？古之封建，其果可行乎？不可行乎？請折衷以已見，用袪萬世之疑。

問：古之為民者四，士農工商是也。兵為國
translation_en:
…Our Emperor Taizu Gao, in his sovereign plans for founding the dynasty, weighed ancient precedents against present circumstances, establishing arrangements free of defects for ten thousand generations. The system of prefectures and counties certainly exists, yet enfeoffment has never been entirely absent either. I have ventured to consider the matter: those who bear the name of enfeoffment without possessing its substance as practiced in previous dynasties are the members of the imperial clan throughout the realm; those who possess its substance without bearing its name as used in previous dynasties are the chieftains of the outlying regions in all four directions. Can the merits of the institutions established in these cases be explained? The enfeoffment practiced during the Three Dynasties and earlier cannot be restored, yet students of the classics and learned scholars still argue in favor of antiquity. This is because, among earlier thinkers, one approved and another rejected it, and no settled judgment has yet emerged. Let us cite a few statements by great Confucian scholars. One said: “The beginnings of making All-under-Heaven public arose with the Qin.” Another said: “Enfeoffment is the great starting point and fundamental basis for making All-under-Heaven public.” Another said: “Enfeoffment is the source of contention and the beginning of disorder.” Another said: “Only through such arrangements can one take making All-under-Heaven public as one’s guiding intention and extend the proper relationship between ruler and subject throughout the realm.” Among these several views, which are right and which are wrong? Can ancient enfeoffment actually be practiced, or can it not? Please weigh these views and offer your own judgment, thereby dispelling doubts for all ages.

Question: In antiquity, the people were divided into four occupations: scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants. Military affairs, for the state…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之大事自黄虞以来盖有之而周制益
詳然稱民止四不及於兵何歟管子内
政有士農之鄉有工商之鄉而士非四
民之士也抑不知四民之士將何以置
之歟其所以為兵亦有可考歟易象曰
君子辨上下定民志程子曰古之時公
卿大夫稱其德農工商賈勤其事而後
民志定公卿大夫即士之流也志定則
安其分而外無所慕各事其業而他無
===
所遷然則舜耕歷山伊尹耕有莘釋耒
耜而致時雍之化去泥塗而任天下之
重果士為農乎抑農為士乎傅說舉於
版築膠鬲舉於魚塩果真工乎果真商
乎是民志未見其為定也程子之言無
乃不足信歟三代以降制不如古隸尺
籍者遍於中土躬甲胄者盈於疆場論
後世之民者亦宜如古所謂士農工商
而不及於兵可乎古之制果盡善否歟
punctuated: 之大事，自黄虞以来盖有之，而周制益詳。然稱民止四，不及於兵，何歟？管子内政有士農之鄉，有工商之鄉，而士非四民之士也。抑不知四民之士將何以置之歟？其所以為兵，亦有可考歟？《易》象曰：「君子辨上下，定民志。」程子曰：「古之時，公卿大夫稱其德，農工商賈勤其事，而後民志定。」公卿大夫即士之流也。志定則安其分，而外無所慕；各事其業，而他無所遷。然則舜耕歷山，伊尹耕有莘，釋耒耜而致時雍之化，去泥塗而任天下之重，果士為農乎？抑農為士乎？傅說舉於版築，膠鬲舉於魚塩，果真工乎？果真商乎？是民志未見其為定也。程子之言，無乃不足信歟？三代以降，制不如古，隸尺籍者遍於中土，躬甲胄者盈於疆場。論後世之民者，亦宜如古所謂士農工商，而不及於兵，可乎？古之制果盡善否歟？
translation_en:
…a major affair of state. Military service has presumably existed since the days of Huangdi and Shun, and its institutions became more detailed under the Zhou. Yet accounts of the people name only four occupations and do not include soldiers. Why is this? In Guanzi’s arrangements for internal administration, there were townships for soldiers and farmers and townships for artisans and merchants. But these “shi,” or soldiers, were not the “shi,” or scholars, of the four occupations. How, then, were the scholars of the four occupations to be accommodated? Can the means by which soldiers were organized also be ascertained?

The Commentary on the Images in the Book of Changes says: “The gentleman distinguishes those above from those below and settles the aspirations of the people.” Master Cheng says: “In ancient times, dukes, ministers, and grand masters held positions commensurate with their virtue, while farmers, artisans, and merchants diligently pursued their occupations; only then were the people’s aspirations settled.” Dukes, ministers, and grand masters belong to the ranks of scholars. When their aspirations are settled, people rest content with their allotted stations, desiring nothing beyond them; each pursues his own occupation without shifting to another.

Yet Shun farmed at Lishan, and Yi Yin farmed at Youshen. They laid aside their plowing implements and brought about an age of harmony; they left the mud of the fields and assumed the weighty responsibilities of governing All under Heaven. Were these actually scholars working as farmers, or farmers becoming scholars? Fu Yue was raised to office from rammed-earth construction, and Jiao Ge from the fish and salt trades. Was the former truly an artisan, and the latter truly a merchant? In these cases, the people’s aspirations do not appear to have been settled. Might Master Cheng’s words, then, be unworthy of belief?

Since the Three Dynasties, institutions have fallen short of those of antiquity. Men enrolled in military registers are found throughout the central lands, and men wearing armor and helmets fill the borderlands. Can those discussing the people of later ages properly follow the ancient practice of speaking of scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants while omitting soldiers? Were the institutions of antiquity indeed entirely good?

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
如其善亦可行於今歟今之為制亦有
近似者歟諸士抱藝而來其於古今世
變展轉於中素矣其悉陳之毋讓
問天地間財止有此數不在於官則在於
民今天下承平日久海内奠安宜乎公
私具足積於無用可也夫何地之所斂
或倍其常而用之所需反乏於舊將以
為在官耶則天下諸省倉廩罕見有紅
腐之積府庫未聞有貫朽之財小有用
===
費輒憂匱乏甚至
内帑之儲戶部之積欲求充盛或亦少之是
不在官也將以為在民耶則四方之民
耕桑多不能為衣食之資俯仰多不遂
事育之願一遇凶荒相率流移甚至膏
腴之地豐稔之年欲求飽煖亦或難之
是又不在民也然所以致此者其故何
由玆欲使國富於上民給於下其處之
必有要而行之必有本焉請著于篇以
punctuated:
如其善，亦可行於今歟？今之為制，亦有近似者歟？諸士抱藝而來，其於古今世變，展轉於中素矣。其悉陳之，毋讓。
問：天地間財止有此數，不在於官，則在於民。今天下承平日久，海内奠安，宜乎公私具足，積於無用可也。夫何地之所斂或倍其常，而用之所需反乏於舊？將以為在官耶？則天下諸省倉廩罕見有紅腐之積，府庫未聞有貫朽之財，小有用費，輒憂匱乏。甚至内帑之儲、戶部之積，欲求充盛，或亦少之。是不在官也。將以為在民耶？則四方之民，耕桑多不能為衣食之資，俯仰多不遂事育之願。一遇凶荒，相率流移。甚至膏腴之地、豐稔之年，欲求飽煖，亦或難之。是又不在民也。然所以致此者，其故何由？玆欲使國富於上，民給於下，其處之必有要，而行之必有本焉。請著于篇，以
translation_en:
…If it is good, can it also be put into practice today? Do present institutions have anything resembling it? You gentlemen have come bearing your scholarly attainments; changes in the world, past and present, have long occupied your thoughts. Set forth your views fully, without holding back.
Question: There is only so much wealth between Heaven and Earth. If it is not held by the government, it must be held by the people. The realm has now enjoyed peace for many years, and all within the seas is secure. Public and private resources ought therefore to be ample, with reserves accumulating beyond what is needed. Why, then, do levies on the land sometimes amount to twice their usual level, while resources available for necessary expenditures are even less adequate than before? Shall we suppose that the wealth is held by the government? Yet in the granaries of the provinces throughout the realm, one rarely sees grain stored until it reddens and rots; nor does one hear of treasuries containing such stores of cash that the strings threading the coins have rotted. Even a small expenditure prompts fears of shortage. Indeed, even the reserves of the palace treasury and the accumulated funds of the Ministry of Revenue may fall short of abundance. Thus the wealth is not held by the government. Shall we suppose that it is held by the people? Yet throughout the land, farming and sericulture often fail to provide the means of obtaining clothing and food, and people often cannot fulfill their wish to support their parents above and nurture their children below. At the first encounter with famine, they follow one another into displacement and migration. Indeed, even on fertile land and in years of abundant harvests, obtaining enough food and warmth may still be difficult. Thus the wealth is not held by the people either. What, then, has brought this about? If we now wish to enrich the state above and ensure sufficiency for the people below, there must be essential measures for addressing the problem and fundamental principles for carrying them out. Please set these down in your essay, so that…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
觀先天下之憂而憂勿謂思出其位
問自古為治者必美教化以善風俗風俗
未善而欲求治者鮮矣以雲貴言之古
為西南夷地我
國家取而郡縣之所以揆文教奮武衛者亦
為詳備固宜與中州等也然而百餘年
来風聲氣習無異於前革故鼎新未收
其效夷民之異言異服者始終莫變盜
賊之肆行劫奪者歲時無已貪財賤義
===
之徒自為得計無情健訟之輩轉相効
尤士或有乖庠序之教女或不知行露
之義親戚之恩或至於薄婚姻之黨或
非所宜民俗如此何由而可善耶或者
以為化導之機本於郡縣而郡縣之職
或為流官或為土官土官以予奪之莫
及而或縱肆其欲流官以更代之不常
而或苟簡其政民之望於聊生尤不可
得而况於俗善也臨之以藩臬之司糾
punctuated:
觀先天下之憂而憂，勿謂思出其位。

問：自古為治者，必美教化以善風俗。風俗未善而欲求治者，鮮矣。以雲貴言之，古為西南夷地，我國家取而郡縣之，所以揆文教、奮武衛者，亦為詳備，固宜與中州等也。然而百餘年来，風聲氣習無異於前，革故鼎新未收其效。夷民之異言異服者，始終莫變；盜賊之肆行劫奪者，歲時無已；貪財賤義之徒，自為得計；無情健訟之輩，轉相効尤。士或有乖庠序之教，女或不知行露之義，親戚之恩或至於薄，婚姻之黨或非所宜。民俗如此，何由而可善耶？或者以為，化導之機本於郡縣，而郡縣之職，或為流官，或為土官。土官以予奪之莫及，而或縱肆其欲；流官以更代之不常，而或苟簡其政。民之望於聊生，尤不可得，而况於俗善也！臨之以藩臬之司，糾
translation_en:
…to see how you would take concern for the world’s troubles before others do. Do not say that such deliberation exceeds your station.

Question: Since antiquity, those who govern have invariably perfected moral instruction in order to improve customs. Few have sought good government successfully while customs remained unimproved. Yunnan and Guizhou were anciently lands of the southwestern non-Han peoples. Our dynasty acquired them and established prefectures and counties there. Its arrangements for directing civil instruction and strengthening military protection have been comprehensive and thorough; these regions ought surely to stand on an equal footing with the central provinces. Yet for more than a hundred years, prevailing customs and habits have remained unchanged, and efforts to discard the old and establish the new have not borne fruit. The non-Han inhabitants retain their distinctive speech and dress without change; bandits carry out robberies and plunder unchecked, year after year. Those who covet wealth and despise righteousness consider their schemes successful, while those who pursue litigation without just grounds emulate one another’s bad example. Some scholars depart from the teachings of the schools; some women do not understand the moral import of “Dew on the Path” (Xing lu). Affection among relatives sometimes grows thin, and marriage alliances are sometimes inappropriate. With popular customs in this state, how can they be improved?

Some hold that the means of moral transformation lie fundamentally with the prefectures and counties, whose offices are held either by regular officials serving on rotation or by native officials. Native officials, beyond the effective reach of rewards and removals, sometimes give free rein to their desires; regular officials, whose replacements occur at irregular intervals, sometimes administer affairs perfunctorily. The people cannot even hope to secure a bare livelihood, much less see their customs improved! They are placed under the oversight of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, and subjected to correction …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之以憲臺之臣律流官者嚴矣果能惕
其心乎令其朝
覲以觀文明之治清其宗派以杜廕襲之爭而
待土官者亦至矣果能易其轍乎風俗
之所責成者果有在於𤰞歟斡旋之機
亦別有其道歟諸生生長𤰞邦目擊其
弊更化之術亦必講之審矣明以告我
以觀有用之學
punctuated: 之以憲臺之臣，律流官者嚴矣，果能惕其心乎？令其朝覲，以觀文明之治；清其宗派，以杜廕襲之爭，而待土官者亦至矣，果能易其轍乎？風俗之所責成者，果有在於𤰞歟？斡旋之機，亦別有其道歟？諸生生長𤰞邦，目擊其弊，更化之術，亦必講之審矣。明以告我，以觀有用之學。
translation_en: …them through officials of the Censorate. The discipline imposed on regularly appointed officials is strict indeed, but can it truly make them vigilant at heart? Hereditary native officials are required to attend court audiences so that they may witness enlightened government, and their lines of descent are clarified to forestall disputes over hereditary succession. The measures governing them are thus thorough indeed, but can these truly change their course? Does responsibility for improving customs indeed rest with those of lower rank [?]? Or is there some other way to bring about change? You students have grown up in this humble region [?] and witnessed its abuses firsthand; surely you have also carefully considered methods of reform. Explain them clearly to me, so that I may assess your learning’s practical worth.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
今吾於人也聽其言而觀其行
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批因文以觀士子之
實此作體認親切知其非徒言者
考試官教諭朱批人顧力行何如錄
此以戒時弊不特取其文也
考試官學正王批能言者每無近裏
===
著己之實此作認得題意取之
聖人之警賢者自言今當求人於實焉盖能言
而行不逮賢者之失也然則今之於人豈可聞
言而信不求觀其行之實哉昔宰予志不能以
帥氣行不能以掩言夫子警之意謂忽於前者
當致謹於今勉於今者斯能善於後彼以言取
人昔焉吾嘗失於易矣過此以往可不知戒乎
以言舉人向焉吾固畧於事矣自是而後可不
知省乎故於今也聞其人之出諸口者一皆務
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

今吾於人也，聽其言而觀其行。

卓文林

同考試官教諭劉批：因文以觀士子之實，此作體認親切，知其非徒言者。

考試官教諭朱批：人顧力行何如？錄此以戒時弊，不特取其文也。

考試官學正王批：能言者每無近裏著己之實，此作認得題意，取之。

聖人之警賢者，自言今當求人於實焉。盖能言而行不逮，賢者之失也。然則今之於人，豈可聞言而信，不求觀其行之實哉？昔宰予志不能以帥氣，行不能以掩言，夫子警之，意謂：忽於前者，當致謹於今；勉於今者，斯能善於後。彼以言取人，昔焉吾嘗失於易矣，過此以往，可不知戒乎？以言舉人，向焉吾固畧於事矣，自是而後，可不知省乎？故於今也，聞其人之出諸口者，一皆務
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Now, in dealing with people, I listen to their words and observe their conduct.”

Zhuo Wenlin

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Through the writing, one observes the candidate’s true substance. This composition shows an intimate and earnest understanding; one can tell that its author does more than merely talk.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: What matters is how earnestly a person puts things into practice. I have selected this piece to warn against the failings of our time, not merely for its literary merits.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: Those skilled in speaking often lack the substance of inward reflection and personal application. This composition grasps the meaning of the topic, and I select it.

In admonishing a worthy man, the sage himself declared that henceforth he should judge people by their actual deeds. For being able to speak while failing to act accordingly is a failing even of the worthy. In dealing with people now, then, how could one trust what one hears them say without seeking to observe the reality of their conduct? Formerly, Zai Yu’s resolve could not command his vital energies, and his conduct could not match his words. The Master admonished him, meaning: What one neglected before, one must attend to carefully now; by exerting oneself now, one can do well hereafter. As for judging people by their words, formerly I erred by doing so too readily. From this point onward, can I fail to take warning? As for recommending people on the strength of their words, previously I indeed paid too little attention to their deeds. Henceforth, can I fail to examine myself? Thus now, when I hear what issues from a person’s mouth, it is all about striving …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
學不倦之談若可與共學矣然有言者未必有
德烏可聞言而遽以為爾耶聆亹亹之發於聲
者一皆求道不已之論若可與適道矣然能言
者或不能踐胡可聆言而遂以為然耶必首察
斯人於燕居獨處之際果於學也嘗加勤勵之
功歟否則付彼為徒言耳夷考若人於日用常
行之間果於道也能效強勉之力歟否則置彼
為空言耳蓋雖聽其言之若是必欲觀其行之
何如固不以人而廢其言亦不以言而信其行
===
聖人言此其警宰予之意何切哉抑論之業精
于勤而荒于嬉自古之聖賢未嘗不以懈惰荒
寧為懼勤勵不息自強夫何宰予以聖門高第
列言語之科顧乃當晝而寢不能如其所言則
是志氣昏惰教無所施宜乎夫子責於前而復
警之以此也雖然豈必因予不逮於行而始聽
言觀行耶特因此立教以警羣弟子使謹於言
而敏於行耳人其可不知勉諸
德者本也財者末也
punctuated:
學不倦之談，若可與共學矣。然有言者未必有德，烏可聞言而遽以為爾耶？聆亹亹之發於聲者，一皆求道不已之論，若可與適道矣。然能言者或不能踐，胡可聆言而遂以為然耶？必首察斯人於燕居獨處之際，果於學也嘗加勤勵之功歟？否則付彼為徒言耳。夷考若人於日用常行之間，果於道也能效強勉之力歟？否則置彼為空言耳。蓋雖聽其言之若是，必欲觀其行之何如，固不以人而廢其言，亦不以言而信其行。
聖人言此，其警宰予之意何切哉！抑論之，業精于勤而荒于嬉，自古之聖賢未嘗不以懈惰荒寧為懼，勤勵不息自強。夫何宰予以聖門高第，列言語之科，顧乃當晝而寢，不能如其所言，則是志氣昏惰，教無所施，宜乎夫子責於前而復警之以此也。雖然，豈必因予不逮於行而始聽言觀行耶？特因此立教，以警羣弟子，使謹於言而敏於行耳。人其可不知勉諸？
德者本也，財者末也。
translation_en:
…talk of learning without weariness, as though one could join him in study. Yet those who speak well do not necessarily possess virtue: how could one hear his words and hastily conclude that he is such a person? Listening to his tireless utterances, one hears only discussions of seeking the Way without cease, as though one could join him in pursuing the Way. Yet those who can speak may be unable to put their words into practice: how could one listen and simply accept that they do? One must first observe this person in the privacy of his dwelling, when he is alone: has he truly applied diligent effort to learning? If not, dismiss his words as mere talk. Examine such a person closely in his everyday conduct: can he truly exert himself strenuously in following the Way? If not, set his words aside as empty talk. Thus, although one hears him speak in this manner, one must see how he acts. Certainly one does not reject his words because of the person, nor does one trust his conduct because of his words.
How earnest was the sage’s intention to admonish Zai Yu in saying this! To consider the matter further: achievement is perfected through diligence and ruined through idle amusement. From antiquity, sages and worthies have always feared indolence and heedless ease, diligently striving without cease to strengthen themselves. Why, then, did Zai Yu, a distinguished disciple of the sage’s school, ranked in the category of eloquence, nevertheless sleep during the day and fail to act in accordance with his words? His resolve and vital spirit were thus benighted and indolent, leaving instruction no purchase upon him. It was fitting that the Master should first rebuke him and then admonish him again with these words. Even so, could it have been only because Yu fell short in conduct that the Master began to listen to people’s words and observe their actions? He merely used this occasion to establish a teaching that would admonish all his disciples, making them cautious in speech and prompt in action. Can anyone fail to recognize the need for effort?
Virtue is the root; wealth is the branch.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖批德為生財之本子
能會意成文是可錄也
考試官教諭朱批講本末意思明白
蓋甞究心於義利之分者
考試官學正王批舎德理財皆非良
圖錄此文以為時政萬一之助
在內之理為所先在外之物為所後蓋德乃理
之在內財乃物之在外者也然德必有財而財
===
由德之致其為本末之先後豈不較然矣乎大
學釋平治之經及此意謂欲盡絜矩之道當明
本末之分彼原於天命而衆理咸備具於人心
而萬事由應所以公其好惡不為一己之私度
於物我能同衆人之欲者德也德何以為本耶
蓋以德感心則兆民允懷而際天薄海皆歸于
邦域以德行仁則萬姓咸若而遐陬僻壤悉入
于版圖不必以利為事也殆見因天分地何利
之弗獲焉不必以富為心也將見任土作貢何
punctuated:
鐵潤

同考試官教諭廖批：德為生財之本，子能會意成文，是可錄也。

考試官教諭朱批：講本末意思明白，蓋甞究心於義利之分者。

考試官學正王批：舎德理財，皆非良圖。錄此文，以為時政萬一之助。

在內之理為所先，在外之物為所後。蓋德乃理之在內，財乃物之在外者也。然德必有財，而財由德之致，其為本末之先後，豈不較然矣乎？大學釋平治之經，及此，意謂欲盡絜矩之道，當明本末之分。彼原於天命而衆理咸備，具於人心而萬事由應，所以公其好惡、不為一己之私，度於物我、能同衆人之欲者，德也。德何以為本耶？蓋以德感心，則兆民允懷，而際天薄海皆歸于邦域；以德行仁，則萬姓咸若，而遐陬僻壤悉入于版圖。不必以利為事也，殆見因天分地，何利之弗獲焉？不必以富為心也，將見任土作貢，何
translation_en:
Tie Run

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “Virtue is the root from which wealth is generated. You have grasped the meaning and developed it into an essay. This merits selection.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of root and branch is clear in meaning. The writer evidently has devoted thought to the distinction between righteousness and profit.”

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “Plans to administer wealth while abandoning virtue are all unsound. I select this essay in the hope that it may offer even a little assistance to the governance of our time.”

Principle within takes precedence; material things outside come afterward. For virtue is principle residing within, while wealth consists of material things outside. Yet virtue necessarily brings wealth, and wealth is attained through virtue. Is their order of precedence as root and branch not perfectly clear? When the Great Learning’s commentary on the classic’s teaching about bringing peace and order reaches this point, its meaning is that anyone wishing fully to practice the Way of the measuring square must understand the distinction between root and branch. That which originates in Heaven’s mandate and encompasses all principles, is present in the human heart and enables it to respond to all affairs, makes one impartial in likes and dislikes rather than selfishly pursuing one’s own interests, and measures others against oneself so that one can share the desires of all people—this is virtue. Why is virtue the root? Because when virtue moves people’s hearts, the countless common people sincerely cherish their ruler, and all lands beneath heaven and bordering the seas come within his realm. When virtue is used to practice benevolence, all the people comply, and distant corners and secluded regions alike enter his territorial registers. There is no need to make profit one’s business: by following Heaven’s seasons and distinguishing the uses of the land, what profit would one fail to obtain? There is no need to set one’s heart on riches: when tribute is assessed according to what the land produces, what…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
富之不有焉德非為本乎謂之本者以財對德
言則德在所先故為本也乃若地利兼收於府
庫之中方物畢集於帑藏之内所以廣儲蓄而
給軍國之需充貨殖以備公家之費者財也財
何以為末耶盖財之為類雖至廣也然亦難於
强求必以德為豐財之大要財之生世雖無窮
也然不容於易得必以德為發財之大方欲財
之聚實原於有土土宇之廣一德以致之也得
土之廣又原於有人人衆之歸一德以招之也
===
財非為末乎謂之末者以德對財言則財在所
後故為末也是則不患財之未足惟患德之未
周此君子所以先慎其德也歟雖然國不可以
無財財乃民之心也古之帝王思以一人治天
下不以天下奉一人凡可以節民財者無不為
之也後世不知以德為本而惟財是圖瓊林大
盈積以萬計卒不免於悖出之禍果何益哉噫
財固不可以過取而亦不可以浪費苟取之盡
錙銖用之如泥沙兩失之矣有天下者宜鑒于
punctuated: 富之不有焉？德非為本乎？謂之本者，以財對德言，則德在所先，故為本也。乃若地利兼收於府庫之中，方物畢集於帑藏之内，所以廣儲蓄而給軍國之需，充貨殖以備公家之費者，財也。財何以為末耶？盖財之為類雖至廣也，然亦難於强求，必以德為豐財之大要；財之生世雖無窮也，然不容於易得，必以德為發財之大方。欲財之聚，實原於有土，土宇之廣，一德以致之也；得土之廣，又原於有人，人衆之歸，一德以招之也。財非為末乎？謂之末者，以德對財言，則財在所後，故為末也。是則不患財之未足，惟患德之未周，此君子所以先慎其德也歟！雖然，國不可以無財，財乃民之心也。古之帝王思以一人治天下，不以天下奉一人，凡可以節民財者，無不為之也。後世不知以德為本，而惟財是圖，瓊林、大盈，積以萬計，卒不免於悖出之禍，果何益哉？噫！財固不可以過取，而亦不可以浪費。苟取之盡錙銖，用之如泥沙，兩失之矣！有天下者宜鑒于
translation_en:
…what wealth would not be possessed? Is virtue not, then, the root? It is called the root because, when wealth is set against virtue, virtue comes first and is therefore the root. As for the yields of the land gathered into the treasuries and storehouses, and the local products assembled in the public repositories: that which enlarges reserves to supply military and state needs, and increases material resources to meet public expenditures, is wealth. Why is wealth the branch? Although wealth takes exceedingly diverse forms, it is difficult to obtain by force; virtue must be the essential means of making wealth abundant. Although wealth is produced in the world without end, it cannot be acquired readily; virtue must be the chief means of bringing wealth forth. The accumulation of wealth actually rests upon possessing territory, and an extensive domain is attained through virtue alone. Acquiring extensive territory rests, in turn, upon having people, and the allegiance of multitudes is attracted through virtue alone. Is wealth not, then, the branch? It is called the branch because, when virtue is set against wealth, wealth comes afterward and is therefore the branch. Thus one should worry not that wealth is insufficient, but only that virtue is incomplete. Is this not why the gentleman first takes care over his virtue?

Nevertheless, a state cannot be without wealth, for wealth is what the people set their hearts upon. The emperors and kings of antiquity sought to have one person govern all under Heaven, rather than have all under Heaven support one person. They did everything that could conserve the people's resources. In later ages, rulers failed to understand that virtue was the root and pursued wealth alone. In the Qionglin and Daying treasuries, they amassed riches counted in tens of thousands, yet ultimately could not escape the calamity of wealth departing through wrongful means. What benefit was there, after all? Alas! Wealth must neither be extracted excessively nor squandered. If one exacts every last fraction of an ounce yet spends it like mud and sand, one errs in both respects! Those who rule all under Heaven should take warning from…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
茲
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
沈淳
同考試官教諭廖批孟子長於取譬而
此子亦善發揮宜錄其文
考試官教諭朱批聖道未易形容此
作就大成處見意蓋妙於文者
考試官學正王批此篇文韻清新自
有優柔平中氣象取之
===
大賢即樂之全而著其由以見聖道之大也夫
大成之樂未易作也必金以宣之玉以收之會
衆樂於一終斯其為大成歟想孟子之意以為
三子之行各極其一偏孔子之道兼全夫衆理
不猶樂之大成乎彼樂有金石絲竹之不同匏
土革木之不一若獨奏一音而自為始終特小
成耳必衆音並舉斯為大成八音各奏而自為
始終亦小成耳必羣樂合作乃為大成然其作
也何如蓋八音之中金石為重方其未作則擊
punctuated:
茲。

集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。
沈淳

同考試官教諭廖批：孟子長於取譬，而此子亦善發揮，宜錄其文。
考試官教諭朱批：聖道未易形容，此作就大成處見意，蓋妙於文者。
考試官學正王批：此篇文韻清新，自有優柔平中氣象，取之。

大賢即樂之全而著其由，以見聖道之大也。夫大成之樂，未易作也，必金以宣之，玉以收之，會衆樂於一終，斯其為大成歟！想孟子之意，以為三子之行各極其一偏，孔子之道兼全夫衆理，不猶樂之大成乎？彼樂有金石絲竹之不同，匏土革木之不一，若獨奏一音而自為始終，特小成耳，必衆音並舉，斯為大成。八音各奏而自為始終，亦小成耳，必羣樂合作，乃為大成。然其作也何如？蓋八音之中，金石為重，方其未作，則擊
translation_en:
…this.

“To bring together the great consummation is to sound the bronze bell and conclude with the jade chime.”
Shen Chun

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “Mencius excelled at drawing analogies, and this candidate likewise develops their meaning well. His essay should be recorded.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The Way of the sage is not easily described. This composition conveys its meaning through the idea of the great consummation: its author is indeed skilled in composition.”

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The literary cadence of this piece is fresh and clear. It naturally possesses an air of ease and balanced moderation [?]. Accept it.”

The great worthy draws upon music in its completeness and makes clear how that completeness is achieved, thereby revealing the greatness of the sage’s Way. Music that achieves the great consummation is not easily performed. Bronze must announce it, and jade must bring it to a close. All the music is gathered into a single conclusion: is this not what makes it the great consummation? I take Mencius’s meaning to be that the conduct of the three masters each attained the utmost in one particular aspect, whereas the Way of Confucius comprehensively embodied all principles. Is this not like the great consummation in music?

In music, there are the different sounds of metal, stone, silk, and bamboo, and the distinct sounds of gourd, clay, hide, and wood. If just one sound is played, with its own beginning and end, this is merely a minor consummation. Only when the various sounds are raised together is there a great consummation. If the eight classes of instruments each play separately, each with its own beginning and end, this too is merely a minor consummation. Only when all the instruments perform together is there a great consummation.

But how is such a performance carried out? Among the eight classes of instruments, metal and stone are the most important. Just before the performance begins, one strikes…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鏄鐘以宣其聲揚六律於鏗鏘之頃播八音於
和鳴之間翕然並作高下以之而有條羣然交
奏清濁由之而不紊是金聲一宣為衆樂之統
宗矣俟其既闋則擊特磬以收其韻肅羣音於
一終之後卷衆樂於九奏之餘高下之音詘然
而遏息清濁之韻截然以終止是玉韻一收為
衆樂之總括矣金以宣於先則凡自一成以至
於九成者莫不由是肇其端玉以收於後則凡
自一變而至於九變者一皆藉此畢其事二者
===
之間脉絡通貫無所不備合衆小成而為一大
成也豈非孔子集三聖之事為一大聖之事乎
抑論夷清尹任惠和所造固各抵於其極但不
免倚著於一偏也惟孔子則仕止久速各當其
可兼三子之聖而時出之先儒謂三子春夏秋
冬各一其時孔子則太和元氣流行於四時信
斯言也孟子于此既即樂以喻之下文復即射
以明之其深知孔子而善於形容者耶此其乃
所願則學孔子
punctuated: 鏄鐘以宣其聲，揚六律於鏗鏘之頃，播八音於和鳴之間，翕然並作，高下以之而有條；羣然交奏，清濁由之而不紊。是金聲一宣，為衆樂之統宗矣。俟其既闋，則擊特磬以收其韻，肅羣音於一終之後，卷衆樂於九奏之餘。高下之音詘然而遏息，清濁之韻截然以終止。是玉韻一收，為衆樂之總括矣。金以宣於先，則凡自一成以至於九成者，莫不由是肇其端；玉以收於後，則凡自一變而至於九變者，一皆藉此畢其事。二者之間，脉絡通貫，無所不備，合衆小成而為一大成也。豈非孔子集三聖之事為一大聖之事乎？抑論夷清、尹任、惠和，所造固各抵於其極，但不免倚著於一偏也。惟孔子則仕止久速，各當其可，兼三子之聖而時出之。先儒謂三子春夏秋冬各一其時，孔子則太和元氣流行於四時，信斯言也。孟子于此既即樂以喻之，下文復即射以明之，其深知孔子而善於形容者耶？此其乃所願則學孔子。
translation_en:
…the great bell [?] to sound its voice, setting the six pitch standards ringing amid its clangor and spreading the sounds of the eight classes of instruments in harmonious resonance. They begin together in full accord, their high and low notes thereby ordered; they play together as an ensemble, their clear and deep tones thereby kept from confusion. Thus, once the sound of metal rings out, it serves as the governing principle of all the music. When the performance is complete, the single suspended chime stone is struck to gather in its resonance, stilling the assembled sounds after their conclusion and drawing all the music to a close after the nine movements. The high and low notes subside into silence; the clear and deep resonances cease decisively. Thus, once the resonance of jade draws to a close, it brings all the music to its consummation. Metal sounds at the beginning: every movement, from the first through the ninth, takes its inception from it. Jade closes at the end: every variation, from the first through the ninth, relies on it for its completion. Between these two, the connecting threads run throughout, leaving nothing lacking and combining the many lesser completions into one great completion. Is this not like Kongzi’s gathering the accomplishments of the three sages into the accomplishment of one great sage?

To consider further: the purity of Bo Yi, the responsibility assumed by Yi Yin, and the harmony of Liuxia Hui each indeed reached its utmost limit, yet each inevitably leaned toward a single aspect. Kongzi alone, whether entering office or withdrawing, remaining long or departing swiftly, always acted as circumstances required. He united the sageliness of all three and manifested it at the appropriate time. Earlier Confucian scholars said that the three sages were each confined to their own season among spring, summer, autumn, and winter, whereas Kongzi was like the primordial vital force of supreme harmony circulating through all four seasons. How true these words are! Here Mengzi has already used music as an analogy; in the passage below, he further uses archery to illuminate the matter. Does this not show how deeply he understood Kongzi and how well he could describe him? Hence his declaration: “What I desire is to learn from Kongzi.”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易
大君之宜吉
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批君臨天下宜不自
用而任賢臣此篇善於道意故録
考試官教諭朱批談易能就人事上
發揮方見心易之妙此作近之
考試官學正王批君道至大臨爻一
言盡之此可見易不徒為卜筮
===
得居尊之體為臨下之善此聖人繫六五爻義
也盖任人則優於天下居尊之體得矣以是而
臨下何有於不善哉且臨之六五以柔中而下
應不自用而任人乃知者之事為大君之宜彼
大君者首出庶物撫蒞萬邦所臨何廣耶苟自
足其善而無操約及廣之方則非所當務也時
乘六龍統御四海所臨何眾耶苟自恃其長而
無務寡服眾之術殆非所當為也惟虛心下賢
不專自用則是萃眾善以為己善萬邦雖廣同
punctuated:
易
大君之宜，吉。
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批：君臨天下，宜不自用而任賢臣。此篇善於道意，故録。
考試官教諭朱批：談易，能就人事上發揮，方見心易之妙。此作近之。
考試官學正王批：君道至大，臨爻一言盡之。此可見易不徒為卜筮。
得居尊之體，為臨下之善，此聖人繫六五爻義也。盖任人則優於天下，居尊之體得矣。以是而臨下，何有於不善哉？且臨之六五，以柔中而下應，不自用而任人，乃知者之事，為大君之宜。彼大君者，首出庶物，撫蒞萬邦，所臨何廣耶！苟自足其善，而無操約及廣之方，則非所當務也。時乘六龍，統御四海，所臨何眾耶！苟自恃其長，而無務寡服眾之術，殆非所當為也。惟虛心下賢，不專自用，則是萃眾善以為己善。萬邦雖廣，同
translation_en:
Book of Changes
“What befits a great ruler: good fortune.”
Zhuo Wenlin

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor: “In presiding over all under Heaven, a ruler should employ worthy ministers rather than rely solely on himself. This essay expresses that meaning well, and therefore has been selected.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: “Only when discussion of the Changes develops its meaning through human affairs does the subtlety of the Changes within the mind become apparent. This composition approaches that ideal.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, a School Instructor: “The Way of the ruler is supremely great, yet a single statement in the lines of Approach exhausts it. Here one can see that the Changes is not merely for divination.”

To grasp the proper manner of occupying an exalted position and thereby excel in governing those below: this is the meaning of the words the Sage appended to the six in the fifth place. By employing others, one can govern all under Heaven with ease, thus attaining the proper manner of occupying an exalted position. Governing those below in this way, how could one fail to do well? Moreover, the six in the fifth place of Approach is yielding and central, and finds a corresponding line below. To employ others rather than rely solely on oneself is the conduct of the wise and what befits a great ruler.

That great ruler stands foremost among the myriad beings and watches over the myriad states. How vast is the domain over which he presides! If he rests content with his own goodness and lacks a method of holding to essentials while reaching far and wide, this is not what he ought to pursue. Riding the six dragons as the times require, he rules all within the Four Seas. How numerous are those over whom he presides! If he relies on his own strengths and lacks the art of concentrating on a few essentials to win the submission of the many, this surely is not what he ought to do. Only by opening his mind, humbling himself before the worthy, and refraining from exclusive reliance on himself does he gather the goodness of the many and make it his own. Though the myriad states are vast, all together …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
歸於乾旋坤轉之中其所當務不在是乎推誠
使能必欲任人則是集衆長以為已長四海雖
衆舉囿於日照月臨之下其所當為果外是乎
夫莫難盡者君之道也今既萃衆善以為臨必
其行合天道而大亨以正之善可獲未易全者
君之德也今既集衆長以有臨必其動皆順說
而教思容保之效可臻推臨之大于以建夫可
大之業繼蠱之元亨而天下治矣行臨之中于
以妙夫用中之極啓觀之神道而天下服矣向
===
使專於自用而不思所以任人固非宜也如吉
何哉抑論五之應二其人君任相之道乎故不
患治之未隆惟患相之未得誠得相而任之則
君逸於上臣勞於下天下之務將無足為者矣
然相之賢否治忽所關人君擇之又不可昧於
邪正之辯故曰知人則哲臨之六五繫以知臨
於此見用人之道其要在知人也
盛德大業至矣哉
戴倫
punctuated:
歸於乾旋坤轉之中，其所當務不在是乎？推誠使能，必欲任人，則是集衆長以為已長，四海雖衆，舉囿於日照月臨之下，其所當為果外是乎？夫莫難盡者，君之道也。今既萃衆善以為臨，必其行合天道，而大亨以正之善可獲；未易全者，君之德也。今既集衆長以有臨，必其動皆順說，而教思容保之效可臻。推臨之大，于以建夫可大之業，繼蠱之元亨，而天下治矣；行臨之中，于以妙夫用中之極，啓觀之神道，而天下服矣。向使專於自用，而不思所以任人，固非宜也，如吉何哉？抑論五之應二，其人君任相之道乎？故不患治之未隆，惟患相之未得。誠得相而任之，則君逸於上，臣勞於下，天下之務將無足為者矣。然相之賢否，治忽所關，人君擇之，又不可昧於邪正之辯。故曰：「知人則哲。」臨之六五繫以知臨，於此見用人之道，其要在知人也。
盛德大業至矣哉！
戴倫
translation_en:
…all come within the revolutions of Heaven and Earth. Is this not what he ought to attend to? By extending his sincerity and employing the capable, determined to entrust responsibilities to others, he gathers the strengths of all and makes them his own. Though the people within the four seas are numerous, all are encompassed beneath the illumination of the sun and moon. Could what he ought to do really lie outside this?
Nothing is harder to fulfill completely than the Way of the ruler. Now that he gathers every excellence in exercising oversight, his conduct will surely accord with the Way of Heaven, and he can attain the goodness of great success through correctness. What is difficult to perfect is the ruler’s virtue. Now that he gathers everyone’s strengths in exercising oversight, his actions will surely accord with compliance and joy, and he can achieve the effects of thoughtful instruction, accommodation, and protection. By extending the greatness of Approach (Lin), he establishes an undertaking capable of greatness; continuing the supreme success of Decay (Gu), he brings order to the world. By practicing the centrality of Approach, he brings the exercise of the mean to its highest refinement; opening the way to the numinous Way of Contemplation (Guan), he wins the submission of the world.
Had he instead relied exclusively on himself without considering how to entrust responsibilities to others, this would certainly have been inappropriate. How could there have been good fortune? Furthermore, does not the correspondence between the fifth and second lines express the Way by which a ruler appoints a chief councilor? Thus he should worry not that good government has yet to flourish, but that he has yet to obtain a chief councilor. If he truly obtains such a councilor and entrusts him with responsibility, the ruler will enjoy ease above while his minister labors below, and the affairs of the world will present no difficulty worth mentioning. Yet whether the chief councilor is worthy or unworthy determines whether there is order or disorder. In choosing him, the ruler must therefore not be ignorant of the distinction between the deviant and the upright. Thus it is said: “To know men is to be wise.” The words “wise approach” are attached to the six in the fifth place of Approach. Here we see that the essential point in the Way of employing people lies in knowing them.
“How consummate are flourishing virtue and great achievement!”
Dai Lun

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭劉批說理文字自是簡
潔此作其庶幾乎
考試官敎諭朱批造化全功一筆寫
出其亦善言易者
考試官學正王批易理無中含有最
難形容詞簡理明僅見是作
大傳贊造化之全功而有以妙其極焉蓋盛德
大業一皆造化之功也所以然者又豈有加於
其間哉宜大傳擧而贊之也且一陰一陽之道
===
無乎不在以在造化者言之方其動而爲德之
發也有象有形無隱不彰可名可狀無微不著
生生者亘古今而相禪化化者貫始終而相繼
是蓋自然而然浩乎不可以淺近窺也德之盛
爲何如及其靜而爲業之本也功有所成斂大
化於無形用有所歸會一元於無迹妙機緘而
莫測者有生成具含變化而至密者隨在各足
是蓋無爲而爲渾乎不可以限量求也業之大
爲何如夫德之發者固爲盛矣使有終窮則非
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭劉批：說理文字，自是簡潔，此作其庶幾乎！
考試官敎諭朱批：造化全功，一筆寫出，其亦善言易者。
考試官學正王批：易理無中含有，最難形容；詞簡理明，僅見是作。
大傳贊造化之全功，而有以妙其極焉。蓋盛德大業，一皆造化之功也。所以然者，又豈有加於其間哉？宜大傳擧而贊之也。且一陰一陽之道，無乎不在。以在造化者言之，方其動而爲德之發也，有象有形，無隱不彰；可名可狀，無微不著。生生者，亘古今而相禪；化化者，貫始終而相繼。是蓋自然而然，浩乎不可以淺近窺也。德之盛爲何如！及其靜而爲業之本也，功有所成，斂大化於無形；用有所歸，會一元於無迹。妙機緘而莫測者，有生成具；含變化而至密者，隨在各足。是蓋無爲而爲，渾乎不可以限量求也。業之大爲何如！夫德之發者，固爲盛矣，使有終窮，則非
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: Writing that expounds principles should naturally be concise and clear. Does this composition not come close to that ideal?
Examiner Zhu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: The entire achievement of creation and transformation is set forth in a single sweep of the brush. Its author is indeed skilled at discussing the Changes.
Examiner Wang, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: The principles of the Changes embrace being within nonbeing and are exceedingly difficult to describe. Only in this composition have I seen such concise language and clear exposition of principle.
The Great Commentary praises the entire achievement of creation and transformation, bringing out the wonder of its utmost perfection. For abundant virtue and great undertaking are, without exception, achievements of creation and transformation. Could anything be added to that which makes them so? Fittingly, the Great Commentary singles them out for praise. Moreover, the Way of alternating yin and yang is present everywhere. To speak of its presence in creation and transformation: when it moves and virtue unfolds, there are images and forms, and nothing hidden fails to become manifest; things can be named and described, and nothing minute fails to become apparent. Generation upon generation succeeds across past and present; transformation upon transformation continues from beginning to end. This happens naturally of itself, so vast that shallow understanding cannot fathom it. How abundant is its virtue!
When it becomes still and serves as the foundation of the undertaking, its achievement reaches completion, gathering the great process of transformation into the formless; its operation finds its resting place, bringing the primal unity together without a trace. That whose wondrous workings are unfathomable possesses the means of generation; that which contains transformation in utmost secrecy is sufficient in itself wherever it is found. This is action without deliberate action, an undivided whole that cannot be grasped through limits or measures. How great is its undertaking!
Now, virtue as it unfolds is certainly abundant; but if it had an end or became exhausted, it would not be …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
盛之至也業之本者固為大矣使有滲漏則非
大之至也今德之盛與時偕行初無終窮之或
間是德之所以行豈復有加其盛乎業之大體
物不遺曾無滲漏之或外是業之所以立尚復
有加其大乎造化之全功如此何莫而非陰陽
之所為也大抵天地之間陰陽兩端而已道具
於陰而行乎陽顯諸仁即天道之元亨誠之通
而為德之發也藏諸用即天道之利貞誠之復
而為業之本也造化之德業如是乃若易簡理
===
得聖人之德業也可久可大賢人之德業也學
者誠能由易知易從而馴造其極則士希賢賢
希聖聖希天矣天人豈有二哉噫非知道者何
足以語此
書
皐陶曰都慎厥身修思永惇叙九族庶明
勵翼邇可遠在兹禹拜昌言曰俞皐陶
曰都在知人在安民禹曰吁咸若時惟
帝其難之
punctuated:
盛之至也。業之本者固為大矣，使有滲漏，則非大之至也。今德之盛，與時偕行，初無終窮之或間，是德之所以行，豈復有加其盛乎？業之大，體物不遺，曾無滲漏之或外，是業之所以立，尚復有加其大乎？造化之全功如此，何莫而非陰陽之所為也？大抵天地之間，陰陽兩端而已。道具於陰而行乎陽，顯諸仁，即天道之元亨，誠之通而為德之發也；藏諸用，即天道之利貞，誠之復而為業之本也。造化之德業如是。乃若易簡理得，聖人之德業也；可久可大，賢人之德業也。學者誠能由易知易從而馴造其極，則士希賢，賢希聖，聖希天矣。天人豈有二哉？噫！非知道者，何足以語此？

書

皐陶曰：「都！慎厥身修，思永，惇叙九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠，在兹。」禹拜昌言，曰：「俞！」皐陶曰：「都！在知人，在安民。」禹曰：「吁！咸若時，惟帝其難之。」
translation_en:
…the utmost flourishing. The foundation of achievement is certainly great, but if anything were to escape its scope, it would not be greatness at its utmost. Now the flourishing of virtue advances with the times, never interrupted by exhaustion or cessation. Such is the way virtue proceeds: could anything further enhance its flourishing? The greatness of achievement gives substance to all things without omission, leaving nothing outside its scope. Such is the way achievement is established: could anything further enhance its greatness? Such is the complete accomplishment of creation and transformation. What part of it is not the work of yin and yang? Broadly speaking, between Heaven and Earth there are only these two poles, yin and yang. The Way is embodied in yin and operates through yang. Its manifestation in benevolence is the origination and flourishing of the Way of Heaven: the free passage of sincerity, constituting the unfolding of virtue. Its concealment in functioning is the benefit and firmness of the Way of Heaven: the return of sincerity, constituting the foundation of achievement. Such are the virtue and achievement of creation and transformation. As for attaining principle through ease and simplicity, this is the virtue and achievement of the sage; the capacity to endure and to grow great is the virtue and achievement of the worthy. If learners can truly proceed through what is easy to know and easy to follow, gradually reaching the utmost, then the scholar will aspire to become worthy, the worthy to become a sage, and the sage to accord with Heaven. How could Heaven and humanity be two? Ah! How could anyone who does not understand the Way be fit to discuss this?

Book of Documents

Gao Yao said: “Ah! Attend carefully to cultivating your person; let your thoughts reach far ahead. Deepen affection and maintain proper order among the nine degrees of kinship, and the many men of discernment will exert themselves to assist you. From those near at hand you can reach those far away: it lies in this.” Yu bowed in acknowledgment of these excellent words and said: “Yes!” Gao Yao said: “Ah! It lies in knowing men and in bringing peace to the people.” Yu said: “Oh! To accomplish all of this—even the emperor finds it difficult.”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖批得皐陶陳謨大要
而大禹俞吁之旨亦能體出録之
考試官教諭朱批寫出禹皐虞廷問
答雍容氣象是用録出
考試官學正王批善體貼收拾可以
見予之會理成文矣
大臣美所問而廣其謨同列深然之大臣美所
言而廣其旨同列深難之盖致治固本於修身
===
尤在於知仁也此大臣推廣而致同列然否之
辭者有以哉思昔虞舜垂拱皐陶陳謨因禹之
然美禹之問乃推廣允迪謨明之義以為治本
於身而修之在慎也必戒謹恐懼使無言行之
失身主於心而思之在永也必深謀遠慮不為
淺近之圖由是推之於家則親親恩篤而家齊
推之於國則羣哲勉輔而國治又由近而可推
之於天下之遠者亦不外是盖身修家齊國治
而天下平矣禹聞斯言遂拜之曰修齊治平非
punctuated:
鐵潤

同考試官教諭廖批：得皐陶陳謨大要，而大禹俞吁之旨亦能體出，録之。

考試官教諭朱批：寫出禹皐虞廷問答雍容氣象，是用録出。

考試官學正王批：善體貼收拾，可以見予之會理成文矣。

大臣美所問而廣其謨，同列深然之；大臣美所言而廣其旨，同列深難之。盖致治固本於修身，尤在於知仁也。此大臣推廣而致同列然否之辭者，有以哉！思昔虞舜垂拱，皐陶陳謨，因禹之然，美禹之問，乃推廣允迪謨明之義，以為治本於身，而修之在慎也，必戒謹恐懼，使無言行之失；身主於心，而思之在永也，必深謀遠慮，不為淺近之圖。由是推之於家，則親親恩篤而家齊；推之於國，則羣哲勉輔而國治；又由近而可推之於天下之遠者，亦不外是。盖身修、家齊、國治而天下平矣。禹聞斯言，遂拜之曰：「修齊治平非
translation_en:
Tie Run

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “This captures the essentials of Gao Yao’s presentation of his counsels and also conveys the import of the Great Yu’s expressions of assent and misgiving. Selected.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “This depicts the composed and dignified manner of the questions and answers exchanged by Yu and Gao Yao at Shun’s court. It is selected on this account.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: “Skillful in entering into the meaning and drawing the threads together; one can see ‘my’ [?] grasp of principle embodied in a composition.”

The great minister praised the question put to him and expanded his counsel; his fellow minister profoundly agreed. The great minister praised what was said and expanded its meaning; his fellow minister expressed profound misgivings. Bringing about good government is indeed rooted in cultivating oneself, but depends especially upon wisdom and benevolence. There was good reason why the great minister’s elaborations elicited expressions of assent and reservation from his colleague!

Consider how, in ancient times, Shun sat with robes hanging down and hands folded while Gao Yao presented his counsels. Responding to Yu’s assent and praising Yu’s question, Gao Yao expanded upon the meaning of following virtue faithfully and making one’s counsels enlightened. He held that government is rooted in the person, and that cultivating the person depends upon vigilance: one must be cautious and apprehensive, allowing no errors in speech or conduct. The person is governed by the heart, and reflection must reach far: one must deliberate deeply and consider the distant future, making no shallow or shortsighted plans. Extending this to the family, affection for one’s kin becomes deep and the family is ordered. Extending it to the state, the assembled wise men strive to assist, and the state is well governed. Extending it further, from what is near to the farthest reaches of all under Heaven, still involves nothing beyond this. Thus, when the person is cultivated, the family ordered, and the state governed, all under Heaven is at peace. Hearing these words, Yu thereupon bowed and said: “Cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to all under Heaven are not…”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
輕言也實盛德之嘉言篤近舉遠非虛語也誠
保邦之要道其深然之者非有契於其心乎夫
致治固不外乎修身然非知人安民又為治之
累也故臯陶因禹之俞而復推廣其未盡之旨
歎美其言以為在於知人必因能授任使野無
遺賢以急知之先務在於安民必布德施惠俾
萬邦咸寧以成仁之極功則允迪謨明之義盡
矣禹聞斯言遂吁之曰仁兼乎知雖帝也其仁
如天而四凶在位知又難能也知兼乎仁雖堯
===
也其知如神而病諸博施仁又難能也其不然
之者非有難於其事乎夫以臯陶之陳謨而大
禹一然於前一難於後者有如此無非所以勸
戒期望於其君也噫至矣哉是知有虞之臣忠
良登於一堂謨猷會於眾見其曰俞曰都者非
阿諛曰吁曰咈者非拂逆言若牴牾而義實相
足外若背馳而内實相孚唐虞雍容氣象可想
見矣夫豈後世之可及哉
太保率西方諸侯入應門左畢公率東方
punctuated:
輕言也，實盛德之嘉言；篤近舉遠非虛語也，誠保邦之要道。其深然之者，非有契於其心乎？夫致治固不外乎修身，然非知人安民，又為治之累也。故臯陶因禹之俞，而復推廣其未盡之旨，歎美其言，以為在於知人，必因能授任，使野無遺賢，以急知之先務；在於安民，必布德施惠，俾萬邦咸寧，以成仁之極功，則允迪謨明之義盡矣。禹聞斯言，遂吁之曰：「仁兼乎知，雖帝也，其仁如天，而四凶在位，知又難能也；知兼乎仁，雖堯也，其知如神，而病諸博施，仁又難能也。」其不然之者，非有難於其事乎？夫以臯陶之陳謨，而大禹一然於前、一難於後者有如此，無非所以勸戒期望於其君也。噫，至矣哉！是知有虞之臣，忠良登於一堂，謨猷會於眾見。其曰俞曰都者，非阿諛；曰吁曰咈者，非拂逆。言若牴牾，而義實相足；外若背馳，而内實相孚。唐虞雍容氣象，可想見矣。夫豈後世之可及哉！

太保率西方諸侯入應門左，畢公率東方
translation_en:
…are no lightly spoken words: they are truly excellent words of abundant virtue. Being devoted to those near and reaching out to those afar is no empty saying: it is truly the essential way to preserve the state.” Was his profound agreement not because these words accorded with his heart? Bringing about good government certainly rests upon cultivating oneself; yet without discerning men's abilities and bringing peace to the people, there will still be impediments to governing. Thus Gao Yao, following Yu's assent, further developed the meaning he had not yet fully expressed. He exclaimed in praise of these words, holding that discerning men requires assigning responsibilities according to ability, so that no worthy man remains overlooked in the countryside: this gives urgency to the foremost task of wisdom. Bringing peace to the people requires spreading virtue and bestowing beneficence, so that the myriad states all enjoy tranquility: this achieves the highest accomplishment of benevolence. The meaning of faithfully practicing virtue and being enlightened in counsel would thereby be fully realized.

Hearing these words, Yu sighed and said: “For benevolence to encompass wisdom—even for the sovereign, whose benevolence was like Heaven, the Four Villains remained in office: wisdom, too, is difficult to attain. For wisdom to encompass benevolence—even for Yao, whose wisdom was like that of a spirit, bestowing benefits universally remained a source of concern: benevolence, too, is difficult to attain.” Was his disagreement not because he found these things difficult to carry out? Such was Gao Yao's presentation of counsel and the Great Yu's response: first assent, then an expression of difficulty. All of this served to encourage and admonish their ruler, and to express their hopes for him. Ah, how consummate it was! From this we know that among the ministers of Shun of Yu, loyal and worthy men gathered in one hall, and their counsels brought together many perspectives. Their “Yes” and “Excellent” were no flattery; their “Ah” and “No” were no defiance. Their words seemed contradictory, yet their meanings actually complemented one another; outwardly they seemed to diverge, yet inwardly they truly trusted one another. We can picture the dignified ease of the age of Tang and Yu. How could later ages ever match it?

text:
諸侯入應門右皆布乘黄朱賓稱奉圭
兼幣曰一二臣衛敢執壤奠皆再拜稽
首
金璽

統之嚴摸寫殆盡當是作手

考試官學正王批叙事整肅令人頓
===
生敬畏壁經中之翹楚也
二伯率諸侯各列覲君之位諸侯獻方物同肅
覲君之儀盖班次分列固朝會之常儀而儀物
兼隆又臣子之正道也自非有周盛時曷克爾
哉昔者康王嗣位羣后畢朝是時太保為西伯
則西方諸侯在所統矣於是率之皆踧踖如也
以入于應門之左畢公為東伯則東方諸侯在

…the regional lords entered on the right of the Ying Gate. All arrayed teams of four yellow horses with red-dyed manes. The guests raised their jade tablets together with offerings of silk, saying: “We, your servants who guard the realm, venture to present offerings from our lands.” All bowed twice and knocked their heads to the ground.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “The strict hierarchy through which Zhou ministers honored their sovereign is depicted almost exhaustively. This is surely an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “You bring out the spirit in which the ministers of the Zhou house honored their sovereign. This also allows us to see your capacity for loyalty.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: “The narration is orderly and solemn, immediately inspiring reverence and awe. This is an outstanding essay on the classic recovered from the wall.”

The two regional chiefs led the regional lords, each taking his appointed place for an audience with the sovereign; the regional lords presented the products of their lands, together solemnly observing the ceremonial forms of that audience. To stand separately according to rank was indeed the customary ceremonial practice of court assemblies; to give full splendor to both ceremony and offerings was also the proper course for ministers. How could this have been achieved except in the flourishing age of Zhou?

Formerly, when King Kang succeeded to the throne, all the regional rulers attended court. At that time, the Grand Guardian served as Chief of the West, and the western regional lords were therefore under his command. The Duke of Bi served as Chief of the East, and the eastern regional lords were therefore under his command. He accordingly led them, all stepping with circumspection, to enter on the right of the Ying Gate. title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
森嚴也內以統外若身之使臂有令而必從截
然其整齊也夫同入其門各列其位至於君前
矣可無物以為贄哉布於庭者則陳四黃馬而

執封內所產以表夫恭敬之心於是又相率皆
拜以至於再若大若小儼一敬於天威之密邇
也相與稽首以至於地若尊若卑罄一誠於龍
===
顏之咫尺也吁班次分於方近所尊之初儀物
備於既近所尊之頃諸侯朝見康王如此正始
之道不於是而可見哉考之王制二百一十國
以為州州有伯八州八伯各率其屬以聽於天
子之老二人則二伯之制蓋始於此矣洛誥召
公語成王以御諸侯之道有曰享多儀儀不及
物惟曰不享而又宮省之禮朝會之位貢獻之
物無非素籌而預定者張子曰為治而不法三
代終苟道也誠哉
punctuated: 森嚴也。內以統外，若身之使臂，有令而必從，截然其整齊也。夫同入其門，各列其位，至於君前矣，可無物以為贄哉？布於庭者，則陳四黃馬而朱其鬣；執於手者，則舉所奉圭而兼以幣。彤之言曰：「藩衛之臣不一，茲其來也，敢執壤地所出，以成夫奠贄之禮；屏翰之臣不一，茲其朝也，敢執封內所產，以表夫恭敬之心。」於是又相率皆拜，以至於再，若大若小，儼一敬於天威之密邇也；相與稽首，以至於地，若尊若卑，罄一誠於龍顏之咫尺也。吁！班次分於方近所尊之初，儀物備於既近所尊之頃，諸侯朝見康王如此，正始之道不於是而可見哉？考之《王制》，二百一十國以為州，州有伯，八州八伯，各率其屬，以聽於天子之老二人，則二伯之制蓋始於此矣。《洛誥》，召公語成王以御諸侯之道，有曰：「享多儀，儀不及物，惟曰不享。」而又宮省之禮、朝會之位、貢獻之物，無非素籌而預定者。張子曰：「為治而不法三代，終苟道也。」誠哉！
translation_en:
…solemn and imposing in their ranks. Those within direct those without, as the body moves its arms: whenever an order is issued, it is obeyed, so exact is their orderliness. Having entered the same gate and each taken their appointed place, they have arrived before their ruler. Could they come without objects to present as audience gifts? For display in the courtyard, they array four yellow horses with their manes dyed vermilion; in their hands, they raise the jade tablets they bear, together with gifts of silk. The words introduced by the doubtful phrase tong zhi 彤之 [?] run: “The ministers who guard your borders are many. Now that we have come, we venture to bring what our lands produce, to fulfill the rite of laying down audience gifts. The ministers who serve as your protective bulwarks are many. Now that we attend court, we venture to bring what is produced within our fiefs, to express our reverence.” Thereupon they all follow one another in bowing, bowing twice. Whether great or small, all solemnly share one reverence in the immediate presence of the awe-inspiring sovereign. Together they knock their heads upon the ground. Whether high or low in rank, all pour forth their wholehearted sincerity within inches of the imperial countenance.

Ah! Their ranks are distinguished as they first approach the one they honor; their ceremonial observances and gifts are fully prepared by the time they have drawn near him. Such was the feudal lords’ audience with King Kang. Is not the way of setting a beginning aright visible here? Consulting the Royal Regulations (Wang zhi), we find that 210 states constituted a region, and each region had a chief. The eight chiefs of the eight regions each led their subordinates to receive instructions from the Son of Heaven’s two senior ministers. The institution of the two regional overlords presumably originated here. In the Announcement at Luo (Luo gao), the Duke of Shao spoke to King Cheng about the way to govern the feudal lords, saying: “Presenting offerings involves many ceremonies. If the ceremonies do not extend to material gifts, it is simply called making no offering.” Moreover, the rites within the palace precincts, the positions at court assemblies, and the objects presented as tribute were all planned beforehand and determined in advance. Master Zhang said: “To govern without taking the Three Dynasties as one’s model is ultimately to follow a way of mere expediency.” How true!

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
詩
其儀一兮心如結兮
王璽
同考試官敎諭程批講君子用心處明白簡易盖亦知心之所用者歟
同考試官敎諭杜批能脫去外占知内之說得詩人渾融之旨錄之
考試官敎諭朱批此題有不容言之妙而子能言之可謂善說詩矣
===
考試官學正王批體認真切而詞足以發之可取
即其動容之善而為用心之善詩人美君子然
也夫儀之所在心之所在也觀君子儀容之一
非其心之如結而何哉鳲鳩之詩詩人美君子
用心均平專一而作也意謂心者一身之主宰
儀者一心之運用心焉不存儀能一乎今觀曹
之君子自燕處以至酬酢凡布於四體之間抑
抑然為之慎密而不過其則自閒居以至應接
punctuated:
詩
「其儀一兮，心如結兮。」
王璽

同考試官敎諭程批：講君子用心處，明白簡易，盖亦知心之所用者歟！
同考試官敎諭杜批：能脫去外占知内之說，得詩人渾融之旨，錄之。
考試官敎諭朱批：此題有不容言之妙，而子能言之，可謂善說詩矣。
考試官學正王批：體認真切，而詞足以發之，可取。

即其動容之善，而為用心之善，詩人美君子然也。夫儀之所在，心之所在也。觀君子儀容之一，非其心之如結而何哉？《鳲鳩》之詩，詩人美君子用心均平專一而作也。意謂心者，一身之主宰；儀者，一心之運用。心焉不存，儀能一乎？今觀曹之君子，自燕處以至酬酢，凡布於四體之間，抑抑然為之慎密，而不過其則；自閒居以至應接，
translation_en:
Book of Poetry
“His deportment is consistent; his heart is as though tied in a knot.”
Wang Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: “His explanation of how the gentleman applies his mind is clear, simple, and accessible. Surely he too understands how the mind is applied!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: “He succeeds in moving beyond the explanation that one knows the inner self by examining outward signs, and grasps the poet’s fully integrated meaning. Accept this essay.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “This topic contains a subtlety that defies expression, yet you have expressed it. You may indeed be called skilled at explaining the Poetry.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “His understanding is earnest and precise, and his language adequately expresses it. Worth accepting.”

From the excellence of his bearing, the poet takes the application of his mind to be excellent: this is how he praises the gentleman. For where deportment is manifested, there the mind is present. When we observe the consistency of the gentleman’s bearing, what can it be but that his heart is as though tied in a knot? The poem ‘The Cuckoo’ (Shijiu) was composed by the poet to praise the gentleman’s evenhanded and single-minded application of his mind. Its meaning is that the mind governs the whole person, while deportment is the mind in operation. If the mind were not present, could deportment be consistent? Now observe the gentleman of Cao: from resting at ease to exchanging courtesies, everything expressed through his four limbs is restrained, careful, and exact, never exceeding the proper standard; from dwelling in private to receiving and responding to others …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
凡見諸一身之際秩秩然為之整肅而不踰其
閑周旋中規折旋中矩而所以中規中矩者久
暫一致初不謹乎大而忽乎小也容止可觀進
退可度而所以可觀可度者終始一誠初不修
於顯而怠於隱也然儀之所以一者豈有他哉
