In the Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji), accounts of summoning assemblies and conducting punitive campaigns appear in the Annals of Huangdi; in the Book of Documents (Shangshu), accounts of inspection tours and court audiences appear in the Canon of Shun. When the system flourished, the states increased and necessarily became numerous. When Yu assembled the feudal lords at Tushan, those bearing jade and silk represented ten thousand states: this inherited the prosperity of Tang and Yu, the ages of Yao and Shun. When the system declined, the states diminished and necessarily became few. When Tang received the Mandate, only somewhat more than three thousand states survived: this inherited the decline of the Xia. King Wu established enfeoffments in five ranks, comprising 1,773 states in all; those serving as protective bulwarks for the royal house all shared the royal surname. In the Spring and Autumn period, 165 states appear in the Classic and its commentaries, including the Man, Yi, Rong, and Di. Flourishing did not occur without cause: it came through concord and harmony. Decline did not occur without cause: it came through annexation. This is a general outline of the origins and subsequent course, flourishing and decline, of enfeoffment. When Qin possessed All-under-Heaven, it broke up the metropolitan centers…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而為之郡邑廢侯衛而為之守宰攝制四
海運於掌握封建之制廢矣漢興以來踵
秦故智悉用郡縣而於封建亦間有之始
以封韓彭英盧而非功臣不得繼以封子
弟親屬而非同姓不與降漢而後異姓者
不可復得而惟同姓矣此古之封建所以
不可復而後世之罪秦者以此也然而議
者紛紛猶以為先王之法不可不用於是
爭辨者互起而矛盾焉栁宗元曰公天下
===
之端自秦始蘇子瞻曰封建者爭之端亂
之始也是以封建為非者矣胡仁仲曰封
建者公天下之大端大本也朱晦庵曰必
如是而後能公天下以為心而達君臣之
義於天下是以封建為是者矣然徐考之
有封建之善亦有封建之弊其弊於夏則
有扈羲和之有罪士師不得以治之六師
徃征必勞天子親總之舉其弊於周文昭
武穆之大封異姓不得以先之數傳而後
punctuated: 而為之郡邑，廢侯衛而為之守宰，攝制四海，運於掌握，封建之制廢矣。漢興以來，踵秦故智，悉用郡縣，而於封建亦間有之。始以封韓、彭、英、盧，而非功臣不得；繼以封子弟親屬，而非同姓不與。降漢而後，異姓者不可復得，而惟同姓矣。此古之封建所以不可復，而後世之罪秦者以此也。然而議者紛紛，猶以為先王之法不可不用，於是爭辨者互起而矛盾焉。栁宗元曰：「公天下之端，自秦始。」蘇子瞻曰：「封建者，爭之端，亂之始也。」是以封建為非者矣。胡仁仲曰：「封建者，公天下之大端大本也。」朱晦庵曰：「必如是而後能公天下以為心，而達君臣之義於天下。」是以封建為是者矣。然徐考之，有封建之善，亦有封建之弊。其弊於夏，則有扈、羲和之有罪，士師不得以治之，六師徃征，必勞天子親總之舉。其弊於周，文昭武穆之大封，異姓不得以先之，數傳而後
translation_en:
…and made them commanderies and counties, abolished the protective domains of the feudal lords, and put governors and magistrates in their place. Holding all within the Four Seas under its control, it managed the realm as though in the palm of its hand. The system of enfeoffment was abolished. From the rise of the Han onward, rulers followed Qin’s old expedient, employing commanderies and counties throughout the realm, while also occasionally practicing enfeoffment. At first, fiefs were granted to Han, Peng, Ying, and Lu, and none but meritorious subjects could receive them. Subsequently, fiefs were granted to sons, younger brothers, and other relatives, and none outside the imperial surname could share in them. After the Han, recipients of other surnames were no longer to be found; only those of the imperial surname remained. This is why the ancient system of enfeoffment could not be restored, and it is for this that later generations condemn Qin.

Yet opinions proliferated, and some still held that the institutions of the former kings must be employed. Thus disputants arose on opposing sides and contradicted one another. Liu Zongyuan said: “The beginning of making the realm public rather than private came with Qin.” Su Zizhan said: “Enfeoffment is the source of contention and the beginning of disorder.” These regarded enfeoffment as wrong. Hu Renzhong said: “Enfeoffment is the great starting point and fundamental basis for making the realm public.” Zhu Hui’an said: “Only by proceeding in this way can one take making the realm public as one’s guiding intention and extend the proper relationship between ruler and subject throughout the realm.” These regarded enfeoffment as right.

Yet upon careful examination, enfeoffment has both advantages and defects. Its defects under the Xia were exemplified by the offenses of Youhu and Xi and He: the judicial officers could not punish them, and the Six Armies had to march against them, requiring the Son of Heaven to undertake personal command. Its defects under the Zhou lay in the extensive enfeoffment of the descendants of King Wen and King Wu, arranged in the zhao and mu generations: those of other surnames could not take precedence over them, and after several generations of succession…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
即有末大不掉之憂在三代之時已有其
弊如此况後世乎柳子蘇子既剖析利害
指陳得失明白切當而程子亦曰封建之
法本出於不得已秦法固不善亦有不可
變者朱子又曰封建只是歷代循襲勢不
容已柳子厚亦說得是而今之論者猶曰
必有公天下之心而後可以行封建自其
出於公心則選賢與能而大小相維之勢
足以綿千載自其出於私心則忌疎畏偪
===
而上下相猜之形不能一朝居此說之行
則持論者猶未免墮於牽制而莫之決也
大抵異姓之封建不可有同姓之封建不
可無歷代行之而不得其宜我
國家處之而曲盡其善
宗室之封徧於天下派天源分玉葉者何其
多也寵以尊崇之禮而不委以政事之煩
備其官屬輔導者有人使令者有人所謂
親之欲其貴也愛之欲其富也是雖非若
punctuated:
即有末大不掉之憂。在三代之時，已有其弊如此，况後世乎？柳子、蘇子既剖析利害，指陳得失，明白切當，而程子亦曰：「封建之法，本出於不得已。秦法固不善，亦有不可變者。」朱子又曰：「封建只是歷代循襲，勢不容已。柳子厚亦說得是。」而今之論者猶曰：「必有公天下之心，而後可以行封建。自其出於公心，則選賢與能，而大小相維之勢足以綿千載；自其出於私心，則忌疎畏偪，而上下相猜之形不能一朝居。」此說之行，則持論者猶未免墮於牽制，而莫之決也。
大抵異姓之封建不可有，同姓之封建不可無。歷代行之而不得其宜，我國家處之而曲盡其善。宗室之封徧於天下，派天源、分玉葉者何其多也！寵以尊崇之禮，而不委以政事之煩；備其官屬，輔導者有人，使令者有人。所謂親之欲其貴也，愛之欲其富也。是雖非若
translation_en:
…there arose the danger that the branches would grow so large that they could no longer be controlled. Such abuses already existed under the Three Dynasties; how much more so in later ages? Master Liu and Master Su have already analyzed the benefits and harms and set forth the gains and losses clearly and aptly. Master Cheng also said: “The system of enfeoffment originally arose out of necessity. The institutions of Qin were admittedly imperfect, yet some could not be changed.” Master Zhu further said: “Enfeoffment was simply inherited from dynasty to dynasty; circumstances made it impossible to discontinue. Liu Zihou was also right in what he said.” Yet present-day commentators still say: “Only with the intention of making All-under-Heaven common to all can one institute enfeoffment. If it proceeds from a public-minded intention, the worthy and able will be selected, and the mutually sustaining relationship between large and small domains will suffice to endure for a thousand years. If it proceeds from selfish intentions, distant relatives will be distrusted and those too close to the throne feared; a situation in which superiors and inferiors suspect one another cannot endure even for a single morning.” With this argument in circulation, those debating the matter still cannot avoid becoming entangled in competing considerations and reaching no decision.
Generally speaking, enfeoffment of those with different surnames from the ruling house must not exist, while enfeoffment of those sharing its surname cannot be dispensed with. Successive dynasties practiced it without finding the proper arrangements; our dynasty has handled it so as to realize its benefits in every respect. Fiefs of the imperial clan extend throughout All-under-Heaven. How numerous are those who branch from the celestial source and spread forth as jade leaves! They are favored with ceremonies of honor and reverence, but are not entrusted with the burdens of government. They are provided with a full complement of subordinate officials: some to assist and guide them, others to carry out their commands. This is what is meant by wishing those one holds dear to enjoy high standing, and wishing those one loves to enjoy wealth. Although this is unlike…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
前代封建之實而所以處之者盡其恩矣
四裔之酋長周於四方服旃裘語侏離者
何其衆也列之以官爵之殊隆之以世襲
之恩別置僚佐既有以分其任亦因以防
其欲有罪則懲之而冀改其過大惡則除
之而更置其賢是雖若有前代封建之實
而所以處之者得其義矣一王之法制萬
代之準繩又何有加之者哉約而論之天
生斯民立之司牧惟在於治安則人心悅
===
而天意得固不必於封建郡縣優劣之分
也堯舜之禪受行於燕噲則亂湯武之仁
義行於桓文則詐是皆務先王之美名而
不知其弊者蘇子曰世無封建而相戕之
禍斯絕仁人君子忍復開之歟斯名言也
執事以為何如
第三問
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖批問目頭緒頗多似
punctuated:
前代封建之實，而所以處之者盡其恩矣。四裔之酋長周於四方，服旃裘、語侏離者何其衆也！列之以官爵之殊，隆之以世襲之恩，別置僚佐，既有以分其任，亦因以防其欲。有罪則懲之，而冀改其過；大惡則除之，而更置其賢。是雖若有前代封建之實，而所以處之者得其義矣。一王之法制，萬代之準繩，又何有加之者哉！約而論之，天生斯民，立之司牧，惟在於治安，則人心悅而天意得，固不必於封建郡縣優劣之分也。堯舜之禪受，行於燕噲則亂；湯武之仁義，行於桓文則詐。是皆務先王之美名，而不知其弊者。蘇子曰：「世無封建，而相戕之禍斯絕。仁人君子忍復開之歟？」斯名言也。執事以為何如？

第三問
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖批：問目頭緒頗多，似
translation_en:
…the substance of enfeoffment in former dynasties, yet the arrangements made for them fully express benevolence toward them. The chieftains of the outer regions are spread throughout the four quarters: how numerous are those who wear felt and fur and speak unintelligible tongues! They are ranked through distinctions of office and noble title, and honored with the favor of hereditary succession. Separate subordinate officials are appointed both to share their responsibilities and to restrain their desires. When they commit offenses, they are punished in the hope that they will amend their faults; when they commit great evils, they are removed and replaced with worthy men from among them. Although this seems to possess the substance of enfeoffment in former dynasties, the arrangements made for them accord with righteousness. These laws and institutions of a sovereign are a standard for ten thousand generations. What could improve upon them?

To state the matter briefly: Heaven brought forth these people and established rulers to shepherd them. The essential aim is good government and peace; then the people's hearts are pleased and Heaven's intent is fulfilled. There is certainly no need to insist on distinguishing the relative merits of enfeoffment and the system of commanderies and counties. The abdication and acceptance of the throne practiced by Yao and Shun brought disorder when enacted by Kuai of Yan; the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu became deception when practiced by Dukes Huan and Wen. These are all instances of pursuing the fine reputation of the former kings without understanding the resulting abuses. Master Su said: “When there is no enfeoffment in the world, the calamity of mutual slaughter will cease. Could humane men and gentlemen bear to open the way to it again?” These are memorable words. What is your judgment, honored examiners?

Third Question
Tie Run
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: The question contains quite a number of distinct threads; it seems…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
難下手此荅如金歸於範形質自
成其文塲中之哲匠也歟
考試官教諭朱批考古論今歷歷指
掌末論兵民之制而所處尤為有
見噫經生所養有如是乎
考試官學正王批民與兵古今不同
亦世道推移使然能不為經生常
談而取必於古者濟時之學也
有古今四民之異有古今制兵之異夫天
===
之生民一也可以為民可以為兵方其兵
寓於民以為四則世質民淳而有可稱及
其兵分於民以為五則世變風移而有可
議是非兵民之能異也所以為古今者不
能以不異也今承明問庸敢無辭以對乎
自夫耒耨之利興天下始有所謂農矣日
中為市之利興天下始有所謂商矣有弧
矢舟楫宮室之制天下始有所謂工矣結
繩而易以書契天下始有所謂士矣然黃
punctuated:
難下手。此荅如金歸於範，形質自成，其文塲中之哲匠也歟！

考試官教諭朱批：考古論今，歷歷指掌。末論兵民之制，而所處尤為有見。噫！經生所養有如是乎！

考試官學正王批：民與兵，古今不同，亦世道推移使然。能不為經生常談而取必於古者，濟時之學也。

有古今四民之異，有古今制兵之異。夫天之生民，一也，可以為民，可以為兵。方其兵寓於民以為四，則世質民淳而有可稱；及其兵分於民以為五，則世變風移而有可議。是非兵民之能異也，所以為古今者，不能以不異也。今承明問，庸敢無辭以對乎？

自夫耒耨之利興，天下始有所謂農矣；日中為市之利興，天下始有所謂商矣；有弧矢、舟楫、宮室之制，天下始有所謂工矣；結繩而易以書契，天下始有所謂士矣。然黃
translation_en:
…difficult to tackle. This answer is like metal entering a mold: its form and substance take shape naturally. Surely its author is a master craftsman of the examination hall!

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: In examining antiquity and discussing the present, everything is as clear as the palm of one's hand. The concluding discussion of the organization of soldiers and civilians is especially perceptive in its proposals. Ah! Can a student of the Classics have cultivated such learning!

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: The relationship between civilians and soldiers differs between antiquity and the present; this too results from changes in the course of the world. To avoid the commonplace arguments of students of the Classics, with their insistence on antiquity as the necessary standard, is learning that can meet the needs of the age.

There are differences between antiquity and the present in the four occupations, and there are differences between antiquity and the present in military organization. Heaven gives birth to the people alike: they may serve as civilians or as soldiers. When soldiers were included among civilians, making four occupational groups, the age was simple and the people sincere, and there was much to commend. When soldiers became separate from civilians, making five groups, the age changed and customs shifted, and there was much to question. These differences do not arise from soldiers and civilians themselves; rather, the circumstances that distinguish antiquity from the present cannot but differ. Now that I have received your illuminating question, how could I dare offer no words in reply?

Once the benefits of plows and hoes were introduced, there first appeared in the world those called farmers. Once the benefits of holding markets at midday were introduced, there first appeared in the world those called merchants. With the making of bows and arrows, boats and oars, and palaces and houses, there first appeared in the world those called artisans. When knotted cords were replaced with written documents, there first appeared in the world those called scholars. Yet Huang…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
帝戰涿鹿虞舜伐有苗兵之來盖亦久矣
稱四民而不及於兵者豈不以兵即民為
之用而亦非所常用者歟語民則兵在其
中矣世有升降人有賢愚古之人方其為
士則道問學及其為農則力稼穡為兵則
善戰陣投之所向無不如意士之有位者
各稱其德有學者不干於進農工商賈所
享有限上下之志以定彼此之分各得古
之為民不可議矣在易之履曰君子辨上
===
下定民志其吾夫子衰世之意乎盖以士
庶公卿日誌於尊榮農工商賈日誌於富
侈億兆之心交騖於利故舜與伊尹之聖
雖農而不足為卑非堯求之急湯聘之勤
畝畝自若也傅說膠鬲之賢雖工商而不
足為賤非武丁舉之文王起之巖市自如
也其志有不定乎程子之論盖未始不脗
合也四民之在古今淳漓如此至於兵制
之異又有可言者焉周為井田之制寓兵
punctuated: 帝戰涿鹿，虞舜伐有苗，兵之來盖亦久矣。稱四民而不及於兵者，豈不以兵即民為之用，而亦非所常用者歟？語民，則兵在其中矣。世有升降，人有賢愚。古之人，方其為士，則道問學；及其為農，則力稼穡；為兵，則善戰陣。投之所向，無不如意。士之有位者，各稱其德；有學者，不干於進。農工商賈，所享有限。上下之志以定，彼此之分各得。古之為民，不可議矣。在《易》之《履》曰：「君子辨上下，定民志。」其吾夫子衰世之意乎？盖以士庶公卿日誌於尊榮，農工商賈日誌於富侈，億兆之心交騖於利。故舜與伊尹之聖，雖農而不足為卑，非堯求之急、湯聘之勤，畝畝自若也。傅說、膠鬲之賢，雖工商而不足為賤，非武丁舉之、文王起之，巖市自如也。其志有不定乎？程子之論，盖未始不脗合也。四民之在古今，淳漓如此。至於兵制之異，又有可言者焉。周為井田之制，寓兵
translation_en:
…Emperor fought at Zhuolu, and Yu Shun campaigned against the Youmiao: the origins of soldiery are indeed ancient. When people spoke of the four occupations without mentioning soldiers, was this not because soldiers were simply the common people put to military use, and such use was not constant? To speak of the people was thus to include soldiers within them. Ages rise and decline; people differ in worth and wisdom. In antiquity, when people served as scholars, they pursued inquiry and learning; when they farmed, they devoted themselves to sowing and reaping; when they served as soldiers, they were skilled in battle formations. Whatever task they were assigned, they fulfilled it satisfactorily. Scholars holding office occupied positions commensurate with their virtue; those possessing learning did not seek advancement. Farmers, artisans, and merchants observed limits in what they enjoyed. The aspirations of high and low were thereby settled, and each obtained his proper station. The condition of the people in antiquity was beyond reproach.

The Book of Changes says in the hexagram Treading (Lü): “The gentleman distinguishes between high and low and settles the aspirations of the people.” Was this perhaps an expression of our Master’s concern for an age of decline? For scholars, commoners, dukes, and ministers daily set their minds on honor and glory, while farmers, artisans, and merchants daily set theirs on wealth and luxury; the hearts of the countless multitudes raced against one another in pursuit of profit. Yet sages such as Shun and Yi Yin were not rendered lowly by farming. Had Yao not sought Shun so urgently, and Tang not so diligently invited Yi Yin into service, they would have remained content in the fields [?]. Worthies such as Fu Yue and Jiao Ge were not rendered base by working as an artisan or merchant. Had Wu Ding not raised Fu Yue to office, and King Wen not summoned Jiao Ge from obscurity, they would have remained at ease among the rocks and in the marketplace. Were their aspirations in any way unsettled? Master Cheng’s discussion was surely entirely in accord with this.

Such was the difference between the simplicity and the deterioration of the four occupations in ancient and later times. As for differences in military institutions, there is more to say. The Zhou established the well-field system and embedded soldiery…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
於農戎馬干戈素具於平時蒐苗獮狩簡
教於農隙無事則為比閭族黨州鄉之民
有事則為伍兩卒旅師軍之衆兵者視農
而益損行者視居而益損兵農之制此其
盡善矣管子內政於都邑近地為士農之
鄉十五以賦三軍在鄉曰農在軍曰士也
為工商之鄉六以給財費工不知卒商不
知軍也惟文學之士特為貴之處以閒燕
之地不雜農工之流國之外無兵國之內
===
無農兵農之分此其作俑矣嗣是而後隷
尺籍者遍於中土躬甲胄者盈於疆場降
而秦漢兵不謀民民不謀兵矣又降而唐
宋兵自為兵民自為民矣惟唐之府兵頗
為近古教閲於農隙之時調發於有事之
日行兵則自置甲胄自備資糧罷兵則將
歸於朝兵散於府固為善矣然亦不旋踵
而廢之四民之外有所謂兵者盖不可得
而易矣周之為制固善豈所望於後世乎
punctuated: 於農，戎馬干戈素具於平時，蒐苗獮狩簡教於農隙。無事則為比閭族黨州鄉之民，有事則為伍兩卒旅師軍之衆。兵者視農而益損，行者視居而益損。兵農之制，此其盡善矣。管子內政於都邑近地，為士農之鄉十五，以賦三軍，在鄉曰農，在軍曰士也；為工商之鄉六，以給財費，工不知卒，商不知軍也。惟文學之士，特為貴之，處以閒燕之地，不雜農工之流。國之外無兵，國之內無農。兵農之分，此其作俑矣。嗣是而後，隷尺籍者遍於中土，躬甲胄者盈於疆場。降而秦漢，兵不謀民，民不謀兵矣；又降而唐宋，兵自為兵，民自為民矣。惟唐之府兵，頗為近古，教閲於農隙之時，調發於有事之日。行兵則自置甲胄，自備資糧；罷兵則將歸於朝，兵散於府，固為善矣。然亦不旋踵而廢之。四民之外，有所謂兵者，盖不可得而易矣。周之為制固善，豈所望於後世乎？
translation_en:
…within agriculture. Warhorses, shields, and spears were kept ready in peacetime, and troops were inspected and trained during the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts, in the intervals between agricultural tasks. When there was no trouble, they were inhabitants organized into bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; when trouble arose, they became troops organized into wu, liang, zu, lü, shi, and jun. The number serving as soldiers increased or decreased in proportion to the farming population, and the number sent out on campaign increased or decreased in proportion to those remaining at home. Here the system integrating soldiers and farmers attained its fullest excellence.

In organizing internal administration in the capital and its vicinity, Guanzi established fifteen townships of soldiers and farmers to furnish three armies: in their townships they were called farmers, and in the army they were called soldiers. He established six townships of artisans and merchants to supply funds and meet expenses: artisans knew nothing of troop units, and merchants knew nothing of armies. Only men of literary learning were especially honored and settled in quiet places of leisure, without being mixed among farmers and artisans. Outside the capital there were no soldiers; within it there were no farmers. This initiated the separation of soldiers from farmers.

Thereafter, men entered on military registers were found throughout the central lands, and men clad in armor and helmets filled the frontier battlefields. By the Qin and Han, soldiers took no thought for civilians, and civilians took no thought for soldiers. Later still, under the Tang and Song, soldiers formed a body unto themselves, and civilians likewise. Only the Tang militia system, the fubing, came fairly close to antiquity. Its men were trained and inspected during intervals between agricultural tasks and mobilized when trouble arose. When campaigning, they provided their own armor and helmets and supplied their own provisions. When hostilities ceased, the generals returned to court and the soldiers dispersed to their military headquarters. This was certainly a good system. Yet it too was abolished before long. The existence of a separate category called soldiers, outside the four occupations, had apparently become impossible to change. The Zhou system was certainly good, but could one expect it of later ages?

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
暑葛寒裘各因其時而不可以倒施章甫
逢掖各有其地而不可以通用亦猶是也
方今之兵民大抵皆歷代遺意執事乃欲
求其近似者愚則以為屯田之制兵以耕
田食以給兵庶幾兵農合一之意然耕者
多不戰戰者多不耕固已不類唐之府兵
矣求三代之制所謂愈似而愈不似焉管
見如斯然尤有耿耿之懷不敢不終其說
居今之世不必求之古矣仰惟我
===
太祖高皇帝之定天下萬姓遵義百度順軌兵
民之在天下亦何讓於古哉然無不弊之
法亦無不變之時以今之四民言士嬉而
荒於學農貧而病於耕工以濫惡欺人商
以虛夸逐利四民之所以弊者如此也以
今之兵制言營乏壯丁伍多虛籍逃避者
不盡心於清補操練者不加意於存恤兵
制之所以弊者如此也是責也典守者其
可辭乎文臣所以親民也清身心敦教
punctuated:
暑葛寒裘，各因其時，而不可以倒施；章甫逢掖，各有其地，而不可以通用，亦猶是也。方今之兵民，大抵皆歷代遺意。執事乃欲求其近似者，愚則以為屯田之制，兵以耕田，食以給兵，庶幾兵農合一之意。然耕者多不戰，戰者多不耕，固已不類唐之府兵矣。求三代之制，所謂愈似而愈不似焉。管見如斯，然尤有耿耿之懷，不敢不終其說。居今之世，不必求之古矣。
仰惟我太祖高皇帝之定天下，萬姓遵義，百度順軌，兵民之在天下，亦何讓於古哉？然無不弊之法，亦無不變之時。以今之四民言，士嬉而荒於學，農貧而病於耕，工以濫惡欺人，商以虛夸逐利。四民之所以弊者，如此也。以今之兵制言，營乏壯丁，伍多虛籍，逃避者不盡心於清補，操練者不加意於存恤。兵制之所以弊者，如此也。是責也，典守者其可辭乎？文臣所以親民也，清身心，敦教
translation_en:
…Light hemp clothing in summer and fur robes in winter each suit their season and cannot be worn in reverse; the zhangfu cap and the broad-sleeved scholar’s robe each have their proper locale and cannot be used everywhere. The same principle applies here. The present arrangements for soldiers and civilians largely preserve the intentions of successive dynasties. You, sir, wish to find what most closely resembles the ancient system. In my humble view, under the military agricultural colony system, soldiers cultivate fields and the produce provisions them: this comes close to the intention of uniting soldiers and farmers. Yet most who farm do not fight, and most who fight do not farm. It thus already differs from the Tang militia system (fubing). If we look to it for the institutions of the Three Dynasties, this is what is meant by becoming ever more unlike them the more it resembles them. Such is my limited view. Yet something still weighs upon my heart, and I dare not leave my argument unfinished. Living in the present age, we need not seek our institutions in antiquity.
I reverently reflect that when our Emperor Taizu Gao brought the realm under his rule, all the people followed righteousness and every institution followed its proper course. How could the arrangements for soldiers and civilians throughout the realm have been inferior to those of antiquity? Yet no law is immune to deterioration, and no age is free from change. Consider the four occupations today: scholars idle away their time and neglect their studies; farmers are impoverished and struggle with cultivation; artisans deceive people with shoddy goods; merchants pursue profit through empty boasts. Such are the failings of the four occupations. Consider the military system today: camps lack able-bodied men, and units have many fictitious entries on their rolls. In cases of desertion and evasion, those responsible do not devote themselves fully to checking the rolls and filling vacancies; those who conduct training give insufficient attention to caring for the soldiers. Such are the failings of the military system. Can those charged with its administration evade responsibility for this? Civil officials are charged with caring for the people. Let them purify their conduct and minds and promote moral instruction…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
化示好惡以臨之明勸懲以警之則可以
還淳厚之風矣武臣所以掌兵也去貪
暴戒驕縱同甘苦以撫之嚴紀律以御之
則可以起廢弛之政矣然所以督率乎文
武臣工者又有道焉文臣三歲述職以行
黜陟者有典要必不以簿書期會者為能
而以留心教化者為善責其效之有無而
以進以退武臣五歲考選以行予奪者有
令要必不以撒堅中的為急而以撫綏軍
===
士為先稽其政之善否而以勸以懲上之
所以責成者在是則下之所以遵循者亦
在是宿弊可革美政可成而求唐虞之治
不難矣若夫任乎人以主考選而悉本於
公廉稽於衆以憑黜陟而不昧於賢否則
在於今日廟堂留意焉非愚生所知也
第四問
張鳳翔
同考試官教諭程 批偏鄉之士能周知
punctuated:
化，示好惡以臨之，明勸懲以警之，則可以還淳厚之風矣。武臣所以掌兵也，去貪暴，戒驕縱，同甘苦以撫之，嚴紀律以御之，則可以起廢弛之政矣。然所以督率乎文武臣工者，又有道焉。文臣三歲述職以行黜陟者有典，要必不以簿書期會者為能，而以留心教化者為善，責其效之有無，而以進以退。武臣五歲考選以行予奪者有令，要必不以撒堅中的為急，而以撫綏軍士為先，稽其政之善否，而以勸以懲。上之所以責成者在是，則下之所以遵循者亦在是。宿弊可革，美政可成，而求唐虞之治不難矣。若夫任乎人以主考選，而悉本於公廉；稽於衆以憑黜陟，而不昧於賢否，則在於今日廟堂留意焉，非愚生所知也。
第四問
張鳳翔
同考試官教諭程批：偏鄉之士能周知
translation_en:
… moral transformation. By making clear what they approve and disapprove of in governing the people, and clarifying rewards and punishments to admonish them, they can restore customs of simplicity and generosity. Military officials are responsible for commanding troops. If they abandon greed and brutality, guard against arrogance and indulgence, share their soldiers’ hardships and comforts in caring for them, and enforce strict discipline in directing them, they can revive administration that has fallen into neglect. Yet there is also a proper way to supervise and guide civil and military officials. Established regulations require civil officials to report on their service every three years, so that demotions and promotions may be made. The essential point is that proficiency in paperwork and meeting deadlines must not be taken as the measure of ability; rather, attention to moral instruction must be regarded as merit. Whether they have achieved results should be examined, and they should accordingly be advanced or dismissed. There are likewise ordinances requiring military officials to undergo assessment and selection every five years, so that appointments may be granted or withdrawn. The essential point is that piercing solid objects [?] and hitting targets must not be treated as the urgent priority; rather, caring for and keeping the soldiers content must come first. The quality of their administration should be examined, and they should accordingly be rewarded or punished. If these are the grounds on which superiors demand results, they will also be the principles followed by subordinates. Long-standing abuses can be eliminated and good government achieved; attaining the government of Tang and Yu—the sage rulers Yao and Shun—will then not be difficult. As for appointing people to preside over assessment and selection, ensuring that everything rests on impartiality and integrity, and consulting the many as a basis for demotion and promotion without failing to distinguish the worthy from the unworthy: these are matters to which the court today must give its attention. They are beyond the knowledge of this ignorant student.
Fourth Question
Zhang Fengxiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: Scholars from remote places who can possess a comprehensive knowledge of …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
天下之務者絕少子何練達如是
豈嘗留心於經濟之學者耶
同考試官教諭杜批洞見財用消息而
歸本於
九重之上可謂芹曝之獻矣
考試官教諭朱批文詞敏妙財用處
置尤為超絕盖有志於經國者宜
用錄出
考試官學正王批說天下財用豐耗
詳悉無遺而忠愛之言尤
當宁所宜聞者異時致用必有大過于人
===
工於經國者既究夫耗財之弊必求其豐
財之本盖耗財者未始不由於奢豐財者
未始不由於儉以天地間有限之財而供
上下無窮之用苟非去其奢之弊求其儉
之本則財益至於耗而不可以望其豐矣
愚嘗觀之以天下之利養天下之人財之
在民者宜足也以天下之賦供天下之用
punctuated:
天下之務者絕少，子何練達如是？豈嘗留心於經濟之學者耶？

同考試官教諭杜批：洞見財用消息，而歸本於九重之上，可謂芹曝之獻矣。

考試官教諭朱批：文詞敏妙，財用處置尤為超絕，盖有志於經國者，宜用錄出。

考試官學正王批：說天下財用豐耗，詳悉無遺，而忠愛之言尤當宁所宜聞者。異時致用，必有大過于人。

工於經國者，既究夫耗財之弊，必求其豐財之本。盖耗財者未始不由於奢，豐財者未始不由於儉。以天地間有限之財，而供上下無窮之用，苟非去其奢之弊，求其儉之本，則財益至於耗，而不可以望其豐矣。愚嘗觀之，以天下之利養天下之人，財之在民者宜足也；以天下之賦供天下之用，
translation_en:
…those who understand the affairs of the realm are exceedingly few. How have you become so practiced and perceptive? Have you perhaps devoted yourself to the study of statecraft?

Associate Examiner Du, Instructor, comments: You perceive thoroughly the ebb and flow of financial resources and trace their ultimate basis to the emperor himself. This may indeed be called a humble offering of celery and sunshine—a well-meant offering to the sovereign.

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: The writing is deft and elegant, and the proposals for managing financial resources are especially outstanding. Evidently the author aspires to administer the state; this piece merits selection for inclusion in the record.

Examiner Wang, Director of Studies, comments: The discussion of abundance and depletion in the realm’s financial resources is exhaustive, leaving nothing out. Its words of loyalty and concern are especially fitting for the emperor to hear. When the author puts his abilities to use in the future, he will surely far surpass others.

One skilled in administering the state, having investigated the abuses that deplete wealth, must seek the foundation for making it abundant. For the depletion of wealth invariably arises from extravagance, and its abundance invariably arises from frugality. The finite wealth between Heaven and Earth must meet the endless expenditures of those above and below. Unless the abuses of extravagance are removed and the foundation of frugality is sought, wealth will become ever more depleted, and there can be no hope of abundance.

I have considered this: when the resources of the realm sustain the people of the realm, the wealth held by the people ought to suffice; when the tax revenues of the realm meet the expenditures of the realm, …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
財之在官者宜足也夫何民無恒産者凶
年饑歲固告病矣而沃土豐年猶不免於
流移是財果在民耶官無餘積者諸省有
司固告匱矣而
內帑戶部猶未見於充實是財果在官耶
國家自洪武永樂至於天順上下之間法度
修明人心儆畏國無妄費民無濫為財用
豐盈海內殷富故雖有兵荒之急不足為
患比年以來遊惰之徒遍於中土不耕而
===
食所謂一夫耕之十人食之者有矣不蠶
而衣所謂一婦蠶之十人衣之者有矣此
其一弊也豪商鉅族僭擬王公置一器用
足當中人之産為一飲食不惜萬錢之費
此又一弊也有民社者惟志温飽綰章綬
者相尚豪華飲食服御必極其盛子女玉
帛必窮其欲此又一弊也京師貴倖衣一
衣乘一馬辦一宴會非窮奢極麗不可其
他所為亦各稱是修一第治一墅創一菴
punctuated: 財之在官者宜足也。夫何民無恒産者，凶年饑歲固告病矣，而沃土豐年猶不免於流移，是財果在民耶？官無餘積者，諸省有司固告匱矣，而內帑戶部猶未見於充實，是財果在官耶？國家自洪武、永樂至於天順，上下之間，法度修明，人心儆畏，國無妄費，民無濫為，財用豐盈，海內殷富，故雖有兵荒之急，不足為患。比年以來，遊惰之徒遍於中土，不耕而食，所謂一夫耕之，十人食之者有矣；不蠶而衣，所謂一婦蠶之，十人衣之者有矣。此其一弊也。豪商鉅族僭擬王公，置一器用，足當中人之産；為一飲食，不惜萬錢之費。此又一弊也。有民社者惟志温飽，綰章綬者相尚豪華，飲食服御必極其盛，子女玉帛必窮其欲。此又一弊也。京師貴倖，衣一衣，乘一馬，辦一宴會，非窮奢極麗不可；其他所為，亦各稱是。修一第，治一墅，創一菴
translation_en:
…wealth held by the government ought likewise to be sufficient. Why, then, do people without a secure livelihood suffer distress not only in years of crop failure and famine, but also find themselves forced to migrate even where the soil is fertile and the harvest abundant? Is wealth really in the hands of the people? As for the government's lack of reserves, not only do the responsible offices in the provinces report shortages, but even the palace treasury and the Ministry of Revenue have yet to achieve adequate stocks. Is wealth really in the hands of the government?

From the Hongwu and Yongle reigns through the Tianshun reign, laws and institutions were well maintained and clearly established at every level, and people's hearts were vigilant and respectful. The state incurred no reckless expenditure, and the people engaged in no excessive pursuits. Financial resources were plentiful, and the realm was prosperous. Thus, even emergencies arising from warfare or famine were insufficient to cause serious concern.

In recent years, idle people have spread throughout the central lands. They eat without plowing: there are indeed cases of what is called “one man plowing and ten people eating.” They wear clothes without raising silkworms: there are indeed cases of what is called “one woman raising silkworms and ten people wearing clothes.” This is one abuse. Wealthy merchants and great families presumptuously emulate princes and dukes. A single utensil they acquire may equal the entire property of a household of middling means; for a single meal, they do not begrudge an expenditure of ten thousand cash. This is another abuse. Those entrusted with the people and their local altars care only for their own comfort and sustenance; those wearing official seals and ribbons vie with one another in luxury. In food, clothing, and personal articles, they insist upon the utmost splendor; in women and young attendants, jade and silk, they indulge their desires to the full. This is another abuse.

The powerful and favored in the capital will accept nothing short of the utmost extravagance and magnificence in wearing a garment, riding a horse, or holding a banquet. Everything else they do is on a matching scale. To build a residence, lay out a country estate, or establish a Buddhist hermitage…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
寺非數萬金不可其餘所蓄尤不可計此
又一弊也課税出於民而流移者負欠無
徵租賦出於地而凶荒者减免其數縣之
所虧者百則郡之所虧者必千矣郡之所
虧者千則省之所虧者必萬矣
內帑供邊者今日出西北明日出東北所需
無間戶部之給俸者今日給文臣明日給
武臣所費不貲他如冗員以鼠雀其間緇
黃以尾閭其內不急之工作例外之賞賚
===
又有不可數計者矣嗚呼天地之生財今
猶古也而生齒日繁國用日益加以數弊
四出而奪之欲國不虛民不困胡可得耶
脫有水旱兵戈吾不知何以為處也為富
國足民計者孰不曰禁遊惰抑鉅族汰贓
吏律貴倖而不知其抑末矣故論當今之
務者勿求其有餘去奢而已勿患其不足
崇儉而已奢去而儉崇則天地所生之財
自足以供上下之用釋此不務而惟目前
punctuated: 寺，非數萬金不可，其餘所蓄尤不可計，此又一弊也。課税出於民，而流移者負欠無徵；租賦出於地，而凶荒者减免其數。縣之所虧者百，則郡之所虧者必千矣；郡之所虧者千，則省之所虧者必萬矣。內帑供邊者，今日出西北，明日出東北，所需無間；戶部之給俸者，今日給文臣，明日給武臣，所費不貲。他如冗員以鼠雀其間，緇黃以尾閭其內，不急之工作，例外之賞賚，又有不可數計者矣。嗚呼！天地之生財，今猶古也，而生齒日繁，國用日益，加以數弊四出而奪之，欲國不虛、民不困，胡可得耶？脫有水旱兵戈，吾不知何以為處也。為富國足民計者，孰不曰禁遊惰、抑鉅族、汰贓吏、律貴倖，而不知其抑末矣。故論當今之務者，勿求其有餘，去奢而已；勿患其不足，崇儉而已。奢去而儉崇，則天地所生之財，自足以供上下之用。釋此不務，而惟目前
translation_en:
…a temple cannot be built without tens of thousands in gold; their other accumulated possessions are still less possible to reckon. This is yet another abuse. Taxes are drawn from the people, but those who have migrated leave arrears that cannot be collected. Land taxes are drawn from the soil, but crop failures and famine require reductions or exemptions. If the shortfall in a county is a hundred, that in a prefecture must be a thousand; if the shortfall in a prefecture is a thousand, that in a province must be ten thousand. Funds from the palace treasury for provisioning the frontier go out today to the northwest and tomorrow to the northeast: the demands never cease. The Ministry of Revenue pays salaries today to civil officials and tomorrow to military officials: the expenditure is immense. Then there are supernumerary officials who nibble away like rats and sparrows, and Buddhist and Daoist clergy who drain resources like the great outlet of the sea. Unnecessary construction projects and rewards granted outside the established rules are likewise beyond reckoning.

Alas! Heaven and earth produce wealth today just as they did in antiquity, yet the population grows daily and state expenditure increases daily. Added to this, these various abuses arise on every side and consume that wealth. How could one hope to keep the state's resources from being exhausted and the people from being impoverished? Should flood, drought, or war occur, I do not know how we would cope. Among those who devise plans to enrich the state and provide sufficiently for the people, who does not advocate prohibiting idleness, restraining powerful families, dismissing corrupt officials, and disciplining powerful imperial favorites? Yet they do not realize that this merely checks the symptoms. Thus, those who discuss the pressing business of the present should not seek a surplus, but simply eliminate extravagance; they should not worry about insufficiency, but simply promote frugality. Once extravagance is eliminated and frugality honored, the wealth produced by heaven and earth will naturally suffice for the needs of those above and below. To set this aside without attending to it, and concern oneself solely with immediate…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之計是圖未見其有濟也然所謂去奢而
崇儉者豈可以他求哉盖京師者天下之
本
朝廷者四方之極欲天下儉焉必自京師始
欲京師儉焉必自
朝廷始昔漢文帝欲作露臺以惜百金之費
而寢其役宋仁宗夜思燒羊恐以為例而
遏其念夫以天下之大百金與燒羊豈足
惜哉盖防其漸則末流自息也我
===
太祖高皇帝以宫中隙地不起臺榭但令種蔬
曰不忍傷民之財勞民之力
太宗文皇帝所服裏衣袖敝垢納而復出曰自
念當惜福每澣濯更進夫以天下之大隙
地與裏衣豈足靳哉盖謹其微則大者可
知也今
天子踐祚之初凡百政化圖維更新將必遠稽
前代近法
祖宗崇儉德以答
punctuated:
之計是圖，未見其有濟也。然所謂去奢而崇儉者，豈可以他求哉？盖京師者，天下之本；朝廷者，四方之極。欲天下儉焉，必自京師始；欲京師儉焉，必自朝廷始。昔漢文帝欲作露臺，以惜百金之費而寢其役；宋仁宗夜思燒羊，恐以為例而遏其念。夫以天下之大，百金與燒羊豈足惜哉？盖防其漸，則末流自息也。
我太祖高皇帝以宫中隙地不起臺榭，但令種蔬，曰：「不忍傷民之財，勞民之力。」太宗文皇帝所服裏衣，袖敝垢，納而復出，曰：「自念當惜福。」每澣濯更進。夫以天下之大，隙地與裏衣豈足靳哉？盖謹其微，則大者可知也。
今天子踐祚之初，凡百政化，圖維更新，將必遠稽前代，近法祖宗，崇儉德以答
translation_en:
…to pursue only immediate expedients—I have yet to see how this could help. Yet can what we call eliminating extravagance and honoring frugality be sought elsewhere? The capital is the foundation of all under Heaven; the court is the standard for the four quarters. To make all under Heaven frugal, one must begin with the capital; to make the capital frugal, one must begin with the court. In former times, Emperor Wen of Han wished to build a terrace for observing dew, but, begrudging the expense of a hundred measures of gold, abandoned the undertaking. Emperor Renzong of Song once craved roast lamb at night, but suppressed the thought for fear of setting a precedent. Given the vast resources of the empire, why should a hundred measures of gold or roast lamb be worth sparing? By guarding against the beginnings of extravagance, however, its later consequences cease of themselves.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao had no terraces or pavilions built on vacant ground within the palace, but ordered only that vegetables be planted there. He said: “I cannot bear to deplete the people's wealth or exhaust their strength.” When the sleeves of Emperor Taizong Wen's inner garment became worn and soiled, it was put away and then brought out again. He said: “I remind myself that I ought to cherish my blessings.” Each time, it was washed and presented to him again. Given the vast resources of the empire, why should vacant ground and an inner garment be worth stinting over? Yet from care in small matters, his conduct in great ones can be known.
Now, at the beginning of the Son of Heaven's reign, plans are being made to renew every aspect of government and moral transformation. He will surely look far back to examine earlier dynasties and, nearer at hand, take his ancestors as models, honoring the virtue of frugality in order to respond to…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
天意節財源以恤民艱思天地生財有限而不
欲盡錙銖之求知國家為費無窮而不忍
如泥沙之用二月賣新絲蠶婦之勞可念
也五月糶新穀農夫之苦可想也運至仁
於
九重渙大號於天下以禁遊惰以抑鉅族以汰
贓吏以律貴倖則推無不準動無不化浮
靡之習可以祛除淳古之風可以挽回矣
在民者何患其有不足而在官者何慮其
===
有不裕乎否則號令雖繁而風俗日流於
富侈會計雖詳而國用愈至於空虚欲天
下財用之足萬無是理也經理之術恐不
外此塵容俗狀得與進而觀
上國之光尚當以芻蕘鄙見陳之
第五問
沈淳
同考試官教諭廖 批舉目前之切要者
為言而治風俗之道實不外是彼
punctuated:
天意，節財源以恤民艱。思天地生財有限，而不欲盡錙銖之求；知國家為費無窮，而不忍如泥沙之用。二月賣新絲，蠶婦之勞可念也；五月糶新穀，農夫之苦可想也。運至仁於九重，渙大號於天下，以禁遊惰，以抑鉅族，以汰贓吏，以律貴倖，則推無不準，動無不化。浮靡之習可以祛除，淳古之風可以挽回矣。在民者何患其有不足，而在官者何慮其有不裕乎？否則，號令雖繁，而風俗日流於富侈；會計雖詳，而國用愈至於空虚。欲天下財用之足，萬無是理也。經理之術，恐不外此。塵容俗狀，得與進而觀上國之光，尚當以芻蕘鄙見陳之。
第五問
沈淳
同考試官教諭廖批：舉目前之切要者為言，而治風俗之道實不外是。彼
translation_en:
…Heaven’s intent, and conserve sources of revenue to relieve the people’s hardships. Reflecting that Heaven and Earth produce wealth in limited quantities, he will not wish to exact every last fraction; knowing that the state’s expenses are endless, he will not bear to spend wealth like mud and sand. When new silk is sold in the second month, the toil of the women who tend silkworms deserves consideration; when new grain is sold in the fifth month, the farmers’ suffering can be imagined. Let him exercise the utmost benevolence within the imperial palace and issue great proclamations throughout the realm to prohibit idleness, restrain powerful clans, dismiss corrupt officials, and discipline influential imperial favorites. Then every extension of these measures will accord with the proper standard, and every action will bring transformation. Habits of extravagance can be eradicated, and the simple customs of antiquity restored. Why should the people worry about having too little, or the officials fear that their resources will be inadequate?
Otherwise, however numerous the commands, customs will daily tend toward opulence and extravagance; however detailed the accounts, the state’s resources will become ever more depleted. To expect the realm’s wealth and resources to suffice under such circumstances is utterly unreasonable. The methods of managing these affairs, I venture to suggest, do not extend beyond this. Should I, with my humble appearance and commonplace bearing, be permitted to advance and behold the splendor of the imperial capital, I shall further present my rustic, lowly views.
Fifth Question
Shen Chun
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: He addresses the most pressing matters of the present, and the way to reform customs indeed lies in these measures. Those who …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
迂談者退避三舍矣
考試官教諭朱批論一方事關繫甚
大意之所到辭足發之而筆力雄
健恢乎有餘可以為文矣
考試官學正王批論事精到鑿鑿可
行舉而措之則風移而俗易矣得
士如此允為科目之光
讀孔子告冉有之言則知民富而後教施
讀孔子答哀公之問則知人存而後政舉
===
夫民俗之未善由民生之未富民生苟富
則其教也不令而從矣民生之未富由有
司之失職有司得人則其富也可立而待
矣為治者因是求之而不失其施為之序
何患風俗之不善耶請陳其說雲貴古西
南夷地風氣晦塞聲教不通淪異域者不
知其幾千萬載我
皇明奄有茲地分郡縣而置官吏列衞所以治
甲兵既以揆文教又以奮武衞百四十年
punctuated:
迂談者退避三舍矣。
考試官教諭朱批：論一方事，關繫甚大，意之所到，辭足發之，而筆力雄健，恢乎有餘，可以為文矣。
考試官學正王批：論事精到，鑿鑿可行，舉而措之，則風移而俗易矣。得士如此，允為科目之光。
讀孔子告冉有之言，則知民富而後教施；讀孔子答哀公之問，則知人存而後政舉。夫民俗之未善，由民生之未富；民生苟富，則其教也不令而從矣。民生之未富，由有司之失職；有司得人，則其富也可立而待矣。為治者因是求之，而不失其施為之序，何患風俗之不善耶？請陳其說。雲貴，古西南夷地，風氣晦塞，聲教不通，淪異域者不知其幾千萬載。我皇明奄有茲地，分郡縣而置官吏，列衞所以治甲兵，既以揆文教，又以奮武衞，百四十年
translation_en:
…those who engage in impractical talk must retreat a full three stages.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: This discussion concerns the affairs of a region, matters of very great consequence. Wherever the author's thought reaches, his language adequately expresses it. His writing is powerful and vigorous, expansive and more than equal to its task. This merits recognition as accomplished writing.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: The discussion is precise and penetrating, and its proposals are demonstrably practicable. Put them into effect, and prevailing ways and customs will change. To obtain a scholar like this is truly a distinction for the examination system.

Reading Confucius's words to Ran You, we understand that the people must become prosperous before instruction can be implemented; reading Confucius's answer to Duke Ai, we understand that government can be carried out only when the right men are present. The people's customs remain unsatisfactory because their livelihoods are not yet abundant. If their livelihoods were abundant, they would follow instruction without being commanded. Their livelihoods are not yet abundant because the responsible officials neglect their duties. If the right men hold office, prosperity can be expected almost immediately. If those who govern seek a solution on this basis and preserve the proper sequence of their measures, why should they worry that customs will fail to improve? Allow me to explain.

Yunnan and Guizhou were anciently the lands of the southwestern Yi. Their prevailing influences were benighted and obstructed, and the court's civilizing instruction did not reach them. They remained outside the realm for untold thousands upon thousands of years. Our august Ming took possession of these lands, divided them into prefectures and counties, and appointed officials. It established guards to administer troops and arms, both ordering civil instruction and strengthening military protection, for one hundred and forty years…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
餘攀鱗附翼之士建功立業之人後先相
望宜乎俗盡衣冠人皆禮義矣然而異言
異服肆行劫奪貪財賤義無情健訟士乖
庠序之教女昧行露之義親戚之恩或薄
婚姻之黨非宜是皆目擊耳聞之實誠有
如執事之所謂者風俗如此果可以為文
明之盛乎愚嘗見其端矣田連阡陌者不
一二而地無立錐者盖多焉身被裘帛者
不數人而體無完衣者盖衆焉欠官租者
===
以貧而鬻子女負私貸者以貧而棄屋廬
遇兵興也闔境困於供需遇災傷也比屋
仆於凍餓貧也如此望其能為禮義廉恥
之事乎又嘗求其故矣土官之設因其類
而撫之也能撫之者誰歟流官之設宣其
化而安之也能安之者誰歟求牧與芻而
不得視其斃者有之刈葵放手而莫恤傷
其根者有之名為輸稅而所取半入於私
家名為
punctuated: 餘，攀鱗附翼之士、建功立業之人，後先相望，宜乎俗盡衣冠，人皆禮義矣。然而異言異服，肆行劫奪，貪財賤義，無情健訟；士乖庠序之教，女昧行露之義；親戚之恩或薄，婚姻之黨非宜。是皆目擊耳聞之實，誠有如執事之所謂者。風俗如此，果可以為文明之盛乎？愚嘗見其端矣：田連阡陌者不一二，而地無立錐者盖多焉；身被裘帛者不數人，而體無完衣者盖衆焉。欠官租者，以貧而鬻子女；負私貸者，以貧而棄屋廬。遇兵興也，闔境困於供需；遇災傷也，比屋仆於凍餓。貧也如此，望其能為禮義廉恥之事乎？又嘗求其故矣：土官之設，因其類而撫之也，能撫之者誰歟？流官之設，宣其化而安之也，能安之者誰歟？求牧與芻而不得，視其斃者有之；刈葵放手而莫恤傷其根者有之。名為輸稅，而所取半入於私家；名為
translation_en:
…and more years, men who attached themselves to the dragon’s scales and wings, and men who established achievements and careers, have followed one another in succession. Surely local customs should by now all reflect civilized dress, and everyone should observe ritual propriety and righteousness. Yet people speak different tongues and wear different clothing, freely plunder and rob, covet wealth and disdain righteousness, and eagerly pursue groundless litigation. Scholars depart from the teachings of the schools, and women fail to understand the meaning of “Dew on the Path” (Xing lu). Affection among relatives is sometimes thin, and marriage alliances are improper. These are all things actually seen and heard, just as you, sir, have said. With customs like these, can this truly be called a flourishing civilization?

I have observed its manifestations. Those whose fields stretch across the paths dividing the farmland are not merely one or two, while those without enough land to stand an awl upon are many. Those who wear furs and silk are only a few, while those without an intact garment are numerous. Those in arrears on government land taxes sell their sons and daughters because of poverty; those burdened by private loans abandon their homes because of poverty. When troops are mobilized, the entire territory suffers from the demands for supplies; when disaster strikes, household after household collapses from cold and hunger. In poverty such as this, can one expect people to act with ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame?

I have also sought the causes. Native officials were appointed to nurture the people in accordance with their own kinds; who among them can truly nurture them? Regular officials were appointed to spread imperial moral instruction and bring the people peace; who among them can truly bring them peace? Some fail to obtain the herdsmen and fodder they seek, and watch their charges perish. Some cut the mallows with an unrestrained hand, heedless of injuring their roots. What is called tax remittance sends half of what is collected into private households; what is called…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
詔恩而斯民不蒙於實惠有司如此望其能有
飽煖安逸之民乎此風俗之所以不善也
為今之計不在責於下而在責於上不在
治其民而在治其官臨以藩臬監以臺臣
此平日之舊規也流官宜知謹矣然守法
者固有而貪饕者甘心於敗伏辜者既往
而方來者蹈轍而行法網之設雖嚴而姦
亦不絕矣其如之何哉嘗觀仕於茲地有
以願告遠方而來者非其年邁則以家貧
===
有以地里非宜而來者道途勞苦資費窘
乏凡此者皆不足為其持廉之地也雲貴
王土也豈宜鄙薄其地而以苟禄者加之
乎是非末學所敢議也在廟堂議也必也
銓選得人而若輩者不以尸位則吾民之
福矣清其宗派令其朝
覲皆近時新典也土官宜知化矣然清宗派固
免爭襲以殃民赴朝
覲不無搔擾而害衆觀光之效未臻而民已受
punctuated:
詔恩，而斯民不蒙於實惠。有司如此，望其能有飽煖安逸之民乎？此風俗之所以不善也。
為今之計，不在責於下，而在責於上；不在治其民，而在治其官。臨以藩臬，監以臺臣，此平日之舊規也。流官宜知謹矣。然守法者固有，而貪饕者甘心於敗；伏辜者既往，而方來者蹈轍而行。法網之設雖嚴，而姦亦不絕矣。其如之何哉？嘗觀仕於茲地，有以願告遠方而來者，非其年邁，則以家貧；有以地里非宜而來者，道途勞苦，資費窘乏。凡此者，皆不足為其持廉之地也。雲貴，王土也，豈宜鄙薄其地，而以苟禄者加之乎？是非末學所敢議也，在廟堂議也。必也銓選得人，而若輩者不以尸位，則吾民之福矣。
清其宗派，令其朝覲，皆近時新典也。土官宜知化矣。然清宗派，固免爭襲以殃民；赴朝覲，不無搔擾而害衆。觀光之效未臻，而民已受
translation_en:
…imperial grace, yet these people receive no tangible benefit. With the responsible officials behaving thus, can one expect the people under them to be well fed, warmly clothed, secure, and at ease? This is why local customs are not good.
The course to take now is to hold those above accountable, rather than those below, and to govern the officials rather than the people. Oversight by the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, and supervision by censorial officials, are longstanding arrangements. Regularly appointed officials ought therefore to know to act circumspectly. Yet although some uphold the law, the rapacious willingly court their own ruin. Those who have suffered punishment pass away, while their successors follow in their tracks. Though the net of the law is tightly drawn, wrongdoing never ceases. What can be done about this? I have observed that among those serving here, some come after requesting assignment to distant regions: they are either advanced in years or impoverished. Others come because their geographical eligibility is unsuitable [?], suffering arduous journeys and lacking funds for their expenses. None of these circumstances provides a sound basis for maintaining their integrity. Yunnan and Guizhou are royal territory. How could it be right to disdain these lands and set over them men concerned only with drawing a salary? This is not something that I, a humble student, dare deliberate upon; it is for the court to deliberate upon. If personnel selection secures suitable men, and such fellows no longer occupy office without fulfilling its duties, this will be a blessing for our people.
Clarifying their lines of descent and requiring them to attend imperial audiences are both recently instituted regulations. Native officials ought therefore to understand and respond to the civilizing influence of the government. Yet although clarifying lines of descent does prevent disputes over hereditary succession from bringing disaster upon the people, journeys to imperial audiences are not free of disturbances that harm the populace. The benefits of witnessing the court’s splendor have yet to materialize, while the people have already suffered…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
困矣其亦如之何哉嘗觀治夷方者律令
不施而有從其土俗之例恩威未及而遂
養成驕惰之風凡此皆不足動其守法之
念也土官王臣也豈宜鄙夷其人而以姑
息者待之乎是非末學所能議也在地方
重臣之議也必也操縱有法而若輩者於
此革心則夷方之慶矣如是則有司者無
不得人而為之上者又從而提撕警覺之
先責之以養民則必有實惠之施而後責
===
之以教民則不為虛文之設為之民者衣
食足而知榮辱倉廩實而知禮節則椎卉
者可以用夏變夷矣刼奪者可以雖賞不
竊矣義利自明而無貪得之恥曲直自喻
而無健訟之非士盡其業而衣食不困於
心女貞其行而禮義可制其慾骨肉之恩
知所念也婚姻之禮有所謹也是則責成
有司固更化之道也斡旋之機又豈外於
是哉雖然此特論雲貴之風俗姑就其所
punctuated: 困矣，其亦如之何哉？嘗觀治夷方者，律令不施，而有從其土俗之例；恩威未及，而遂養成驕惰之風。凡此皆不足動其守法之念也。土官，王臣也，豈宜鄙夷其人，而以姑息者待之乎？是非末學所能議也，在地方重臣之議也。必也操縱有法，而若輩者於此革心，則夷方之慶矣。如是，則有司者無不得人，而為之上者又從而提撕警覺之。先責之以養民，則必有實惠之施；而後責之以教民，則不為虛文之設。為之民者，衣食足而知榮辱，倉廩實而知禮節，則椎卉者可以用夏變夷矣，刼奪者可以雖賞不竊矣。義利自明，而無貪得之恥；曲直自喻，而無健訟之非。士盡其業，而衣食不困於心；女貞其行，而禮義可制其慾。骨肉之恩知所念也，婚姻之禮有所謹也。是則責成有司，固更化之道也，斡旋之機又豈外於是哉？雖然，此特論雲貴之風俗，姑就其所
translation_en:
…have suffered hardship. What, then, can be done about this? I have observed that those who govern the non-Han regions fail to enforce the statutes and ordinances, invoking precedents for following local customs; their benevolence and authority have not reached the people, and they have consequently fostered habits of arrogance and indolence. None of this is sufficient to stir a resolve to observe the law. Native officials are servants of the sovereign: how could it be proper to look down upon them and treat them with indulgence? This is not something that I, a junior scholar, am competent to discuss; it is for the senior regional officials to deliberate upon. If restraint and latitude are exercised according to proper methods, and these men thereby reform their hearts, this will be a blessing for the non-Han regions.

In this way, every administrative post will be filled by a suitable man, and those above them will further instruct and admonish them. First, hold them responsible for sustaining the people, and they will certainly confer tangible benefits; afterward, hold them responsible for teaching the people, and their efforts will not become mere empty formalities. When the people under their rule have sufficient clothing and food, they will understand honor and disgrace; when their granaries are full, they will understand ritual and propriety. Then those who wear their hair in mallet-shaped knots and clothe themselves in grasses can be transformed through Chinese civilization, and those who rob and plunder can be brought to refrain from stealing even if offered a reward for doing so. The distinction between righteousness and profit will become clear of itself, and there will be no shameful greed for gain; right and wrong will become self-evident, and there will be no wrongful addiction to litigation. Scholars will devote themselves fully to their studies, their minds untroubled by the need for clothing and food; women will be chaste in their conduct, and ritual and righteousness will restrain their desires. People will know to cherish the bonds of affection among blood relatives and scrupulously observe the rites of marriage.

Thus, holding the responsible officials accountable for results is indeed the way to effect reform. How could the means of bringing about this transformation lie outside it? Nevertheless, this discusses only the customs of Yunnan and Guizhou, provisionally addressing what is…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
宜者言之若夫一道德以同俗因奢儉以
示教是則敦本之論不可無者而規模廣
大綱領宏闊未遽行焉今日之事則當先
於其要者而後及於是可也譬之醫家先
之薑桂大黃以破其痼疾而後以參苓芝
术以養其元氣則病可去而人可壽醫之
道得矣以風俗為念者用治疾之道治之
則不善之弊庶幾其少瘳矣乎狂斐之言
未達至計進退之則惟命
alt_text:
宜者言之若夫一道德以同俗因奢儉以
示敎是則敦本之論不可無者而規模廣
大綱領宏闊未遽行焉今日之事則當先
於其要者而後及於是可也譬之醫家先
之薑桂大黃以破其痼疾而後以參苓芝
术以養其元氣則病可去而人可壽醫之
道得矣以風俗為念者用治疾之道治之
則不善之弊庶幾其少瘳矣乎狂斐之言
未達至計進退之則惟命
===
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□
punctuated: 宜者言之。若夫一道德以同俗，因奢儉以示教，是則敦本之論不可無者，而規模廣大，綱領宏闊，未遽行焉。今日之事，則當先於其要者，而後及於是可也。譬之醫家，先之薑桂大黃以破其痼疾，而後以參苓芝术以養其元氣，則病可去而人可壽，醫之道得矣。以風俗為念者，用治疾之道治之，則不善之弊庶幾其少瘳矣乎？狂斐之言，未達至計，進退之則，惟命。
translation_en: …speaking of measures appropriate to them. As for unifying moral principles to bring customs into accord, and providing instruction according to prevailing extravagance or frugality, these are indispensable proposals for strengthening the foundations. Yet their scope is vast and their guiding principles far-reaching; they cannot be put into effect immediately. In present circumstances, we should first address the most urgent matters and then proceed to these broader measures. This is comparable to a physician first administering ginger, cinnamon, and rhubarb to overcome a chronic illness, and then using ginseng, poria, lingzhi, and atractylodes to nourish the patient's vital energy. The illness can then be eliminated and the patient's life prolonged: the physician has mastered the proper method. If those concerned with customs treat them as they would an illness, might the harmful practices not be somewhat alleviated? These rash and presumptuous words fall short of the best counsel. Whether they are to be accepted or rejected, I await your command.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄後序
聖天子正位大寶之初適天下開
科取士寔
龍飛盛舉也有司慎重厥事聘儒
紳以專文柄麒濫竿焉嘗考
諸志在昔西南諸郡半隷雲
南後始割為貴州故士之應
===
試者猶附先時有議雲貴設
科法者
孝宗敬皇帝申命折衷定以雲南
三十一人貴州十九人仍合
試之特名其錄為雲貴鄉試
遵
制取擇其文之議論詞氣正者萃
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄後序

聖天子正位大寶之初，適天下開科取士，寔龍飛盛舉也。有司慎重厥事，聘儒紳以專文柄，麒濫竿焉。嘗考諸志，在昔西南諸郡半隷雲南，後始割為貴州，故士之應試者猶附。先時有議雲貴設科法者，孝宗敬皇帝申命折衷，定以雲南三十一人、貴州十九人，仍合試之，特名其錄為雲貴鄉試。遵制取擇其文之議論詞氣正者，萃
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

At the beginning of the sage Son of Heaven’s accession to the imperial throne, examinations were being held throughout the realm to recruit men of talent—a splendid undertaking indeed to mark the dragon’s ascent. The responsible officials treated the matter with care, inviting learned gentlemen to take charge of literary assessment. I, Qi, unworthily joined their ranks.

I have examined the gazetteers: formerly, half the prefectures of the southwest belonged to Yunnan; only later were they separated to form Guizhou. Thus, candidates taking the examination continued to be attached to Yunnan. Earlier, when proposals were made concerning the arrangements for examinations in Yunnan and Guizhou, Emperor Xiaozong Jing issued further orders to settle the matter, fixing the quota at thirty-one men for Yunnan and nineteen for Guizhou, while retaining a joint examination. Its record was specifically entitled the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination. In obedience to the imperial directive, those compositions whose arguments and literary expression were correct were selected and gathered together …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而為録將以
進呈傳諸天下麒謹序之切惟
我
國家取士以科目為正途當時
以科目所出之士為正流士
之所業以六經為正學爾諸
士從正學履正途稱正流其
===
為號大矣盍思所以圖之孔
子曰政者正也行將上春官
對
大廷駸駸嚮用從政有日烏可
不迪于正耶必正心以脩身
正己以率物正其誼而不謀
其利在
punctuated: 而為録，將以進呈，傳諸天下。麒謹序之。切惟我國家取士，以科目為正途；當時以科目所出之士為正流；士之所業，以六經為正學。爾諸士從正學，履正途，稱正流，其為號大矣！盍思所以圖之？孔子曰：「政者，正也。」行將上春官，對大廷，駸駸嚮用，從政有日，烏可不迪于正耶？必正心以脩身，正己以率物，正其誼而不謀其利，在
translation_en: …and compile them into a record, to be respectfully presented to the throne and circulated throughout the realm. I, Qi, respectfully compose this preface. I earnestly reflect that our dynasty takes the examinations as the proper path for recruiting men of talent; the age regards those who emerge through the examinations as the proper stream of scholars; and the Six Classics constitute the orthodox learning that scholars pursue. You scholars follow orthodox learning, tread the proper path, and bear the designation of the proper stream. Weighty indeed is that designation! Why not consider how to live up to it? Confucius said: “To govern is to rectify.” Soon you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites and answer before the imperial court, advancing steadily toward appointment. The day when you take part in government is approaching: how could you fail to walk in rectitude? You must rectify your minds to cultivate yourselves, rectify yourselves to lead others, and uphold what is right without scheming for personal profit. When in…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
朝廷則以正道事
君居民社則以正令善俗其或所
遭不同亦必確乎以正自持
凡意料所不及者吾惟順受
其正焉庶幾不負所學不負
所取不負所稱而有以全天
地之正氣無愧於正人君子
===
之流矣顧不偉歟舎此曲學
以阿世枉道以徇人俾天下
後世指其名而非議之則非
今日主司之所望也自洪武
設科至于今凡數十舉矣毎
科必有錄毎錄必有序毎序
必有說麒無能加敢謂道莫
punctuated: 朝廷則以正道事君，居民社則以正令善俗。其或所遭不同，亦必確乎以正自持。凡意料所不及者，吾惟順受其正焉。庶幾不負所學，不負所取，不負所稱，而有以全天地之正氣，無愧於正人君子之流矣，顧不偉歟？舎此，曲學以阿世，枉道以徇人，俾天下後世指其名而非議之，則非今日主司之所望也。自洪武設科至于今，凡數十舉矣。毎科必有錄，毎錄必有序，毎序必有說。麒無能加，敢謂道莫
translation_en:
…at court, serve the sovereign according to the upright Way; when administering local communities, improve their customs through upright ordinances. Even if the circumstances you encounter differ, you must remain firmly upright in your conduct. Whatever lies beyond your expectations, accept submissively only what properly falls to your lot. Thus you may prove worthy of what you have learned, of your selection, and of the designation you bear, preserving intact the upright vital force of Heaven and Earth and standing without shame among upright men and gentlemen. Would this not be a great achievement? To abandon this, twisting your learning to curry favor with the world and bending the Way to accommodate others, so that people throughout the realm and in later generations point to your names in condemnation—this is not what those presiding over today’s examination hope for.

From the establishment of the examinations in the Hongwu reign until now, several dozen examinations have been held. Every examination must have a record, every record a preface, and every preface something to say. I, Qi, have nothing to add, but venture to say that, as for the Way, nothing …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄕試錄序
皇上登寶位之二年適
龍飛第一科鄕試巡按雲南監察
御史陳天祥謹循舊典諗于
有司禮聘儒紳以專校文而
貴州應試之士例亦附焉時
兩藩奉
===
命內外臣工鎭守太監崔安張誠
右少監孫清總兵官黔國公
沐崑巡撫右副都御史吳文
度右僉都御史王質巡按監
察御史董𨯅朱衮清刑郎中
朱塗皆愼重其事傅等如期
畢至以八月丁丑入院傅與
punctuated:
雲貴鄕試錄序

皇上登寶位之二年，適龍飛第一科鄕試。巡按雲南監察御史陳天祥謹循舊典，諗于有司，禮聘儒紳以專校文，而貴州應試之士例亦附焉。時兩藩奉命內外臣工，鎭守太監崔安、張誠，右少監孫清，總兵官黔國公沐崑，巡撫右副都御史吳文度，右僉都御史王質，巡按監察御史董𨯅、朱衮，清刑郎中朱塗，皆愼重其事。傅等如期畢至，以八月丁丑入院，傅與
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination

The second year after His Majesty ascended the imperial throne coincided with the first Provincial Examination of his reign. Chen Tianxiang, Investigating Censor on a surveillance tour of Yunnan, respectfully followed established precedents and notified the responsible authorities, ceremonially inviting Confucian scholars and gentlemen to take sole charge of evaluating the examination compositions. Candidates from Guizhou were also included, as customary.

At that time, the officials of the inner court and outer administration serving under imperial orders in the two provinces were the Regional Guard Grand Eunuchs Cui An and Zhang Cheng; Junior Director of the Right Sun Qing; Regional Commander Mu Kun, Duke of Qianguo; Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Wu Wendu; Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhi; Investigating Censors on surveillance tours Dong [?] 董𨯅 and Zhu Gun; and Bureau Director Zhu Tu, charged with reviewing criminal cases. All treated this undertaking with great care. Fu and the others all arrived as scheduled and entered the examination compound on the dingchou day of the eighth month. Fu and…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
教諭朱麒為考試官劉謙劉
漢杜誥廖軫程一嘉為同考
試官提調則左布政使熊禄
左參議陳一經監試則副使
李裕中僉事王經而左布政
使任弘按察使劉杲左右參
政沈林馬金孫春副使丁珝
===
陳振朱璣左右參議黎民表
胡拱林鐄僉事朱儀張弘宜
范玶彭程則協恭於外也合
雲貴就試生儒一千二百有
奇皆提學副使彭綱毛科所
擇三試之得士五十人以文
之優者萃而為錄傅僭序之
punctuated:
教諭朱麒為考試官，劉謙、劉漢、杜誥、廖軫、程一嘉為同考試官。提調則左布政使熊禄、左參議陳一經，監試則副使李裕中、僉事王經。而左布政使任弘、按察使劉杲、左右參政沈林、馬金、孫春、副使丁珝、陳振、朱璣、左右參議黎民表、胡拱、林鐄、僉事朱儀、張弘宜、范玶、彭程，則協恭於外也。
合雲貴就試生儒一千二百有奇，皆提學副使彭綱、毛科所擇。三試之，得士五十人。以文之優者萃而為錄，傅僭序之。
translation_en:
…and Instructor Zhu Qi served as Examiners. Liu Qian, Liu Han, Du Gao, Liao Zhen, and Cheng Yijia served as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Xiong Lu and Left Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Yijing. Surveillance Vice Commissioner Li Yuzhong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Jing monitored the examination. Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Ren Hong; Surveillance Commissioner Liu Gao; Left and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners Shen Lin, Ma Jin, and Sun Chun; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Ding Xu, Chen Zhen, and Zhu Ji; Left and Right Assistant Provincial Administration Commissioners Li Minbiao, Hu Gong, and Lin Huang; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhu Yi, Zhang Hongyi, Fan Ping, and Peng Cheng respectfully cooperated in supporting the proceedings outside the examination compound.
Altogether, more than twelve hundred students from Yunnan and Guizhou presented themselves for examination, all selected by Education Intendants Peng Gang and Mao Ke. After three examination sessions, fifty men were selected. The finest of their compositions were gathered into this record, for which I, Fu, have presumed to write a preface.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
竊惟世運一新文運隨之故
曰八音與政通而文章與時
高下况
國家景運重開制度文為翕張
變化天下萬國耳震霆之洪
音目太陽之赫曜莫不動心
駭目手舞足蹈以鼓舞維新
===
之政而文章之在世表裏元
化感動轉旋之機尤莫先焉
與試之士固皆
列聖培養之素而
皇上又作新之譬諸稼焉耕耘盡
人之力雨露得天之功而收
穫之際風日清美飽滿成就
punctuated: 竊惟世運一新，文運隨之。故曰：「八音與政通，而文章與時高下。」况國家景運重開，制度文為翕張變化，天下萬國耳震霆之洪音，目太陽之赫曜，莫不動心駭目，手舞足蹈，以鼓舞維新之政。而文章之在世，表裏元化，感動轉旋之機，尤莫先焉。與試之士，固皆列聖培養之素，而皇上又作新之。譬諸稼焉，耕耘盡人之力，雨露得天之功，而收穫之際，風日清美，飽滿成就
translation_en:
I humbly consider that when the fortunes of the age are renewed, those of letters follow. Thus it is said: “The eight musical timbres communicate with government, and literary composition rises and falls with the times.” How much more is this so now, when our state's glorious fortunes have opened anew, and its institutions and cultural endeavors unfold and undergo transformation! Throughout the realm and the myriad countries, all hear the mighty peal of thunder and behold the sun's brilliant radiance. None remain unmoved in heart or undazzled in sight; they wave their hands and stamp their feet in joy, celebrating the renewed government. As for literary composition in the world, it works both inwardly and outwardly with the primal processes of transformation; among the means of stirring hearts and turning the course of affairs, none takes precedence over it.

The candidates taking this examination have all long been nurtured by the successive sage emperors, and now His Majesty renews them once more. To compare them to crops: plowing and weeding exhaust human effort, while rain and dew confer Heaven's benefits. When harvest comes, the breeze and sunlight are clear and lovely, and the grain grows full and ripens …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無淫霖爛之疾風化之宜乎
得美稼矣傅忝司文柄凡諸
士之文悉得過目佳者類亦
不一或淵奧蒼古或宏博富
麗或平淡爾雅或舂容紆徐
或簡勁奇偉光彩絢爛精神
流動其盛矣哉夫以雲貴僻
===
地而學者之造詣如此非世
運一新之會人自磨濯何以
致之雖然諸士負文藝而至
主司懸文鑑以臨之固一以
文事相與也科舉之設止文
而已乎盖將因文求人而措
之用者也自德行興賢高不
punctuated:
無淫霖爛之、疾風化之，宜乎得美稼矣。傅忝司文柄，凡諸士之文，悉得過目。佳者類亦不一：或淵奧蒼古，或宏博富麗，或平淡爾雅，或舂容紆徐，或簡勁奇偉，光彩絢爛，精神流動，其盛矣哉！夫以雲貴僻地，而學者之造詣如此，非世運一新之會，人自磨濯，何以致之？

雖然，諸士負文藝而至，主司懸文鑑以臨之，固一以文事相與也。科舉之設，止文而已乎？盖將因文求人而措之用者也。自德行興賢，高不
translation_en:
…with no excessive rains to rot it or violent winds to spoil it [?], it is fitting that a fine crop should be obtained. I, Fu, unworthily entrusted with authority over literary assessment, have had the opportunity to read all the candidates’ compositions. The excellent ones are of several kinds: some profound and archaically vigorous; some expansive, learned, rich, and splendid; some plain and classically elegant; some measured and unhurried; and some concise, forceful, extraordinary, and imposing. Their brilliance is dazzling, their spirit flows freely—how flourishing they are! That scholars in such remote places as Yunnan and Guizhou should attain this level: how could this have come about unless, at a time when the fortunes of the age were renewed, each had refined and purified himself?

Nevertheless, the candidates arrive bearing their literary accomplishments, and the examiners confront them with the mirror of literary judgment held aloft. Their dealings are indeed conducted entirely through writing. But were the civil-service examinations established merely for writing? Surely the intention is to seek men through their writing and put them to use. Since promoting worthy men on the basis of virtuous conduct is too lofty to…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
可考射御選士卑不足行於
是後世不能不設科求之其
為制莫盛於唐宋若韓柳之
文章韓范之功業周程張朱
之道學率由是而進者科目
得人盖不誣也我
國家右文崇儒遠過前代自洪
===
武永樂以来所得魁傑命世
之英視前賢無讓者不可悉
數科目之盛可謂極矣諸士
與登鄉書其陟於有位可待
尚期近追
當代之英遠繼往古之哲為科
目之光以無負
punctuated: 可考，射御選士卑不足行，於是後世不能不設科求之。其為制，莫盛於唐宋。若韓柳之文章、韓范之功業、周程張朱之道學，率由是而進者，科目得人，盖不誣也。我國家右文崇儒，遠過前代。自洪武永樂以来，所得魁傑命世之英，視前賢無讓者，不可悉數。科目之盛，可謂極矣。諸士與登鄉書，其陟於有位可待。尚期近追當代之英，遠繼往古之哲，為科目之光，以無負
translation_en:
…could not be assessed, while selecting men through archery and charioteering was too lowly to be practicable. Thus later ages could not but establish examinations to seek worthy men. This institution flourished most under the Tang and Song. Men distinguished by literary achievement, such as Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan; by meritorious service, such as Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan; and by Learning of the Way, such as Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, generally advanced through this route. The claim that the examinations obtained worthy men is indeed no falsehood.

Our dynasty esteems letters and honors Confucian learning, far surpassing earlier ages. Since the Hongwu and Yongle reigns, the outstanding men it has obtained—talents born to distinguish their age, who bear comparison with former worthies without yielding to them—are too numerous to recount. The flourishing of the examinations may be said to have reached its height. You gentlemen have gained places on the provincial register of successful candidates, and your advancement to official positions may be anticipated. We further hope that you will emulate the outstanding men of the present age and carry forward the legacy of the sages of antiquity, bringing honor to the examinations and thereby not disappointing…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
龍飛第一鄉試之選斯為得之
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正
王傳謹序
punctuated:
龍飛第一鄉試之選，斯為得之。
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正王傳謹序。
translation_en:
…the selection made at the first Provincial Examination following His Majesty’s accession; only thus will its purpose be fulfilled.
Respectfully prefaced by Wang Chuan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region (Zhili).

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
正德二年雲貴鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史陳天祥〔元吉武功左衛籍直隸吳江縣人丙辰進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使熊禄〔曰貴江西進賢縣人戊戌進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參議陳一經〔宗文四川成都後衛人甲辰進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司副使李裕中〔容正四川資陽縣人丁未進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事王經〔文濟□□山陰縣人庚戌進士〕
===
考試官
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正王傅〔希說廣東番禺縣人壬子貢士〕
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭朱麒〔汝祥福建懷安縣人丙午貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭劉謙〔益之山東濱州人己酉貢士〕
四川重慶府榮昌縣儒學教諭劉漢〔天章湖廣麻城縣人戊午貢士〕
順天府薊州豐潤縣儒學教諭杜誥〔汝欽山東即墨縣人辛酉貢士〕
浙江處州府雲和縣儒學教諭廖軫〔鍾宿江西崇仁縣人戊午貢士〕
直隸寧國府宣城縣儒學教諭程嘉〔懋中福建莆田縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
正德二年雲貴鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按雲南監察御史陳天祥〔元吉，武功左衛籍，直隸吳江縣人，丙辰進士〕。

提調官：
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使熊禄〔曰貴，江西進賢縣人，戊戌進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參議陳一經〔宗文，四川成都後衛人，甲辰進士〕。

監試官：
雲南等處提刑按察司副使李裕中〔容正，四川資陽縣人，丁未進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事王經〔文濟，□□山陰縣人，庚戌進士〕。

考試官：
直隸揚州府泰州儒學學正王傅〔希說，廣東番禺縣人，壬子貢士〕。
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭朱麒〔汝祥，福建懷安縣人，丙午貢士〕。

同考試官：
河南開封府祥符縣儒學教諭劉謙〔益之，山東濱州人，己酉貢士〕。
四川重慶府榮昌縣儒學教諭劉漢〔天章，湖廣麻城縣人，戊午貢士〕。
順天府薊州豐潤縣儒學教諭杜誥〔汝欽，山東即墨縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
浙江處州府雲和縣儒學教諭廖軫〔鍾宿，江西崇仁縣人，戊午貢士〕。
直隸寧國府宣城縣儒學教諭程嘉〔懋中，福建莆田縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination, second year of Zhengde (1507).

Supervising Official:
Chen Tianxiang, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Yunnan, courtesy name Yuanji, was registered in the Wugong Left Guard and was a native of Wujiang County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the bingchen year.

Proctors:
Xiong Lu, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, courtesy name Yuegui, was a native of Jinxian County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuxu year.
Chen Yijing, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Yunnan, courtesy name Zongwen, was from the Chengdu Rear Guard, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.

Examination Monitors:
Li Yuzhong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, courtesy name Rongzheng, was a native of Ziyang County, Sichuan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.
Wang Jing, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Yunnan, courtesy name Wenji, was a native of Shanyin County, in an illegible region [□□]. He became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.

Examiners:
Wang Fu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Xishuo, was a native of Panyu County, Guangdong. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renzi year.
Zhu Qi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Ruxiang, was a native of Huai'an County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.

Associate Examiners:
Liu Qian, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xiangfu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Binzhou, Shandong. He was a tribute scholar of the jiyou year.
Liu Han, Instructor in the Confucian School of Rongchang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, courtesy name Tianzhang, was a native of Macheng County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Du Gao, Instructor in the Confucian School of Fengrun County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture, courtesy name Ruqin, was a native of Jimo County, Shandong. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.
Liao Zhen, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yunhe County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Zhongsu, was a native of Chongren County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Cheng Jia, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Maozhong, was a native of Putian County, Fujian. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
印卷官
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事陳鎰〔用之湖廣臨武縣人吏員〕
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事袁銳〔廷用四川成都中衛人監生〕
收掌試卷官
雲南府知府葉元〔本貞江西貴溪縣人甲午貢士〕
尋甸軍民府知府李逵〔士行直隸固安縣人丙辰進士〕
受卷官
大理府同知張壇〔主器福建龍溪縣人丁酉貢士〕
楚雄府同知曾顯〔克達江西泰和縣人丁酉貢士〕
===
彌封官
鶴慶軍民府同知楊金〔時重四川左護衛人丙午貢士〕
臨安府通判趙繼宗〔叔敬浙江慈谿縣人庚戌進士〕
澂江府通判晁必登〔汝吉四川宜賓縣人庚戌進士〕
謄錄官
景東府通判劉瑞〔世吉河南衛輝守禦所人壬子貢士〕
順寧府通判韓奎〔文東江西永豐縣人丙午貢士〕
對讀官
曲靖軍民府馬龍州知州陳亮〔志明直隸廣德州人戊戌進士〕
punctuated:
印卷官
雲南等處承宣布政使司經歷司都事陳鎰〔用之，湖廣臨武縣人，吏員〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司經歷司知事袁銳〔廷用，四川成都中衛人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官
雲南府知府葉元〔本貞，江西貴溪縣人，甲午貢士〕。
尋甸軍民府知府李逵〔士行，直隸固安縣人，丙辰進士〕。

受卷官
大理府同知張壇〔主器，福建龍溪縣人，丁酉貢士〕。
楚雄府同知曾顯〔克達，江西泰和縣人，丁酉貢士〕。

彌封官
鶴慶軍民府同知楊金〔時重，四川左護衛人，丙午貢士〕。
臨安府通判趙繼宗〔叔敬，浙江慈谿縣人，庚戌進士〕。
澂江府通判晁必登〔汝吉，四川宜賓縣人，庚戌進士〕。

謄錄官
景東府通判劉瑞〔世吉，河南衛輝守禦所人，壬子貢士〕。
順寧府通判韓奎〔文東，江西永豐縣人，丙午貢士〕。

對讀官
曲靖軍民府馬龍州知州陳亮〔志明，直隸廣德州人，戊戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Officials for Printing Examination Papers
Chen Yi, Chief Clerk in the Registry of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Yongzhi, was from Linwu County, Huguang, and entered service as a clerk.
Yuan Rui, Clerk in the Registry of the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Tingyong, was from Chengdu Central Guard, Sichuan, and was an Imperial University student.
