title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
今吾於人也聽其言而觀其行
德者本也財者末也
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
易
大君之宜吉
揚于王庭孚號有厲告自邑不利即戎
盛德大業至矣哉
===
天地設位聖人成能
書
皐陶曰都慎厥身修思永惇叙九族庶明
勵翼邇可遠在茲禹拜昌言曰俞皐陶
曰都在知人在安民禹曰吁咸若時惟
帝其難之
俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一哉王心
曰聖時風若
太保率西方諸侯入應門左畢公率東方
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
今吾於人也，聽其言而觀其行。
德者，本也；財者，末也。
集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。

易
大君之宜，吉。
揚于王庭，孚號有厲，告自邑，不利即戎。
盛德大業，至矣哉！
天地設位，聖人成能。

書
皐陶曰：「都！慎厥身修，思永，惇叙九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠，在茲。」禹拜昌言，曰：「俞！」皐陶曰：「都！在知人，在安民。」禹曰：「吁！咸若時，惟帝其難之。」
俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」
曰：「聖，時風若。」
太保率西方諸侯入應門左，畢公率東方
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“Now, in judging people, I listen to their words and observe their conduct.”
“Virtue is the root; wealth is the branches.”
“To bring together the complete achievement is to begin with the sounding of bronze bells and conclude with the resonance of jade chimes.”

Book of Changes
“What befits a great ruler: auspicious.”
“Proclaim it in the royal court; cry out sincerely that there is danger. Make the announcement from your own city. It is not advantageous to resort to arms.”
“Abundant virtue and great achievement—how consummate they are!”
“Heaven and earth establish their positions; the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment.”

Book of Documents
“Gao Yao said: ‘Ah! Be vigilant in cultivating yourself; think of the long term; bring the nine degrees of kinship into harmonious order through generosity. Let the many worthy men diligently assist you. From those nearby, your influence can reach those far away: herein lies the way.’ Yu bowed in acknowledgment of these excellent words and said: ‘Yes!’ Gao Yao said: ‘Ah! It lies in understanding people and bringing peace to the people.’ Yu said: ‘Ah! To accomplish all this—even the emperor would find it difficult.’”
“Cause the myriad families all to say: ‘How great are the king’s words!’ And again: ‘How single-minded is the king’s heart!’”
“It is said: ‘Sageliness: seasonable winds respond in accord.’”
“The Grand Guardian led the regional lords of the west into the left side of the Ying Gate; the Duke of Bi led those of the east …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
諸侯入應門右皆布乘黄朱賓稱奉圭
兼幣曰一二臣衛敢執壤奠皆再拜稽
首
詩
其儀一兮心如結兮
樂只君子天子葵之
其胤維何天被爾禄君子萬年景命有僕
其僕維何釐爾女士釐爾女士從以孫
子
===
令妻壽母宜大夫庶士邦國是有
春秋
元年〔隱公〕
無駭帥師入極〔隱公二年〕季孫行父如齊
〔宣公元年〕晉侯使士匄來聘〔襄公八年〕
叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋
向戌衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭
罕虎許人曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕仲孫何
忌會晉韓不信齊高張宋仲幾衛世叔
punctuated:
諸侯入應門右，皆布乘黄朱。賓稱奉圭兼幣，曰：「一二臣衛，敢執壤奠。」皆再拜稽首。

詩
其儀一兮，心如結兮。
樂只君子，天子葵之。
其胤維何？天被爾禄。君子萬年，景命有僕。其僕維何？釐爾女士。釐爾女士，從以孫子。
令妻壽母，宜大夫庶士，邦國是有。

春秋
元年〔隱公〕。
無駭帥師入極〔隱公二年〕。季孫行父如齊〔宣公元年〕。晉侯使士匄來聘〔襄公八年〕。
叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕。仲孫何忌會晉韓不信、齊高張、宋仲幾、衛世叔
translation_en:
…the regional lords entered on the right of the Ying Gate. All arrayed teams of four yellow horses with red manes. The guests raised and presented jade tablets together with silk offerings, saying: “We, your servants who guard the realm, venture to present the offerings of our lands.” All bowed twice and knocked their heads to the ground.

Book of Odes
His bearing is constant; his heart is as firmly bound as a knot.
Joyful is the noble lord; the Son of Heaven appraises him.
What is his continuing inheritance? Heaven bestows its blessings upon you. May the noble lord live ten thousand years; may the great mandate abide with him. How does it abide with him? By granting you a virtuous wife. By granting you a virtuous wife, followed by grandchildren and sons.
He brings honor to his wife and long life to his mother; he acts fittingly toward the grandees and the many officers, and holds possession of his state.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The first year〔of Duke Yin〕.
Wuhai led an army into Ji〔the second year of Duke Yin〕. Jisun Xingfu went to Qi〔the first year of Duke Xuan〕. The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a mission of courteous inquiry to our court〔the eighth year of Duke Xiang〕.
Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao〔the first year of Duke Zhao〕. Zhongsun Heji met with Han Buxin of Jin, Gao Zhang of Qi, Zhong Ji of Song, and Shishu of Wei…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
申鄭國參曹人莒人薛人杞人小邾人
城成周〔昭公三十二年〕
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭同
盟于戲〔襄公九年〕
用田賦〔哀公十二年〕
禮記
臨財毋苟得臨難毋苟免
以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟以和夫婦
===
發號出令而民說謂之和
其寬裕有如此者儒有內稱不辟親外舉
不辟怨
第貳場
論
仁義人主之術
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元〕
〔元年〕
punctuated:
申、鄭國參、曹人、莒人、薛人、杞人、小邾人城成周。〔昭公三十二年〕
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕
用田賦。〔哀公十二年〕
禮記
臨財毋苟得，臨難毋苟免。
以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以和夫婦。
發號出令而民說，謂之和。
其寬裕有如此者。儒有內稱不辟親，外舉不辟怨。
第貳場
論
仁義，人主之術。
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔。〔建元〕〔元年〕
translation_en:
…Shen, Guo Can of Zheng, and men of Cao, Ju, Xue, Qi, and Lesser Zhu fortified Chengzhou. 〔Thirty-second year of Duke Zhao〕
The duke joined the marquis of Jin, the duke of Song, the marquis of Wei, the earl of Cao, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, the viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. They jointly entered into a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕
A levy on farmland was instituted. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Ai〕
Record of Rites
When faced with wealth, do not seek to acquire it improperly; when faced with danger, do not seek to escape it improperly.
Thereby to set right the relationship between ruler and minister, deepen affection between father and son, foster amity between brothers, and bring harmony between husband and wife.
When proclamations and commands are issued and the people are pleased, this is called harmony.
Such is his breadth of mind and generosity. In recommending people from within his own circle, a Confucian scholar does not exclude relatives; in recommending those from outside it, he does not exclude enemies.
Second Session
Discourse
Benevolence and righteousness are the ruler’s art.
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty calling for the recommendation of men who are worthy and good, upright and correct, and capable of speaking frankly and remonstrating unreservedly. 〔Jianyuan〕〔First year〕

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬纂修
孝宗敬皇帝實錄成
進呈表
判語〔五條〕
講讀律令
賦役不均
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
干名犯義
===
第叁場
策五道
問帝王之興宜有一代之文以為教於天
下後世是之謂君師之道然天之於人
不能使之盡得其全而無少不足者大
哉帝堯君哉帝舜二典之載特史臣所
紀之詞堯舜未嘗發於精神心術以為
文也若六經之文孔子以是為萬代事
punctuated:
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬纂修孝宗敬皇帝實錄成進呈表。
判語〔五條〕：講讀律令、賦役不均、服舍違式、優恤軍屬、干名犯義。
第叁場
策五道
問：帝王之興，宜有一代之文，以為教於天下後世，是之謂君師之道。然天之於人，不能使之盡得其全而無少不足者。大哉帝堯，君哉帝舜，二典之載，特史臣所紀之詞。堯舜未嘗發於精神心術以為文也。若六經之文，孔子以是為萬代事
translation_en:
Compose a simulated Tang edict appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor. 〔Third year of Zhenguan〕
Compose a simulated memorial presenting the completed Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong Jing.
Legal judgments 〔five topics〕: Lecturing on and reading the statutes and ordinances; unequal assessment of taxes and labor services; clothing and dwellings contravening prescribed standards; preferential relief for military dependents; offending familial hierarchy and violating moral duty.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: When emperors and kings arise, they ought to produce writings for their age to instruct all under Heaven and later generations. This is what is called the Way of the ruler and teacher. Yet Heaven cannot enable every person to attain completeness without the slightest deficiency. “Great indeed was Emperor Yao!” “A true ruler was Emperor Shun!” What is recorded in the two Canons consists only of words set down by the court historians. Yao and Shun never gave expression to their spiritual powers and the workings of their minds in writings of their own. As for the writings of the Six Classics, Confucius made these his undertaking for all ages…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
業堯舜所不得與者而君師之位孔子
未之有焉造化之不足於人者固如是
乎我
太祖高皇帝有大誥三編
太宗文皇帝有為善陰隲孝順事實二書
宣宗章皇帝有五倫書
列聖皆以天地之德帝王之位奎璧之文齊堯
舜而兼孔子矣天之所以全其賦畀者
亦有可知者歟生斯世為斯民居治教
===
之中於
聖製之大固宜服膺也試舉宏綱大要一二與
諸生論之
大誥之布至於再三屢出而不厭者其故何
居丁寧而不已者其指安在其間為條
凡幾何者為始何者為終可得言歟
為善陰隲有治獄而能活人者何人有用兵
而能活人者何人昆蟲之活細事也何
以亦獲天之報瓜菓之設小善也何以
punctuated:
業，堯舜所不得與者，而君師之位，孔子未之有焉。造化之不足於人者，固如是乎？我太祖高皇帝有《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝有《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》二書，宣宗章皇帝有《五倫書》。列聖皆以天地之德、帝王之位、奎璧之文，齊堯舜而兼孔子矣。天之所以全其賦畀者，亦有可知者歟？生斯世，為斯民，居治教之中，於聖製之大，固宜服膺也。試舉宏綱大要一二，與諸生論之。
《大誥》之布，至於再三，屢出而不厭者，其故何居？丁寧而不已者，其指安在？其間為條凡幾？何者為始？何者為終？可得言歟？
《為善陰隲》有治獄而能活人者，何人？有用兵而能活人者，何人？昆蟲之活，細事也，何以亦獲天之報？瓜菓之設，小善也，何以
translation_en:
…an enduring achievement in which Yao and Shun could have no share; yet Confucius never held the position of sovereign and teacher. Is this indeed how the workings of creation leave human beings incomplete? Our Emperor Taizu Gao produced the Grand Pronouncements in three compilations; Emperor Taizong Wen produced the two books Doing Good and Hidden Recompense and True Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience; and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang produced the Book of the Five Human Relationships. All these sage emperors, possessing the virtue of Heaven and Earth, the station of emperors, and literary brilliance like the Kui and Bi constellations, equaled Yao and Shun while also combining in themselves the qualities of Confucius. Can we discern how Heaven bestowed its gifts upon them in their fullness? Born in this age, numbered among its people, and living under its government and instruction, we should surely take to heart the greatness of these imperial compositions. Let us select one or two of their broad principles and essential points for discussion with you candidates.
The Grand Pronouncements were promulgated a second and a third time. Why were they issued repeatedly without wearying of the task? What was the intent of their unceasing admonitions? How many articles do they contain in all? Which comes first, and which last? Can you explain?
In Doing Good and Hidden Recompense, who was able to save lives when adjudicating criminal cases? Who was able to save lives when conducting military operations? Saving insects is a trifling matter: why did it nevertheless receive Heaven’s recompense? Providing melons and fruit is a small act of goodness: why…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
亦獲福之隆
孝順事實孰為帝王之孝孰為公卿之孝孝
一也而何以有孝忠孝義之異又何以
有孝友孝節之殊
五倫書所載君臣之倫何其詳父子兄弟夫
婦之倫何其略堯舜禹湯君之聖也謙
德之所載無堯節儉之所載無舜豈舜
不能儉而堯不能謙乎叙君道臣道之
善行為類各四十有八其間亦各有序
===
乎否也
三誥三書有司者懼吾人莫不飲食鮮能知
味也故於秋闈發之諸生試鋪張而條
答焉則與凡民異矣
問封建之制古有之矣肇於何時盛於何
代何為而國增益多何為而國減復少
秦罷侯置守廢封建而為郡縣後世論
封建者惟秦之罪然自漢以来封建之
行何代無之豈秦之所廢者果非此乎
punctuated:
亦獲福之隆？
《孝順事實》，孰為帝王之孝？孰為公卿之孝？孝一也，而何以有孝忠、孝義之異？又何以有孝友、孝節之殊？
《五倫書》所載，君臣之倫何其詳，父子、兄弟、夫婦之倫何其略？堯舜禹湯，君之聖也，謙德之所載無堯，節儉之所載無舜，豈舜不能儉而堯不能謙乎？叙君道、臣道之善行，為類各四十有八，其間亦各有序乎？否也？
三誥三書，有司者懼吾人莫不飲食，鮮能知味也，故於秋闈發之。諸生試鋪張而條答焉，則與凡民異矣。
問：封建之制，古有之矣。肇於何時？盛於何代？何為而國增益多？何為而國減復少？秦罷侯置守，廢封建而為郡縣。後世論封建者，惟秦之罪。然自漢以来，封建之行，何代無之？豈秦之所廢者果非此乎？
translation_en:
…also receive such abundant blessings?
In Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), which examples illustrate the filial piety of emperors and kings, and which that of dukes and high ministers? Filial piety is one virtue: why, then, are there distinctions between filial piety joined with loyalty and filial piety joined with righteousness? Why, too, are there differences between filial piety joined with fraternal affection and filial piety joined with steadfast integrity?
In the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), why is the relationship between ruler and minister treated in such detail, while those between father and son, brothers, and husband and wife are treated so briefly? Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang were sage rulers. Yet the accounts of humility do not include Yao, and those of frugality do not include Shun. Could it be that Shun was incapable of frugality and Yao incapable of humility? The good deeds illustrating the way of rulers and the way of ministers are arranged in forty-eight categories each. Is there also an order within each of these, or not?
Concerning the three Grand Pronouncements and the three books, the responsible officials fear that, although all of us eat and drink, few can discern the flavor. They have therefore raised these matters in the autumn Provincial Examination. Let you candidates expound upon them and answer point by point; you will thereby distinguish yourselves from the common people.
Question: The system of enfeoffment existed in antiquity. When did it originate, and in which age did it flourish? What caused the states to increase and become more numerous? What caused them to diminish and become fewer again? Qin abolished the lords and appointed commandery governors, replacing enfeoffment with commanderies and counties. Those of later ages who discuss enfeoffment lay the blame solely on Qin. Yet from the Han onward, in what dynasty was enfeoffment not practiced? Could it be that what Qin abolished was actually something other than this?

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
我
太祖高皇帝立國廟謨酌古準今萬代無弊郡
縣之制固在而封建之制亦未嘗無甞
竊論之有封建之名而非前代封建之
實者天下之
宗室是也有封建之實而非前代封建之名
者四裔之酋長是也其間立法之善有
可得而言歟三代以上之封建不可復
矣而經生學士尚有是古之論盖以前
===
人甲可乙否迄無定說姑舉一二大儒
言之有曰公天下之端自秦始有曰封
建者公天下之大端大本也有曰封建
者爭之端亂之始也有曰必如是然後
能公天下以為心而達君臣之義於天
下數家之說孰得孰失古之封建其果
可行乎不可行乎請折衷以巳見用袪
萬世之疑
問古之為民者四士農工商是也兵為國
punctuated:
我太祖高皇帝立國，廟謨酌古準今，萬代無弊。郡縣之制固在，而封建之制亦未嘗無。甞竊論之：有封建之名而非前代封建之實者，天下之宗室是也；有封建之實而非前代封建之名者，四裔之酋長是也。其間立法之善，有可得而言歟？三代以上之封建不可復矣，而經生學士尚有是古之論。盖以前人甲可乙否，迄無定說。姑舉一二大儒言之：有曰：「公天下之端自秦始。」有曰：「封建者，公天下之大端大本也。」有曰：「封建者，爭之端，亂之始也。」有曰：「必如是，然後能公天下以為心，而達君臣之義於天下。」數家之說，孰得孰失？古之封建，其果可行乎？不可行乎？請折衷以巳見，用袪萬世之疑。
問：古之為民者四，士農工商是也。兵為國
translation_en:
When our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty, his plans for governing weighed ancient precedents against present circumstances, leaving no defects for ten thousand generations. The system of commanderies and counties certainly exists, yet the system of enfeoffment has never been absent either. I have ventured to consider this: those who possess the name of enfeoffment but not the substance of enfeoffment under earlier dynasties are the members of the imperial clan throughout the realm; those who possess its substance but not its name under earlier dynasties are the chieftains of the four border regions. Can the merits of the institutions established in these cases be explained? The enfeoffment of the Three Dynasties and earlier cannot be restored, yet students of the classics and learned men still argue that antiquity was right. This is because, among earlier thinkers, one approved and another rejected it, and no settled judgment has yet emerged. Let us cite a few great Confucian scholars. One said: “The beginning of making All under Heaven public dates from Qin.” Another said: “Enfeoffment is the great starting point and fundamental basis for making All under Heaven public.” Another said: “Enfeoffment is the source of contention and the beginning of disorder.” Another said: “Only in this way can one take making All under Heaven public as one’s guiding intention and extend the proper relationship between ruler and minister throughout the realm.” Among these thinkers’ views, which are right and which are wrong? Can ancient enfeoffment actually be put into practice, or can it not? Please adjudicate these views according to your own judgment, thereby dispelling the doubts of all ages.
Question: In antiquity, the people comprised four groups: scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants. Military affairs, for the state, are…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之大事自黃虞以来盖有之而周制益
詳然稱民止四不及於兵何歟管子内
政有士農之郷有工商之郷而士非四
民之士也抑不知四民之士將何以置
之歟其所以為兵亦有可考歟易象曰
君子辯上下定民志程子曰古之時公
卿大夫稱其德農工商賈勤其事而後
民志定公卿大夫即士之流也志定則
安其分而外無所慕各事其業而他無
===
所遷然則舜耕歷山伊尹耕有莘釋耒
耜而致時雍之化去泥塗而任天下之
重果士為農乎抑農為士乎傅說舉於
版築膠鬲舉於魚塩果真工乎果真商
乎是民志未見其為定也程子之言無
乃不足信歟三代以降制不如古隷尺
籍者遍於中土躬甲胄者盈於疆場論
後世之民者亦宜如古所謂士農工商
而不及於兵可乎古之制果盡善否歟
punctuated: 之大事，自黃虞以来盖有之，而周制益詳。然稱民止四，不及於兵，何歟？管子内政有士農之郷，有工商之郷，而士非四民之士也。抑不知四民之士，將何以置之歟？其所以為兵，亦有可考歟？易象曰：「君子辯上下，定民志。」程子曰：「古之時，公卿大夫稱其德，農工商賈勤其事，而後民志定。」公卿大夫即士之流也。志定則安其分，而外無所慕，各事其業，而他無所遷。然則舜耕歷山，伊尹耕有莘，釋耒耜而致時雍之化，去泥塗而任天下之重，果士為農乎？抑農為士乎？傅說舉於版築，膠鬲舉於魚塩，果真工乎？果真商乎？是民志未見其為定也。程子之言，無乃不足信歟？三代以降，制不如古，隷尺籍者遍於中土，躬甲胄者盈於疆場。論後世之民者，亦宜如古所謂士農工商，而不及於兵，可乎？古之制果盡善否歟？
translation_en:
…a great affair of the state, warfare presumably existed from the time of Huangdi and Shun, and its institutions became more detailed under the Zhou. Yet the people were classified into only four groups, without including soldiers. Why was this? In Guanzi’s arrangements for internal government, there were townships for soldiers and farmers and townships for artisans and merchants; but the shi here were not the shi, or scholars, of the four categories of people. Where, then, were the scholars of those four categories to be placed? Can the way soldiers were organized also be ascertained?

The Image commentary of the Book of Changes says: “The gentleman distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people’s aspirations.” Master Cheng says: “In ancient times, dukes, ministers, and grand masters held positions commensurate with their virtue, while farmers, artisans, and merchants diligently pursued their occupations; only then were the people’s aspirations settled.” Dukes, ministers, and grand masters belonged to the scholarly class. Once their aspirations were settled, people were content with their allotted stations and coveted nothing beyond them; each pursued his own occupation without turning to another.

Yet Shun ploughed at Lishan, and Yi Yin ploughed at Youshen. They laid aside their ploughs and brought about a transformation toward universal harmony; they left the muddy fields and assumed responsibility for all under Heaven. Were these truly scholars working as farmers, or farmers becoming scholars? Fu Yue was raised to office from building rammed-earth walls, and Jiao Ge from the fish and salt trade. Was one really an artisan, and the other really a merchant? In these cases, the people’s aspirations do not appear to have been settled. Might Master Cheng’s words, then, be unworthy of belief?

Since the Three Dynasties, institutions have differed from those of antiquity. Men enrolled in military registers are found throughout the central lands, and men clad in armor and helmets fill the frontier battlefields. When discussing the people of later ages, is it permissible likewise to follow the ancient categories of scholars, farmers, artisans, and merchants, without including soldiers? Were the institutions of antiquity indeed good in every respect?

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
如其善亦可行於今歟今之為制亦有
近似者歟諸士抱藝而來其於古今世
變展轉於中素矣其悉陳之母讓
問天地間財止有此數不在於官則在於
民今天下承平日久海內奠安宜乎公
私具足積於無用可也夫何地之所斂
或倍其常而用之所需反乏於舊將以
為在官耶則天下諸省倉廩罕見有紅
腐之積府庫未聞有貫朽之財小有用
===
費輒憂匱乏甚至
內帑之儲戶部之積欲求充盛或亦少之是
不在官也將以為在民耶則四方之民
耕桑多不能為衣食之資俯仰多不遂
事育之願一遇凶荒相率流移甚至膏
腴之地豐稔之年欲求飽煖亦或難之
是又不在民也然所以致此者其故何
由玆欲使國富於上民給於下其處之
必有要而行之必有本焉請著于篇以
punctuated:
如其善，亦可行於今歟？今之為制，亦有近似者歟？諸士抱藝而來，其於古今世變，展轉於中素矣。其悉陳之，母讓。

問：天地間財止有此數，不在於官，則在於民。今天下承平日久，海內奠安，宜乎公私具足，積於無用可也。夫何地之所斂，或倍其常，而用之所需，反乏於舊？將以為在官耶？則天下諸省倉廩，罕見有紅腐之積；府庫，未聞有貫朽之財。小有用費，輒憂匱乏。甚至內帑之儲、戶部之積，欲求充盛，或亦少之。是不在官也。將以為在民耶？則四方之民，耕桑多不能為衣食之資，俯仰多不遂事育之願。一遇凶荒，相率流移。甚至膏腴之地、豐稔之年，欲求飽煖，亦或難之。是又不在民也。然所以致此者，其故何由？玆欲使國富於上，民給於下，其處之必有要，而行之必有本焉。請著于篇，以
translation_en:
…If it was good, could it also be put into practice today? Do present institutions have anything resembling it? You candidates have come equipped with your learning and have long pondered the changes in circumstances from antiquity to the present. Set forth your views fully, without holding back.

Question: The wealth between Heaven and Earth amounts to only so much: if it is not held by the government, it must be held by the people. Now that the realm has long enjoyed peace and all within the seas is secure, public and private resources ought to be ample, with surpluses accumulating beyond any need for them. Why, then, do collections from the land sometimes amount to twice the usual levy, while resources available to meet expenditure are even less adequate than before? Shall we suppose that the wealth is held by the government? Yet among the granaries of the provinces throughout the realm, one seldom sees grain accumulated until it reddens and rots; nor does one hear of money held in treasuries until the strings threading the coins decay. Even a small expenditure immediately raises fears of shortage. Indeed, even the reserves of the imperial treasury and the accumulated funds of the Ministry of Revenue may fall short of abundance. Thus the wealth is not held by the government. Shall we suppose that it is held by the people? Yet throughout the land, farming and sericulture often fail to provide the means of clothing and feeding them, and they often cannot fulfill their wish to support their parents and rear their children. At the first encounter with famine, they follow one another into displacement and migration. Even on fertile land and in years of plentiful harvests, obtaining adequate food and warmth may prove difficult. Thus the wealth is not held by the people either. What, then, has brought about this state of affairs? If we now wish to make the state wealthy above and the people adequately provided for below, there must be essential principles for addressing the problem and a foundation for putting them into practice. Please set these out in your essay, so that…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
觀先天下之憂而憂勿謂思出其位
問自古為治者必美教化以善風俗風俗
未善而欲求治者鮮矣以雲貴言之古
為西南夷地我
國家取而郡縣之所以揆文教奮武衛者亦
為詳備固宜與中州等也然而百餘年
来風聲氣習無異於前革故鼎新未收
其效夷民之異言異服者始終莫變盜
賊之肆行劫奪者嵗時無巳貪財賤義
===
之徒自為得計無情健訟之輩轉相効
尤士或有乖庠序之教女或不知行露
之義親戚之恩或至於薄婚姻之黨或
非所宜民俗如此何由而可善耶或者
以為化導之機本於郡縣而郡縣之職
或為流官或為土官土官以予奪之莫
及而或縱肆其欲流官以更代之不常
而或苟簡其政民之望於聊生尤不可
得而况於俗善也臨之以藩臬之司糾
punctuated:
觀先天下之憂而憂，勿謂思出其位。

問：自古為治者，必美教化以善風俗。風俗未善而欲求治者，鮮矣。以雲貴言之，古為西南夷地。我國家取而郡縣之，所以揆文教、奮武衛者，亦為詳備，固宜與中州等也。然而百餘年来，風聲氣習無異於前，革故鼎新未收其效。夷民之異言異服者，始終莫變；盜賊之肆行劫奪者，嵗時無巳；貪財賤義之徒，自為得計；無情健訟之輩，轉相効尤。士或有乖庠序之教，女或不知行露之義，親戚之恩或至於薄，婚姻之黨或非所宜。民俗如此，何由而可善耶？或者以為化導之機，本於郡縣，而郡縣之職，或為流官，或為土官。土官以予奪之莫及，而或縱肆其欲；流官以更代之不常，而或苟簡其政。民之望於聊生，尤不可得，而况於俗善也。臨之以藩臬之司，糾
translation_en:
…to discern your concern for the world’s troubles before others become concerned. Do not say that such deliberation goes beyond your station.

Question: Since antiquity, those who govern have invariably refined moral instruction in order to improve customs. Few have sought good government successfully while customs remained unimproved. Consider Yunnan and Guizhou: in antiquity, these were lands of the southwestern Yi. Our dynasty took possession of them and established prefectures and counties. Its measures for directing civil instruction and strengthening military protection have been comprehensive and thorough; these regions should surely have become equal to the Central Plains. Yet for more than a hundred years, prevailing attitudes and customary practices have remained unchanged, and efforts to replace the old with the new have borne no fruit. The Yi people’s distinctive speech and dress have remained unchanged throughout. Bandits brazenly plunder year after year without cease. Those who covet wealth and scorn righteousness consider their schemes successful, while those who pursue litigation without just grounds emulate one another’s wrongdoing. Some scholars depart from the teachings of the schools; some women do not understand the moral principles of “Dew on the Path” (Xing lu). Affection among relatives sometimes grows thin, and marriage alliances are sometimes improper. With popular customs in this condition, how can they be improved?

Some hold that the means of moral transformation lie fundamentally with the prefectures and counties. Yet their offices are held either by regularly appointed officials or by native officials. Native officials, beyond the reach of the authorities’ power to grant or withdraw privileges, sometimes indulge their desires without restraint. Regularly appointed officials, because their postings change unpredictably, sometimes administer their jurisdictions perfunctorily. The people cannot even attain their hope of eking out a livelihood; how much less can their customs improve? They are placed under the supervision of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, and subjected to disciplinary scrutiny…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之以憲臺之臣律流官者嚴矣果能惕
其心乎令其朝
覲以觀文明之治清其宗派以杜廕襲之爭而
待土官者亦至矣果能易其轍乎風俗
之所責成者果有在於쫡歟斡旋之機
亦別有其道歟諸生生長쫡邦目擊其
弊更化之術亦必講之審矣明以告我
以觀有用之學
punctuated: 之以憲臺之臣，律流官者嚴矣，果能惕其心乎？令其朝覲，以觀文明之治；清其宗派，以杜廕襲之爭，而待土官者亦至矣，果能易其轍乎？風俗之所責成者，果有在於쫡歟？斡旋之機，亦別有其道歟？諸生生長쫡邦，目擊其弊，更化之術，亦必講之審矣。明以告我，以觀有用之學。
translation_en: …and subject them to correction by officials of the Censorate. The discipline imposed upon officials appointed through the regular bureaucracy is strict indeed, but can it truly make them vigilant at heart? Hereditary native officials are required to attend court audiences so that they may observe enlightened government; their lines of descent are clarified to prevent disputes over hereditary succession. The measures applied to native officials are thus thorough indeed, but can they truly change their ways? Does responsibility for bringing about improvements in customs indeed lie in [?]? Or is there another way to effect such a transformation? You students have grown up in this region [?] and witnessed its abuses firsthand. You must also have carefully considered the means of reform. Explain them clearly to me, so that I may see learning that can be put to use.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
今吾於人也聽其言而觀其行
卓文林
同考試官敎諭劉批因文以觀士子之
實此作體認親切知其非徒言者
考試官敎諭朱批人顧力行何如錄
此以戒時弊不特取其文也
考試官學正王批能言者每無近裏
===
着巳之實此作認得題意取之
聖人之警賢者自言今當求人於實焉盖能言
而行不逮賢者之失也然則今之於人豈可聞
言而信不求觀其行之實哉昔宰予志不能以
帥氣行不能以掩言夫子警之意謂忽於前者
當致謹於今勉於今者斯能善於後彼以言取
人昔焉吾嘗失於易矣過此以往可不知戒乎
以言舉人向焉吾固畧於事矣自是而後可不
知省乎故於今也聞其人之出諸口者一皆務
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

今吾於人也，聽其言而觀其行。

卓文林

同考試官敎諭劉批：因文以觀士子之實，此作體認親切，知其非徒言者。

考試官敎諭朱批：人顧力行何如？錄此以戒時弊，不特取其文也。

考試官學正王批：能言者每無近裏着巳之實，此作認得題意，取之。

聖人之警賢者，自言今當求人於實焉。盖能言而行不逮，賢者之失也。然則今之於人，豈可聞言而信，不求觀其行之實哉？昔宰予志不能以帥氣，行不能以掩言。夫子警之，意謂：忽於前者，當致謹於今；勉於今者，斯能善於後。彼以言取人，昔焉吾嘗失於易矣，過此以往，可不知戒乎？以言舉人，向焉吾固畧於事矣，自是而後，可不知省乎？故於今也，聞其人之出諸口者，一皆務
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Now, in judging people, I listen to their words and observe their conduct.”

Zhuo Wenlin

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Through a candidate’s writing we observe his true substance. This composition shows an intimate and earnest understanding; we can tell that its author is not merely a man of words.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: What matters is how diligently a person puts things into practice. I include this piece to admonish the failings of our time, not merely for its literary merits.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: Those who speak well often lack the substance of inward understanding applied to themselves [?]. This composition grasps the meaning of the topic; I select it.

In admonishing a worthy man, the Sage himself declared that henceforth he must seek the true substance of people. To speak well while falling short in conduct is a failing even of the worthy. How, then, in judging people now, could he trust what he heard them say without seeking to observe the reality of their conduct? Formerly, Zai Yu’s resolve could not command his vital impulses, and his conduct could not measure up to his words. The Master admonished him, meaning: What was treated carelessly before must now be treated with caution; exertion now will make it possible to do well hereafter. In judging people by their words, I once erred by being too ready to accept them. From this point onward, can I fail to take warning? In recommending people on the strength of their words, I formerly paid too little attention to their deeds. Henceforth, can I fail to reflect upon this? Thus now, when I hear what a person utters, all of it expressing an endeavor to …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
學不倦之欲若可與共學矣然有言者不必有
德烏可聞言而遽以為爾耶聆其言之發於聲
者一皆求道不已之論若可與適道矣然能言
者或不能踐胡可聆言而遂以為然耶必省察
斯人於燕居獨處之際果於學也嘗加勤勵之
功歟否則付彼為徒言耳夷考若人於日用常
行之間果於道也能效強勉之力歟否則置彼
為空言耳盖雖聽其言之若是必欲觀其行之
何如固不以人而廢其言亦不以言而信其行
===
聖人言此其警宰予之意何切哉抑論之業精
于勤而荒于嬉也古之聖賢未嘗不以懈惰荒
寧為懼勤勵不息自强夫何宰予以聖門高第
列言語之科顧乃當晝而寢不能如其所言則
是志氣昏惰教無所施宜乎夫子責於前而復
警之以此也雖然豈必因予不逮於行而始聽
言觀行耶特因此立教以警羣弟子使謹於言
而敏於行耳人其可不知勉諸
德者本也財者末也
punctuated:
學不倦之欲，若可與共學矣。然有言者不必有德，烏可聞言而遽以為爾耶？聆其言之發於聲者，一皆求道不已之論，若可與適道矣。然能言者或不能踐，胡可聆言而遂以為然耶？必省察斯人於燕居獨處之際，果於學也嘗加勤勵之功歟？否則付彼為徒言耳。夷考若人於日用常行之間，果於道也能效強勉之力歟？否則置彼為空言耳。盖雖聽其言之若是，必欲觀其行之何如，固不以人而廢其言，亦不以言而信其行。
聖人言此，其警宰予之意何切哉！抑論之，業精于勤而荒于嬉也。古之聖賢未嘗不以懈惰荒寧為懼，勤勵不息自强。夫何宰予以聖門高第，列言語之科，顧乃當晝而寢，不能如其所言，則是志氣昏惰，教無所施。宜乎夫子責於前，而復警之以此也。雖然，豈必因予不逮於行，而始聽言觀行耶？特因此立教，以警羣弟子，使謹於言而敏於行耳。人其可不知勉諸？
德者本也，財者末也。
translation_en:
…a desire to study tirelessly, as though he were someone with whom one could learn. Yet those who have eloquence do not necessarily possess virtue: how could one hear his words and hastily conclude that he was such a person? Listening to what he voices, one hears nothing but talk of ceaselessly seeking the Way, as though he were someone with whom one could advance toward it. Yet those who can speak may be unable to put their words into practice: how could one listen and immediately accept them as true? One must examine this person when he is at leisure and alone: has he really devoted diligent effort to learning? If not, dismiss what he says as mere talk. Examine such a person impartially in his everyday conduct: can he really exert himself strenuously in following the Way? If not, set his words aside as empty talk. Thus, even though one hears him speak in this manner, one must observe what his conduct is like. Certainly one does not reject words because of the person who speaks them; neither does one trust a person's conduct on the strength of his words.
How earnest was the sage's intention to admonish Zai Yu in saying this! Moreover, skill in one's pursuits is perfected through diligence and ruined through frivolity. The sages and worthies of antiquity invariably feared slackness, indolence, dissipation, and ease; they worked diligently and strengthened themselves without cease. How was it, then, that Zai Yu, an outstanding disciple in the sage's school, ranked in the category of eloquence, nevertheless slept during the day and could not live up to his words? This meant that his resolve and spirit were benighted and indolent, leaving instruction no purchase. It was fitting that the Master, having rebuked him earlier, should admonish him again with these words. Even so, could it really have been only because Yu fell short in conduct that the Master began to listen to people's words and observe their actions? He merely used this occasion to establish a teaching that would admonish all his disciples, making them cautious in speech and prompt in action. Can anyone fail to recognize the need for effort?
Virtue is the root; wealth is the branch.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鐵澗
同考試官教諭廖批德為生財之本子
能會意成文是可錄也
考試官教諭朱批講本末意思明白
盖嘗究心於義利之分者
考試官學正王批舎德理財皆非良
圖錄此文以為時政萬一之助
在內之理為所先在外之物為所後盖德乃理
之在內財乃物之在外者也然德必有財而財
===
由德之致其為本末之先後豈不較然矣乎大
學釋平治之經及此意謂欲盡絜矩之道當明
本末之分彼原於天命而衆理咸備具於人心
而萬事由應所以公其好惡不為一己之私度
於物我能同衆人之欲者德也德何以為本邪
盖以德感心則兆民允懷而際天薄海皆歸于
邦域以德行仁則萬姓咸若而遐陬僻壤悉入
于版圖不必以利為事也殆見因天分地何利
之弗獲焉不必以富為心也將見任土作貢何
punctuated:
鐵澗

同考試官教諭廖批：德為生財之本，子能會意成文，是可錄也。

考試官教諭朱批：講本末意思明白，盖嘗究心於義利之分者。

考試官學正王批：舎德理財，皆非良圖。錄此文，以為時政萬一之助。

在內之理為所先，在外之物為所後。盖德乃理之在內，財乃物之在外者也。然德必有財，而財由德之致，其為本末之先後，豈不較然矣乎？《大學》釋平治之經，及此，意謂欲盡絜矩之道，當明本末之分。彼原於天命而衆理咸備，具於人心而萬事由應，所以公其好惡，不為一己之私，度於物我，能同衆人之欲者，德也。德何以為本邪？盖以德感心，則兆民允懷，而際天薄海皆歸于邦域；以德行仁，則萬姓咸若，而遐陬僻壤悉入于版圖。不必以利為事也，殆見因天分地，何利之弗獲焉？不必以富為心也，將見任土作貢，何
translation_en:
Tie Jian

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: Virtue is the root from which wealth grows. You have grasped the meaning and fashioned it into an essay; this deserves inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The explanation of root and branch is clear in meaning. The writer evidently has devoted thought to the distinction between righteousness and profit.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Any scheme for managing wealth that abandons virtue is unsound. We include this essay in the hope that it may offer even the slightest assistance to present governance.

Principle within must come first; material things outside must come after. Virtue is principle residing within, while wealth consists of material things outside. Yet virtue necessarily brings wealth, and wealth is obtained through virtue. Is their order as root and branch not perfectly clear? When the Great Learning, in explaining the canonical passages on bringing peace to the world and governing the state, reaches this point, its meaning is that anyone wishing fully to practice the way of the measuring square must understand the distinction between root and branch. That which originates in Heaven’s mandate and encompasses all principles, resides in the human heart and enables it to respond to all affairs, makes one impartial in likes and dislikes rather than selfishly pursuing one’s own interests, and enables one, in weighing others against oneself, to share the desires of all people—this is virtue. Why is virtue the root? When one moves hearts through virtue, the myriad people sincerely give their allegiance, and all lands reaching to the horizon and bordering the seas come within the realm. When one practices benevolence through virtue, all the people submit, and remote corners and secluded regions alike enter the territorial registers. There is no need to make profit one’s business: one will surely see that, by following Heaven’s seasons and apportioning the land, no benefit remains unobtained. There is no need to set one’s heart on wealth: one will see that, by assessing tribute according to the land’s productive capacity, what …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
富之不有焉德非為本乎謂之本者以財對德
言則德在所先故為本也乃若地利兼收於府
庫之中方物畢集於帑藏之内所以廣儲蓄而
給軍國之需充貨殖以備公家之費者財也財
何以為末耶盖財之為類雖至廣也然亦難於
强求必以德為豐財之大要財之生世雖無窮
也然不容於易得必以德為發財之大方欲財
之聚實原於有土土宇之廣一德以致之也得
土之廣又原於有人人衆之歸一德以招之也
===
財非為末乎謂之末者以德對財言則財在所
後故為末也是則不患財之未足惟患德之未
周此君子所以先慎其德也歟雖然國不可以
無財財乃民之心也古之帝王思以一人治天
下不以天下奉一人凡可以節民財者無不為
之也後世不知以德為本而惟財是圖瓊林大
盈積以萬計卒不免於悖出之禍果何益哉噫
財固不可以過取而亦不可以浪費苟取之盡
錙銖用之如泥沙兩失之矣有天下者宜鑒于
punctuated: 富之不有焉？德非為本乎？謂之本者，以財對德言，則德在所先，故為本也。乃若地利兼收於府庫之中，方物畢集於帑藏之内，所以廣儲蓄而給軍國之需，充貨殖以備公家之費者，財也。財何以為末耶？盖財之為類雖至廣也，然亦難於强求，必以德為豐財之大要；財之生世雖無窮也，然不容於易得，必以德為發財之大方。欲財之聚，實原於有土，土宇之廣，一德以致之也；得土之廣，又原於有人，人衆之歸，一德以招之也。財非為末乎？謂之末者，以德對財言，則財在所後，故為末也。是則不患財之未足，惟患德之未周，此君子所以先慎其德也歟？雖然，國不可以無財，財乃民之心也。古之帝王思以一人治天下，不以天下奉一人，凡可以節民財者，無不為之也。後世不知以德為本，而惟財是圖，瓊林、大盈，積以萬計，卒不免於悖出之禍，果何益哉？噫！財固不可以過取，而亦不可以浪費。苟取之盡錙銖，用之如泥沙，兩失之矣。有天下者宜鑒于
translation_en:
…what wealth would not be possessed? Is virtue not, then, the root? It is called the root because, when wealth is set against virtue, virtue takes precedence; hence it is the root. As for the yields of the land gathered into the storehouses and treasuries, and the local products assembled within the vaults—what enlarges reserves to meet military and state needs, and increases material resources to provide for public expenditure, is wealth. Why is wealth the branch? Although wealth embraces a very broad range of things, it is difficult to obtain by force; virtue must be the essential means of making wealth abundant. Although the world's production of wealth is inexhaustible, wealth cannot readily be acquired; virtue must be the principal means of generating it. The accumulation of wealth is, in fact, rooted in possessing territory, and virtue alone brings about the expansion of that territory. The acquisition of extensive territory is, in turn, rooted in having people, and virtue alone draws the multitudes into allegiance. Is wealth not, then, the branch? It is called the branch because, when virtue is set against wealth, wealth comes afterward; hence it is the branch. Thus one should worry not that wealth is insufficient, but only that virtue is incomplete. Is this not why the gentleman first attends carefully to his virtue?

Nevertheless, a state cannot do without wealth, for wealth is what the people hold dear. The emperors and kings of antiquity sought to govern All under Heaven through one person, rather than make All under Heaven support one person. They did everything possible to conserve the people's resources. In later ages, rulers did not understand that virtue should be the root, and sought only wealth. In the Qionglin and Daying treasuries they amassed riches reckoned in tens of thousands, yet ultimately could not escape the calamity of wealth departing through wrongful means. What benefit was there in this? Alas! Wealth must neither be exacted excessively nor squandered. If one takes every last fraction from the people but spends it like mud and sand, one errs on both counts. Those who rule All under Heaven should take warning from…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
茲
集大成也者金聲而玉振之也
沈淳
同考試官教諭廖批孟子長於取譬而
此子亦善發揮宜錄其文
考試官教諭朱批聖道未易形容此
作就大成處見意蓋妙於文者
考試官學正王批此篇文韻清新自
有優柔平中氣象取之
===
大賢即樂之全而著其由以見聖道之大也夫
大成之樂未易作也必金以宣之玉以收之會
衆樂於一終斯其為大成歟想孟子之意以為
三子之行各極其一偏孔子之道兼全夫衆理
不猶樂之大成乎彼樂有金石絲竹之不同匏
土革木之不一若獨奏一音而自為始終特小
成耳必衆音並舉斯為大成八音各奏而自為
始終亦小成耳必羣樂合作乃為大成然其作
也何如蓋八音之中金石為重方其未作則擊
punctuated:
茲。

「集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。」
沈淳

同考試官教諭廖批：孟子長於取譬，而此子亦善發揮，宜錄其文。
考試官教諭朱批：聖道未易形容，此作就大成處見意，蓋妙於文者。
考試官學正王批：此篇文韻清新，自有優柔平中氣象，取之。

大賢即樂之全而著其由，以見聖道之大也。夫大成之樂未易作也，必金以宣之，玉以收之，會衆樂於一終，斯其為大成歟！想孟子之意，以為三子之行各極其一偏，孔子之道兼全夫衆理，不猶樂之大成乎？彼樂有金石絲竹之不同，匏土革木之不一。若獨奏一音而自為始終，特小成耳，必衆音並舉，斯為大成。八音各奏而自為始終，亦小成耳，必羣樂合作，乃為大成。然其作也何如？蓋八音之中，金石為重。方其未作，則擊
translation_en:
…this.

“To bring together the great consummation is to sound the bronze bells and conclude with the jade chimes.”
Shen Chun

Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: Mencius excelled at drawing analogies, and this candidate likewise develops their meaning well. His essay merits inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The Way of the sage is not easily described. This composition conveys its meaning through the idea of the great consummation; its author is indeed skilled in literary composition.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: This essay has a fresh and lucid literary cadence, with an unhurried, balanced quality of its own [?]. Accept it.

The great worthy takes music in its completeness and explains how it comes about, thereby revealing the greatness of the sage’s Way. Music that achieves the great consummation is not easily performed. Bronze bells must open it, and jade chimes must bring it to a close, gathering all the music into a single conclusion. Is this not what constitutes its great consummation? I imagine Mencius meant that the conduct of the three masters each reached the utmost in one particular aspect, whereas the Way of Confucius comprehensively embodied all principles. Was this not like the great consummation in music?

In music, there are distinctions among metal, stone, silk, and bamboo, and differences among gourd, clay, hide, and wood. If just one kind of sound is played, with its own beginning and end, this is merely a lesser consummation. Only when all the sounds are raised together is there a great consummation. If the eight kinds of instruments are each played separately, each with its own beginning and end, this too is merely a lesser consummation. Only when all the instruments perform together is there a great consummation.

But how is such music performed? Among the eight kinds of instruments, metal and stone are of foremost importance. Just before the music begins, one strikes…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鎛鐘以宣其聲揚六律於鏗鏘之頃播八音於
和鳴之間翕然並作高下以之而有條羣然交
奏清濁由之而不紊是金聲一宣為衆樂之統
宗矣俟其既闋則擊特磬以收其韻肅羣音於
一終之後卷衆樂於九奏之餘高下之音詘然
而遏息清濁之韻截然以終止是玉韻一收為
衆樂之總括矣金以宣於先則凡自一成以至
於九成者莫不由是肇其端玉以收於後則凡
自一變而至於九變者一皆藉此畢其事二者
===
之間脉絡通貫無所不備合衆小成而為一大
成也豈非孔子集三聖之事為一大聖之事乎
抑論夷清尹任惠和所造固各抵於其極但不
免倚著於一偏也惟孔子則仕止久速各當其
可兼三子之聖而時出之先儒謂三子春夏秋
冬各一其時孔子則太和元氣流行於四時信
斯言也孟子于此既即樂以喻之下文復即射
以明之其深知孔子而善於形容者耶此其乃
所願則學孔子
punctuated:
鎛鐘以宣其聲，揚六律於鏗鏘之頃，播八音於和鳴之間，翕然並作，高下以之而有條；羣然交奏，清濁由之而不紊。是金聲一宣，為衆樂之統宗矣。俟其既闋，則擊特磬以收其韻，肅羣音於一終之後，卷衆樂於九奏之餘。高下之音詘然而遏息，清濁之韻截然以終止。是玉韻一收，為衆樂之總括矣。金以宣於先，則凡自一成以至於九成者，莫不由是肇其端；玉以收於後，則凡自一變而至於九變者，一皆藉此畢其事。二者之間，脉絡通貫，無所不備，合衆小成而為一大成也。豈非孔子集三聖之事為一大聖之事乎？
抑論夷清、尹任、惠和，所造固各抵於其極，但不免倚著於一偏也。惟孔子則仕止久速，各當其可，兼三子之聖而時出之。先儒謂三子春夏秋冬各一其時，孔子則太和元氣流行於四時。信斯言也！孟子于此既即樂以喻之，下文復即射以明之，其深知孔子而善於形容者耶？此其乃所願則學孔子。
translation_en:
…the great bell to send forth its sound, raising the six pitch standards amid its ringing and spreading the sounds of the eight classes of instruments in harmonious resonance. All begin together, their high and low notes thereby ordered; all play in concert, their clear and deep tones thereby free from confusion. Thus, once the bronze sounds forth, it becomes the governing principle of the entire ensemble. When the performance has ended, the single suspended chime stone is struck to gather in its resonances, stilling the assembled sounds after their conclusion and drawing the whole ensemble to a close after nine movements. The high and low notes subside and cease; the clear and deep resonances come decisively to an end. Thus, once the jade gathers in the sound, it brings the entire ensemble to its conclusion. When bronze sounds forth at the beginning, every movement, from the first through the ninth, takes its start from it. When jade gathers in the sound at the end, every variation, from the first through the ninth, relies upon it for completion. Between these two, the connecting threads run throughout, leaving nothing unprovided for: the many lesser accomplishments are united into one great accomplishment. Is this not like Confucius gathering together the achievements of the three sages into the achievement of one great sage?
Now, considering the purity of Boyi, the responsibility assumed by Yi Yin, and the harmony of Liuxia Hui, each indeed reached the utmost in his attainment, yet none escaped leaning toward a single aspect. Confucius alone entered office or withdrew, remained long or departed swiftly, as circumstances required. He combined the sagehood of all three and manifested it as the occasion demanded. Earlier Confucian scholars said that the three sages each represented a particular season among spring, summer, autumn, and winter, whereas Confucius was like the primordial vital energy of supreme harmony circulating through all four seasons. How true these words are! Here Mengzi has used music as an analogy; in the passage below, he again uses archery to make the matter clear. Does this not show how profoundly he understood Confucius and how well he could portray him? This, then, is why his wish was to emulate Confucius [?].

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易
大君之宜吉
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批君臨天下宜不自
用而任賢臣此篇善於道意故錄
考試官教諭朱批談易能就人事上
發揮方見心易之妙此作近之
考試官學正王批君道至大臨爻一
言盡之此可見易不徒為卜筮
===
得居尊之體為臨下之善此聖人繫六五爻義
也盖任人則優於天下居尊之體得矣以是而
臨下何有於不善哉且臨之六五以柔中而下
應不自用而任人乃知者之事為大君之宜彼
大君者首出庶物撫蒞萬邦所臨何廣耶苟自
足其善而無操約及廣之方則非所當務也時
乘六龍統御四海所臨何眾耶苟自恃其長而
無務寡服眾之術殆非所當為也惟虛心下賢
不專自用則是萃眾善以為己善萬邦雖廣同
punctuated:
易
大君之宜，吉。
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批：君臨天下，宜不自用而任賢臣。此篇善於道意，故錄。
考試官教諭朱批：談易，能就人事上發揮，方見心易之妙。此作近之。
考試官學正王批：君道至大，臨爻一言盡之。此可見易不徒為卜筮。
得居尊之體，為臨下之善，此聖人繫六五爻義也。盖任人則優於天下，居尊之體得矣。以是而臨下，何有於不善哉？且臨之六五，以柔中而下應，不自用而任人，乃知者之事，為大君之宜。彼大君者，首出庶物，撫蒞萬邦，所臨何廣耶！苟自足其善，而無操約及廣之方，則非所當務也。時乘六龍，統御四海，所臨何眾耶！苟自恃其長，而無務寡服眾之術，殆非所當為也。惟虛心下賢，不專自用，則是萃眾善以為己善。萬邦雖廣，同
translation_en:
Book of Changes
“What befits a great ruler: auspicious.”
Zhuo Wenlin

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: In ruling All-under-Heaven, a ruler should not rely solely on himself but entrust affairs to worthy ministers. This essay expresses that meaning well and is therefore included.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Only when discussion of the Changes develops its meaning through human affairs does the subtlety of the Changes within the mind become apparent. This composition approaches that achievement.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: The Way of the ruler is supremely great, yet a single statement in a line of the hexagram Approach exhausts it. This shows that the Changes is not merely for divination.

To grasp the proper manner of occupying an exalted position and to excel in governing those below: this is the meaning the sage attached to the six in the fifth place. For by entrusting affairs to others, one can govern All-under-Heaven with ample ease, thereby grasping the proper manner of occupying an exalted position. Governing those below in this way, how could one fail to do well? Moreover, the six in the fifth place of Approach is yielding and central, and finds a corresponding line below. To entrust affairs to others instead of relying solely on oneself is the conduct of the wise and what befits a great ruler. Such a ruler stands foremost among the myriad beings and governs and tends the myriad states. How vast is the realm over which he presides! If he is content with his own goodness and lacks a method for grasping the essentials so as to reach far and wide, he is not attending to his proper task. Riding the six dragons as the times require, he rules all within the Four Seas. How numerous are those over whom he presides! If he relies on his own strengths and lacks the art of attending to a few essentials so as to win the allegiance of the multitude, this surely is not what he ought to do. Only by emptying his mind, deferring to the worthy, and refraining from relying exclusively on himself does he gather the goodness of others and make it his own. Though the myriad states are vast, together …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
歸於乾旋坤轉之中其所當務不在是乎推誠
使能必欲任人則是集衆長以為己長四海雖
衆舉囿於日照月臨之下其所當為果外是乎
夫莫難盡者君之道也今既萃衆善以為臨必
其行合天道而大亨以正之善可獲未易全者
君之德也今既集衆長以有臨必其動皆順說
而教思容保之效可臻推臨之大于以建夫可
大之業繼蠱之元亨而天下治矣行臨之中于
以妙夫用中之極啓觀之神道而天下服矣向
===
使專於自用而不思所以任人固非宜也如吉
何哉抑論五之應二其人君任相之道乎故不
患治之未隆惟患相之未得誠得相而任之則
君逸於上臣勞於下天下之務將無足為者矣
然相之賢否治忽所關人君擇之又不可昧於
邪正之辨故曰知人則哲臨之六五繫以知臨
於此見用人之道其要在知人也
盛德大業至矣哉
戴倫
punctuated:
歸於乾旋坤轉之中，其所當務不在是乎？推誠使能，必欲任人，則是集衆長以為己長，四海雖衆，舉囿於日照月臨之下，其所當為果外是乎？夫莫難盡者，君之道也。今既萃衆善以為臨，必其行合天道，而大亨以正之善可獲。未易全者，君之德也。今既集衆長以有臨，必其動皆順說，而教思容保之效可臻。推臨之大，于以建夫可大之業，繼蠱之元亨而天下治矣；行臨之中，于以妙夫用中之極，啓觀之神道而天下服矣。向使專於自用，而不思所以任人，固非宜也，如吉何哉？抑論五之應二，其人君任相之道乎？故不患治之未隆，惟患相之未得。誠得相而任之，則君逸於上，臣勞於下，天下之務將無足為者矣。然相之賢否，治忽所關，人君擇之，又不可昧於邪正之辨。故曰：「知人則哲。」臨之六五繫以知臨，於此見用人之道，其要在知人也。

盛德大業至矣哉
戴倫
translation_en:
…come within the turning of Heaven and Earth. Is this not what he ought to attend to? By extending his sincerity and employing the capable, determined to entrust affairs to others, he gathers the strengths of all and makes them his own. Though those within the Four Seas are numerous, all are encompassed beneath the light of the sun and moon. Can what he ought to do really lie outside this?

Nothing is harder to fulfill completely than the Way of the ruler. Having now gathered every excellence to exercise authority over those below, his conduct will surely accord with the Way of Heaven, and he can attain the blessing of great success through correctness. Nor is the ruler’s virtue easily perfected. Having now gathered everyone’s strengths to exercise authority, his actions will surely be compliant and joyful, and he can achieve the effects of thoughtful instruction, magnanimity, and protection. Extending the greatness of Approach (Lin), he thereby establishes an undertaking capable of greatness; continuing the supreme success of Remedying Decay (Gu), he brings order to the world. Practicing the centrality of Approach, he thereby achieves the utmost refinement in applying the mean; opening the way to the spiritual efficacy of Contemplation (Guan), he brings the world to submit.

Had he instead relied exclusively upon himself, without considering how to entrust affairs to others, this would certainly have been inappropriate. How could there have been good fortune? Moreover, if we consider the correspondence of the fifth line with the second, does it not represent the way a ruler entrusts office to a chief minister? Thus he need not worry that good government has not yet flourished, but only that he has not yet found a chief minister. If he truly finds such a minister and entrusts affairs to him, the ruler will be at ease above and the minister will labor below; the affairs of the world will then present nothing difficult to accomplish.

Yet whether the chief minister is worthy or unworthy determines order or disorder. In choosing him, the ruler must not fail to distinguish the wicked from the upright. Hence the saying: “To know men is to be discerning.” The text attached to the six in the fifth place of Approach speaks of “wise approach.” Here we see that, in the way of employing others, the essential thing is to know them.

“How consummate are flourishing virtue and great achievement!”
Dai Lun

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉批說理文字自是簡
潔此作其庶幾乎
考試官教諭朱批造化全功一筆寫
出其亦善言易者
考試官學正王批易理無中含有最
難形容詞簡理明僅見是作
大傳贊造化之全功而有以妙其極焉蓋盛德
大業一皆造化之功也所以然者又豈有加於
其間哉宜大傳舉而贊之也且一陰一陽之道
===
無乎不在以在造化者言之方其動而為德之
發也有象有形無隱不彰可名可狀無微不著
生生者亘古今而相禪化化者貫始終而相繼
是蓋自然而然浩乎不可以淺近窺也德之盛
為何如及其靜而為業之本也功有所成斂大
化於無形用有所歸會一元於無迹妙機緘而
莫測者有生咸具含變化而至密者隨在各足
是蓋無為而為渾乎不可以限量求也業之大
為何如夫德之發者固為盛矣使有終窮則非
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉批：說理文字，自是簡潔。此作其庶幾乎！

考試官教諭朱批：造化全功，一筆寫出，其亦善言易者。

考試官學正王批：易理無中含有，最難形容。詞簡理明，僅見是作。

大傳贊造化之全功，而有以妙其極焉。蓋盛德大業，一皆造化之功也。所以然者，又豈有加於其間哉？宜大傳舉而贊之也。且一陰一陽之道，無乎不在。以在造化者言之，方其動而為德之發也，有象有形，無隱不彰；可名可狀，無微不著。生生者亘古今而相禪，化化者貫始終而相繼。是蓋自然而然，浩乎不可以淺近窺也。德之盛為何如！及其靜而為業之本也，功有所成，斂大化於無形；用有所歸，會一元於無迹。妙機緘而莫測者，有生咸具；含變化而至密者，隨在各足。是蓋無為而為，渾乎不可以限量求也。業之大為何如！夫德之發者，固為盛矣；使有終窮，則非
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Writing that elucidates principles is naturally concise and lucid. This composition comes close to that ideal!

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The entire achievement of creation and transformation is expressed in a single sweep of the brush. Its author, too, is skilled in expounding the Book of Changes.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: In the principles of the Book of Changes, nonbeing contains being—a matter exceedingly difficult to describe. Only in this composition have I seen such concise language and clear reasoning.

The Great Commentary praises the entire achievement of creation and transformation, wonderfully conveying its utmost perfection. For magnificent virtue and great enterprise are, without exception, the achievements of creation and transformation. As for what makes them so, could anything further be added to them? It is fitting that the Great Commentary should single them out for praise. Moreover, the Way of alternating yin and yang is present everywhere. To speak of its presence in creation and transformation: when it moves and becomes the unfolding of virtue, it has images and forms; nothing hidden fails to become manifest. It can be named and described; nothing minute fails to become apparent. Life generating life extends across past and present in unbroken succession; transformation following transformation continues from beginning to end. This occurs spontaneously, its vastness beyond the scrutiny of shallow understanding. How magnificent is this virtue!

When it becomes still and forms the foundation of enterprise, its achievement reaches completion, gathering the great process of transformation into formlessness; its operation finds its resting place, bringing the primal unity together without a trace. Its wondrous workings, unfathomable, are possessed by all living things; its utmost subtlety, containing change and transformation, is fully present in each thing wherever it may be. This is action through nonaction, an undivided wholeness that cannot be apprehended through finite measures. How great is this enterprise! Now, the unfolding of virtue is certainly magnificent; yet if it had an end or could be exhausted, it would not be…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
盛之至也業之本者固為大矣使有滲漏則非
大之至也今德之盛與時偕行初無終窮之或
間是德之所以行豈復有加其盛乎業之大體
物不遺曽無滲漏之或外是業之所以立尚復
有加其大乎造化之全功如此何莫而非陰陽
之所為也大抵天地之間陰陽兩端而已道具
於陰而行乎陽顯諸仁即天道之元亨誠之通
而為德之發也藏諸用即天道之利貞誠之復
而為業之本也造化之德業如是乃若易簡理
===
得聖人之德業也可乆可大賢人之德業也學
者誠能由易知易從而馴造其極則士希賢賢
希聖聖希天矣天人豈有二哉噫非知道者何
足以語此
書
皐陶曰都慎厥身修思永惇叙九族庶明
勵翼邇可遠在兹禹拜昌言曰俞皐陶
曰都在知人在安民禹曰吁咸若時惟
帝其難之
punctuated:
盛之至也。業之本者固為大矣，使有滲漏，則非大之至也。今德之盛，與時偕行，初無終窮之或間，是德之所以行，豈復有加其盛乎？業之大，體物不遺，曽無滲漏之或外，是業之所以立，尚復有加其大乎？造化之全功如此，何莫而非陰陽之所為也？大抵天地之間，陰陽兩端而已。道具於陰而行乎陽，顯諸仁，即天道之元亨，誠之通而為德之發也；藏諸用，即天道之利貞，誠之復而為業之本也。造化之德業如是。乃若易簡理得，聖人之德業也；可乆可大，賢人之德業也。學者誠能由易知易從而馴造其極，則士希賢，賢希聖，聖希天矣。天人豈有二哉？噫！非知道者，何足以語此？

書

皐陶曰：「都！慎厥身修，思永，惇叙九族，庶明勵翼，邇可遠，在兹。」禹拜昌言，曰：「俞！」皐陶曰：「都！在知人，在安民。」禹曰：「吁！咸若時，惟帝其難之。」
translation_en:
…the utmost flourishing. The foundation of achievement is indeed great, but if anything leaked away, it would not be greatness at its utmost. Now the flourishing of virtue advances together with the seasons, never interrupted by any ending or exhaustion. Such is the operation of virtue: could anything further enhance its flourishing? The greatness of achievement embodies all things without omission, leaving nothing outside through any leakage. Such is the establishment of achievement: could anything further enhance its greatness? Such is the complete accomplishment of creation and transformation. What part of it is not the work of yin and yang?

Broadly speaking, between Heaven and Earth there are only the two poles, yin and yang. The Way is fully present in yin and operates through yang. Its manifestation in benevolence is precisely the origination and flourishing of Heaven’s Way: the free passage of sincerity, constituting virtue’s unfolding. Its concealment in functioning is precisely the benefit and constancy of Heaven’s Way: the return of sincerity, constituting the foundation of achievement. Such are the virtue and achievement of creation and transformation. As for grasping principle through ease and simplicity, these are the virtue and achievement of the sage; the capacity to endure and to grow great constitutes the virtue and achievement of the worthy. If learners can truly proceed from what is easy to know and easy to follow, gradually reaching the utmost, then the scholar will aspire to become worthy, the worthy to become a sage, and the sage to accord with Heaven. How could Heaven and humanity be two? Ah! How could anyone who does not understand the Way be qualified to discuss this?

Book of Documents

Gao Yao said: “Ah! Be watchful over the cultivation of your person, and think of the long term. Generously maintain due order among the nine degrees of kinship, and let the many enlightened men encourage and assist you. What begins nearby can extend afar: it rests on this.” Yu bowed before these excellent words and said: “Yes!” Gao Yao said: “Ah! It lies in knowing people; it lies in bringing peace to the people.” Yu said: “Oh! To accomplish all of this—even the emperor finds it difficult.”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖批得臯陶陳謨大要
而大禹俞吁之旨亦能體出錄之

===

辭者有以哉思昔虞舜垂拱臯陶陳謨因禹之
然美禹之問乃推廣允迪謨明之義以為治本

推之於國則羣哲勉輔而國治又由近而可推

Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: “He grasps the essentials of Gao Yao’s exposition of his counsels, and also succeeds in conveying the meaning of the Great Yu’s assent and exclamation. Accept this essay.”

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “He brings out the gracious, unhurried atmosphere of the exchanges between Yu and Gao Yao at the court of Shun. For this reason, it is selected.”

The great minister praised the question put to him and expanded his counsel; his fellow minister profoundly agreed. Bringing about good government is certainly rooted in cultivating oneself, but depends especially upon wisdom and benevolence. He held that government is rooted in the self, and that cultivating the self depends upon vigilance. One must be cautious and watchful, apprehensive and fearful, so that neither speech nor conduct goes astray. The self is governed by the mind, and reflection must reach far. One must deliberate deeply and consider the distant consequences, rather than devise shallow, shortsighted plans. Extending this to the family, affection for one’s kin becomes steadfast and the family is ordered. Extending it to the state, the many wise men exert themselves in assisting, and the state is well governed. Extending it further, from what is near to the far reaches of all under Heaven, likewise involves nothing beyond this. Thus, when the self is cultivated, the family ordered, and the state well governed, all under Heaven is brought to peace. title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
輕言也實盛德之嘉言篤近舉遠非虛語也誠
保邦之要道其深然之者非有契於其心乎夫
致治固不外乎修身然非知人安民又為治之
累也故臯陶因禹之俞而復推廣其未盡之旨
歎美其言以為在於知人必因能授任使野無
遺賢以急知之先務在於安民必布德施惠俾
萬邦咸寧以成仁之極功則允迪謨明之義盡
矣禹聞斯言遂吁之曰仁兼乎知雖帝也其仁
如天而四凶在位知又難能也知兼乎仁雖堯
===
也其知如神而病諸博施仁又難能也其不然
之者非有難於其事乎夫以臯陶之陳謨而大
禹一然於前一難於後者有如此無非所以勸
戒期望於其君也噫至矣哉是知有虞之臣忠
良登於一堂謨猷會於眾見其曰俞曰都者非
阿諛曰吁曰咈者非拂逆言若牴牾而義實相
足外若背馳而內實相孚唐虞雍容氣象可想
見矣夫豈後世之可及哉
太保率西方諸侯入應門左畢公率東方
punctuated:
輕言也，實盛德之嘉言；篤近舉遠非虛語也，誠保邦之要道。其深然之者，非有契於其心乎？夫致治固不外乎修身，然非知人安民，又為治之累也。故臯陶因禹之俞，而復推廣其未盡之旨，歎美其言，以為在於知人，必因能授任，使野無遺賢，以急知之先務；在於安民，必布德施惠，俾萬邦咸寧，以成仁之極功，則允迪謨明之義盡矣。禹聞斯言，遂吁之曰：「仁兼乎知，雖帝也，其仁如天，而四凶在位，知又難能也；知兼乎仁，雖堯也，其知如神，而病諸博施，仁又難能也。」其不然之者，非有難於其事乎？夫以臯陶之陳謨，而大禹一然於前、一難於後者，有如此，無非所以勸戒期望於其君也。噫，至矣哉！是知有虞之臣，忠良登於一堂，謨猷會於眾見。其曰俞曰都者，非阿諛；曰吁曰咈者，非拂逆。言若牴牾，而義實相足；外若背馳，而內實相孚。唐虞雍容氣象，可想見矣。夫豈後世之可及哉！

太保率西方諸侯入應門左，畢公率東方
translation_en:
…words to be spoken lightly; they are indeed excellent words born of abundant virtue. Being devoted to those near at hand and extending one's influence to those far away is no empty saying; it is truly the essential way to preserve the realm.” Was his profound agreement not because these words resonated with his heart? Bringing about good government certainly depends upon cultivating oneself. Yet failure to discern men's abilities and bring peace to the people also burdens government. Thus, prompted by Yu's assent, Gao Yao further elaborated the meaning he had not yet fully expressed. He praised these words and explained that discerning men requires assigning responsibilities according to ability, so that no worthy person remains overlooked outside office, thereby attending urgently to wisdom's foremost task. Bringing peace to the people requires spreading virtue and bestowing kindness, so that the myriad states all enjoy tranquillity, thereby bringing benevolence to its fullest accomplishment. Only then is the meaning of truly putting virtue into practice and exercising enlightened counsel fully expressed.

Hearing these words, Yu sighed and said: “For benevolence to encompass wisdom—even for the emperor, whose benevolence was like Heaven, the Four Evildoers remained in office: wisdom, too, is difficult to attain. For wisdom to encompass benevolence—even for Yao, whose wisdom was like that of a spirit, bestowing benefits universally taxed his powers: benevolence, too, is difficult to attain.” Was his disagreement not because he perceived difficulty in the undertaking? Such was Great Yu's response to Gao Yao's presentation of counsel: first he assented, and then he raised a difficulty. All of this served to encourage and admonish their ruler and express their hopes for him. Ah, how consummate it was!

From this we know that among the ministers of Shun, loyal and worthy men assembled in one hall, and counsel and plans emerged from their collective insights. Their words of assent and admiration were no flattery; their sighs and objections were no defiance. Their words seemed contradictory, yet their meanings actually complemented one another. Outwardly they seemed to diverge, yet inwardly they trusted one another. We can picture the harmonious and dignified atmosphere of the reigns of Yao and Shun. How could later ages ever equal it!

===
顏之咫尺也吁班次分於方近所尊之初儀物
備於既近所尊之頃諸侯朝見康王如此正始
之道不於是而可見哉考之王制二百一十國
以為州州有伯八州八伯各率其屬以聽於天
子之老二人則二伯之制蓋始於此矣洛誥召
公語成王以御諸侯之道有曰享多儀儀不及
物惟曰不享而又宮省之禮朝會之位貢獻之
物無非素籌而預定者張子曰為治而不法三
代終苟道也誠哉
punctuated:
森嚴也。內以統外，若身之使臂，有令而必從，截然其整齊也。夫同入其門，各列其位，至於君前矣，可無物以為贄哉？布於庭者，則陳四黃馬而朱其鬣；執於手者，則舉所奉圭而兼以幣。形之言曰：「藩衞之臣不一，茲其來也，敢執壤地所出，以成夫奠贄之禮；屏翰之臣不一，茲其朝也，敢執封內所產，以表夫恭敬之心。」於是又相率皆拜，以至於再，若大若小，儼一敬於天威之密邇也；相與稽首，以至於地，若尊若卑，罄一誠於龍顏之咫尺也。
吁！班次分於方近所尊之初，儀物備於既近所尊之頃。諸侯朝見康王如此，正始之道不於是而可見哉？考之《王制》，二百一十國以為州，州有伯，八州八伯，各率其屬以聽於天子之老二人，則二伯之制蓋始於此矣。《洛誥》召公語成王以御諸侯之道，有曰：「享多儀，儀不及物，惟曰不享。」而又宮省之禮、朝會之位、貢獻之物，無非素籌而預定者。張子曰：「為治而不法三代，終苟道也。」誠哉！
translation_en:
… solemn and imposing. Those within direct those without, as the body commands its arms: whenever an order is issued, it must be obeyed. How exact their orderliness! They enter the same gate, take their respective places, and arrive before their ruler. Could they have no objects to present as audience gifts? Arrayed in the courtyard are four yellow horses with their manes dyed red; held up in their hands are the jade tablets they bear, together with offerings of silk. They give voice to their intentions, saying: “We ministers who guard the realm are many. In coming here, we venture to bring what our lands yield, to fulfill the rite of presenting audience gifts. We ministers who serve as its protective bulwarks are many. In attending court, we venture to bring what is produced within our fiefs, to express our reverent hearts.” Then, following one another, they all bow, and bow a second time. Whether rulers of great or small domains, they stand solemnly united in reverence, so close to the heavenly majesty. Together they kowtow until their heads touch the ground. Whether high or low in rank, they pour forth a single sincerity, within mere feet of the imperial countenance.
Ah! Their ranks and places are distinguished as they first approach the one they honor; their ceremonial observances and offerings are fully prepared by the time they have drawn near. Such was the way the feudal lords attended an audience with King Kang. Can we not see here the principle of setting a reign on the right course from its beginning? Examining the Royal Regulations, we find that 210 states constituted a region, and each region had a chief. The eight regions had eight chiefs, each leading his subordinate lords to receive instructions from the Son of Heaven’s two senior ministers. The institution of the two regional overlords thus presumably originated here. In the Announcement concerning Luo, the Duke of Shao spoke to King Cheng about the way to govern the feudal lords, saying: “Presentations require many ceremonial observances. If the observances do not extend to the offerings, it is simply called making no presentation.” Furthermore, the rites of palace inspection [?], the positions at court assemblies, and the objects offered as tribute were all planned beforehand and determined in advance. Master Zhang said: “To govern without taking the Three Dynasties as one’s model is, in the end, merely an expedient way.” How true!

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
詩
其儀一兮心如結兮
王璽
同考試官教諭程批講君子用心處明
白簡易盖亦知心之所用者歟
同考試官教諭杜批能脫去外占知内
之説得詩人渾融之旨錄之
考試官教諭朱批此題有不容言之
妙而子能言之可謂善説詩矣
===
考試官學正王批體認真切而詞足
以發之可取
即其動容之善而為用心之善詩人美君子然
也夫儀之所在心之所在也觀君子儀容之一
非其心之如結而何哉鳲鳩之詩詩人美君子
用心均平專一而作也意謂心者一身之主宰
儀者一心之運用心焉不存儀能一乎今觀曹
之君子自燕處以至酬酢凡布於四體之間抑
抑然為之慎密而不過其則自閒居以至應接
punctuated:
詩

其儀一兮，心如結兮。

王璽

同考試官教諭程批：講君子用心處，明白簡易，盖亦知心之所用者歟！

同考試官教諭杜批：能脫去外占知内之説，得詩人渾融之旨，錄之。

考試官教諭朱批：此題有不容言之妙，而子能言之，可謂善説詩矣。

考試官學正王批：體認真切，而詞足以發之，可取。

即其動容之善，而為用心之善，詩人美君子然也。夫儀之所在，心之所在也。觀君子儀容之一，非其心之如結而何哉？鳲鳩之詩，詩人美君子用心均平專一而作也。意謂心者，一身之主宰；儀者，一心之運用。心焉不存，儀能一乎？今觀曹之君子，自燕處以至酬酢，凡布於四體之間，抑抑然為之慎密，而不過其則；自閒居以至應接，
translation_en:
Book of Odes

“His deportment is consistent; his heart is as though tied in a knot.”

Wang Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: His explanation of how the gentleman applies his mind is clear, simple, and accessible. Surely he too understands how the mind is employed!

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: He succeeds in moving beyond the explanation that one divines the inward from the outward [?], and grasps the poet’s integrated meaning. Select this essay.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: This topic contains a subtlety that defies expression, yet you have expressed it. You may indeed be called adept at explaining the Odes.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: His understanding is genuine and precise, and his language adequately expresses it. Worth selecting.

From the excellence of the gentleman’s movements and bearing, the poet establishes the excellence of his application of mind: thus does he praise the gentleman. For where deportment is manifest, there too is the mind. When we observe the consistency of the gentleman’s deportment, what can it be but his heart being as though tied in a knot? The ode “The Cuckoo” (Shijiu) was composed by the poet to praise the gentleman’s evenhanded and single-minded application of his mind. Its meaning is that the mind governs the whole person, while deportment is the mind’s operation. If the mind is not present, can deportment remain consistent? Now observe the gentleman of Cao: from resting at ease to exchanging courtesies, in everything expressed through his four limbs, he is composed, careful, and attentive, never exceeding the proper standards; from dwelling in private to receiving and dealing with others …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
凡見諸一身之際秩秩然為之整肅而不踰其
閑周旋中規折旋中矩而所以中規中矩者久
暫一致初不謹乎大而忽乎小也容止可觀進
退可度而所以可觀可度者終始一誠初不修
於顯而怠於隱也然儀之所以一者豈有他哉
蓋以威儀之著見莫非精神心術之微容貌之
展舒莫非虛靈知覺之妙念慮所施有以管攝
乎四體心思所及有以檢制其一身大者此心
小者此心一心之精誠合久暫而無間不有如
===
物之堅固不可解乎顯者此心隱者此心一心
之妙用貫終始而不渝不有如物之凝結不可
散乎是則心所以維持此儀而儀所以運行是
心豈儀自儀而心自心耶若曹之詩人亦可謂
善觀君子者矣嗟夫心之於人亦大矣宰一身
而統萬事貫一理而妙萬化也然以心而觀心
則隱而難知以儀而觀心則顯而易見此則詩
人之深意也況蕞爾之曹狃於風聲氣習舊矣
孰知此心為用者幾何人哉故詠候人者有赤
punctuated: 凡見諸一身之際，秩秩然為之整肅而不踰其閑。周旋中規，折旋中矩，而所以中規中矩者，久暫一致，初不謹乎大而忽乎小也。容止可觀，進退可度，而所以可觀可度者，終始一誠，初不修於顯而怠於隱也。然儀之所以一者，豈有他哉？蓋以威儀之著見，莫非精神心術之微；容貌之展舒，莫非虛靈知覺之妙。念慮所施，有以管攝乎四體；心思所及，有以檢制其一身。大者此心，小者此心，一心之精誠合久暫而無間，不有如物之堅固不可解乎？顯者此心，隱者此心，一心之妙用貫終始而不渝，不有如物之凝結不可散乎？是則心所以維持此儀，而儀所以運行是心，豈儀自儀而心自心耶？若曹之詩人，亦可謂善觀君子者矣。嗟夫！心之於人亦大矣，宰一身而統萬事，貫一理而妙萬化也。然以心而觀心，則隱而難知；以儀而觀心，則顯而易見。此則詩人之深意也。況蕞爾之曹，狃於風聲氣習舊矣，孰知此心為用者幾何人哉？故詠《候人》者有赤…
translation_en: …in everything manifested in his person, he maintains orderly composure and solemnity, never transgressing the bounds of propriety. His circling movements accord with the compass, and his angular turns with the square. What makes them accord with compass and square remains consistent over long and short periods alike: he never attends carefully to great matters while neglecting small ones. His bearing is worthy of contemplation, and his advances and withdrawals conform to proper measure. What makes them worthy of contemplation and properly measured is a single sincerity maintained from beginning to end: he never cultivates himself in public while growing lax in private. Is there any other reason why his deportment is consistent? Every outward manifestation of dignified deportment expresses the subtle workings of his spirit and mind; every movement of his countenance expresses the wondrous capacity of his receptive, lucid awareness. Wherever his thoughts are directed, they govern his limbs; wherever his reflection reaches, it regulates his whole person. In great matters there is this mind; in small matters there is this mind. The perfect sincerity of this single mind unites long and short periods without interruption—is it not like something so firmly bound that it cannot be untied? In public there is this mind; in private there is this mind. The subtle functioning of this single mind runs unchanged from beginning to end—is it not like something so closely joined that it cannot be dispersed? Thus the mind sustains this deportment, while deportment puts this mind into action. How could deportment exist on its own and the mind on its own? The poet of Cao may indeed be called a keen observer of the gentleman. Ah! How great is the mind’s importance to a person! It rules the whole person and governs the myriad affairs; it comprehends the single principle and works wondrously through the myriad transformations. Yet observing the mind through the mind leaves it hidden and difficult to know; observing the mind through deportment makes it manifest and easy to see. This is the poet’s profound meaning. Moreover, tiny Cao had long been habituated to its prevailing customs and ingrained ways. Who knows how many people there understood the workings of this mind? Thus the poet who sang of The Waiting Officers offered criticism concerning the red …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
芾之譏詠蜉蝣者有麻衣之歎回視淑人君子
能無愧乎此刪詩者所以特表而出之又斡旋
風化之一大機也不可不知
樂只君子天子葵之
周瑭
同考試官教諭程批當時君臣腹心相
孚氣象模寫殆盡
同考試官教諭杜批詞理精切說出人
君推誠待臣之意
===
考試官教諭朱批詩正而葩此作蓋
得其遺緒者
考試官學正王批寫出周廷明良之
盛宛然在目
王者於諸侯嘉其人而度其心也盖諸侯可樂
則其心之所蘊也可知王者寧不有以度之哉
采菽之詩天子所以答魚藻也意以為下者禮
有所忽則為上者或有所忌何有於可樂乎今
我諸侯念朝廷之分所尚者嚴君臣之禮所主
punctuated:
芾之譏，詠蜉蝣者有麻衣之歎。回視淑人君子，能無愧乎？此刪詩者所以特表而出之，又斡旋風化之一大機也，不可不知。

「樂只君子，天子葵之。」
周瑭

同考試官教諭程批：當時君臣腹心相孚氣象，模寫殆盡。

同考試官教諭杜批：詞理精切，說出人君推誠待臣之意。

考試官教諭朱批：詩正而葩，此作蓋得其遺緒者。

考試官學正王批：寫出周廷明良之盛，宛然在目。

王者於諸侯，嘉其人而度其心也。盖諸侯可樂，則其心之所蘊也可知，王者寧不有以度之哉？《采菽》之詩，天子所以答《魚藻》也。意以為下者禮有所忽，則為上者或有所忌，何有於可樂乎？今我諸侯念朝廷之分，所尚者嚴；君臣之禮，所主
translation_en:
…the criticism of red knee-covers; those who sang “Mayflies” (Fuyou) voiced their lament over hempen robes. Looking back upon the good man, the gentleman, could they feel no shame? This is why the editor of the Odes singled this poem out for prominence. It is also a major means of transforming customs through moral influence, something one must understand.

“Joyful are the gentlemen; the Son of Heaven appraises their hearts.”
Zhou Tang

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: The atmosphere of heartfelt mutual trust between ruler and ministers at that time is depicted almost to the full.

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: Precise and apt in expression and reasoning, this brings out the ruler’s intention to treat his ministers with wholehearted sincerity.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The Odes are upright yet richly adorned; this composition has surely inherited something of their tradition.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: It depicts the flourishing age of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers at the Zhou court, vividly present before our eyes.

In his dealings with the feudal lords, the king commends their persons and appraises their hearts. Since the feudal lords are a source of joy, what their hearts hold can be known. How could the king fail to have a means of appraising them? The ode “Gathering Beans” (Caishu) is the Son of Heaven’s response to “Fish among the Waterweeds” (Yuzao). Its meaning is that, if those below neglect ritual propriety in any respect, those above may harbor misgivings about them. What joy could there be in that? Now our feudal lords bear in mind the distinctions of rank at court, esteeming strict observance; in the ritual relations between ruler and minister, what they take as their guiding principle…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
者敢望龍衮於穆清俯伏舞蹈之容翼如也接
其丰采而天顏為之一開何樂似之瞻堂廉於
堂陛拜手稽首之儀蹌如也覩其輝光而天威
為之一霽何樂如之吾知一恭足以諧帝旨一
敬足以悟宸衷天子必曰惟爾諸侯向也出涖
侯服視天階盖九重也雖曰為上為德孰與其
忠今焉彼交匪紓而愛君之心畢露於朝見之
頃一念忠貞不惟諸侯自許而天子亦許之昔
也出守侯邦視君門盖萬里也雖曰為下為民
孰亮其誠今焉彼交匪敖而愛國之心洞徹於
會同之日一腔忠赤不惟諸侯自知而天子亦
知之以翼翼之恭蘊而為忠貞之節凡可以緝
熈帝載者無不黙運於心思豈必於其来也見
諸獻納而後與其忠哉以肅肅之敬篤而為忠
赤之忱凡可以圖惟化理者靡不潜孚於念慮
豈必於其至也措諸行事而後亮其誠哉是知
非諸侯之樂只固無以致天子之揆非天子之
推誠又何以知諸侯之心君臣之間可謂各盡
punctuated: 者敢望龍衮於穆清，俯伏舞蹈之容翼如也。接其丰采，而天顏為之一開，何樂似之？瞻堂廉於堂陛，拜手稽首之儀蹌如也。覩其輝光，而天威為之一霽，何樂如之？吾知一恭足以諧帝旨，一敬足以悟宸衷。天子必曰：「惟爾諸侯，向也出涖侯服，視天階盖九重也。雖曰為上為德，孰與其忠？今焉彼交匪紓，而愛君之心畢露於朝見之頃，一念忠貞，不惟諸侯自許，而天子亦許之。昔也出守侯邦，視君門盖萬里也。雖曰為下為民，孰亮其誠？今焉彼交匪敖，而愛國之心洞徹於會同之日，一腔忠赤，不惟諸侯自知，而天子亦知之。」以翼翼之恭，蘊而為忠貞之節，凡可以緝熈帝載者，無不黙運於心思，豈必於其来也見諸獻納，而後與其忠哉？以肅肅之敬，篤而為忠赤之忱，凡可以圖惟化理者，靡不潜孚於念慮，豈必於其至也措諸行事，而後亮其誠哉？是知非諸侯之樂只，固無以致天子之揆；非天子之推誠，又何以知諸侯之心？君臣之間，可謂各盡
translation_en:
…they venture to gaze upon the dragon robes in the august, tranquil court, their bearing reverent as they prostrate themselves and perform the ceremonial dance. Beholding their graceful presence, the imperial countenance brightens: what joy could compare with this? They look toward the edge of the hall from its steps, their movements measured as they bow with clasped hands and touch their foreheads to the ground. Beholding their radiance, the imperial sternness softens: what joy could equal this? I know that a single act of deference suffices to accord with the emperor’s wishes, and a single act of reverence suffices to move his heart.

The Son of Heaven will surely say: “You lords formerly went forth to govern your domains, viewing the steps to the imperial throne as nine enclosures away. Though you were said to serve your sovereign and practice virtue, who could acknowledge your loyalty? Now, ‘in their bearing they are not slack,’ and their love for their ruler is fully revealed in the moment of audience. Their steadfast loyalty is affirmed not only by the lords themselves, but also by the Son of Heaven. Formerly they went forth to guard their states, viewing the sovereign’s gate as ten thousand li away. Though they were said to serve those below and act for the people, who could discern their sincerity? Now, ‘in their bearing they are not arrogant,’ and their love for the state is plainly revealed on the day of their assembly at court. Their wholehearted devotion is known not only to the lords themselves, but also to the Son of Heaven.”

Their attentive deference is inwardly cultivated into steadfast loyalty. Whatever might sustain and glorify the emperor’s undertakings is silently considered in their hearts. Must they first present counsel when they come to court before their loyalty can be acknowledged? Their solemn reverence deepens into wholehearted sincerity. Whatever might advance moral transformation and good governance finds an inward response in their thoughts. Must they first put it into practice upon their arrival before their sincerity can be discerned?

Thus we know that without the lords’ joyous bearing, there would indeed be no basis for the Son of Heaven to fathom them; yet without the Son of Heaven’s extension of his own sincerity to others, how could he know the lords’ hearts? Between ruler and ministers, each may be said to fulfill…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
其道矣雖然古之聖君不患臣禮之不吾盡也
而患體悉之未周古之賢臣不患君恩之不吾
隆也而患敬禮之未至今觀有周君臣其來朝
也則曰彼交匪紓敬禮至矣其燕饗也則曰天
子葵之體悉周矣此所以君臣相得而為有周
之盛也千載而下猶可想見其氣象
春秋
元年〔隱公〕
張嵩
===
同考試官教諭劉批發明人君之用心
學之傳深得聖人紀元之意宜錄
考試官教諭朱批塲中泥於元日元
紀對乾元坤元惟此作獨出羣昧
考試官學正王批體元以正心處而
述古之意宛然寓於其中傑作也
春秋托魯君嗣位之初著人君體元之義此見
夫子祖述憲章以體元為人君之職也夫經世
之志何如哉且仲尼一筆大聖攸係是故假魯
punctuated:
其道矣。雖然，古之聖君不患臣禮之不吾盡也，而患體悉之未周；古之賢臣不患君恩之不吾隆也，而患敬禮之未至。今觀有周君臣，其來朝也，則曰「彼交匪紓」，敬禮至矣；其燕饗也，則曰「天子葵之」，體悉周矣。此所以君臣相得而為有周之盛也。千載而下，猶可想見其氣象。
春秋
元年〔隱公〕
張嵩
同考試官教諭劉批：發明人君之用心，學之傳，深得聖人紀元之意，宜錄。
考試官教諭朱批：塲中泥於元日、元紀，對乾元、坤元，惟此作獨出羣昧。
考試官學正王批：體元以正心處，而述古之意宛然寓於其中，傑作也。
春秋托魯君嗣位之初，著人君體元之義。此見夫子祖述憲章，以體元為人君之職也。夫經世之志何如哉！且仲尼一筆，大聖攸係，是故假魯
translation_en:
…their respective ways. Nevertheless, the sage rulers of antiquity worried not that their ministers failed to fulfill their obligations of courtesy toward them, but that their own sympathetic understanding was incomplete. The worthy ministers of antiquity worried not that their rulers bestowed insufficient favor upon them, but that their own reverence and courtesy fell short. Now consider the rulers and ministers of Zhou. Of the ministers’ attendance at court, it is said, “In their dealings they are never remiss”: their reverence and courtesy were complete. Of their banqueting, it is said, “The Son of Heaven takes their measure”: his sympathetic understanding was comprehensive. This is why ruler and ministers understood one another and brought about the flourishing of Zhou. Even a thousand years later, one can still picture its atmosphere.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“The first year” 〔Duke Yin〕
Zhang Song
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates how a ruler should apply his mind and the transmission of learning [?], and deeply grasps the Sage’s intent in recording the inaugural year. It merits inclusion.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The candidates here cling to ‘the first day’ and ‘the inaugural reckoning’ [?], pairing them with the primal beginnings of Qian and Kun. This composition alone rises above the general lack of understanding.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “In the passage on embodying the primal beginning to rectify the mind, the intent of transmitting antiquity is clearly embedded. A masterful composition.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals uses the beginning of the ruler of Lu’s succession to the throne to make manifest the principle that a ruler must embody the primal beginning. This shows that the Master, in transmitting the ancient sages’ ways and taking their institutions as his model, regarded embodying the primal beginning as a ruler’s duty. How great was his resolve to put the world in order! Moreover, with each stroke of Zhongni’s brush, the significance of the great Sage was at stake. Therefore, he made use of Lu…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
是以修春秋因衰世而立治法乃於隱公即位
之始年不謂之一年而謂之元年者意以嗣位
雖諸侯之常春秋實天子之事彼大哉乾元萬
物資始天之用也至哉坤元萬物資生地之用
也人君成位乎其中則與天地參者也可不體
乾坤之元以為用邪元者何仁是也仁者何心
是也吾覆幬乎天當思所以法天而覆幬乎民
吾持載乎地當思所以則地而持載乎衆以仁
存心以心應物建立萬法酬酢萬事無非此心
===
之運用統馭萬夫統理萬國無非此心之經綸
必也動焉正夫此心靜焉正夫此心而使萬法
萬事莫不咸歸於至正之中語焉正夫此心默
焉正夫此心而使萬夫萬國靡不悉歸至正之
內將見陰陽調而風雨時與乾之始萬物也同
一功群生和而萬民殖與坤之生萬物也同一
化體元之用不其大乎如二帝之所以帝天下
者此元也夫子元年之紀其亦祖述舜典紀元
日之遺意歟三王之所以王天下者此元也夫
punctuated: 是以修《春秋》，因衰世而立治法。乃於隱公即位之始年，不謂之一年而謂之元年者，意以嗣位雖諸侯之常，《春秋》實天子之事。彼大哉乾元，萬物資始，天之用也；至哉坤元，萬物資生，地之用也。人君成位乎其中，則與天地參者也，可不體乾坤之元以為用邪？元者何？仁是也。仁者何？心是也。吾覆幬乎天，當思所以法天而覆幬乎民；吾持載乎地，當思所以則地而持載乎衆。以仁存心，以心應物，建立萬法，酬酢萬事，無非此心之運用；統馭萬夫，統理萬國，無非此心之經綸。必也動焉正夫此心，靜焉正夫此心，而使萬法萬事莫不咸歸於至正之中；語焉正夫此心，默焉正夫此心，而使萬夫萬國靡不悉歸至正之內。將見陰陽調而風雨時，與乾之始萬物也同一功；群生和而萬民殖，與坤之生萬物也同一化。體元之用，不其大乎？如二帝之所以帝天下者，此元也。夫子元年之紀，其亦祖述《舜典》紀元日之遺意歟？三王之所以王天下者，此元也。夫
translation_en:
… Thus he compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, establishing principles of government in response to an age of decline. When he called the opening year of Duke Yin’s accession the “primal year” (yuan nian), rather than the “first year,” his meaning was that, although succession to the throne was an ordinary affair among the feudal lords, the Spring and Autumn Annals was truly the business of the Son of Heaven. “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things depend upon it for their beginning”: this is Heaven’s operation. “Perfect indeed is the primal power of Kun! All things depend upon it for their birth”: this is Earth’s operation. The ruler takes his place between them and thus forms a triad with Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to embody the primal power of Qian and Kun and put it into practice?

What is this primal power? It is benevolence. What is benevolence? It is the heart-mind. Sheltered by Heaven, I should consider how to emulate Heaven in sheltering the people; borne by Earth, I should consider how to model myself on Earth in sustaining the multitude. Preserve the heart-mind through benevolence and respond to things through the heart-mind: establishing all laws and handling all affairs are nothing other than the operation of this heart-mind. Commanding all people and governing all states are nothing other than its ordering work. In activity one must rectify this heart-mind, and in stillness rectify this heart-mind, so that all laws and affairs return to the center of utmost correctness. In speech one must rectify this heart-mind, and in silence rectify this heart-mind, so that all people and states come within the bounds of utmost correctness. Then yin and yang will be in harmony, and wind and rain will arrive in season: this shares the achievement of Qian in initiating all things. All living beings will be harmonious, and the people will flourish: this shares the transforming work of Kun in giving birth to all things. Is not the efficacy of embodying the primal power great?

This primal power was what enabled the Two Emperors to rule All under Heaven as emperors. In recording the “primal year,” was the Master not also transmitting the inherited intention of the Canon of Shun in its record of the “primal day”? This primal power was what enabled the Three Kings to rule All under Heaven as kings. The Master …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
子元年之稱其亦憲章商訓稱元祀之舊章歟
吁德之大者莫大於乾坤用之大者莫大於天
地聖人欲人君體乾坤之德以參天地之用其
致望之意深矣抑論心者人之神明所以具衆
理而應萬事者也堯舜禹以天下相傳首曰人
心惟危道心惟微周公稱乃考文王亦曰克宅
厥心乃立兹常事聖人修春秋亦欲人君以正
心為要前聖後聖異世同符於此亦可驗矣雖
然體元者固人君之職而調元者乃宰相之事
===
此又經國者所當知
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭 同
盟于戲 襄公九年
趙鳴鴻
同考試官教諭劉 批 說鄭恐鄭成而楚
屈如目擊當時行軍之法者可取
考試官教諭朱 批 服鄭所以敝楚褒
恩威斬然且蒼古謹嚴當是作手
punctuated:
子元年之稱，其亦憲章商訓稱元祀之舊章歟？吁！德之大者，莫大於乾坤；用之大者，莫大於天地。聖人欲人君體乾坤之德，以參天地之用，其致望之意深矣！抑論心者，人之神明，所以具衆理而應萬事者也。堯舜禹以天下相傳，首曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微。」周公稱乃考文王，亦曰：「克宅厥心，乃立兹常事。」聖人修《春秋》，亦欲人君以正心為要。前聖後聖，異世同符，於此亦可驗矣。雖然，體元者固人君之職，而調元者乃宰相之事，此又經國者所當知。
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭，同盟于戲。襄公九年。
趙鳴鴻。
同考試官教諭劉批：「說鄭、恐鄭，成而楚屈，如目擊當時行軍之法者，可取。」
考試官教諭朱批：「服鄭所以敝楚，褒恩威斬然，且蒼古謹嚴，當是作手。」
translation_en:
…the Master’s designation of the “first year”: was this likewise modeled on the ancient precedent of calling it the “first sacrificial year” in the Instructions of Shang?
Ah! No virtue is greater than that of Qian and Kun; no operation is greater than that of Heaven and Earth. The sage wished rulers to embody the virtue of Qian and Kun and thereby participate in the workings of Heaven and Earth. How profound were the hopes he placed in them! Now, to discuss the mind: it is the spiritual intelligence of a person, that which possesses the manifold principles and responds to the myriad affairs. When Yao, Shun, and Yu transmitted the realm to one another, their foremost words were: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle.” The Duke of Zhou, speaking of “your deceased father, King Wen,” likewise said: “He could settle his mind, and thus established these enduring affairs.” In compiling the Spring and Autumn Annals, the sage likewise wished rulers to make rectifying the mind their essential concern. That earlier and later sages accorded with one another despite living in different ages can also be verified here. Nevertheless, embodying the primal principle is indeed the ruler’s duty, while harmonizing it is the grand councilor’s responsibility. This, too, is something those who govern the state should understand.
