“The duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, to attack Zheng. They jointly covenanted at Xi.” Ninth year of Duke Xiang.
Zhao Minghong.
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Persuading Zheng and intimidating Zheng: these succeeded, and Chu submitted [?]. It is as though he had witnessed the methods of conducting the campaign at the time. This is commendable.”
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Subduing Zheng was the means of wearing down Chu. His commendation of favor and might is sharply delineated [?]; moreover, his writing is antique in style, careful, and rigorous. He must be an accomplished writer.”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正王批寫悼公用武子之
謀服鄭以駕楚者胷中有兵甲者
觀霸主之於貳國也既用善令以致其從復用
善謀以堅其從于以見悼公能從武子之謀故
不戰而成服鄭之功也觀春秋所書而意自白
矣昔鄭自鄢陵之後而從楚之心益堅晉自次
鄫以來而服鄭之心尤切至是鄭也方及子貞
以為平晉也遂合諸侯以致討夫列辟偕行其
師固為强矣苟非用令之善未必能得鄭之從
===
也幸而悼公獨斷于衷拒荀偃之謀而不用其
號于大眾也命雖不同惟欲振我之威而不使
有意外之虞也其令于列國也詞雖有異惟欲
慰彼之心而不使懷長往之念也不亟亟以迫
其從惟徐徐以致其服由是鄭人恐懼乃遣使
以行成焉然鄭之所以行成於晉者非真有幡
然改圖之心也良由悼公發令之善有以悚動
之耳夫鄭之從晉其跡固可喜矣苟非處之有
道亦未必能得彼之心也幸而悼公廣詢於眾
punctuated:
考試官學正王批：寫悼公用武子之謀，服鄭以駕楚者，胷中有兵甲者。
觀霸主之於貳國也，既用善令以致其從，復用善謀以堅其從，于以見悼公能從武子之謀，故不戰而成服鄭之功也。觀春秋所書，而意自白矣。昔鄭自鄢陵之後，而從楚之心益堅；晉自次鄫以來，而服鄭之心尤切。至是，鄭也方及子貞以為平，晉也遂合諸侯以致討。夫列辟偕行，其師固為强矣；苟非用令之善，未必能得鄭之從也。幸而悼公獨斷于衷，拒荀偃之謀而不用。其號于大眾也，命雖不同，惟欲振我之威，而不使有意外之虞也；其令于列國也，詞雖有異，惟欲慰彼之心，而不使懷長往之念也。不亟亟以迫其從，惟徐徐以致其服。由是鄭人恐懼，乃遣使以行成焉。然鄭之所以行成於晉者，非真有幡然改圖之心也，良由悼公發令之善，有以悚動之耳。夫鄭之從晉，其跡固可喜矣；苟非處之有道，亦未必能得彼之心也。幸而悼公廣詢於眾，
translation_en:
Examiner Wang, School Headmaster, comments: “He depicts Duke Dao employing Wuzi’s strategy to bring Zheng into submission and thereby gain the upper hand over Chu. This is a writer who carries arms and armor within his breast.”
Consider how a hegemon deals with a state of divided allegiance: he first uses well-judged commands to secure its adherence, then employs sound strategy to make that adherence firm. Here we see that Duke Dao could follow Wuzi’s strategy and thus bring Zheng into submission without fighting. Read what the Spring and Autumn Annals records, and the meaning becomes clear of itself. Since the battle of Yanling, Zheng’s determination to follow Chu had grown ever firmer; since encamping at Zeng, Jin’s determination to subdue Zheng had become especially keen. At this point, Zheng had just made peace with Zizhen, and Jin accordingly assembled the feudal lords to mount a punitive expedition. With the various rulers marching together, their army was certainly powerful. Yet without skillfully framed commands, they might not have secured Zheng’s adherence. Fortunately, Duke Dao made his own firm decision and rejected Xun Yan’s proposal. In his proclamations to the assembled host, although the commands differed, his sole aim was to display his own side’s might while guarding against unforeseen dangers. In his orders to the various states, although the wording varied, his sole aim was to reassure them and prevent them from entertaining thoughts of departing for good. He did not press urgently to compel Zheng’s adherence, but proceeded gradually to bring about its submission. The people of Zheng consequently became afraid and sent an envoy to seek peace. Yet Zheng’s reason for seeking peace with Jin was no genuine desire to reverse course and change its plans. It was simply that Duke Dao’s skill in issuing commands had frightened them into action. Zheng’s adherence to Jin was certainly gratifying as an outward act. Yet unless it was handled in the proper way, Jin might still fail to win its sincere allegiance. Fortunately, Duke Dao consulted widely among those assembled…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
□知罃之策而必從大勞未艾非君子之心□
寧休兵以釋鄭不久役以勞乎衆也暴骨以逞
非先王之制也寧還師以敵楚不亟戰以病乎
民也不以戰勝為功惟以謀成為事由是許鄭
之成而使之得與於盟事焉然鄭之所以結成
於晉者非誠有確然不易之心也良由悼公用
謀之善有以感化之耳吁晉之服鄭有道如此
非徒欲服鄭也將以駕楚也鄭既服則楚自屈
矣若悼公者其亦善於安攘者與雖然晉之服
===
鄭駕楚固云善矣然非悼公之謀也乃智武子
之謀也智武子明於善陣之法以佐晉悼公屢
與諸侯伐鄭楚輒救之而不與之戰楚師遂屈
得善勝之道矣故春秋於三駕伐鄭之下而書
蕭魚之會以美之讀是經者屬比而觀則悼公
君臣之善自不容掩矣
禮記
以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟以和夫婦
陳鶚
punctuated:
□知罃之策而必從。大勞未艾，非君子之心□，寧休兵以釋鄭，不久役以勞乎衆也；暴骨以逞，非先王之制也，寧還師以敵楚，不亟戰以病乎民也。不以戰勝為功，惟以謀成為事。由是許鄭之成，而使之得與於盟事焉。然鄭之所以結成於晉者，非誠有確然不易之心也，良由悼公用謀之善，有以感化之耳。吁！晉之服鄭有道如此，非徒欲服鄭也，將以駕楚也。鄭既服，則楚自屈矣。若悼公者，其亦善於安攘者與？雖然，晉之服鄭駕楚，固云善矣，然非悼公之謀也，乃智武子之謀也。智武子明於善陣之法，以佐晉悼公，屢與諸侯伐鄭，楚輒救之，而不與之戰，楚師遂屈，得善勝之道矣。故《春秋》於三駕伐鄭之下，而書蕭魚之會以美之。讀是經者，屬比而觀，則悼公君臣之善，自不容掩矣。

《禮記》
以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以和夫婦。
陳鶚
translation_en:
…[?] Zhi Ying’s strategy and resolved to follow it. To leave great hardship unabated was contrary to the gentleman’s heart [?]; he therefore preferred to rest his troops and release Zheng from pressure, rather than weary the multitude through prolonged service. To leave bones exposed in pursuit of one’s ambitions was contrary to the institutions of the former kings; he therefore preferred to bring his army back and stand against Chu, rather than distress the people with incessant fighting. He regarded victory in battle as no achievement, concerning himself instead with securing peace through strategy. Accordingly, he accepted Zheng’s request for peace and allowed it to participate in the covenant. Yet Zheng’s conclusion of peace with Jin did not mean that it sincerely possessed a firm and unchanging resolve. It was simply that Duke Dao’s skill in employing strategy had moved and transformed it.

Ah! Jin brought Zheng into submission by such proper means, not merely to subdue Zheng, but also to gain mastery over Chu. Once Zheng submitted, Chu would naturally yield. Was not Duke Dao skilled in securing peace within and repelling threats from without? Nevertheless, although Jin’s submission of Zheng and mastery over Chu may indeed be called excellent, the strategy was not Duke Dao’s, but Zhi Wuzi’s. Zhi Wuzi understood the methods of skillful military deployment and used them to assist Duke Dao of Jin. Repeatedly they joined the feudal lords in attacking Zheng. Whenever Chu came to its rescue, they refrained from engaging it in battle, until Chu’s army was finally worn down. Thus they grasped the way of achieving victory skillfully. For this reason, the Spring and Autumn Annals records the meeting at Xiaoyu after the three campaigns against Zheng, thereby praising them. Those who read this classic and examine its entries in relation to one another will find that the excellence of Duke Dao and his minister cannot be obscured.

Book of Rites (Liji)
“To rectify the relations between ruler and minister, to deepen affection between father and son, to foster concord between brothers, and to bring harmony between husband and wife.”
Chen E

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭米批推原聖人與魯蜡
祭有懷古望今之意且文詞爾雅
可佳
考試官學正王批敦禮義以風化天
下亦今日之務也此子能發其意
豈特以文字取之
王者維持大倫一本乎禮義為用焉夫禮義人
之大閑也王者維持大倫舍禮義其何以哉昔
孔子與魯蜡祭而懷古傷今之意謂夫太古之
===
時風俗淳美彞倫攸叙無為之化不可及矣迨
至三代古風漸降不能不以禮義為治焉是故
相臨也而為君臣相親也而為父子此人之大
倫也由是以禮義正乎君臣也則朝廷之上君
以仁臨其下臣以敬事其上截然冠履之分明
矣以禮義篤乎父子也則家庭之内父以慈畜
其子子以孝事其父秩然天倫之分正矣君臣
也父子也一範圍乎禮義之中豈復有相凌相
夷之患哉同一氣而為兄弟合二姓而為夫婦
punctuated:
考試官教諭米批：推原聖人與魯蜡祭，有懷古望今之意，且文詞爾雅，可佳。

考試官學正王批：敦禮義以風化天下，亦今日之務也。此子能發其意，豈特以文字取之？

王者維持大倫，一本乎禮義為用焉。夫禮義，人之大閑也。王者維持大倫，舍禮義其何以哉？昔孔子與魯蜡祭，而懷古傷今之意，謂夫太古之時，風俗淳美，彞倫攸叙，無為之化不可及矣。迨至三代，古風漸降，不能不以禮義為治焉。是故相臨也而為君臣，相親也而為父子，此人之大倫也。由是以禮義正乎君臣也，則朝廷之上，君以仁臨其下，臣以敬事其上，截然冠履之分明矣。以禮義篤乎父子也，則家庭之内，父以慈畜其子，子以孝事其父，秩然天倫之分正矣。君臣也，父子也，一範圍乎禮義之中，豈復有相凌相夷之患哉？同一氣而為兄弟，合二姓而為夫婦，
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Mi, Instructor: He traces the sage’s participation in the year-end zha sacrifice in Lu to its underlying meaning: cherishing antiquity and holding hopes for the present. His language, too, is refined and elegant, and merits praise.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: To strengthen ritual propriety and righteousness and thereby transform the customs of All-under-Heaven is also a task for our own day. This candidate can bring out that meaning. How could we select him merely for his literary skill?

In sustaining the great human relationships, the true king bases his practice entirely upon ritual propriety and righteousness. Ritual propriety and righteousness are the great restraints upon human conduct. Without them, how could the king sustain the great relationships? When Confucius attended the zha sacrifice in Lu, his feelings of longing for antiquity and sorrow over the present concerned this: in remotest antiquity, customs were pure and good, the enduring human relationships were duly ordered, and the transforming influence of rule through nonaction was beyond later ages’ reach. By the time of the Three Dynasties, ancient customs had gradually declined, and rulers could not but govern through ritual propriety and righteousness. Thus, relations of authority constitute those of ruler and minister, and relations of affection constitute those of father and son. These are great human relationships. Accordingly, when ritual propriety and righteousness rectify the relationship between ruler and minister, the ruler at court presides over his subordinates with benevolence, and ministers serve their superior with reverence. The distinction between their stations becomes as clear-cut as that between cap and shoes. When ritual propriety and righteousness deepen the relationship between father and son, the father within the household nurtures his son with kindness, and the son serves his father with filial devotion. The distinctions within this natural relationship are thereby properly ordered. When ruler and minister, father and son, are all kept within the bounds of ritual propriety and righteousness, how could there remain any danger of their encroaching upon or injuring one another? Sharing the same vital breath, they are brothers; joining two surnames, they become husband and wife …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
亦人之大倫也由是以禮義睦乎兄弟則兄友
弟恭而如手如足藹藹乎一塤篪之迭奏也以
禮義和乎夫婦則夫義婦聽如賓如友雝雝乎
一琴瑟之和鳴也兄弟也夫婦也咸維持乎禮
義之內豈復有相戕相褻之患哉孔子因蜡祭
而歷言三王禮義之治如此將有望於魯復興
周道於東歟抑論之大朴散而人心不古若矣
聖王作則以人情為田脩禮以畊之陳義以種
之故耐以天下為一家中國為一人而成大順
===
之治也若治國不以禮義猶無耜而耕耕而弗
種豈能經綸乎天下之大經而成大一統之治
哉有天下國家者不可不知
發號出令而民說謂之和
楊紹軻
考試官教諭米批太和氣象未易形
容此篇詞不費而意自完當是作
手
考試官學正王批題有關於治體此
punctuated:
亦人之大倫也。由是以禮義睦乎兄弟，則兄友弟恭，而如手如足，藹藹乎一塤篪之迭奏也；以禮義和乎夫婦，則夫義婦聽，如賓如友，雝雝乎一琴瑟之和鳴也。兄弟也，夫婦也，咸維持乎禮義之內，豈復有相戕相褻之患哉？孔子因蜡祭而歷言三王禮義之治如此，將有望於魯復興周道於東歟？抑論之，大朴散而人心不古若矣。聖王作，則以人情為田，脩禮以畊之，陳義以種之，故耐以天下為一家，中國為一人，而成大順之治也。若治國不以禮義，猶無耜而耕，耕而弗種，豈能經綸乎天下之大經，而成大一統之治哉？有天下國家者不可不知。

發號出令而民說謂之和
楊紹軻

考試官教諭米批：「太和氣象，未易形容。此篇詞不費而意自完，當是作手。」

考試官學正王批：「題有關於治體，此
translation_en:
…are also among the great human relationships. Thus, when ritual propriety and righteousness foster affection between brothers, the elder is friendly and the younger respectful; they are like hands and feet, their warmth resembling the alternating music of the earthenware ocarina and bamboo flute. When ritual propriety and righteousness bring harmony between husband and wife, the husband acts rightly and the wife heeds him; they treat each other as guests and friends, their concord resembling the harmonious music of the qin and se zithers. When brothers and spouses are all sustained within ritual propriety and righteousness, how could there again be any danger of their injuring or dishonoring one another? On the occasion of the year-end zha sacrifice, Confucius recounted in this way the government through ritual propriety and righteousness of the Three Kings. Was he perhaps hoping that Lu would revive the Way of Zhou in the east?

To consider the matter further: once the great primordial simplicity had dispersed, human hearts were no longer as they had been in antiquity. When sage kings arose, they therefore took human feelings as their field, cultivated ritual propriety to plow it, and set forth righteousness to sow it. Thus they could make all under Heaven one family and the Central States one person, achieving government characterized by great concord. To govern a state without ritual propriety and righteousness is like plowing without a plowshare, or plowing without sowing. How could one thereby order the great guiding relationships of the world and achieve government under a grand unity? Those who possess the realm, a state, or a ruling house must understand this.

“To issue proclamations and commands that please the people is called harmony.”
Yang Shaoke

Comment by Examiner Mi, Instructor: “The atmosphere of supreme harmony is not easily described. This essay conveys its meaning fully without wasting words. Its author must be an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The topic concerns the fundamental principles of government. This …”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
作亦善發揮三復其文知必為佳
士也取之
君命施於上人心順於下此和之所由名也蓋
世道之和必原於民無不悅也自非君命之善
疇克以臻此歟且夫人君以一身而尊居九重
運一心而統理萬化非發號無以新天下之觀
聽也必渙其大號由朝廷以及於閭閻一雷霆
之鼓舞焉非出令無以一天下之心志也必施
其正令自王畿以至於侯甸一天風之播盪焉
===
然號之所發莫非因時制宜而有以合人之情
殆見萬姓交歡舉欣然而有喜色矣令之所出
罔非更化善治而有以得人之心殆見羣黎咸
樂舉油然而生喜意矣夫未易致者民之悅也
苟發號而拂其情則嗟怨日興如乖戾何至難
得者民之悅也苟出令而失其心則愁嘆日滋
如悖戾何故惟大號一發民悅隨之則是四海
之內心既和而氣亦無不和矣太和之化流動
充滿得不謂之和哉正令一施民悅應之則是
punctuated:
作亦善發揮，三復其文，知必為佳士也，取之。

君命施於上，人心順於下，此和之所由名也。蓋世道之和，必原於民無不悅也。自非君命之善，疇克以臻此歟？且夫人君以一身而尊居九重，運一心而統理萬化，非發號無以新天下之觀聽也。必渙其大號，由朝廷以及於閭閻，一雷霆之鼓舞焉；非出令無以一天下之心志也。必施其正令，自王畿以至於侯甸，一天風之播盪焉。然號之所發，莫非因時制宜，而有以合人之情，殆見萬姓交歡，舉欣然而有喜色矣。令之所出，罔非更化善治，而有以得人之心，殆見羣黎咸樂，舉油然而生喜意矣。夫未易致者，民之悅也。苟發號而拂其情，則嗟怨日興，如乖戾何？至難得者，民之悅也。苟出令而失其心，則愁嘆日滋，如悖戾何？故惟大號一發，民悅隨之，則是四海之內，心既和而氣亦無不和矣。太和之化，流動充滿，得不謂之和哉？正令一施，民悅應之，則是
translation_en:
…This composition also develops the subject well. Having read it three times, I know that its author must be a worthy scholar. Accept him.

The ruler’s commands are put into effect above, and the people’s hearts acquiesce below: this is what gives harmony its name. For harmony in the world must have its source in the contentment of all the people. Unless the ruler’s commands are good, who could bring this about? The ruler, in his single person, occupies his exalted place within the ninefold palace gates; exercising his single mind, he governs the myriad transformations. Without issuing proclamations, he has no means of renewing what all under Heaven see and hear. He must therefore broadcast his great proclamations, reaching from the court to the lanes of ordinary households, stirring all alike as thunder does. Without issuing ordinances, he has no means of unifying the hearts and purposes of all under Heaven. He must therefore put his proper ordinances into effect, reaching from the royal domain to the territories of the lords and the outer domains, sweeping through all alike as a wind from Heaven does.

Now, when every proclamation issued makes arrangements suited to the times and accords with the people’s feelings, one may expect to see all the people rejoicing together, each delighted and showing pleasure on their faces. When every ordinance issued reforms governance and improves administration, thereby winning the people’s hearts, one may expect to see the common people all content, each spontaneously feeling joy. The people’s contentment is not easily brought about. If proclamations run counter to their feelings, sighs and grievances will arise daily: what can then be done about such discord? The people’s contentment is exceedingly difficult to secure. If ordinances lose their hearts, sorrow and lamentation will increase daily: what can then be done about such disharmony? Thus, only when a great proclamation is issued and the people’s delight follows it are hearts throughout the Four Seas in harmony, with the vital forces likewise wholly harmonious. The transforming influence of supreme harmony flows everywhere and fills all things: could this fail to be called harmony? Once a proper ordinance is put into effect and the people respond with delight, then…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
允有之間形旣和而聲亦無不和矣至和之妙
薰蒸洋溢豈不謂之和哉吁君命敷於有言之
表人心樂於忘言之天此世道以和而治效所
由盛也抑論太古之春皇以道化民不知號令
為何物自世降而王乃有所謂號令者然當時
之民踴躍惟恐或後夫何後世號令一布而民
疾首蹙額之不暇者何哉盖其法網太密時禁
過嚴惟欲使民戰慄而不容犯故耳求如古之
民悅而和其可得乎噫渙王居无咎此先王號
===
令之初意也君人者其鑒諸
第貳塲
論
仁義人主之術
卓文林
同考試官敎諭劉 批講為術處議論最
正知其人必心術正者行將有官
守言責之寄愼勿以他術雜之
考試官敎諭朱 批通篇渾厚和平了
punctuated:
允有之間，形旣和而聲亦無不和矣。至和之妙，薰蒸洋溢，豈不謂之和哉？吁！君命敷於有言之表，人心樂於忘言之天，此世道以和，而治效所由盛也。抑論太古之春皇，以道化民，不知號令為何物。自世降而王，乃有所謂號令者。然當時之民，踴躍惟恐或後。夫何後世號令一布，而民疾首蹙額之不暇者，何哉？盖其法網太密，時禁過嚴，惟欲使民戰慄而不容犯故耳。求如古之民悅而和，其可得乎？噫！「渙王居，无咎」，此先王號令之初意也。君人者其鑒諸！
第貳塲
論
仁義人主之術
卓文林
同考試官敎諭劉批：講為術處，議論最正，知其人必心術正者。行將有官守言責之寄，愼勿以他術雜之。
考試官敎諭朱批：通篇渾厚和平，了
translation_en:
…within [the realm?; the transcription 允有 is doubtful], outward forms are already harmonious, and sounds too are without disharmony. The wondrous workings of perfect harmony permeate and overflow: how could this not be called harmony? Ah! The ruler’s commands extend beyond what words express, and people’s hearts rejoice in a realm where words are forgotten. Through this, the world becomes harmonious and the achievements of government flourish. Consider, moreover, the Sovereign of Spring [?] in remotest antiquity: he transformed the people through the Way, and they did not know what proclamations and commands were. Only as the ages declined and kings arose did proclamations and commands come into being. Yet the people of that time eagerly responded, fearing only that they might lag behind. Why, then, in later ages, does the mere issuance of a command leave the people overwhelmed with distress and furrowed brows? It is simply because the net of laws is too closely woven and prohibitions imposed from time to time are too severe: rulers wish only to make the people tremble, allowing no infringement. Could one thereby obtain the joy and harmony of the people of antiquity? Alas! “Dispersing the king’s accumulations: no blame”—this was the original intent behind the former kings’ proclamations and commands. Let those who rule others take this as their mirror!
Second Session
Discourse
Benevolence and Righteousness Are the Ruler’s Methods
Zhuo Wenlin
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Where the essay explains these as methods, its argument is most correct; one can tell that its author must be a man whose intentions are upright. Soon he will be entrusted with official duties and the responsibility to speak out. Take care not to adulterate these with other methods.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: The entire piece is substantial, harmonious, and balanced, entirely…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無雕琢委靡之習治世之文固如
是乎錄之足以華國
考試官學正王批詞氣沛然若不竟
其說者昔人謂汪洋大肆决非膚
淺之人其子也乎
論治者必本於德德而能用其全則人主之道
得矣夫天下以一人為主一人以一心為主心
者德之所具而運用之以御天下者也故治本
於德而德貴於全然以全為名則必有所謂偏
===
也德果有偏全乎理得於心渾淪備具而泛應
於外用各不同人之用或不得其全於是本無
偏者始有所謂偏耳是盖仁義之謂也有過於
仁而不知用夫義者有過於義而不知用夫仁
者是豈仁義之過哉用仁義者過之也故仁義
可全也不可過也過則偏矣惟仁也而後可以
悅天下之心惟義也而後可以警天下之心於
一己之全德而並用之久安長治之道在是矣
人主之術尚何有加於此耶今夫仁義之理其
punctuated:
無雕琢委靡之習，治世之文固如是乎！錄之足以華國。

考試官學正王批：詞氣沛然，若不竟其說者。昔人謂汪洋大肆，决非膚淺之人，其子也乎！

論治者必本於德，德而能用其全，則人主之道得矣。夫天下以一人為主，一人以一心為主。心者，德之所具，而運用之以御天下者也。故治本於德，而德貴於全。然以全為名，則必有所謂偏也。德果有偏全乎？理得於心，渾淪備具，而泛應於外，用各不同。人之用或不得其全，於是本無偏者，始有所謂偏耳。是盖仁義之謂也。有過於仁而不知用夫義者，有過於義而不知用夫仁者，是豈仁義之過哉？用仁義者過之也。故仁義可全也，不可過也；過則偏矣。惟仁也，而後可以悅天下之心；惟義也，而後可以警天下之心。於一己之全德而並用之，久安長治之道在是矣。人主之術，尚何有加於此耶？今夫仁義之理，其
translation_en:
…free of the habits of artificial embellishment and feebleness. Surely this is what writing in a well-governed age should be! Its inclusion in this record suffices to bring distinction to the realm.

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Director: His language and spirit flow abundantly, as though his exposition could never be exhausted. The ancients spoke of writing that was vast and freely expansive, the work assuredly of no shallow person. Might you be such a man?

Those who discuss government must ground it in virtue. If virtue can be employed in its entirety, the way of the ruler is attained. All under Heaven takes one man as its master, and that man takes his own heart as his master. The heart is where virtue resides; by putting virtue into operation, it governs all under Heaven. Thus government is grounded in virtue, and what is prized in virtue is its completeness. Yet to speak of completeness necessarily implies something called partiality. Does virtue really admit of partiality and completeness? Principle, apprehended in the heart, is integrally and fully present; yet in responding broadly to external affairs, its applications differ. People may fail to employ it in its entirety. Only then does what was originally without partiality come to exhibit what is called partiality. This refers, indeed, to benevolence and righteousness. Some go too far in benevolence without knowing how to employ righteousness; others go too far in righteousness without knowing how to employ benevolence. Can this be the fault of benevolence and righteousness? It is those who employ them who take them too far. Thus benevolence and righteousness should be fully realized, but must not be carried to excess: excess produces partiality. Only through benevolence can one gladden the hearts of all under Heaven; only through righteousness can one admonish their hearts. To employ both together as aspects of the complete virtue within oneself: herein lies the way to enduring peace and lasting good government. What further art of rulership could surpass this? Now, the principles of benevolence and righteousness—might they …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
本於太極乎太極者陰陽兩端而已天地萬化
生焉所以為天地者不越乎兩端陰陽是也所
以為人者亦不越乎兩端仁義是也試觀諸天
地焉陽既舒矣必繼之以陰陽盖未嘗有所偏
也陰既慘矣必繼之以陽陰亦未嘗有所偏也
天地之德惟其全也故日月星辰水火土石之
體無所變洪纖高下飛潜動植之類無所虧元
會運世歳月日時之運不見其有所斷續天地
於是乎奠位矣人禀夫天地之氣囿於太極之
===
理而人主又父天母地為之子者仁義固其所
具而所以用仁義又其所急人主之仁一天地
之陽舒也人主之義一天地之陰慘也人主之
主乎兆民猶天地之主乎萬物天地主萬物以
陰陽而本於無心人主主萬民以仁義而渉於
有心則經緯之方運用之妙皆謂之術非後世
之所謂智數權謀也即修道之教制用之法也
仁義果足以盡人主之術耶天下亦大矣大川
長谷異制民生其間異俗剛柔輕重遲速異齊
punctuated:
本於太極乎？太極者，陰陽兩端而已，天地萬化生焉。所以為天地者，不越乎兩端，陰陽是也；所以為人者，亦不越乎兩端，仁義是也。試觀諸天地焉：陽既舒矣，必繼之以陰，陽盖未嘗有所偏也；陰既慘矣，必繼之以陽，陰亦未嘗有所偏也。天地之德，惟其全也，故日月星辰、水火土石之體無所變，洪纖高下、飛潜動植之類無所虧，元會運世、歳月日時之運不見其有所斷續，天地於是乎奠位矣。人禀夫天地之氣，囿於太極之理，而人主又父天母地，為之子者，仁義固其所具，而所以用仁義又其所急。人主之仁，一天地之陽舒也；人主之義，一天地之陰慘也。人主之主乎兆民，猶天地之主乎萬物。天地主萬物以陰陽，而本於無心；人主主萬民以仁義，而渉於有心。則經緯之方、運用之妙，皆謂之術，非後世之所謂智數權謀也，即修道之教、制用之法也。
仁義果足以盡人主之術耶？天下亦大矣，大川長谷異制，民生其間異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，
translation_en:
…have their root in the Supreme Ultimate? The Supreme Ultimate consists simply of the two poles, yin and yang; from it arise the myriad transformations of Heaven and Earth. What makes Heaven and Earth what they are does not extend beyond these two poles: yin and yang. What makes human beings what they are likewise does not extend beyond two poles: benevolence and righteousness. Consider Heaven and Earth: once yang has brought forth its gentle warmth, yin must follow it; thus yang has never operated exclusively. Once yin has brought forth its severity, yang must follow it; thus yin, too, has never operated exclusively. It is precisely because the virtue of Heaven and Earth is complete that the forms of sun, moon, stars, water, fire, earth, and stone remain unchanged; the categories of things—large and small, high and low, flying and swimming, moving and rooted—remain undiminished; and the cycles of cosmic epochs, conjunctions, revolutions, and generations, and of years, months, days, and hours, show no interruption. Thus Heaven and Earth take their established places. Human beings receive the vital energy of Heaven and Earth and are encompassed within the principle of the Supreme Ultimate. The ruler, moreover, takes Heaven as his father and Earth as his mother and is their son. Benevolence and righteousness are certainly inherent in him, but how to employ them is his urgent concern. The ruler’s benevolence is one with the gentle warmth of the yang of Heaven and Earth; his righteousness is one with the severity of their yin. His rule over the multitudes is like the rule of Heaven and Earth over the myriad things. Heaven and Earth govern the myriad things through yin and yang, acting fundamentally without conscious intention; the ruler governs the myriad people through benevolence and righteousness, acting with conscious intention. The methods by which he orders affairs and the subtle skill with which he puts them into practice are all called the art of government. This is not what later ages call cunning calculation and expedient scheming; it is the teaching that cultivates the Way and the method that regulates its application.
Are benevolence and righteousness indeed sufficient to encompass the ruler’s entire art of government? The realm is vast indeed. Its great rivers and long valleys differ in configuration, and the people living among them differ in customs. In firmness and gentleness, lightness and gravity, slowness and swiftness, their dispositions differ…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
愛惡相攻而吉凶生遠近相取而悔吝生情偽
相感而利害生於是紛紛者難一也擾擾者難
定也渙散者不可以收拾也獨不有其術乎是
故人心雖衆而操簡御繁者自有其具天下雖
大而以靜制動者自有其規要不出乎仁義而
已人心不離斯可以言治也必其人心自不忍
離而後其合也堅人心不叛斯可以言治也必
其人心自不敢叛而後其服也久仁義者所以
致人心於不忍離不敢叛者也宜舉其全而不
===
可以偏害之也曷為仁惻隱慈愛寛裕溫柔者
是也曷為義發强剛毅嚴威儼恪者是也萬物
一體八荒我闥有仁民愛物有老安少懷有博
施濟衆凡此者皆仁之施也制民之欲防民之
行刑以弼教兵以止亂有親賢遠奸有彰善癉
惡有立綱陳紀凡此者皆義之施也寛大之政
忠厚之風于是乎寓焉操縱之妙闔闢之機于
是乎在焉禮樂刑政皆所以為仁義之具條教
號令皆所以達仁義之施履寶位開明堂所宣
punctuated: 愛惡相攻而吉凶生，遠近相取而悔吝生，情偽相感而利害生。於是紛紛者難一也，擾擾者難定也，渙散者不可以收拾也，獨不有其術乎？是故人心雖衆，而操簡御繁者自有其具；天下雖大，而以靜制動者自有其規。要不出乎仁義而已。人心不離，斯可以言治也；必其人心自不忍離，而後其合也堅。人心不叛，斯可以言治也；必其人心自不敢叛，而後其服也久。仁義者，所以致人心於不忍離、不敢叛者也。宜舉其全，而不可以偏害之也。曷為仁？惻隱慈愛、寛裕溫柔者是也。曷為義？發强剛毅、嚴威儼恪者是也。萬物一體，八荒我闥，有仁民愛物，有老安少懷，有博施濟衆，凡此者皆仁之施也。制民之欲，防民之行，刑以弼教，兵以止亂，有親賢遠奸，有彰善癉惡，有立綱陳紀，凡此者皆義之施也。寛大之政、忠厚之風，于是乎寓焉；操縱之妙、闔闢之機，于是乎在焉。禮樂刑政，皆所以為仁義之具；條教號令，皆所以達仁義之施。履寶位，開明堂，所宣
translation_en:
…Love and hatred contend with one another, giving rise to good and ill fortune; the distant and the near draw upon one another, giving rise to regret and shame; sincerity and deceit interact, giving rise to benefit and harm. Thus the manifold are difficult to unite, the turbulent difficult to settle, and the scattered impossible to gather together. Surely there must be an art for this? Therefore, although the hearts of the people are many, one who grasps the simple to govern the complex has the requisite means; although the realm is vast, one who uses stillness to control movement has the requisite principles. In essence, these extend no further than benevolence and righteousness. When the people's hearts do not turn away, one may speak of good government; yet only when they themselves cannot bear to turn away is their unity firm. When the people's hearts do not rebel, one may speak of good government; yet only when they themselves dare not rebel is their submission lasting. Benevolence and righteousness bring the people's hearts to the point where they cannot bear to turn away and dare not rebel. They should be employed in their entirety, without allowing partiality toward one to impair the whole.

What is benevolence? Compassion and loving kindness, generosity and gentleness. What is righteousness? Vigor and firmness, stern authority and solemn attentiveness. To regard all things as one body and the eight remotest regions as within one's own gates; to be benevolent toward the people and loving toward living things; to give the aged peace and cherish the young; to bestow benefits broadly and aid the multitude—all these are applications of benevolence. To regulate the people's desires and restrain their conduct; to use punishments to support moral instruction and armed force to stop disorder; to draw close to the worthy and distance oneself from the wicked; to commend goodness and chastise evil; to establish guiding principles and set forth rules—all these are applications of righteousness. Generous government and a spirit of loyalty and kindness reside in these; the subtle art of restraining and releasing, and the workings of closing and opening, lie in these. Rites, music, punishments, and government are all instruments of benevolence and righteousness; regulations, instructions, proclamations, and commands all serve to put benevolence and righteousness into effect. Ascending the precious throne and opening the Hall of Light, what the ruler proclaims…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
奉者非仁以育民則義以正民也負斧扆正南
面所申命者非漸民以仁則摩民以義也仁柔
也義剛也剛柔得其宜是即沉潜剛克高明柔
克者矣仁寬也義嚴也寬嚴盡其道是即猛以
濟寬寬以濟猛者矣和氣氤氲甘澤流布人主
之仁風被於四海矣雷霆其威霜雪其厲人主
之義氣昌於九有矣是所謂人主之術也是所
謂用其全而不以偏害之者也由是仁之所及
天下莫不愛義之所及天下莫不畏愛則親上
===
之意油然而興如水之朝宗星之拱極無睂睂
胥讒之態矣畏則尊君之意惕然以靜如風之
偃草臂之運指無敢有越厥志之為矣仁義行
於家家之愛畏同也仁義行於朝朝之愛畏同
也仁義行於國國之愛畏同也仁義行於天下
天下之愛畏同也納六合於範圍之內置宇宙
於把握之中紛紛者以一擾擾者以定渙散者
亦皆會萃而聽命矣災害不生禍亂不作禎祥
以至歌頌以興宗社以安國運以延人主之全
punctuated: 奉者，非仁以育民，則義以正民也。負斧扆，正南面，所申命者，非漸民以仁，則摩民以義也。仁，柔也；義，剛也。剛柔得其宜，是即沉潜剛克、高明柔克者矣。仁，寬也；義，嚴也。寬嚴盡其道，是即猛以濟寬、寬以濟猛者矣。和氣氤氲，甘澤流布，人主之仁風被於四海矣。雷霆其威，霜雪其厲，人主之義氣昌於九有矣。是所謂人主之術也，是所謂用其全而不以偏害之者也。由是仁之所及，天下莫不愛；義之所及，天下莫不畏。愛則親上之意油然而興，如水之朝宗、星之拱極，無睂睂胥讒之態矣。畏則尊君之意惕然以靜，如風之偃草、臂之運指，無敢有越厥志之為矣。仁義行於家，家之愛畏同也；仁義行於朝，朝之愛畏同也；仁義行於國，國之愛畏同也；仁義行於天下，天下之愛畏同也。納六合於範圍之內，置宇宙於把握之中，紛紛者以一，擾擾者以定，渙散者亦皆會萃而聽命矣。災害不生，禍亂不作，禎祥以至，歌頌以興，宗社以安，國運以延，人主之全……
translation_en: …what he upholds is either benevolence for nurturing the people or righteousness for setting them right. With the axe-patterned screen behind him, seated facing south, the commands he issues either imbue the people with benevolence or mold them through righteousness. Benevolence is yielding; righteousness is firm. When firmness and yielding each find their proper application, this is precisely overcoming the retiring and reserved through firmness, and the lofty and assertive through gentleness. Benevolence is lenient; righteousness is stern. When leniency and sternness are fully exercised in accordance with the Way, this is precisely using severity to temper leniency and leniency to temper severity. Harmonious influences gather and beneficent rain spreads: the ruler’s benevolent influence extends throughout the Four Seas. Thunder is his majesty, frost and snow his severity: the ruler’s spirit of righteousness flourishes throughout the nine regions. This is what is called the ruler’s art; this is what is meant by employing it in its entirety without allowing partiality to impair it. Thus, wherever benevolence reaches, none under Heaven fail to love him; wherever righteousness reaches, none under Heaven fail to hold him in awe. Love spontaneously awakens the desire to draw close to one’s superior, like waters flowing toward the sea or stars clustering around the Pole Star; there is no disposition to mutual slander [?]. Awe brings the desire to honor the sovereign into vigilant stillness, like grass bending before the wind or an arm moving its fingers; none dare act contrary to his will. When benevolence and righteousness are practiced within the family, all in the family share this love and awe; when practiced at court, all at court share this love and awe; when practiced in the state, all in the state share this love and awe; when practiced throughout all under Heaven, all under Heaven share this love and awe. The six directions are brought within his compass, and the universe is placed within his grasp. The divided are thereby united, the unsettled are thereby pacified, and even the scattered all gather together and obey his commands. Disasters do not arise, calamity and disorder do not break out, auspicious signs arrive, songs of praise arise, the ancestral temples and altars of state are secured, and the state’s allotted span is prolonged. The ruler’s completeness…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
德致功用之盛有如是夫三代之君若相授受
然者故拯昏墊泣罪人禹之仁也而塗山之會
防風之戮非其義乎解網祝禽自責禱旱湯之
仁也而十一國之征南巢之舉非其義乎不侮
鰥寡重民五教文武之仁也而遏徂莒之衆興
弔伐之師非文武之義乎開創者以是而作於
先守成者以是而為於後是以祚運靈長四百
載於夏六百載於殷八百載於周享國之福鮮
克儷矣後世如漢之文帝恬靜玄默慈祥淡泊
===
可謂有仁矣而風流篤厚禁網疏闊似有過於
仁宣帝之綜核名實信賞必罰可謂有義矣而
刑名之苛誅戮之頻則有過於義是又得其一
而遺其二者也夫過於仁者姑息緩縱而猶不
失為寬厚長者之風過於義者迫促褊急而未
免有慘刻少恩之失夫人未始不生於優游閑
易而困於束縛馳驟者也故仁可過也義不可
過也與其為宣帝之義莫如為文帝之仁與其
為文帝之仁又莫如為禹湯文武仁義兼隆而
punctuated:
德致功用之盛，有如是夫！三代之君若相授受然者。故拯昏墊、泣罪人，禹之仁也；而塗山之會、防風之戮，非其義乎？解網祝禽、自責禱旱，湯之仁也；而十一國之征、南巢之舉，非其義乎？不侮鰥寡、重民五教，文武之仁也；而遏徂莒之衆、興弔伐之師，非文武之義乎？開創者以是而作於先，守成者以是而為於後。是以祚運靈長，四百載於夏，六百載於殷，八百載於周，享國之福鮮克儷矣。
後世如漢之文帝，恬靜玄默，慈祥淡泊，可謂有仁矣；而風流篤厚，禁網疏闊，似有過於仁。宣帝之綜核名實，信賞必罰，可謂有義矣；而刑名之苛、誅戮之頻，則有過於義。是又得其一而遺其二者也。夫過於仁者，姑息緩縱，而猶不失為寬厚長者之風；過於義者，迫促褊急，而未免有慘刻少恩之失。夫人未始不生於優游閑易，而困於束縛馳驟者也。故仁可過也，義不可過也。與其為宣帝之義，莫如為文帝之仁；與其為文帝之仁，又莫如為禹湯文武仁義兼隆而
translation_en:
…virtue and bring about such abundant achievements! The rulers of the Three Dynasties seemed to transmit these principles from one to another. Thus, rescuing people from the engulfing flood and weeping over offenders exemplified Yu’s benevolence; were the assembly at Tushan and the execution of Fangfeng not expressions of his righteousness? Loosening the hunting nets and offering a prayer for the birds, blaming himself and praying for relief from drought exemplified Tang’s benevolence; were his campaigns against eleven states and his expedition to Nanchao not expressions of his righteousness? Not mistreating widowers and widows, and attaching importance to the people’s instruction in the five moral relationships exemplified the benevolence of Kings Wen and Wu; were restraining the host advancing toward Ju [?] and raising an army to console the people and punish their oppressors not expressions of their righteousness? Those who founded dynasties acted upon these principles first; those who preserved their achievements followed them afterward. Thus their dynastic fortunes endured: four hundred years for Xia, six hundred for Yin, and eight hundred for Zhou. Few could match their good fortune in possessing the realm.
Among later rulers, Emperor Wen of Han was calm and quiet, reserved and taciturn, kindly and free from extravagant desires. He could be said to possess benevolence. Yet the prevailing customs were earnest and generous, and the net of prohibitions was loosely drawn: he seems to have carried benevolence too far. Emperor Xuan comprehensively scrutinized whether actual performance matched nominal responsibilities, reliably rewarded merit, and invariably punished wrongdoing. He could be said to possess righteousness. Yet the severity of his penal administration and the frequency of executions carried righteousness too far. These, again, were men who attained one aspect but neglected the other [literally, “the second”]. Those who carry benevolence too far indulge others and are lax in restraint, yet still retain the manner of a generous and kindly elder. Those who carry righteousness too far are overbearing, narrow-minded, and impatient, and cannot avoid the fault of cruelty and scant kindness. People invariably thrive amid ease and freedom from trouble, but suffer under restraints and incessant demands. Thus benevolence may be carried to excess, but righteousness must not be. Rather than practice Emperor Xuan’s righteousness, it is better to practice Emperor Wen’s benevolence; yet rather than practice Emperor Wen’s benevolence, it is better still to emulate Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, in whom benevolence and righteousness flourished together, and…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
人古世治效淺深享國久近盖有明效為治者
奚知所擇耶後世之君莫不欲天下之治智不
出此昧其術而為之或欲富國或欲强兵或欲
設險守國或欲粉飾治具而於人心之愛畏漫
不知省故雖采章文物不足以為盛金城湯池
不足以為固帶甲組練不足以為勇紅腐貫朽
不足以為富治亂相尋否泰相仍未有極也是
不得其為術故也雖然仁義固人主之術人主
之仁義亦有未易言者必有是德而後有是事
非聲音笑貌可得而為之苟無實德於中則假
仁之名亦足以違道而干百姓之譽假義之名
亦足以拂百姓從已之欲然矯誣之行自不可
掩虚誕之事尚何克有終乎人主欲行仁義其
亦本之於誠存誠之功又在於靜存動察去聲
色貨利之欲絶便嬖諛佞之徒親賢人君子以
養其本然之天則本深末茂實大聲宏言行政
事之間無適而非仁義是知仁義為人主之術
而存誠又為仁義之術
punctuated:
人古世治效淺深、享國久近，盖有明效，為治者奚知所擇耶？後世之君莫不欲天下之治，智不出此，昧其術而為之，或欲富國，或欲强兵，或欲設險守國，或欲粉飾治具，而於人心之愛畏漫不知省。故雖采章文物不足以為盛，金城湯池不足以為固，帶甲組練不足以為勇，紅腐貫朽不足以為富。治亂相尋，否泰相仍，未有極也，是不得其為術故也。
雖然，仁義固人主之術，人主之仁義亦有未易言者。必有是德而後有是事，非聲音笑貌可得而為之。苟無實德於中，則假仁之名，亦足以違道而干百姓之譽；假義之名，亦足以拂百姓從已之欲。然矯誣之行自不可掩，虚誕之事尚何克有終乎？人主欲行仁義，其亦本之於誠。存誠之功，又在於靜存動察，去聲色貨利之欲，絶便嬖諛佞之徒，親賢人君子，以養其本然之天，則本深末茂，實大聲宏，言行政事之間，無適而非仁義。是知仁義為人主之術，而存誠又為仁義之術。
translation_en:
…[The opening characters are unclear: 人古世.] The degree of success in bringing about good government and the length of a dynasty’s tenure provide clear evidence. How could those who govern know what to choose [?]? Every ruler of later ages desired order in the realm, yet their understanding did not extend beyond this. Ignorant of the proper method, they acted: some sought to enrich the state, some to strengthen its armies, some to establish strategic defenses to safeguard it, and some to embellish the outward apparatus of government. Yet they gave no thought to examining what wins the people’s love and inspires their awe. Thus, splendid insignia and cultural institutions do not suffice for greatness; metal-like ramparts and moats like boiling water do not suffice for security; armored troops and ranks clad in silk armor do not suffice for valor; grain stored until it reddens and rots, and cash hoarded until its strings decay, do not suffice for wealth. Order and disorder succeed one another, adversity and prosperity follow in turn, without end. This is because they have failed to grasp the proper method.
Nevertheless, although benevolence and righteousness are indeed the ruler’s method, the ruler’s benevolence and righteousness are not easy to discuss. Only when one possesses these virtues can one perform the corresponding deeds; they cannot be achieved merely through tone of voice, smiles, and facial expressions. If there is no genuine virtue within, invoking the name of benevolence can serve to violate the Way and court the people’s praise; invoking the name of righteousness can serve to thwart the people and indulge one’s own desires. Yet deceitful conduct cannot remain concealed. How could empty and fraudulent undertakings ever reach a successful conclusion? If a ruler wishes to practice benevolence and righteousness, he must ground them in sincerity. The work of preserving sincerity, in turn, lies in maintaining it in stillness and examining oneself in action, removing desires for music, sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit, severing ties with favorites and flattering sycophants, and drawing close to worthy men and gentlemen, thereby nourishing his inherent Heaven-given nature. Then the roots will be deep and the branches luxuriant; substantial inner virtue will bring far-reaching renown. In speech, conduct, administration, and affairs, there will be nothing that is not benevolent and righteous. Thus we know that benevolence and righteousness are the ruler’s method, while preserving sincerity is itself the method for achieving benevolence and righteousness.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
表
擬纂修
孝宗敬皇帝實錄成
進呈表
董雲漢
同考試官教諭劉批表擬
實錄豈是淺易題目子能優爲之高于人矣
考試官教諭朱批寫出
先帝聖德神功萬世共見豈直應試之文
===
考試官學正王批錦綺成章咸韶協
律表之佳者
伏以
二典首經仰見唐虞之致治四詩兼史爰
徵文武之興邦匪由簡冊之傳曷覩
帝王之盛肇初於古大備於今惟
先皇之功德難名在
嗣聖之孝思罔極心存盛事天啓斯文既成編
述之功當謹
punctuated:
表
擬纂修《孝宗敬皇帝實錄》成進呈表。
董雲漢。
同考試官教諭劉批：「表擬實錄，豈是淺易題目？子能優爲之，高于人矣。」
考試官教諭朱批：「寫出先帝聖德神功，萬世共見，豈直應試之文？」
考試官學正王批：「錦綺成章，咸韶協律，表之佳者。」
伏以：二典首經，仰見唐虞之致治；四詩兼史，爰徵文武之興邦。匪由簡冊之傳，曷覩帝王之盛？肇初於古，大備於今。惟先皇之功德難名，在嗣聖之孝思罔極。心存盛事，天啓斯文。既成編述之功，當謹
translation_en:
Memorial
A simulated memorial presenting the completed Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong Jing.
By Dong Yunhan.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor: “A simulated memorial concerning the Veritable Records—how could this be a shallow or easy topic? You have handled it admirably, surpassing others.”

Comment by Examiner Zhu, an Instructor: “It portrays the late emperor’s sagely virtue and divine achievements for all generations to behold. How could it be merely an examination composition?”

Comment by Examiner Wang, an Instructor: “Brocaded splendor forms its composition; the Xianchi and Shao music harmonize with the pitch standards. An excellent memorial.”

We humbly submit: The two Canons stand at the head of the Classic of Documents, allowing us reverently to behold the perfected governance of Tang and Yu. The four divisions of the Classic of Poetry also serve as history, attesting to how Kings Wen and Wu brought their state to greatness. Without transmission through written records, how could we behold the splendor of emperors and kings? This practice began in antiquity and has attained full elaboration today. The late emperor’s achievements and virtues defy description; the succeeding sage sovereign’s filial devotion knows no bounds. His heart cherishes this splendid undertaking, and Heaven has inspired this literary work. Now that the work of compilation has been accomplished, we should reverently…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
進呈之舉
一人繼志
九廟增光恭惟
孝宗建天明道誠純中正聖文神武至仁大德
敬皇帝天縱之資生知之聖
青宮育德儲前星少海之祥
紫極御天膺出震繼離之責追先王之逸駕幸
太學而耕籍田驅當代之異端放法王而
流佛子聖經賢傳每資乙夜之觀竒獸珍
===
禽旋罷四方之獻敦儉約以先臣庶辨誠
邪以治身心視膳問安隆
重闈之大孝保邦圖治纘
皇祖之詒謀議
祧祫而深仁大義之無偏建
皇儲而早定豫教之有則奠玉帛於
郊祀誠敬格
天收賢才於制科英雄入彀一念絕遊畋之好
萬幾躬宵旰之勤
punctuated:
進呈之舉。一人繼志，九廟增光。
恭惟孝宗建天明道誠純中正聖文神武至仁大德敬皇帝，天縱之資，生知之聖。青宮育德，儲前星少海之祥；紫極御天，膺出震繼離之責。追先王之逸駕，幸太學而耕籍田；驅當代之異端，放法王而流佛子。聖經賢傳，每資乙夜之觀；竒獸珍禽，旋罷四方之獻。敦儉約以先臣庶，辨誠邪以治身心。視膳問安，隆重闈之大孝；保邦圖治，纘皇祖之詒謀。議祧祫而深仁大義之無偏，建皇儲而早定豫教之有則。奠玉帛於郊祀，誠敬格天；收賢才於制科，英雄入彀。一念絕遊畋之好，萬幾躬宵旰之勤；
translation_en:
…the act of respectfully presenting it to the throne. The sovereign carries forward his predecessor’s intentions; the nine ancestral temples gain added glory.
We reverently reflect that Emperor Xiaozong—Reverent Emperor Who Established Heaven’s Order and Illuminated the Way, Sincere and Pure, Central and Upright, Sagely in Civil Accomplishment and Divine in Martial Prowess, Supremely Benevolent and Great in Virtue—possessed Heaven-bestowed gifts and the wisdom of a sage who knows from birth. Nurturing his virtue in the crown prince’s palace, he embodied the auspicious promise of the Crown Prince’s Star and the Lesser Sea. Upon ascending the imperial throne, he assumed the responsibility of emerging as the eldest son and continuing the imperial radiance, as figured by the trigrams Zhen and Li. He followed the swift chariots of the former kings, visiting the Imperial University and plowing the imperial ritual field. He expelled the heterodox teachings of his age, banishing the Dharma Kings and exiling the Sons of Buddha. The sages’ classics and the worthies’ commentaries regularly furnished his reading during the second watch of the night; he promptly discontinued the presentation of exotic beasts and rare birds from every quarter. He cultivated frugality to set an example for officials and commoners, and distinguished sincerity from perversity to discipline his person and mind. Attending to meals and inquiring after health, he displayed profound filial devotion toward the senior generations in the palace. Safeguarding the realm and striving for good government, he carried forward the plans bequeathed by his imperial ancestors. In deliberating upon the removal of ancestral tablets and the collective ancestral sacrifice, his profound benevolence and great righteousness were impartial. In establishing the imperial heir, he settled the succession early and provided orderly instruction in advance. He offered jade and silk at the suburban sacrifices, his sincerity and reverence reaching Heaven. He recruited worthy talent through the state examinations, bringing outstanding men within his bow’s range. His mind wholly renounced a taste for excursions and hunting; amid the myriad affairs of government, he personally labored from before dawn until late in the day…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
大問公卿欲究太平之績優容臺諫盡聞忠
讜之言降絲綸而愛惜人材設警蹕而親
裁獄訟處
朝廷
宮闈一皆王道之公遇
后戚
宗藩不為私恩之繋録開國元勲之後盟續
河山增孔庭從祀之賢禮加籩豆脩
大明會典昭邦家治世之規崇安國春秋示學
者明經之要小人不敢以傷善類邪慝不
得以亂正經豈惟文事之輝煌抑且武功
之赫奕
臨軒遣將再摧北虜之鋒
下詔出師兩掃南蠻之穴猺獞屢征於嶺海苗
民薄伐於洞庭寰宇清寧
皇風敷暢億兆同聲而作頌蠻夷重譯以来王
豈意玉几就憑龍髯莫挽遽歛萬年之慶
聿興九有之思
punctuated:
大問公卿，欲究太平之績；優容臺諫，盡聞忠讜之言。降絲綸而愛惜人材，設警蹕而親裁獄訟。處朝廷、宮闈，一皆王道之公；遇后戚、宗藩，不為私恩之繋。録開國元勲之後，盟續河山；增孔庭從祀之賢，禮加籩豆。脩《大明會典》，昭邦家治世之規；崇安國《春秋》，示學者明經之要。小人不敢以傷善類，邪慝不得以亂正經。豈惟文事之輝煌，抑且武功之赫奕！

臨軒遣將，再摧北虜之鋒；下詔出師，兩掃南蠻之穴。猺獞屢征於嶺海，苗民薄伐於洞庭。寰宇清寧，皇風敷暢。億兆同聲而作頌，蠻夷重譯以来王。豈意玉几就憑，龍髯莫挽，遽歛萬年之慶，聿興九有之思！
translation_en:
…He consulted widely with the highest ministers, seeking to bring the achievements of Great Peace to completion; he treated the censors and remonstrance officials with forbearance, hearing all their loyal and forthright counsel. He issued imperial pronouncements cherishing men of talent, and, with the ceremonial warnings announcing his presence, personally adjudicated legal cases. In his conduct at court and within the palace, all accorded with the impartiality of the kingly Way; in his treatment of the empress’s relatives and the imperial princes, he was not bound by private favor. He recognized the descendants of the dynasty’s founding heroes, renewing pledges enduring as the Yellow River and the mountains. He added worthy men to those receiving associated sacrifices in Confucius’s temple, extending to them the offerings in ritual vessels. He compiled the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming, making manifest the state’s rules for orderly government; he honored Anguo’s commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, showing scholars the essentials of understanding the classics. Petty men dared not harm the worthy, and the wicked could not corrupt the orthodox classics. Not only were his civil achievements resplendent; his military accomplishments were also magnificent!

He appeared in state to dispatch generals, twice blunting the northern foes’ advance; he issued edicts sending forth armies, twice sweeping away the southern Man peoples’ strongholds. Campaigns repeatedly subdued the Yao and Zhuang in the Linghai region, and punitive expeditions struck the Miao people around Dongting. All under heaven was peaceful and tranquil, and imperial influence spread freely. The countless multitudes raised songs of praise with one voice, while distant peoples came through successive interpreters to acknowledge his sovereignty. Who could have imagined that he would come to lean upon the jade armrest of his deathbed, and that none could grasp the dragon’s beard to hold him back? Suddenly the blessings hoped to last ten thousand years were brought to an end, awakening longing throughout the nine regions!

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
皇上雖在諒陰謹求典禮用鋪張於
德業將永久於乾坤乃
召儒臣弘開史舘處鳳閣鸞坡之禁紬木天
金匱之藏既分檢於諸司尤博求於四海
奏牘具在卷帙咸登浩若烟雲炳如星日
窮探極索悉巨細以無遺並蓄兼收盡始
終以備載系月編年而標題循序左言右
事而會萃同歸幸巳卒編庶幾脫藁錄盡
當時之實書成一代之全十八年之繼體
===
守文五百歲之本支應運摹
天地而繪日月其曷能之窮造化而亘古今不
可尚已伏願
羹墻在念常懷
謨烈之光
夙夜惟勤永保雍熈之治臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所修
實錄若干卷隨表上
punctuated: 皇上雖在諒陰，謹求典禮，用鋪張於德業，將永久於乾坤。乃召儒臣，弘開史舘，處鳳閣鸞坡之禁，紬木天金匱之藏。既分檢於諸司，尤博求於四海。奏牘具在，卷帙咸登，浩若烟雲，炳如星日。窮探極索，悉巨細以無遺；並蓄兼收，盡始終以備載。系月編年而標題循序，左言右事而會萃同歸。幸巳卒編，庶幾脫藁。錄盡當時之實，書成一代之全。十八年之繼體守文，五百歲之本支應運。摹天地而繪日月，其曷能之？窮造化而亘古今，不可尚已。伏願羹墻在念，常懷謨烈之光；夙夜惟勤，永保雍熈之治。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所修實錄若干卷隨表上
translation_en:
Although Your Majesty was in mourning, you conscientiously sought out the prescribed rites, to proclaim the late emperor’s virtue and achievements and preserve them forever between Heaven and Earth. You therefore summoned Confucian officials and opened wide the Historiography Office, housing it within the palace precincts of the Phoenix Pavilion and the Luan Terrace, and drawing upon the collections of the imperial library and its golden coffers. Documents were sought separately from the various offices and, more broadly still, throughout the realm. Memorials were all available, and volumes were all brought in: vast as clouds and mist, brilliant as stars and sun. We searched exhaustively, omitting nothing great or small; we gathered comprehensively, recording everything from beginning to end. Events were arranged by year and month, with headings in sequence; words and deeds, recorded by the scribes of the left and right, were brought together into a single whole. Fortunately, compilation is now complete, and the draft is at last ready. The record exhausts the facts of the time, forming a complete account of one reign: eighteen years of succeeding to the throne and preserving the inherited institutions, and a lineage whose main stem and branches answered the destiny that comes once in five hundred years. How could we portray Heaven and Earth or depict the sun and moon? His accomplishments encompassed the workings of creation and extended across past and present; they cannot be surpassed.

We humbly pray that you keep him in mind, as though seeing him in your soup and upon the wall, and always cherish the radiance of his counsels and achievements; that you remain diligent morning and night, forever preserving harmonious and prosperous government. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with feelings of utmost fervor and trembling reverence. We respectfully submit, together with this memorial, the Veritable Records we have compiled, in so many juan…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
進以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
王璽
同考試官教諭程批能言我
祖宗之所以盛而於
聖製又條答無遺足見學識
===
同考試官教諭杜批
本朝為天地循環之初氣惟
聖祖言之子能發揮其說盖凡民中豪傑者
考試官教諭朱批此問欲觀士子知
列聖道冠百王處答者千百莫喻其旨子獨得
之敬錄以詔天下
考試官學正王批此策關涉最大子
能條答詳明在末場文字中猶五
緯麗天芒寒色正者也
punctuated:
進以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
王璽

同考試官教諭程批：能言我祖宗之所以盛，而於聖製又條答無遺，足見學識。

同考試官教諭杜批：本朝為天地循環之初氣，惟聖祖言之。子能發揮其說，盖凡民中豪傑者。

考試官教諭朱批：此問欲觀士子知列聖道冠百王處，答者千百莫喻其旨，子獨得之，敬錄以詔天下。

考試官學正王批：此策關涉最大，子能條答詳明，在末場文字中，猶五緯麗天、芒寒色正者也。
translation_en:
…submitted for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Wang Xi

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: You can explain why our imperial ancestors attained such greatness, and you also respond point by point to the imperial composition, omitting nothing. This amply demonstrates your learning and discernment.

Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: That our dynasty embodies the primal qi at the beginning of the cycle of Heaven and Earth was declared by the sagely founder alone. You can elucidate his explanation and are surely an outstanding man among the common people.

Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: This question seeks to see whether candidates understand wherein the Way of our successive sage emperors surpasses that of all former kings. Among the hundreds and thousands who answered, none understood its purport; you alone grasped it. We respectfully record your answer to make it known throughout the realm.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: This policy question touches upon matters of the greatest importance. You answer point by point with detail and clarity. Among the writings of the final session, yours is like the five planets shining in the heavens, their rays crisp and their colors true.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
有天地循環之大運有
聖人御世之全功夫天道人事未始不相關也
而况聖人之於世功用之偏全夫豈偶然
之故哉造化之意盖有黙行乎其間者於
此有以知堯舜之文或缺孔子之位不遇
豈固有待於我
列聖之出盡發而全畀之也歟請試陳之自鴻
荒既遠人文以宣君師之道不可不寄之
於人也天故篤生聖人以為之主功用之
===
大非一人兼總之也必歷數聖人而後得
其全盖文明之漸氣運然也堯舜雖不待
於文而有以盡君之道孔子雖不待於位
而有以盡師之道然亦天有以不足之焉
先民有言堯舜以上道之元堯舜以下道
之亨洙泗魯鄒道之利濂洛關閩道之貞
造化之盛氣為之一終而君師之道息矣
於是元以夷狄亂華人紀絶滅成開闢所
無之禍為天地莫大之汚夫不有大亂則
punctuated:
有天地循環之大運，有聖人御世之全功。夫天道人事，未始不相關也，而况聖人之於世，功用之偏全，夫豈偶然之故哉？造化之意，盖有黙行乎其間者。於此有以知堯舜之文或缺，孔子之位不遇，豈固有待於我列聖之出，盡發而全畀之也歟？請試陳之。
自鴻荒既遠，人文以宣，君師之道不可不寄之於人也。天故篤生聖人以為之主。功用之大，非一人兼總之也，必歷數聖人而後得其全，盖文明之漸，氣運然也。堯舜雖不待於文而有以盡君之道，孔子雖不待於位而有以盡師之道，然亦天有以不足之焉。先民有言：堯舜以上，道之元；堯舜以下，道之亨；洙泗魯鄒，道之利；濂洛關閩，道之貞。造化之盛氣，為之一終，而君師之道息矣。於是元以夷狄亂華，人紀絶滅，成開闢所無之禍，為天地莫大之汚。夫不有大亂，則
translation_en:
There is the great cycle of Heaven and Earth, and there is the complete achievement of sages in governing the world. The Way of Heaven and human affairs have never been unrelated. How, then, could it be mere chance that the achievements of sages in the world are partial or complete? The intent of the creative transformations surely operates silently within this process. From this we may understand why the cultural accomplishments of Yao and Shun were in some respects incomplete, and why Kongzi did not obtain his proper position. Was this indeed awaiting the emergence of our succession of sage emperors, so that these capacities might be fully manifested and bestowed upon them in their entirety? Allow me to set this forth.
As the primeval age receded into the distant past and human culture unfolded, the Way of ruler and teacher necessarily had to be entrusted to human beings. Heaven therefore brought forth sages to preside over it. The greatness of their achievements could not be encompassed by any single person: only through a succession of sages could completeness be attained. That civilization advanced by stages was the consequence of the cycles of cosmic vital force. Although Yao and Shun could fulfill the Way of the ruler without relying on cultural elaboration, and Kongzi could fulfill the Way of the teacher without relying on official position, Heaven nevertheless left each deficient in some respect. Our predecessors have said: in the time of Yao and Shun and before, the Way was in its phase of origination; after Yao and Shun, in its phase of flourishing; at Zhu and Si, Lu and Zou, in its phase of benefit; and at Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, in its phase of constancy. The abundant vital force of the creative transformations thus completed a cycle, and the Way of ruler and teacher ceased. Thereupon the Yuan, through the barbarians, threw Chinese civilization into disorder. The principles of human relations were extinguished, producing a calamity without precedent since the opening of Heaven and Earth, and the greatest defilement of Heaven and Earth. For without great disorder, then …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
不足以有終不有大治則不足以為始故
剥盡而復貞下起元我
太祖高皇帝取帝王之中國以自立掃宇宙之
腥膻於一空自謂當天地循環之初氣於
御製閱江樓記發之大哉
王言真有以知造化之有在也
皇祖開天於前則有大誥三編
太宗文皇帝
宣宗章皇帝繼統於後則有為善陰隲孝順事
===
實五倫書是則我
朝為大治之朝
列聖為大全之聖君師之道齊堯舜而兼孔子
者不有在於斯乎凡我臣民何幸遭其盛
也
奎璧麗於層霄光輝被於下土萬世共覩而
齊聞者宏綱大要其有不知者耶
大誥之布凡三屢出不厭者以善良率教而
凶頑梗化也丁寧不已者無非善可為法
punctuated:
不足以有終，不有大治，則不足以為始。故剥盡而復，貞下起元。我太祖高皇帝取帝王之中國以自立，掃宇宙之腥膻於一空，自謂當天地循環之初氣，於御製《閱江樓記》發之。大哉，王言！真有以知造化之有在也。
皇祖開天於前，則有《大誥》三編；太宗文皇帝、宣宗章皇帝繼統於後，則有《為善陰隲》《孝順事實》《五倫書》。是則我朝為大治之朝，列聖為大全之聖，君師之道齊堯舜而兼孔子者，不有在於斯乎？凡我臣民，何幸遭其盛也！
奎璧麗於層霄，光輝被於下土，萬世共覩而齊聞者，宏綱大要，其有不知者耶？
《大誥》之布凡三，屢出不厭者，以善良率教而凶頑梗化也。丁寧不已者，無非善可為法
translation_en:
…there could be no completion; without great order, there could be no beginning. Thus, when Stripping Away is exhausted, Return follows; beneath the phase of consummation, a new beginning arises. Our founding emperor, Taizu Gao, took possession of the Central Kingdom of the ancient emperors and kings and established his rule, utterly sweeping away the rank stench that filled the universe. He described himself as living at the first stirring of vital energy in a new cycle of Heaven and Earth, expressing this in his imperially composed Record of the River-Viewing Tower. How great are these royal words! They truly show an understanding of where the workings of cosmic transformation reside.
Our imperial ancestor inaugurated a new heaven at the outset, producing the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements. Emperor Taizong Wen and Emperor Xuanzong Zhang subsequently succeeded to the imperial line, producing Doing Good and Hidden Virtue, True Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience, and the Book of the Five Human Relationships. Thus our dynasty is a dynasty of great order, and its successive sage emperors are sages of complete perfection. Is it not here that their fulfillment of the Way of ruler and teacher equals that of Yao and Shun while also encompassing that of Confucius? How fortunate all of us, subjects and people alike, are to live amid such flourishing greatness!
The Kui and Bi constellations shine in the heavens above, their radiance spreading over the earth below. As for the broad principles and essential points that all generations alike behold and hear, could anyone remain ignorant of them?
The Grand Pronouncements were issued three times in all. Their repeated issuance without weariness was because the good and upright followed the teachings, while the wicked and obstinate resisted moral transformation. The unceasing earnest admonitions all concern how goodness can serve as a model…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而惡可為戒也首編為目七十有四首君
臣同遊而終之以頒行
大誥續編為目八十有七首申明五常而終
之以頒行
續誥三編為目四十有三首臣民倚法為奸
而終之以頒行
三誥
為善陰隲治獄而能活人者雖非一人何比
干之存活數千乃為其尤用兵而能活人
===
者亦非一人曹彬之不妄殺人則為最顯
設瓜餉客而孫鍾之後王吳編竹渡蟻而
宋郊之第首選是其一念之仁雖形於細
故而存心之厚必不忽於終身冥冥之報
夫豈爽耶
孝順事實帝王之孝則虞舜文王武王漢文
是也公卿之孝狄仁傑崔玄暐張九齡廉
希憲是也高登之孝忠李植之孝義曰忠
曰義固由於孝之推郭全之孝友庾氏之
punctuated:
而惡可為戒也。首編為目七十有四，首「君臣同遊」，而終之以「頒行大誥」。續編為目八十有七，首「申明五常」，而終之以「頒行續誥」。三編為目四十有三，首「臣民倚法為奸」，而終之以「頒行三誥」。
《為善陰隲》：治獄而能活人者，雖非一人，何比干之存活數千，乃為其尤；用兵而能活人者，亦非一人，曹彬之不妄殺人，則為最顯。設瓜餉客，而孫鍾之後王吳；編竹渡蟻，而宋郊之第首選。是其一念之仁，雖形於細故，而存心之厚，必不忽於終身。冥冥之報，夫豈爽耶？
《孝順事實》：帝王之孝，則虞舜、文王、武王、漢文是也；公卿之孝，狄仁傑、崔玄暐、張九齡、廉希憲是也。高登之孝忠，李植之孝義，曰忠曰義，固由於孝之推。郭全之孝友，庾氏之
translation_en:
…and evil can serve as a warning. The first compilation contains seventy-four sections, beginning with “Ruler and Ministers Roaming Together” and ending with “Promulgating the Grand Pronouncement.” The continuation contains eighty-seven sections, beginning with “Elucidating the Five Constant Virtues” and ending with “Promulgating the Continued Pronouncement.” The third compilation contains forty-three sections, beginning with “Subjects Exploiting the Law to Commit Wrongdoing” and ending with “Promulgating the Third Pronouncement.”
Doing Good and Hidden Blessings (Weishan yinzhi): Among those who saved lives while adjudicating criminal cases, He Bigan was certainly not alone, but his saving several thousand people was especially outstanding. Nor was there only one person who saved lives while conducting military campaigns, but Cao Bin's refusal to kill indiscriminately was the most conspicuous example. Sun Zhong set out melons to feed guests, and his descendants became rulers of Wu; Song Jiao fashioned bamboo into a bridge for ants, and he was selected for first place in the examination. Although their impulse of benevolence manifested itself in small matters, the generosity they cherished in their hearts surely never faltered throughout their lives. How could recompense from the unseen realm fail them?
True Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi): Examples of filial piety among emperors and kings are Shun of Yu, King Wen, King Wu, and Emperor Wen of Han. Examples among high ministers are Di Renjie, Cui Xuanwei, Zhang Jiuling, and Lian Xixian. Gao Deng's filial piety manifested itself in loyalty, and Li Zhi's in righteousness. Both loyalty and righteousness indeed arise from extending filial piety. Guo Quan's filial piety manifested itself in fraternal affection, and Lady Yu's…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
孝節曰友曰節亦本於孝之發盖孝為百
行之本衆善之原會萬為一夫何異耶
五倫書君臣之倫所以綱紀乎天下之大則
其所載不得不詳父子兄弟夫婦朋友之
倫不過關係乎一身之微則其所載不得
不畧謙德無堯節儉無舜盖對舉而互見
之非堯不能謙而舜不能儉也叙君道之
善行始聖德而終教育臣道之善行首輔
德而終恬退盖以序而編類焉先乎其大
===
而後乎其細也伏讀
聖製仰而思之孟子所謂天下之生乆矣一治
一亂盖亦本造化之運言之其間治亂相
因之大至我
朝而極
皇祖撥亂反正之功雖禹抑洪水周公兼夷狄
驅猛獸且莫能及而漢唐宋諸君何足擬
哉
誥書之作與六經垂訓而無窮
punctuated:
孝節，曰友曰節，亦本於孝之發。盖孝為百行之本，衆善之原，會萬為一，夫何異耶？
《五倫書》，君臣之倫所以綱紀乎天下之大，則其所載不得不詳；父子、兄弟、夫婦、朋友之倫，不過關係乎一身之微，則其所載不得不畧。謙德無堯，節儉無舜，盖對舉而互見之，非堯不能謙而舜不能儉也。叙君道之善行，始聖德而終教育；臣道之善行，首輔德而終恬退。盖以序而編類焉，先乎其大而後乎其細也。伏讀聖製，仰而思之，孟子所謂「天下之生乆矣，一治一亂」，盖亦本造化之運言之。其間治亂相因之大，至我朝而極。皇祖撥亂反正之功，雖禹抑洪水、周公兼夷狄、驅猛獸，且莫能及，而漢、唐、宋諸君何足擬哉！誥書之作，與六經垂訓而無窮。
translation_en:
…filial devotion and chastity. Fraternal affection and chastity likewise arise from the expression of filial devotion. For filial devotion is the foundation of all conduct and the source of every good deed. The myriad virtues converge into one: how could they differ?
In the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), the relationship between ruler and minister orders the vast realm of all under Heaven, so its treatment necessarily must be detailed. The relationships between father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friends concern only the small sphere of an individual’s life, so their treatment necessarily must be brief. Yao is absent from the section on humility, and Shun from that on frugality: these subjects are presented in parallel, each illuminating the other. This does not mean that Yao could not be humble or that Shun could not be frugal. The account of good conduct in the way of the ruler begins with sagely virtue and ends with education; that of good conduct in the way of the minister begins with assisting the ruler’s virtue and ends with tranquil retirement. These categories have been compiled in an ordered sequence, placing major matters before minor ones.
I reverently read the imperial composition and reflect upon it with admiration. What Mencius meant by saying, “The world has existed for a long time, with alternating periods of order and disorder,” was also grounded in the workings of cosmic transformation. The great succession of order and disorder through the intervening ages has reached its culmination in our dynasty. The imperial ancestor’s achievement in quelling disorder and restoring proper rule cannot be equaled even by Yu’s restraining the floodwaters or the Duke of Zhou’s subjugating the Yi and Di and driving away ferocious beasts. How could the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song possibly compare! The composition of the Book of Admonitions (Gaoshu) transmits instruction without end alongside the Six Classics …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
大寶之傳與天地並立而為久愚也寓天地生
成之內居
君師治教之中不敢以凡民自棄平日之竊有
所見者如此僭陳於右惟執事其進教之
第二問
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批封建之說為世儒
纏繞古今自是異宜豈可拘泥我
朝所行可為萬代法此作盖知所從違矣
===
考試官教諭朱批抑揚開闔不拘問
目古今事如貫珠而斷制允當其
有兼人之學而懷高世之見者乎
考試官學正王批謂異姓封建不可
有同姓封建不可無一篇大旨在
此二句聖人復起不易斯言矣
先王之法行之者必因乎時諸儒之論求
之者必當乎理夫先王之法莫要於封建
也諸儒之論亦莫詳於封建也先王之法
punctuated:
大寶之傳，與天地並立而為久。愚也寓天地生成之內，居君師治教之中，不敢以凡民自棄。平日之竊有所見者如此，僭陳於右，惟執事其進教之。
第二問
卓文林
同考試官教諭劉批：封建之說，為世儒纏繞。古今自是異宜，豈可拘泥？我朝所行，可為萬代法。此作盖知所從違矣。
考試官教諭朱批：抑揚開闔，不拘問目，古今事如貫珠，而斷制允當。其有兼人之學，而懷高世之見者乎？
考試官學正王批：謂異姓封建不可有，同姓封建不可無，一篇大旨在此二句。聖人復起，不易斯言矣。
先王之法，行之者必因乎時；諸儒之論，求之者必當乎理。夫先王之法，莫要於封建也；諸儒之論，亦莫詳於封建也。先王之法
translation_en:
…The transmission of the imperial throne will endure alongside Heaven and Earth. In my humble person, I live within the life-giving and nurturing workings of Heaven and Earth, under the government and instruction of the ruler and teacher. I dare not dismiss myself as merely a common person. Such are the views I have privately formed in my daily reflections. I have presumptuously set them forth above and ask you, honored examiners, to instruct me further.
Second Question
Zhuo Wenlin
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The theory of enfeoffment has become entangled in the arguments of scholars of our age. Antiquity and the present naturally call for different arrangements; how can one cling rigidly to precedent? The practices of our dynasty can serve as a model for ten thousand generations. This essay evidently understands what to follow and what to reject.
Comment by Examiner Zhu, Instructor: In its emphases and qualifications, its development and resolution, the essay is not confined by the question's particulars. Events ancient and modern are strung together like pearls, and its judgments are sound and fitting. Might its author possess learning surpassing that of others and insights transcending his age?
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: He says that enfeoffment of those with a different surname must not exist, while enfeoffment of those with the same surname must not be absent. The main purport of the entire essay lies in these two statements. Were a sage to arise again, he would not alter these words.
Those who implement the institutions of the former kings must adapt them to the times; those who examine the arguments of the Confucian scholars must accord with principle. Among the institutions of the former kings, none was more important than enfeoffment; among the arguments of the Confucian scholars, likewise, none has been treated more fully than enfeoffment. The institutions of the former kings…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
行於古而不可行於今則論之者亦豈可
不審於今而徒泥諸古哉盖其可行者時
也不可行者亦時也可行者固理之在也
不可行者亦理之在也必如是而求之則
封建之是非可得而我
朝封建之法制度之善固無不行亦不泥古
度越百王者在是矣明問所及其能默焉
而已乎夫封建莫知其所從始也史記召
會征討之事見於黄帝紀尚書巡狩朝覲
===
之事見於舜典其盛也國增必多禹會諸
侯塗山執玉帛者萬國盖承唐虞之盛其
衰也國減必少湯受命之時其能存者三
千餘國盖承有夏之衰武王定五等之封
凡千七百七十三國藩屏王室則皆同姓
春秋之世見於經傳者一百六十五國蠻
夷戎狄亦在其間盛非無故而盛以協和
而盛衰非無故而衰以吞併而衰此其封
建本末盛衰之太畧也秦有天下裂都會
punctuated:
行於古而不可行於今，則論之者亦豈可不審於今而徒泥諸古哉？盖其可行者時也，不可行者亦時也；可行者固理之在也，不可行者亦理之在也。必如是而求之，則封建之是非可得，而我朝封建之法制度之善，固無不行，亦不泥古，度越百王者在是矣。明問所及，其能默焉而已乎？
夫封建莫知其所從始也。《史記》召會征討之事見於《黄帝紀》，《尚書》巡狩朝覲之事見於《舜典》。其盛也，國增必多。禹會諸侯塗山，執玉帛者萬國，盖承唐虞之盛。其衰也，國減必少。湯受命之時，其能存者三千餘國，盖承有夏之衰。武王定五等之封，凡千七百七十三國，藩屏王室則皆同姓。春秋之世，見於經傳者一百六十五國，蠻夷戎狄亦在其間。盛非無故而盛，以協和而盛；衰非無故而衰，以吞併而衰。此其封建本末盛衰之太畧也。秦有天下，裂都會
translation_en:
…was practiced in antiquity but cannot be practiced today, how could those discussing it fail to examine present circumstances and merely cling to ancient precedents? Whether it can be practiced depends on the times; whether it cannot be practiced likewise depends on the times. Its practicability certainly accords with principle, but its impracticability likewise accords with principle. Only by investigating in this way can we determine what is right and wrong about enfeoffment. Herein lies the excellence of our dynasty’s laws and institutions of enfeoffment: they are fully practicable, yet do not cling to antiquity, and surpass those of the hundred kings. Since your discerning question touches upon this matter, how could I simply remain silent?
No one knows where enfeoffment began. In the Records of the Grand Historian, accounts of summoning assemblies and conducting punitive campaigns appear in the “Annals of Huangdi” [?]; in the Book of Documents, accounts of inspection tours and court audiences appear in the “Canon of Shun.” In times of flourishing, the states increased and necessarily became numerous. When Yu assembled the feudal lords at Tushan, ten thousand states brought jade and silk: this inherited the flourishing conditions of Tang and Yu. In times of decline, the states diminished and necessarily became few. When Tang received the Mandate, only somewhat more than three thousand states remained: this inherited the decline of the Xia. King Wu established enfeoffment in five ranks, with a total of 1,773 states; those serving as protective bulwarks for the royal house all bore the royal surname. In the Spring and Autumn period, 165 states appear in the Classic and its commentaries, including the Man, Yi, Rong, and Di peoples. Flourishing did not occur without cause: they flourished through concord and harmony. Decline did not occur without cause: they declined through annexation. This is a broad outline of the origins and subsequent course, flourishing and decline, of enfeoffment. When Qin possessed all under Heaven, it divided the metropolitan centers…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而為之郡邑廢侯衞而為之守宰攝制四
海運於掌握封建之制廢矣漢興以來踵
秦故智悉用郡縣而於封建亦間有之始
以封韓彭英盧而非功臣不得繼以封子
弟親属而非同姓不與降漢而後異姓者
不可復得而惟同姓矣此古之封建所以
不可復而後世之罪秦者以此也然而議
者紛紛猶以為先王之法不可不用於是
爭辯者互起而矛盾焉栁宗元曰公天下
===
之端自秦始蘇子瞻曰封建者爭之端亂
之始也是以封建為非者矣胡仁仲曰封
建者公天下之大端大本也朱晦庵曰必
如是而後能公天下以為心而達君臣之
義於天下是以封建為是者矣然徐考之
有封建之善亦有封建之弊其弊於夏則
有扈羲和之有罪士師不得以治之六師
往征必勞天子親總之舉其弊於周文昭
武穆之大封異姓不得以先之數傳而後
punctuated:
而為之郡邑，廢侯衞而為之守宰，攝制四海，運於掌握，封建之制廢矣。漢興以來，踵秦故智，悉用郡縣，而於封建亦間有之。始以封韓彭英盧，而非功臣不得；繼以封子弟親属，而非同姓不與。降漢而後，異姓者不可復得，而惟同姓矣。此古之封建所以不可復，而後世之罪秦者以此也。然而議者紛紛，猶以為先王之法不可不用，於是爭辯者互起而矛盾焉。
栁宗元曰：「公天下之端自秦始。」蘇子瞻曰：「封建者，爭之端，亂之始也。」是以封建為非者矣。胡仁仲曰：「封建者，公天下之大端大本也。」朱晦庵曰：「必如是而後能公天下以為心，而達君臣之義於天下。」是以封建為是者矣。
然徐考之，有封建之善，亦有封建之弊。其弊於夏，則有扈羲和之有罪，士師不得以治之，六師往征，必勞天子親總之舉。其弊於周，文昭武穆之大封，異姓不得以先之，數傳而後
translation_en:
…and made them commanderies and counties, abolished the feudal lords and their protective domains, and established governors and magistrates in their place. He controlled all within the four seas, directing it as though it lay in the palm of his hand; the system of enfeoffment was abolished. From the rise of the Han onward, rulers followed Qin’s old strategy, employing commanderies and counties throughout, though enfeoffment was also practiced on occasion. At first, Han, Peng, Ying, and Lu were enfeoffed, and none but meritorious ministers could receive such grants. Subsequently, sons, younger brothers, and other relatives were enfeoffed, and none outside the imperial clan were included. After the Han, those of other surnames could no longer obtain enfeoffment; only members of the imperial clan could. This is why the ancient system of enfeoffment could not be restored, and why later generations condemned Qin. Yet opinions proliferated: some still held that the institutions of the former kings must be employed. Thus disputants arose on opposing sides and contradicted one another.
Liu Zongyuan said: “The first step toward making the realm public began with Qin.” Su Zizhan said: “Enfeoffment is the source of contention and the beginning of disorder.” These regarded enfeoffment as wrong. Hu Renzhong said: “Enfeoffment is the great starting point and fundamental basis for making the realm public.” Zhu Hui’an said: “Only through this can one take making the realm public as one’s guiding purpose and extend the proper relationship between ruler and minister throughout the realm.” These regarded enfeoffment as right.
Yet, upon careful examination, enfeoffment has both benefits and defects. Its defects under the Xia were such that, when Youhu and Xi and He committed offenses, the Minister of Justice could not punish them. The Six Armies had to march against them, necessarily troubling the Son of Heaven to take personal command. Its defects under the Zhou were such that, in the extensive enfeoffment of King Wen’s descendants in the zhao line and King Wu’s descendants in the mu line, those of other surnames could not take precedence over them. After several generations…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
即有末大不掉之憂在三代之時已有其
弊如此况後世乎柳子蘇子既剖析利害
指陳得失明白切當而程子亦曰封建之
法本出於不得已秦法固不善亦有不可
變者朱子又曰封建只是歷代循襲勢不
容已柳子厚亦說得是而今之論者猶曰
必有公天下之心而後可以行封建自其
出於公心則選賢與能而大小相維之勢
足以綿千載自其出於私心則忌疎畏偪
===
而上下相猜之形不能一朝居此說之行
則持論者猶未免墮於牽制而莫之决也
大抵異姓之封建不可有同姓之封建不
可無歷代行之而不得其宜我
國家處之而曲盡其善
宗室之封徧於天下派天源分玉葉者何其
多也寵以尊崇之禮而不委以政事之煩
備其官屬輔導者有人使令者有人所謂
親之欲其貴也愛之欲其富也是雖非若
punctuated:
即有末大不掉之憂。在三代之時，已有其弊如此，况後世乎？柳子、蘇子既剖析利害，指陳得失，明白切當，而程子亦曰：「封建之法，本出於不得已。秦法固不善，亦有不可變者。」朱子又曰：「封建只是歷代循襲，勢不容已。柳子厚亦說得是。」而今之論者猶曰：「必有公天下之心，而後可以行封建。自其出於公心，則選賢與能，而大小相維之勢足以綿千載；自其出於私心，則忌疎畏偪，而上下相猜之形不能一朝居。」此說之行，則持論者猶未免墮於牽制，而莫之决也。
大抵異姓之封建不可有，同姓之封建不可無。歷代行之而不得其宜，我國家處之而曲盡其善。宗室之封徧於天下，派天源、分玉葉者何其多也！寵以尊崇之禮，而不委以政事之煩；備其官屬，輔導者有人，使令者有人。所謂親之欲其貴也，愛之欲其富也。是雖非若
translation_en:
…there arose the fear that the branches would grow too large to be controlled. Such abuses already existed in the age of the Three Dynasties; how much more so in later ages! Master Liu and Master Su have already analyzed the advantages and disadvantages and explained the gains and losses clearly and aptly. Master Cheng also said: “The system of enfeoffment originally arose from necessity. The Qin system was certainly not good, yet it too contains elements that cannot be changed.” Master Zhu further said: “Enfeoffment was simply inherited from dynasty to dynasty; circumstances made it impossible to discontinue. Liu Zihou’s account is also correct.” Yet present-day commentators still say: “Only with the intention of treating all under Heaven as a common possession can one practice enfeoffment. If it proceeds from a public-minded intention, the worthy and capable will be selected, and the mutual support of greater and lesser domains will suffice to sustain it for a thousand years. If it proceeds from a selfish intention, one will distrust distant relatives and fear those whose power presses too close; a situation in which superiors and inferiors suspect one another cannot endure even for a single morning.” While this view prevails, those advancing arguments remain caught in conflicting considerations and reach no decision.
In general, enfeoffment of those of other surnames must not exist, while enfeoffment of those bearing the ruling house’s surname cannot be dispensed with. Successive dynasties practiced it without finding the proper arrangements; our dynasty has handled it so as to realize its benefits in every particular. The fiefs of the imperial clan extend throughout the realm. How numerous are those who branch from the celestial source and spread forth as jade leaves! They are honored with ceremonies of exalted respect but are not burdened with the troublesome business of government. They are provided with a full complement of officials and attendants: some to assist and guide them, others to carry out their commands. This is what is meant by wishing those one holds dear to enjoy high rank and those one loves to enjoy wealth. Although this is not like…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
前代封建之實而所以處之者盡其恩矣
四裔之酋長周於四方服旃裘語侏離者
何其衆也列之以官爵之殊隆之以世襲
之恩別置僚佐既有以分其任亦因以防
其欲有罪則懲之而冀改其過大惡則除
之而更置其賢是雖若有前代封建之實
而所以處之者得其義矣一王之法制萬
代之準繩又何有加之者哉約而論之天
生斯民立之司牧惟在於治安則人心悅
===
而天意得固不必於封建郡縣優劣之分
也堯舜之禪受行於燕噲則亂湯武之仁
義行於桓文則詐是皆務先王之美名而
不知其弊者蘇子曰世無封建而相戕之
禍斯絕仁人君子忍復開之歟斯名言也
執事以為何如
第三問
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖 批問目頭緒頗多似
punctuated:
前代封建之實，而所以處之者盡其恩矣。四裔之酋長周於四方，服旃裘、語侏離者何其衆也！列之以官爵之殊，隆之以世襲之恩，別置僚佐，既有以分其任，亦因以防其欲。有罪則懲之，而冀改其過；大惡則除之，而更置其賢。是雖若有前代封建之實，而所以處之者得其義矣。一王之法制，萬代之準繩，又何有加之者哉！約而論之，天生斯民，立之司牧，惟在於治安，則人心悅而天意得，固不必於封建、郡縣優劣之分也。堯舜之禪受，行於燕噲則亂；湯武之仁義，行於桓文則詐。是皆務先王之美名，而不知其弊者。蘇子曰：「世無封建，而相戕之禍斯絕。仁人君子忍復開之歟？」斯名言也。執事以為何如？

第三問
鐵潤
同考試官教諭廖批：問目頭緒頗多，似
translation_en:
…the actual enfeoffment practices of former dynasties, yet the way they are treated fully expresses benevolence toward them. Chieftains of the outer regions are found in every direction: how numerous are those who wear felt and furs and speak unfamiliar tongues! They are ranked through distinctions of office and noble title and honored with the favor of hereditary succession. Additional subordinate officials are appointed both to share their responsibilities and to restrain their desires. When they commit offenses, they are punished in the hope that they will mend their ways; when they commit great evils, they are removed and worthy men appointed in their place. Although this seems to retain the substance of former dynasties’ enfeoffment, the way they are treated accords with righteousness. These institutions of a sovereign are a standard for ten thousand generations: what could improve upon them?

To put it briefly, Heaven brought forth these people and established rulers to shepherd them. The essential aim is orderly and peaceful government; then the people’s hearts are pleased and Heaven’s intent is fulfilled. There is certainly no need to insist on distinguishing the relative merits of enfeoffment and the commandery-and-county system. The abdication and succession of Yao and Shun, when practiced by Kuai of Yan, brought disorder; the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu, when practiced by Duke Huan and Duke Wen, became deception. These were all cases of pursuing the glorious reputation of the former kings without understanding the attendant abuses. Master Su said: “Once the world is without enfeoffment, the calamity of mutual slaughter will cease. Could humane men and gentlemen bear to reopen the way to it?” These are memorable words. What is your judgment, sir?

Third Policy Question
Tie Run
Comment by Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor: “The question has quite a number of distinct threads, and seems…”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
難下手此答如金歸於範形質自
成其文場中之哲匠也歟
考試官教諭朱批考古論今歷歷指
掌末論兵民之制而所處尤為有
見噫經生所養有如是乎
考試官學正王批民與兵古今不同
亦世道推移使然能不為經生常
談而取必於古者濟時之學也
有古今四民之異有古今制兵之異夫天
===
之生民一也可以為民可以為兵方其兵
寓於民以為四則世質民淳而有可稱及
其兵分於民以為五則世變風移而有可
議是非兵民之能異也所以為古今者不
能以不異也今承明問庸敢無辭以對乎
自夫耒耨之利興天下始有所謂農矣日
中為市之利興天下始有所謂商矣有弧
矢舟楫宮室之制天下始有所謂工矣結
繩而易以書契天下始有所謂士矣然蕡
punctuated:
難下手，此答如金歸於範，形質自成，其文場中之哲匠也歟！
考試官教諭朱批：考古論今，歷歷指掌。末論兵民之制，而所處尤為有見。噫！經生所養有如是乎！
考試官學正王批：民與兵，古今不同，亦世道推移使然。能不為經生常談而取必於古者，濟時之學也。
有古今四民之異，有古今制兵之異。夫天之生民，一也，可以為民，可以為兵。方其兵寓於民以為四，則世質民淳而有可稱；及其兵分於民以為五，則世變風移而有可議。是非兵民之能異也，所以為古今者，不能以不異也。今承明問，庸敢無辭以對乎？自夫耒耨之利興，天下始有所謂農矣；日中為市之利興，天下始有所謂商矣；有弧矢、舟楫、宮室之制，天下始有所謂工矣；結繩而易以書契，天下始有所謂士矣。然蕡
translation_en:
…difficult to tackle. This answer is like metal poured into a mold: its form and substance take shape naturally. Is its author not a master craftsman of the examination hall?
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: His examination of antiquity and discussion of the present are lucid, as clear as pointing to something in one's palm. At the end he discusses the organization of soldiers and civilians, and his proposed arrangements show particular insight. Ah! Can a student of the Classics have cultivated learning such as this?
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: The relationship between civilians and soldiers differs between antiquity and the present; this too results from changes in the course of the world. To avoid the stock talk of classical scholars who insist on taking antiquity as the standard is learning that can meet the needs of the age.
There are differences between antiquity and the present in the four occupations, and differences between antiquity and the present in military organization. Heaven gives life to the people alike: they may serve as civilians or as soldiers. When soldiers were included among civilians, making four occupational groups, the age was simple and the people sincere, and there was much to commend. When soldiers became separate from civilians, making five groups, the age changed and customs shifted, and there was much to debate. These differences do not arise from any inherent capacity of soldiers and civilians to differ; rather, the conditions that distinguish antiquity from the present cannot remain the same. Now that I have received your illuminating question, how could I dare offer no words in reply?
Once the benefits of plows and hoes were introduced, there first appeared in the world those called farmers. Once the benefits of holding markets at midday were introduced, there first appeared those called merchants. With the making of bows and arrows, boats and oars, and palaces and houses, there first appeared those called artisans. When knotted cords were replaced with written documents, there first appeared those called scholars. Yet Fen [?]…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
帝戰涿鹿虞舜伐有苗兵之來盖亦久矣
稱四民而不及於兵者豈不以兵即民為
之用而亦非所常用者歟語民則兵在其
中矣世有升降人有賢愚古之人方其為
士則道問學及其為農則力稼穡為兵則
善戰陣投之所向無不如意士之有位者
各稱其德有學者不干於進農工商賈所
享有限上下之志以定彼此之分各得古
之為民不可議矣在易之履曰君子辨上
===
下定民志其吾夫子衰世之意乎盖以士
庶公卿日志於尊榮農工商賈日志於富
侈億兆之心交騖於利故舜與伊尹之聖
雖農而不足為卑非堯求之急湯聘之勤
畝畝自若也傅說膠鬲之賢雖工商而不
足為賤非武丁舉之文王起之巖市自如
也其志有不定乎程子之論盖未始不脗
合也四民之在古今淳漓如此至於兵制
之異又有可言者馬周為井田之制寓兵
punctuated: 帝戰涿鹿，虞舜伐有苗，兵之來盖亦久矣。稱四民而不及於兵者，豈不以兵即民為之用，而亦非所常用者歟？語民則兵在其中矣。世有升降，人有賢愚。古之人，方其為士則道問學，及其為農則力稼穡，為兵則善戰陣，投之所向，無不如意。士之有位者，各稱其德；有學者，不干於進。農工商賈，所享有限，上下之志以定，彼此之分各得，古之為民不可議矣。在《易》之《履》曰：「君子辨上下，定民志。」其吾夫子衰世之意乎？盖以士庶公卿日志於尊榮，農工商賈日志於富侈，億兆之心交騖於利。故舜與伊尹之聖，雖農而不足為卑，非堯求之急、湯聘之勤，畝畝自若也。傅說、膠鬲之賢，雖工商而不足為賤，非武丁舉之、文王起之，巖市自如也。其志有不定乎？程子之論，盖未始不脗合也。四民之在古今，淳漓如此。至於兵制之異，又有可言者。馬周為井田之制，寓兵
translation_en:
…the emperor fought at Zhuolu, and Yu Shun campaigned against the Youmiao: soldiers have indeed existed for a very long time. When people speak of the four classes of the populace without mentioning soldiers, is this not because soldiers are simply the people put to military use, and such use is not constant? Speak of the people, and soldiers are included among them. Ages rise and decline; people differ in worth and understanding. In antiquity, when people served as scholars, they pursued inquiry and learning; when they farmed, they devoted themselves to sowing and reaping; when they served as soldiers, they were skilled in battle formations. Whatever task they were assigned, they fulfilled it satisfactorily. Scholars who held office each occupied a position commensurate with their virtue; those possessed of learning did not seek advancement. Farmers, artisans, and merchants enjoyed benefits within prescribed limits. The aspirations of those above and below were thus settled, and each attained his proper station. The condition of the people in antiquity was beyond reproach.

In the Book of Changes, the hexagram Treading says: “The gentleman distinguishes those above from those below and settles the aspirations of the people.” Might this express our Master Confucius’s concern in an age of decline? For scholars, commoners, dukes, and ministers daily set their hearts on honor and glory, while farmers, artisans, and merchants daily set their hearts on wealth and luxury. The hearts of the countless multitude all raced after profit. Yet sages such as Shun and Yi Yin, though farmers, were not thereby lowly. Had Yao not sought Shun so urgently, and Tang not so diligently invited Yi Yin to serve, they would have remained content in the fields [?]. Worthy men such as Fu Yue and Jiao Ge, though engaged in craft and commerce, were not thereby base. Had Wu Ding not promoted the former and King Wen not raised up the latter, they would have remained at ease among the rocks and in the marketplace. Were their aspirations in any way unsettled? Master Cheng’s discussion has indeed always accorded with this.

Such is the contrast between the simplicity and the degeneration of the four classes in ancient and later times. As for changes in military institutions, there is more to be said. Ma Zhou [?] instituted the well-field system, embedding soldiers…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
於農戎馬干戈素具於平時蒐苗獮狩簡
教於農隙無事則為比閭族黨州鄉之民
有事則為伍兩卒旅師軍之衆兵者視農
而益損行者視居而益損兵農之制此其
盡善矣管子內政於都邑近地為士農之
鄉十五以賦三軍在鄉曰農在軍曰士也
為工商之鄉六以給財費工不知卒商不
知軍也惟文學之士特為貴之處以閒燕
之地不雜農工之流國之外無兵國之內
===
無農兵農之分此其作俑矣嗣是而後隷
尺籍者遍於中土躬甲胄者盈於疆塲降
而秦漢兵不謀民民不謀兵矣又降而唐
宋兵自為兵民自為民矣惟唐之府兵頗
為近古教閱於農隙之時調發於有事之
日行兵則自置甲胄自備資糧罷兵則將
歸於朝兵散於府固為善矣然亦不旋踵
而廢之四民之外有所謂兵者蓋不可得
而易矣周之為制固善豈所望於後世乎
punctuated: 於農，戎馬干戈素具於平時，蒐苗獮狩簡教於農隙。無事則為比閭族黨州鄉之民，有事則為伍兩卒旅師軍之衆。兵者視農而益損，行者視居而益損。兵農之制，此其盡善矣。管子內政於都邑近地，為士農之鄉十五，以賦三軍，在鄉曰農，在軍曰士也；為工商之鄉六，以給財費，工不知卒，商不知軍也。惟文學之士，特為貴之，處以閒燕之地，不雜農工之流。國之外無兵，國之內無農。兵農之分，此其作俑矣。嗣是而後，隷尺籍者遍於中土，躬甲胄者盈於疆塲。降而秦漢，兵不謀民，民不謀兵矣；又降而唐宋，兵自為兵，民自為民矣。惟唐之府兵頗為近古，教閱於農隙之時，調發於有事之日。行兵則自置甲胄，自備資糧；罷兵則將歸於朝，兵散於府，固為善矣。然亦不旋踵而廢之。四民之外有所謂兵者，蓋不可得而易矣。周之為制固善，豈所望於後世乎？
translation_en:
…among the farmers. Warhorses, shields, and spears were regularly kept ready in peacetime, and troops were inspected and trained during the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts, in the intervals between agricultural labors. When there was no fighting, they were people organized into the civil units of bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; when fighting arose, they were troops organized into the military units of wu, liang, zu, lü, shi, and jun.
