The number of soldiers increased or decreased according to the number of farmers, and the number sent on campaign increased or decreased according to the number remaining at home. This system uniting soldiers and farmers was perfect in its goodness.

Master Guan organized internal administration in the capital and its surrounding lands, establishing fifteen townships of soldiers and farmers to supply the three armies. In their townships they were called farmers; in the army they were called soldiers. He established six townships of artisans and merchants to provide financial resources and meet expenses. Artisans knew nothing of the troops, and merchants nothing of the armies. Only men of literary learning were especially honored and settled in quiet, secluded places, apart from farmers and artisans. Outside the capital there were no soldiers; within it there were no farmers. This set the precedent for separating soldiers from farmers.

From this time onward, men entered on military registers were found throughout the central lands, and men clad in armor and helmets filled the frontier regions. By the Qin and Han, soldiers took no thought for civilians, and civilians took no thought for soldiers. Later still, under the Tang and Song, soldiers formed their own distinct body, and civilians theirs. Only the Tang militia system, the fubing, came fairly close to antiquity. Men were trained and inspected in the intervals between agricultural labors, and mobilized when military needs arose. When campaigning, they supplied their own armor and helmets and provided their own funds and provisions. When hostilities ended, the commanders returned to court and the troops dispersed to their military headquarters. This was certainly a good system. Yet it too was abolished before long. The existence of a category called soldiers outside the four occupations has, it seems, become impossible to change. The Zhou system was certainly good, but could one expect it of later ages?

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
暑葛寒裘各因其時而不可以倒施章甫
逢掖各有其地而不可以通用亦猶是也
方今之兵民大抵皆歷代遺意執事乃欲
求其近似者愚則以為屯田之制兵以耕
田食以給兵庶幾兵農合一之意然耕者
多不戰戰者多不耕固已不類唐之府兵
矣求三代之制所謂愈似而愈不似焉管
見如斯然尤有耿耿之懷不敢不終其說
居今之世不必求之古矣仰惟我
===
太祖高皇帝之定天下萬姓遵義百度順軌兵
民之在天下亦何讓於古哉然無不弊之
法亦無不變之時以今之四民言士嬉而
荒於學農貧而病於耕工以濫惡欺人商
以虛夸逐利四民之所以弊者如此也以
今之兵制言營乏壯丁伍多虛籍逃避者
不盡心於清補操練者不加意於存恤兵
制之所以弊者如此也是責也典守者其
可辭乎文臣所以親民者也清身心敦敎
punctuated:
暑葛寒裘，各因其時而不可以倒施；章甫逢掖，各有其地而不可以通用，亦猶是也。方今之兵民，大抵皆歷代遺意。執事乃欲求其近似者，愚則以為屯田之制，兵以耕田，食以給兵，庶幾兵農合一之意。然耕者多不戰，戰者多不耕，固已不類唐之府兵矣。求三代之制，所謂愈似而愈不似焉。管見如斯，然尤有耿耿之懷，不敢不終其說。
居今之世，不必求之古矣。仰惟我太祖高皇帝之定天下，萬姓遵義，百度順軌，兵民之在天下，亦何讓於古哉？然無不弊之法，亦無不變之時。以今之四民言，士嬉而荒於學，農貧而病於耕，工以濫惡欺人，商以虛夸逐利，四民之所以弊者如此也。以今之兵制言，營乏壯丁，伍多虛籍，逃避者不盡心於清補，操練者不加意於存恤，兵制之所以弊者如此也。是責也，典守者其可辭乎？文臣所以親民者也，清身心，敦敎
translation_en:
Wearing ramie cloth in the heat and fur garments in the cold each accords with its season; their uses cannot be reversed. The zhangfu ceremonial cap and broad-sleeved robes each have their proper locality and cannot be used everywhere indiscriminately. The same principle applies here. The present arrangements for soldiers and civilians largely preserve ideas inherited from successive dynasties. You, sir, wish to find among them something approximating the ancient system. In my humble opinion, the military agricultural colony system, in which soldiers till the fields and the produce feeds the troops, comes close to the idea of uniting soldiers and farmers. Yet most of those who farm do not fight, and most of those who fight do not farm. Thus it already differs from the Tang militia system. If measured against the institutions of the Three Dynasties, it is a case of what is called “the more it resembles them, the less it resembles them.” Such is my limited view. Yet something still weighs upon my mind, and I dare not leave my argument unfinished.
Living in the present age, we need not seek our models in antiquity. I reverently consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao brought all under Heaven to order: the myriad families followed righteousness, and all institutions ran their proper course. How could the arrangements for soldiers and civilians throughout the realm have been inferior to those of antiquity? Yet no law is immune to deterioration, and no age is free from change. Consider the four occupations today: scholars idle away their time and neglect learning; farmers are impoverished and struggle at their tillage; artisans deceive people with shoddy goods; merchants pursue profit through empty boasts. Such are the failings of the four occupations. Consider the military system today: camps lack able-bodied men, and unit registers contain many fictitious entries. Those responsible for dealing with deserters do not devote themselves fully to checking the rolls and filling vacancies; those responsible for training give insufficient attention to caring for the troops. Such are the failings of the military system. Can those entrusted with its administration evade this responsibility? Civil officials are charged with caring for the people: they should purify their conduct and minds and strengthen moral instruction…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
化示好惡以臨之明勸懲以警之則可以
還淳厚之風矣武臣所以掌兵必也去貪
暴戒驕縱同甘苦以撫之嚴紀律以御之
則可以起廢弛之政矣然所以督率乎文
武臣工者又有道焉文臣三歲述職以行
黜陟者有典要必不以簿書期會者為能
而以留心教化者為善責其效之有無而
以進以退武臣五歲考選以行予奪者有
令要必不以撒堅中的為急而以撫綏軍
===
士為先稽其政之善否而以勸以懲上之
所以責成者在是則下之所以遵循者亦
在是宿弊可革美政可成而求唐虞之治
不難矣若夫任乎人以主考選而悉本於
公廉稽於衆以憑黜陟而不昧於賢否則
在於今日廟堂留意焉非愚生所知也
第四問
張鳳翔
同考試官教諭程 批偏鄉之士能周知
punctuated:
化，示好惡以臨之，明勸懲以警之，則可以還淳厚之風矣。武臣所以掌兵，必也去貪暴，戒驕縱，同甘苦以撫之，嚴紀律以御之，則可以起廢弛之政矣。然所以督率乎文武臣工者，又有道焉。文臣三歲述職以行黜陟者有典，要必不以簿書期會者為能，而以留心教化者為善，責其效之有無，而以進以退。武臣五歲考選以行予奪者有令，要必不以撒堅中的為急，而以撫綏軍士為先，稽其政之善否，而以勸以懲。上之所以責成者在是，則下之所以遵循者亦在是。宿弊可革，美政可成，而求唐虞之治不難矣。若夫任乎人以主考選，而悉本於公廉；稽於衆以憑黜陟，而不昧於賢否，則在於今日廟堂留意焉，非愚生所知也。
第四問
張鳳翔
同考試官教諭程 批：偏鄉之士能周知
translation_en:
… transformation. By making clear what they approve and disapprove of in governing the people, and making rewards and punishments explicit to admonish them, they can restore customs of simplicity and generosity. As for military officials charged with commanding troops, they must abandon greed and brutality, guard against arrogance and license, share their men's hardships and comforts in caring for them, and enforce strict discipline in directing them. They can then revive administration that has fallen into neglect.
There are also proper ways to supervise and direct civil and military officials. Established regulations require civil officials to report on their service every three years so that demotions and promotions may be made. Competence must not be judged by paperwork and the observance of deadlines; rather, attention to moral instruction should count as merit. They should be held accountable for whether they have achieved results, and promoted or demoted accordingly. Ordinances require military officials to undergo assessment and selection every five years so that appointments may be granted or withdrawn. The priority must not be breaking through strong defenses [?] and hitting targets, but caring for and reassuring the soldiers. The quality of their administration should be examined, and they should be rewarded or punished accordingly. If these are the grounds on which superiors demand results, they will also be the standards that subordinates follow. Long-standing abuses can be eliminated and good government achieved; attaining the order of Tang and Yu—the age of Yao and Shun—will then not be difficult.
As for appointing people to preside over assessment and selection who act entirely on impartiality and integrity, and consulting the many as a basis for demotions and promotions without misjudging the worthy and unworthy, these are matters to which the present court must give its attention. They lie beyond the knowledge of this ignorant student.
Fourth Question
Zhang Fengxiang
Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: “A scholar from a remote district who can have a comprehensive knowledge of …”

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
天下之務者絕少子何練達如是
豈嘗留心於經濟之學者耶
同考試官教諭杜批洞見財用消息而
歸本於
九重之上可謂芹曝之獻矣
考試官教諭朱批文詞敏妙財用處
置尤為超絕蓋有志於經國者宜
用錄出
考試官學正王批說天下財用豐耗
===
詳悉無遺而忠愛之言尤
當宁所宜聞者異時致用必有大過于人
工於經國者既究夫耗財之弊必求其豐
財之本蓋耗財者未始不由於奢豐財者
未始不由於儉以天地間有限之財而供
上下無窮之用苟非去其奢之弊求其儉
之本則財益至於耗而不可以望其豐矣
愚嘗觀之以天下之利養天下之人財之
在民者宜足也以天下之賦供天下之用
punctuated:
天下之務者絕少，子何練達如是？豈嘗留心於經濟之學者耶？

同考試官教諭杜批：洞見財用消息，而歸本於九重之上，可謂芹曝之獻矣。

考試官教諭朱批：文詞敏妙，財用處置尤為超絕，蓋有志於經國者，宜用錄出。

考試官學正王批：說天下財用豐耗，詳悉無遺，而忠愛之言，尤當宁所宜聞者。異時致用，必有大過于人。

工於經國者，既究夫耗財之弊，必求其豐財之本。蓋耗財者未始不由於奢，豐財者未始不由於儉。以天地間有限之財，而供上下無窮之用，苟非去其奢之弊，求其儉之本，則財益至於耗，而不可以望其豐矣。愚嘗觀之，以天下之利養天下之人，財之在民者宜足也；以天下之賦供天下之用，
translation_en:
…very few understand the affairs of the realm comprehensively. How have you become so versed in them? Have you devoted yourself to the study of statecraft?

Associate Examiner Du, Instructor, comments: You clearly discern the waxing and waning of financial resources and trace their foundation to the emperor himself. This may indeed be called a humble offering of celery and sunshine—a modest contribution made with sincere intent.

Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: The writing is deft and elegant, and the handling of financial matters is especially outstanding. Here is someone with aspirations to govern the state; this piece merits selection for inclusion in the record.

Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: The discussion of the abundance and depletion of the realm’s financial resources is thorough and leaves nothing out. Its words of loyalty and concern are especially fitting for the emperor to hear. When put to practical service in the future, this man will surely surpass others by a great margin.

Those skilled in governing the state, having investigated the abuses that deplete wealth, must seek the foundation for increasing it. For the depletion of wealth invariably arises from extravagance, and its increase invariably arises from frugality. The finite wealth between Heaven and Earth must supply the limitless needs of those above and below. Unless the abuses of extravagance are eliminated and the foundation of frugality is sought, wealth will become ever more depleted, and there can be no hope of abundance. I have considered this: when the resources of the realm sustain its people, the wealth held by the people ought to suffice; when the taxes of the realm supply its expenditures, …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
財之在官者宜足也夫何民無恒産者凶
年饑歳固告病矣而沃土豐年猶不免於
流移是財果在民耶官無餘積者諸省有
司固告匱矣而
内帑户部猶未見於充實是財果在官耶
國家自洪武永樂至於天順上下之間法度
修明人心儆畏國無妄費民無濫為財用
豐盈海内殷富故雖有兵荒之急不足為
患比年以來遊惰之徒遍於中土不耕而
===
食所謂一夫耕之十人食之者有矣不蠶
而衣所謂一婦蠶之十人衣之者有矣此
其一弊也豪商鉅族僭擬王公置一器用
足當中人之産為一飲食不惜萬錢之費
此又一弊也有民社者惟志温飽綰章綬
者相尚豪華飲食服御必極其盛子女玉
帛必窮其欲此又一弊也京師貴倖衣一
衣乗一馬辦一宴會非窮奢極麗不可其
他所為亦各稱是修一第治一墅創一庵
punctuated:
財之在官者宜足也。夫何民無恒産者，凶年饑歳固告病矣，而沃土豐年猶不免於流移，是財果在民耶？官無餘積者，諸省有司固告匱矣，而内帑户部猶未見於充實，是財果在官耶？
國家自洪武、永樂至於天順，上下之間，法度修明，人心儆畏，國無妄費，民無濫為，財用豐盈，海内殷富。故雖有兵荒之急，不足為患。
比年以來，遊惰之徒遍於中土，不耕而食，所謂「一夫耕之，十人食之」者有矣；不蠶而衣，所謂「一婦蠶之，十人衣之」者有矣。此其一弊也。豪商鉅族僭擬王公，置一器用，足當中人之産；為一飲食，不惜萬錢之費。此又一弊也。有民社者惟志温飽，綰章綬者相尚豪華，飲食服御必極其盛，子女玉帛必窮其欲。此又一弊也。京師貴倖，衣一衣，乗一馬，辦一宴會，非窮奢極麗不可；其他所為，亦各稱是。修一第，治一墅，創一庵……
translation_en:
…the wealth held by the government ought to be sufficient. Why, then, do people without a secure livelihood admittedly suffer in years of famine, yet even in fertile regions and abundant years still find themselves forced to wander elsewhere? Is wealth really held by the people? As for the absence of reserves in government, the responsible offices in the provinces admittedly report shortages, yet neither the imperial treasury nor the Ministry of Revenue appears well supplied either. Is wealth really held by the government?
From the Hongwu and Yongle reigns down to the Tianshun reign, laws and institutions were maintained in good order throughout the realm, and people were vigilant and respectful. The state incurred no reckless expenses, and the people engaged in no excessive undertakings. Financial resources were plentiful, and the realm was prosperous. Thus even the emergencies of war and famine were insufficient to cause serious trouble.
In recent years, idle people have spread throughout the land. They eat without plowing: there are indeed instances of what is called “one man plows, and ten people eat from his labor.” They wear clothing without raising silkworms: there are indeed instances of what is called “one woman raises silkworms, and ten people are clothed from her labor.” This is one abuse. Wealthy merchants and great families presumptuously emulate princes and dukes. Purchasing a single utensil costs as much as the property of a household of middling means; for a single meal, they do not begrudge an expenditure of ten thousand cash. This is another abuse. Those entrusted with governing the people care only for their own comfort and sustenance; those who wear official seals and ribbons vie with one another in extravagance. Their food, clothing, and equipage must be of the utmost splendor, and they indulge to the full their desires for women and boys, jade and silk. This is another abuse. The nobles and favorites of the capital will wear no garment, ride no horse, and hold no banquet unless it reaches the height of extravagance and magnificence. Everything else they do is on a corresponding scale. They build a mansion, lay out a country estate, establish a hermitage…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
寺非數萬金不可其餘所蓄尤不可計此
又一弊也課税出於民而流移者負欠無
徵租賦出於地而凶荒者减免其數縣之
所虧者百則郡之所虧者必千矣郡之所
虧者千則省之所虧者必萬矣
内帑供邊者今日出西北明日出東北所需
無間户部之給俸者今日給文臣明日給
武臣所費不貲他如冗員以鼠雀其間緇
黄以尾閭其内不急之工作例外之賞賚
===
又有不可數計者矣嗚呼天地之生財今
猶古也而生齒日繁國用日益加以數弊
四出而奪之欲國不虚民不困胡可得耶
脱有水旱兵戈吾不知何以為處也為富
國足民計者孰不曰禁遊惰抑鉅族汰贓
吏律貴倖而不知其抑末矣故論當今之
務者勿求其有餘去奢而已勿患其不足
崇儉而已奢去而儉崇則天地所生之財
自足以供上下之用釋此不務而惟目前
punctuated:
寺，非數萬金不可，其餘所蓄，尤不可計，此又一弊也。課税出於民，而流移者負欠無徵；租賦出於地，而凶荒者减免其數。縣之所虧者百，則郡之所虧者必千矣；郡之所虧者千，則省之所虧者必萬矣。内帑供邊者，今日出西北，明日出東北，所需無間；户部之給俸者，今日給文臣，明日給武臣，所費不貲。他如冗員以鼠雀其間，緇黄以尾閭其内，不急之工作，例外之賞賚，又有不可數計者矣。
嗚呼！天地之生財，今猶古也，而生齒日繁，國用日益，加以數弊四出而奪之，欲國不虚、民不困，胡可得耶？脱有水旱兵戈，吾不知何以為處也。為富國足民計者，孰不曰禁遊惰、抑鉅族、汰贓吏、律貴倖，而不知其抑末矣。故論當今之務者，勿求其有餘，去奢而已；勿患其不足，崇儉而已。奢去而儉崇，則天地所生之財，自足以供上下之用。釋此不務，而惟目前
translation_en:
…temple requires tens of thousands in gold; their other accumulated possessions are still more impossible to reckon. This is yet another abuse. Taxes are levied on the people, but arrears owed by those who have migrated or become displaced cannot be collected. Land taxes are levied on the soil, but crop failures and famine require reductions or remissions. If a county’s shortfall is a hundred, a prefecture’s must be a thousand; if a prefecture’s shortfall is a thousand, a province’s must be ten thousand. Funds from the imperial treasury for supplying the frontiers go out to the northwest today and to the northeast tomorrow: the demands never cease. The Ministry of Revenue pays salaries to civil officials today and military officials tomorrow, at immense expense. Beyond these, superfluous officials gnaw away like rats and sparrows, while Buddhist and Daoist clergy drain resources like the outlet of the sea. Nonessential construction projects and rewards granted outside the established rules also entail expenditures beyond reckoning.
Alas! Heaven and earth produce wealth now just as they did in antiquity, yet the population grows daily and state expenditure increases daily. Added to this, these various abuses arise on every side and consume that wealth. How can one hope to keep the state’s coffers from being emptied and the people from being impoverished? Should floods, droughts, or warfare occur, I do not know how we could cope. Among those who devise plans to enrich the state and provide sufficiently for the people, who does not advocate prohibiting idleness, restraining great families, dismissing corrupt officials, and disciplining powerful imperial favorites? Yet they fail to recognize that these measures merely suppress the symptoms. Thus, those who discuss the pressing tasks of the present should not seek a surplus, but simply eliminate extravagance; they should not worry about insufficiency, but simply promote frugality. Once extravagance is eliminated and frugality esteemed, the wealth produced by heaven and earth will naturally suffice for the needs of both high and low. To set this aside and neglect it, attending only to the immediate…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之計是圖未見其有濟也然所謂去奢而
崇儉者豈可以他求哉盖京師者天下之
本
朝廷者四方之極欲天下儉焉必自京師始
欲京師儉焉必自
朝廷始昔漢文帝欲作露臺以惜百金之費
而寢其役宋仁宗夜思燒羊恐以為例而
遏其念夫以天下之大百金與燒羊豈足
惜哉盖防其漸則末流自息也我
===
太祖高皇帝以宮中隙地不起臺榭但令種蔬
曰不忍傷民之財勞民之力
太宗文皇帝所服裏衣袖敝垢納而復出曰自
念當惜福每澣濯更進夫以天下之大隙
地與裏衣豈足靳哉盖謹其微則大者可
知也今
天子踐祚之初凡百政化圖維更新將必遠稽
前代近法
祖宗崇儉德以答
punctuated:
之計是圖，未見其有濟也。然所謂去奢而崇儉者，豈可以他求哉？盖京師者，天下之本；朝廷者，四方之極。欲天下儉焉，必自京師始；欲京師儉焉，必自朝廷始。昔漢文帝欲作露臺，以惜百金之費而寢其役；宋仁宗夜思燒羊，恐以為例而遏其念。夫以天下之大，百金與燒羊豈足惜哉？盖防其漸，則末流自息也。
我太祖高皇帝以宮中隙地不起臺榭，但令種蔬，曰：「不忍傷民之財，勞民之力。」太宗文皇帝所服裏衣，袖敝垢，納而復出，曰：「自念當惜福。」每澣濯更進。夫以天下之大，隙地與裏衣豈足靳哉？盖謹其微，則大者可知也。
今天子踐祚之初，凡百政化，圖維更新，將必遠稽前代，近法祖宗，崇儉德以答
translation_en:
…to pursue only immediate expedients: I have yet to see how this can bring relief. Yet how could what we call eliminating extravagance and honoring frugality be sought elsewhere? The capital is the foundation of the realm, and the imperial court is the pole toward which all regions turn. To make the realm frugal, one must begin with the capital; to make the capital frugal, one must begin with the imperial court. Formerly, Emperor Wen of Han wished to build an open terrace, but canceled the work because he begrudged the expense of a hundred jin of gold. Emperor Renzong of Song craved roast lamb at night, but suppressed the thought for fear of establishing a precedent. Given the vastness of the realm, were a hundred jin of gold and roast lamb really worth sparing? By guarding against the beginnings of extravagance, its downstream consequences cease of themselves.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao had no terraces or pavilions built on vacant ground within the palace, but ordered only that vegetables be planted there. He said, “I cannot bear to deplete the people's wealth or toil their strength away.” When the sleeves of Emperor Taizong Wen's inner garment became worn and dirty, it was put away and then brought out again [?]. He said, “I remind myself that I should cherish my blessings.” Each time it was washed, it was presented to him again. Given the vastness of the realm, were vacant ground and an inner garment really worth being sparing over? By attending carefully to small matters, one's conduct in great matters can be understood.
Now, at the beginning of the Son of Heaven's reign, plans are being made to renew every aspect of government and moral transformation. He will surely look far back to earlier dynasties for guidance and take his own imperial ancestors as his nearer models, honoring the virtue of frugality in order to respond to…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
大意節財源以恤民艱思天地生財有限而不
欲盡錙銖之求知國家為費無窮而不忍
如泥沙之用二月賣新絲蠶婦之勞可念
也五月糶新穀農夫之苦可想也運至仁
於
九重渙大號於天下以禁遊惰以抑鉅族以汰
贓吏以律貴倖則推無不準動無不化浮
靡之習可以祛除淳古之風可以挽回矣
在民者何患其有不足而在官者何慮其
===
有不裕乎否則號令雖繁而風俗日流於
富侈會計雖詳而國用愈至於空虛欲天
下財用之足萬無是理也經理之術恐不
外此塵容俗狀得與進而觀
上國之光尚當以芻蕘鄙見陳之
第五問
沈淳
同考試官教諭廖 批舉目前之切要者
為言而治風俗之道實不外是彼
punctuated:
大意，節財源以恤民艱，思天地生財有限，而不欲盡錙銖之求；知國家為費無窮，而不忍如泥沙之用。二月賣新絲，蠶婦之勞可念也；五月糶新穀，農夫之苦可想也。運至仁於九重，渙大號於天下，以禁遊惰，以抑鉅族，以汰贓吏，以律貴倖，則推無不準，動無不化。浮靡之習可以祛除，淳古之風可以挽回矣。在民者何患其有不足，而在官者何慮其有不裕乎？否則，號令雖繁，而風俗日流於富侈；會計雖詳，而國用愈至於空虛。欲天下財用之足，萬無是理也。經理之術，恐不外此。塵容俗狀，得與進而觀上國之光，尚當以芻蕘鄙見陳之。
第五問
沈淳
同考試官教諭廖批：舉目前之切要者為言，而治風俗之道實不外是。彼
translation_en:
…the great intent [?], conserving financial resources to relieve the people's hardships. He will consider that Heaven and Earth produce wealth in limited quantities and will not wish to exact every last fraction; he will recognize that the state's expenses are endless and will not have the heart to spend wealth as though it were mud and sand. When new silk is sold in the second month, the toil of the women who raise silkworms deserves consideration; when new grain is sold in the fifth month, the hardship of the farmers can be imagined. Let him exercise consummate benevolence within the imperial palace and promulgate a great proclamation throughout the realm, prohibiting idle wandering, restraining powerful clans, dismissing corrupt officials, and disciplining influential imperial favorites. Then every extension of his policies will accord with the proper standard, and every action will bring transformation. Habits of frivolous extravagance can be eliminated, and the simple customs of antiquity restored. Why should the people fear insufficiency, or officials worry that their resources will not be ample?
Otherwise, however numerous the commands, customs will slide daily toward opulence and extravagance; however detailed the accounts, the state's resources will become increasingly depleted. To expect the realm's financial resources to suffice under such circumstances is utterly unreasonable. The methods of managing them, I believe, go no further than this. Though dusty in appearance and commonplace in bearing, I have been permitted to advance and behold the splendor of the imperial realm; I should therefore present my humble views, like those of a grass-cutter or wood-gatherer.
Fifth Question
Shen Chun
Associate Examiner Liao, Instructor, comments: He addresses the most pressing matters of the present, and the way to regulate social customs indeed lies in these measures. Those who …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
迂談者退避三舍矣
考試官教諭朱批論一方事關繫甚
大意之所到辭足發之而筆力雄
健恢乎有餘可以為文矣
考試官學正王批論事精到鑿鑿可
行舉而措之則風移而俗易矣得
士如此允為科目之光
讀孔子告冉有之言則知民富而後教施
讀孔子荅哀公之問則知人存而後政舉
===
夫民俗之未善由民生之未富民生茍富
則其教也不令而從矣民生之未富由有
司之失職有司得人則其富也可立而待
矣為治者因是求之而不失其施為之序
何患風俗之不善耶請陳其說雲貴古西
南夷地風氣晦塞聲教不通淪異域者不
知其幾千萬載我
皇明奄有茲地分郡縣而置官吏列衛所以治
甲兵既以揆文教又以奮武衛百四十年
punctuated:
迂談者退避三舍矣。
考試官教諭朱批：論一方事，關繫甚大。意之所到，辭足發之，而筆力雄健，恢乎有餘，可以為文矣。
考試官學正王批：論事精到，鑿鑿可行，舉而措之，則風移而俗易矣。得士如此，允為科目之光。
讀孔子告冉有之言，則知民富而後教施；讀孔子荅哀公之問，則知人存而後政舉。
夫民俗之未善，由民生之未富；民生茍富，則其教也，不令而從矣。民生之未富，由有司之失職；有司得人，則其富也，可立而待矣。為治者因是求之，而不失其施為之序，何患風俗之不善耶？請陳其說。雲貴，古西南夷地，風氣晦塞，聲教不通，淪異域者，不知其幾千萬載。我皇明奄有茲地，分郡縣而置官吏，列衛所以治甲兵，既以揆文教，又以奮武衛，百四十年
translation_en:
…those who indulge in impractical talk must retreat three full stages.
Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “This essay discusses the affairs of a region, matters of very great consequence. Its language fully expresses the reach of its ideas, and its writing is vigorous and forceful, expansive and more than equal to its task. This qualifies as accomplished composition.”
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: “The discussion is precise and penetrating, and its proposals are demonstrably practicable. Put them into effect, and prevailing habits and customs will change. To obtain a scholar such as this truly brings distinction to the examination system.”
Reading what Confucius told Ran You, we know that instruction can be implemented only after the people have become prosperous; reading Confucius’s answer to Duke Ai’s question, we know that government can be carried out only when the right men are present.
The failure of popular customs to become good arises from the people’s lack of prosperity. If their livelihoods become prosperous, they will follow instruction without being commanded. Their lack of prosperity arises from the responsible officials’ neglect of their duties. If the right men fill these offices, the people’s prosperity can be expected almost immediately. If those who govern pursue the matter on this basis and preserve the proper sequence of measures, why should they worry that customs will not become good? Allow me to explain. Yunnan and Guizhou were anciently the territory of the southwestern Yi. Their prevailing influences were benighted and obstructed, and the civilizing instruction of the imperial court did not reach them. Who knows how many thousands or tens of thousands of years they remained outside the realm? Our august Ming took possession of this land, divided it into prefectures and counties and appointed officials, and established guards and battalions to administer troops and armaments. It both directed civil instruction and strengthened military protection, for one hundred and forty years…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
餘攀鱗附翼之士建功立業之人後先相
望宜乎俗盡衣冠人皆禮義矣然而異言
異服肆行刼奪貪財賤義無情健訟士乖
庠序之教女昧行露之義親戚之恩或薄
婚姻之黨非宜是皆目擊耳聞之實誠有
如執事之所謂者風俗如此果可以為文
明之盛乎愚甞見其端矣田連阡陌者不
一二而地無立錐者盖多焉身被裘帛者
不數人而體無完衣者盖衆焉欠官租者
===
以貧而鬻子女負私貸者以貧而棄屋廬
遇兵興也闔境困於供需遇災傷也比屋
仆於凍餓貧也如此望其能為禮義廉耻
之事乎又甞求其故矣土官之設因其類
而撫之也能撫之者誰歟流官之設宣其
化而安之也能安之者誰歟求牧與芻而
不得視其斃者有之刈葵放手而莫恤傷
其根者有之名為輸稅而所取半入於私
家名為
punctuated:
餘，攀鱗附翼之士、建功立業之人，後先相望。宜乎俗盡衣冠，人皆禮義矣。然而異言異服，肆行刼奪，貪財賤義，無情健訟，士乖庠序之教，女昧《行露》之義，親戚之恩或薄，婚姻之黨非宜。是皆目擊耳聞之實，誠有如執事之所謂者。風俗如此，果可以為文明之盛乎？
愚甞見其端矣。田連阡陌者不一二，而地無立錐者盖多焉；身被裘帛者不數人，而體無完衣者盖衆焉。欠官租者以貧而鬻子女，負私貸者以貧而棄屋廬。遇兵興也，闔境困於供需；遇災傷也，比屋仆於凍餓。貧也如此，望其能為禮義廉耻之事乎？
又甞求其故矣。土官之設，因其類而撫之也，能撫之者誰歟？流官之設，宣其化而安之也，能安之者誰歟？求牧與芻而不得，視其斃者有之；刈葵放手而莫恤，傷其根者有之。名為輸稅，而所取半入於私家；名為
translation_en:
…and more, men who attached themselves to the dragon’s scales and wings—those who rose through service to the dynasty—and men who established achievements and careers have followed one another in succession. Surely, then, everyone should have adopted the dress of civilized society and observed ritual propriety and righteousness. Yet people speak different tongues and wear different dress, brazenly plunder and rob, prize wealth and slight righteousness, lack proper feeling and are quick to litigate. Scholars depart from the teachings of the schools; women fail to understand the moral import of “Drenched with Dew” (Xing lu). Affection between relatives is sometimes thin, and marriage alliances are improper. These are all things actually seen and heard, and indeed accord with what you, sir, have described. With customs like these, can this truly be called a flourishing civilization?
I have observed signs of the problem. Those whose fields stretch across the paths dividing the land are scarcely one or two, while those without enough ground to plant an awl are many. Those clad in furs and silk number only a few, while those without an intact garment are numerous. Those owing government land taxes sell their sons and daughters because of poverty; those burdened by private loans abandon their homes because of poverty. When troops are mobilized, the entire territory is distressed by demands for supplies; when disaster strikes, household after household collapses from cold and hunger. With poverty such as this, can we expect people to act with ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame?
I have also sought the causes. Native officials were established to govern and care for people according to their own kind; but who among them can truly care for the people? Regular officials were established to spread the dynasty’s civilizing influence and bring the people peace; but who among them can truly bring peace? Some seek pasture and fodder, fail to obtain them, and simply watch their charges perish. Some cut mallows with an unchecked hand, heedlessly injuring their roots. In name they collect taxes, but half of what they take enters private households; in name…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
詔恩而斯民不蒙於實惠有司如此望其能有
飽煖安逸之民乎此風俗之所以不善也
為今之計不在責於下而在責於上不在
治其民而在治其官臨以藩臬監以臺臣
此平日之舊規也流官宜知謹矣然守法
者固有而貪饕者甘心於敗伏辜者既往
而方来者蹈轍而行法網之設雖嚴而姦
亦不絕矣其如之何哉嘗觀仕於茲地有
以願告遠方而来者非其年邁則以家貧
===
有以地里非宜而来者道途勞苦資費窘
乏凡此者皆不足為其持廉之地也雲貴
王土也豈宜鄙薄其地而以苟禄者加之
乎是非末學所敢議也在廟堂議也必也
銓選得人而若輩者不以尸位則吾民之
福矣清其宗派令其朝
覲皆近時新典也土官宜知化矣然清宗派固
免爭襲以殃民赴朝
覲不無搔擾而害衆觀光之效未臻而民已受
punctuated:
詔恩，而斯民不蒙於實惠。有司如此，望其能有飽煖安逸之民乎？此風俗之所以不善也。
為今之計，不在責於下，而在責於上；不在治其民，而在治其官。臨以藩臬，監以臺臣，此平日之舊規也。流官宜知謹矣。然守法者固有，而貪饕者甘心於敗；伏辜者既往，而方来者蹈轍而行。法網之設雖嚴，而姦亦不絕矣。其如之何哉？嘗觀仕於茲地，有以願告遠方而来者，非其年邁，則以家貧；有以地里非宜而来者，道途勞苦，資費窘乏。凡此者，皆不足為其持廉之地也。雲貴，王土也，豈宜鄙薄其地，而以苟禄者加之乎？是非末學所敢議也，在廟堂議也。必也銓選得人，而若輩者不以尸位，則吾民之福矣。
清其宗派，令其朝覲，皆近時新典也。土官宜知化矣。然清宗派，固免爭襲以殃民；赴朝覲，不無搔擾而害衆。觀光之效未臻，而民已受
translation_en:
…imperial favor proclaimed by edict, yet these people receive no tangible benefit. With the responsible officials behaving thus, can one expect the people under them to be well fed, warmly clothed, and at ease? This is why local customs are unsatisfactory.
The policy needed now is to hold those above accountable, rather than those below, and to regulate the officials rather than the people. Placing them under the authority of the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners and the oversight of censorial officials is the established practice. The centrally appointed officials ought therefore to know to act circumspectly. Yet although some do observe the law, the rapacious willingly court their own downfall. Those who have suffered punishment pass from the scene, while newcomers follow in their tracks. Though the net of the law is tightly drawn, wrongdoing never ceases. What can be done about this? I have observed that among those serving here, some have come after petitioning for service in distant regions: if they are not advanced in years, they come because their families are poor. Others have come because geographical considerations made an appointment elsewhere unsuitable [?]; they endure arduous journeys and lack sufficient funds for their expenses. None of these circumstances provides a sound basis for maintaining integrity. Yunnan and Guizhou are the sovereign’s territory. How could it be right to disparage these lands and set over them men who merely seek a salary? This is not something that an insignificant scholar such as I dares to deliberate upon; it is for deliberation at court. If personnel selection secures suitable men and people of that sort no longer occupy offices without fulfilling their duties, it will be a blessing for our people.
Clarifying their lines of descent and requiring them to attend imperial audiences are both recently instituted regulations. The native officials ought therefore to know to reform themselves. Yet while clarifying lines of descent does prevent succession disputes from bringing calamity upon the people, journeys to attend imperial audiences are not without disturbances that harm the populace. Before their visits to behold the splendor of the court have achieved their intended effect, the people have already suffered…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
困矣其亦如之何哉嘗觀治夷方者律令
不施而有從其土俗之例恩威未及而遂
養成驕惰之風凡此皆不足動其守法之
念也土官王臣也豈宜鄙夷其人而以姑
息者待之乎是非末學所能議也在地方
重臣之議也必也操縱有法而若輩者於
此革心則夷方之慶矣如是則有司者無
不得人而為之上者又從而提撕警覺之
先責之以養民則必有實惠之施而後責
===
之以教民則不為虛文之設為之民者衣
食足而知榮辱倉廩實而知禮節則椎卉
者可以用夏變夷矣刼奪者可以雖賞不
竊矣義利自明而無貪得之恥曲直自喻
而無健訟之非士盡其業而衣食不困於
心女貞其行而禮義可制其慾骨肉之恩
知所念也婚姻之禮有所謹也是則責成
有司固更化之道也斡旋之機又豈外於
是哉雖然此特論雲貴之風俗姑就其所
punctuated:
困矣，其亦如之何哉？嘗觀治夷方者，律令不施，而有從其土俗之例；恩威未及，而遂養成驕惰之風。凡此皆不足動其守法之念也。土官，王臣也，豈宜鄙夷其人，而以姑息者待之乎？是非末學所能議也，在地方重臣之議也。必也操縱有法，而若輩者於此革心，則夷方之慶矣。
如是，則有司者無不得人，而為之上者又從而提撕警覺之。先責之以養民，則必有實惠之施；而後責之以教民，則不為虛文之設。為之民者，衣食足而知榮辱，倉廩實而知禮節，則椎卉者可以用夏變夷矣，刼奪者可以雖賞不竊矣。義利自明，而無貪得之恥；曲直自喻，而無健訟之非。士盡其業，而衣食不困於心；女貞其行，而禮義可制其慾。骨肉之恩知所念也，婚姻之禮有所謹也。是則責成有司，固更化之道也，斡旋之機又豈外於是哉？雖然，此特論雲貴之風俗，姑就其所
translation_en:
…hardship. What, then, can be done about this? I have observed that those who govern the non-Han regions fail to enforce the statutes and ordinances, invoking precedents for following local customs; their beneficence and authority do not reach these regions, and thus they foster habits of arrogance and indolence. None of this can stir a resolve to abide by the law. Native officials are subjects of the sovereign: how could it be right to look down upon them and treat them with indulgence? This is not something that I, a humble student, am competent to discuss; it is for the senior officials in charge of these regions to deliberate upon. If restraint and latitude are exercised according to proper principles, and these men thereby undergo a change of heart, this will be a blessing for the non-Han regions.
In this way, all responsible offices will be filled by suitable men, and their superiors will further guide and admonish them. First require them to provide for the people, and they will have to confer tangible benefits; then require them to instruct the people, and their efforts will not amount to empty formalities. Once the people under their charge have adequate clothing and food, they will understand honor and disgrace; once their granaries are full, they will understand ritual and propriety. Those who wear their hair in mallet-shaped knots and clothe themselves in grasses can then be transformed through the civilization of the central lands, and those who plunder and rob can become unwilling to steal even if rewarded for doing so. The distinction between righteousness and profit will become clear of itself, removing the shame of grasping for gain; right and wrong will become self-evident, removing the fault of habitual litigation. Men will fully pursue their occupations, without anxiety over clothing and food weighing upon their minds; women will remain chaste in conduct, and ritual and righteousness will restrain their desires. People will know to cherish the bonds of kinship and carefully observe the rites of marriage. Thus, holding the responsible officials accountable for results is indeed the way to transform customs. How could the means of bringing about such a change lie elsewhere? Nevertheless, this discusses only the customs of Yunnan and Guizhou, provisionally addressing what…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
宜者言之若夫一道德以同俗因奢儉以
示教是則敦本之論不可無者而規模廣
大綱領宏闊未遽行焉今日之事則當先
於其要者而後及於是可也譬之醫家先
之薑桂大黃以破其痼疾而後以參苓芝
术以養其元氣則病可去而人可壽醫之
道得矣以風俗為念者用治疾之道治之
則不善之弊庶幾其必瘳矣乎狂斐之言
未達至計進退之則惟命
punctuated: 宜者言之。若夫一道德以同俗，因奢儉以示教，是則敦本之論不可無者，而規模廣大，綱領宏闊，未遽行焉。今日之事，則當先於其要者，而後及於是可也。譬之醫家，先之薑桂大黃以破其痼疾，而後以參苓芝术以養其元氣，則病可去而人可壽，醫之道得矣。以風俗為念者，用治疾之道治之，則不善之弊庶幾其必瘳矣乎！狂斐之言，未達至計，進退之則惟命。
translation_en: …speaking of what is appropriate. As for unifying moral principles to bring customs into accord, and adapting instruction to extravagance or frugality, these are indispensable arguments for strengthening the foundations. Yet their scope is vast and their guiding principles far-reaching; they cannot be implemented at once. In handling present affairs, one should first address the most pressing matters and only afterward proceed to these broader measures. By analogy with medical practice, first use ginger, cinnamon, and rhubarb to overcome a chronic illness, and afterward use ginseng, poria, lingzhi, and atractylodes to nourish the patient's vital energy. Then the illness can be removed and the patient's life prolonged: the proper method of medicine has been attained. If those concerned with customs treat them by the methods used to cure illness, might not their harmful defects surely be healed? These rash and ill-considered words fall short of the best counsel. Whether they are accepted or rejected, I submit entirely to your command.

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試録後序
聖天子正位大寳之初適天下開
科取士寔
龍飛盛舉也有司慎重厥事聘儒
紳以專文柄麒濫竽焉嘗考
諸志在昔西南諸郡半隷雲
南後始割為貴州故士之應
===
試者猶附先時有議雲貴設
科法者
孝宗敬皇帝申命折衷定以雲南
三十一人貴州十九人仍合
試之特名其録為雲貴鄉試
遵
制取擇其文之議論詞氣正者萃
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試録後序

聖天子正位大寳之初，適天下開科取士，寔龍飛盛舉也。有司慎重厥事，聘儒紳以專文柄，麒濫竽焉。嘗考諸志，在昔西南諸郡半隷雲南，後始割為貴州，故士之應試者猶附。先時有議雲貴設科法者，孝宗敬皇帝申命折衷，定以雲南三十一人、貴州十九人，仍合試之，特名其録為《雲貴鄉試》。遵制取擇其文之議論詞氣正者，萃
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

At the beginning of the sagely Son of Heaven’s accession to the imperial throne, examinations were duly held throughout the realm to select scholars—a truly grand undertaking marking the dragon’s ascent. The responsible officials treated this matter with great care, inviting learned gentlemen to take charge of evaluating the compositions. I, Qi, unworthily served among them.

I once consulted the gazetteers: in former times, half the prefectures of the southwest belonged to Yunnan; only later were lands separated to form Guizhou. Thus scholars presenting themselves for examination continued to be attached to Yunnan. Earlier, when proposals were made concerning the arrangements for holding examinations in Yunnan and Guizhou, Emperor Xiaozong Jing issued further instructions settling the matter: the quotas were fixed at thirty-one men for Yunnan and nineteen for Guizhou, with the examination still held jointly. Its record was specifically entitled “Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination.” In obedience to the imperial directive, we selected compositions whose arguments, diction, and tenor were correct, and gathered them …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而為錄將以
進呈傳諸天下麒謹序之切惟
我
國家取士以科目為正途當時
以科目所出之士為正流士
之所業以六經為正學爾諸
士從正學履正途稱正流其
===
為號大矣盍思所以圖之孔
子曰政者正也行將上春官
對
大廷駸駸嚮用從政有日烏可
不迪于正耶必正心以脩身
正己以率物正其誼而不謀
其利在
punctuated: 而為錄，將以進呈，傳諸天下。麒謹序之。切惟我國家取士，以科目為正途；當時以科目所出之士為正流；士之所業，以六經為正學。爾諸士從正學，履正途，稱正流，其為號大矣！盍思所以圖之？孔子曰：「政者，正也。」行將上春官，對大廷，駸駸嚮用，從政有日，烏可不迪于正耶？必正心以脩身，正己以率物，正其誼而不謀其利。在
translation_en: …and compile them into a record, to be respectfully presented to the throne and circulated throughout the realm. I, Qi, respectfully provide this preface. I earnestly reflect that our dynasty regards the examinations as the proper path for recruiting officials; the present age regards men who emerge from the examinations as the orthodox stream of scholars; and, in their studies, scholars regard the Six Classics as orthodox learning. You scholars follow orthodox learning, tread the proper path, and are called the orthodox stream. These are weighty designations! Should you not consider how to live up to them? Confucius said: “To govern is to be upright.” Soon you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites for examination and answer questions in the imperial court. You will steadily advance toward appointment, and the day will come when you participate in government. How could you fail to walk in uprightness? You must rectify your hearts to cultivate yourselves, rectify yourselves to lead others, and uphold what is right without seeking personal profit. In …

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
朝廷則以正道事
君居民社則以正令善俗其或所
遭不同亦必確乎以正自持
凡意料所不及者吾惟順受
其正焉庶幾不負所學不負
所取不負所稱而有以全天
地之正氣無愧於正人君子
===
之流矣顧不偉歟舍此曲學
以阿世枉道以徇人俾天下
後世指其名而非議之則非
今日主司之所望也自洪武
設科至于今凡數十舉矣每
科必有錄每錄必有序每序
必有說〔麒〕無能加敢謂道莫
punctuated:
朝廷則以正道事君，居民社則以正令善俗。其或所遭不同，亦必確乎以正自持。凡意料所不及者，吾惟順受其正焉。庶幾不負所學，不負所取，不負所稱，而有以全天地之正氣，無愧於正人君子之流矣。顧不偉歟？舍此，曲學以阿世，枉道以徇人，俾天下後世指其名而非議之，則非今日主司之所望也。
自洪武設科至于今，凡數十舉矣。每科必有錄，每錄必有序，每序必有說。〔麒〕無能加，敢謂道莫
translation_en:
…at court, serve the ruler by the upright Way; when administering local communities, improve their customs through upright ordinances. Even if the circumstances encountered differ, one must remain firmly upright in one's conduct. Whatever lies beyond one's anticipation, one should accept submissively in accordance with what is right. Thus one may hope to betray neither what one has learned, nor the grounds on which one was selected, nor the designation one bears, and thereby preserve intact the upright vital force of Heaven and Earth, without shame among upright men and gentlemen. Would this not be magnificent? To abandon this, distorting one's learning to curry favor with the age and bending the Way to accommodate others, so that people throughout the realm and in later generations point to one's name and condemn it—this is not what today's examination officials hope for.
From the establishment of the examinations in the Hongwu reign until now, there have been several dozen sittings. Every examination has its record, every record its preface, and every preface its exposition. I, 〔Qi 麒〕[?], have nothing to add, but venture to say that, as for the Way, nothing…

title: 正德二年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
大於正願與就有道而正焉
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教
諭朱祺謹序
punctuated:
大於正，願與就有道而正焉。
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭朱祺謹序。
translation_en:
…greater than rectitude. I wish to join others in seeking out those who possess the Way and receiving their correction.
Respectfully composed as a preface by Zhu Qi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
